Engineering Manager

Sheffield

Full-time / Permanent

Set the direction. Raise the standard. Deliver engineering that works.…

At Eclipse Magnetics, part of the Spear & Jackson Group, we’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our Sheffield-based team. Reporting to the Operations Manager, you’ll take ownership of engineering delivery across the business, from day-to-day design work to new product development, cost control, and technical compliance.

You’ll oversee the design of orders and development of new products, ensuring everything meets company standards and relevant regulations, including Machinery and ATEX directives. Alongside this, you’ll manage departmental costs, review technical costings, and lead continuous improvement initiatives that reduce waste and improve efficiency.

This role is as much about structure as it is about delivery. You’ll refine engineering workflows, embed best practices across design and documentation, and ensure the team consistently delivers accurate, high-quality work. You’ll identify risks early, remove bottlenecks, and keep projects moving at pace without compromising standards.

You’ll also work closely with other departments, keeping communication clear and making sure engineering supports wider business priorities. From cost estimates to lead times, your input will help ensure projects are realistic, achievable, and well executed.

At its core, this is a leadership role. You’ll manage and develop the engineering team, building a high-performing environment where people are supported, challenged, and able to grow. Through regular feedback and a hands-on approach, you’ll strengthen capability and close any skills gaps within the team.

We’re looking for someone with experience in a fast-paced 

manufacturing environment, who has led teams and delivered projects successfully. You’ll be confident using CAD tools such as SolidWorks and AutoCAD, and comfortable working within regulated engineering frameworks. Strong organisation, clear communication, and practical problem-solving are key.

This is a full-time, site-based role in Sheffield. If you’re looking for a role where you can shape how engineering is delivered, not just what gets delivered, this is an opportunity to make a real impact.

A Package of Employee Benefits:

At Eclipse Magnetics we constantly recognise that our success has been built by the hard work, talent and ingenuity of our employees. We invest in our employees and also strive to make Eclipse Magnetics an attractive proposition to new employees. We offer a range of employee benefits: -

· Company sponsored learning and development - training courses, further education, vocational training

· Modern working environment - complete with free on-site parking

· Employee discounts - excellent discounts on group products including Spear & Jackson Garden and hand tools

· A range of social and charity fund raising initiatives

· Life Assurance Scheme - death in service cover

· Company supported volunteer days - support local good causes without losing pay or holiday entitlement

· Free social BBQs during work time - enabling inter-department relationships to flourish

· Free fresh fruit - helping our employees eat healthily

· December shutdown leave of 3 days in addition to your annual leave entitlement

· Access to free independent mortgage advice for you, your family, and friends

· Promoting health & wellbeing - awareness programmes, voluntary healthcare cash plan, Workplace Mental Health First Aiders

· Employee Assistance Programme - 24-hour personal and life management support service for you and members of your household

About Abion
Abion is a fast-growing and purpose-built IP firm on a mission to become Europe's leading intellectual property powerhouse. With nearly 30 years of experience at the crossroads of law and technology, we offer a full ecosystem of IP solutions spanning across trademark management, domain name management, web security, and online brand protection.
We help the world's most ambitious brands protect their intellectual property across domains, trademarks, and digital channels. We combine deep legal expertise with a growing technology platform, and becoming a data-driven, AI-powered business is a clear focus of our strategy. This role is central to that ambition.
About the Role
Abion is building its data and AI function from the ground up, and this is one of the first roles in it. As a Data Platform Engineer, you will report into the Head of Data and AI and be a senior, hands-on engineer at the heart of the build, creating the enterprise analytics and integration layer that brings data together from across Abion’s systems into a complete, trusted source for the whole business.
You’ll take work from first conversations with the business through to secure, scalable production solutions, using modern AI-assisted tools to deliver quickly without compromising on quality. We see data as the foundation for everything we want to achieve with analytics and AI, and the platform you build will underpin the insights, applications and AI services used across the business.
Key Responsibilities
We’re building a modern, cloud-based data platform on open standards, with the flexibility to adopt the best tools as the market evolves. That means Lakehouse platforms, event-driven and real-time integration, knowledge graph technologies and AI-assisted engineering, giving Abion near real-time insight and a complete, trusted view of the business.
• Build Abion’s enterprise data platform, establishing a scalable, trusted foundation for analytics, integration and AI.
• Integrate data from a wide range of business systems and external sources using modern techniques such as APIs, change data capture, event streaming and mirroring, enabling near real-time reporting.
• Build a complete, trusted knowledge layer, connecting data with business definitions and context so that people, applications and AI can use it with confidence.
• Develop robust ETL/ELT pipelines and model data into tested, reusable datasets, working with business owners to define and certify the data and KPIs that matter most.
• Deliver trusted, self-service reporting and make data available to applications and AI tools across the business.
• Put governance in place from the start: access control, sensitive data classification, lineage, data quality and observability.
• Monitor platform performance and cost, keeping both under control as use of data services grows.
• Use AI-assisted development tools to accelerate delivery while maintaining high engineering standards.
• Work directly with teams across the business and Technology, and champion data, AI and modern ways of working.
Must haves
• Minimum of 7 years of hands-on experience working professionally with data, in any capacity such as engineering, analytics, architecture, or platform development.
• Significant experience building and running a modern data platform on Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake or similar, using a medallion architecture, including managing ingestion performance and forecasting platform costs.
• Strong Python/PySpark and SQL, with a track record of production ETL/ELT pipelines integrating data from varied business systems, including less well-documented sources.
• Experience delivering self-service data and reporting through tools such as Power BI or custom solutions, with governance (access control, classification, lineage and data quality) implemented in practice.
• Hands-on experience with an enterprise-wide data catalogue in active use for cross-system governance, ownership models and access management.
• Experience working with unstructured data and building on top of it, for example through knowledge graphs or ontologies.
• Experience building secure, scalable solutions on Azure or an equivalent cloud platform.
• Regular use of AI-assisted development tools, such as Claude Code or Cursor, with the judgement to review and validate AI-generated output.
• The knowledge to architect solutions that use AI and apply best practice when building with it, including security, data privacy, testing and cost control.
• Proven end-to-end delivery, from concept to production, in a small, high-impact team, using CI/CD and DevOps best practices and working in an agile, iterative way.
Nice to have
• Experience delivering enterprise AI solutions, such as agents and workflows built on Microsoft Foundry or similar.
• Experience in IP, legal tech or compliance-adjacent industries.
• Awareness of AI and data regulations and standards, such as the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001 and GDPR, and how they shape the way solutions are designed and governed.
About you
• A builder who loves exploring and finding solutions to hard problems.
• Able to break down complex system and data problems into clear, deliverable work.
• Driven, dedicated and keen to see ideas through to production.
• Passionate about data and AI, up to date with new trends, and happy to bring fresh ideas to the table.
• Enthusiastic and personable, with the technical depth to back up your stakeholder skills.
Why choose Abion?
Join Europe’s leading Intellectual Property firm, where you'll thrive in a fast-paced, international environment that values transparency, openness, and accountability.
At Abion, we believe in working hard and having fun together. In this dynamic role, you’ll make an impact in the IP world while collaborating with a talented, global team of experts. We encourage a balanced lifestyle, offering freedom with responsibility. Plus, we love celebrating successes and enjoying team activities that bring us closer together!
Ready to Join Us?
If you are ready to make a significant impact in the Intellectual Property industry, we would love to hear from you!

As a CX Engineer, you will discover, design, build, test, and support the go-live of Zoom Contact Center, Zoom AI and Zoom Phone for our enterprise and public sector clients across every industry.
You'll own the technical delivery of a client project from kick-off through to go-live. That means running discovery workshops, designing the solution, configuring the platform, testing it properly, training the client, porting their numbers and standing beside them on go-live day.

• Zoom Contact Center, including Quality Management and Workforce Management

• Zoom AI, including Zoom Virtual Agent and AI Expert Assist

• Zoom Phone & Zoom Workplace

Why This Role is Exciting
• Real AI, in production: You'll design and build agentic AI agents with Zoom Virtual Agent and AI Expert Assist, with proper guardrails, for live contact centres handling real customer contacts.

• End-to-end ownership: You will see a project through from kick-off to go-live, working on every phase to deliver meaningful outcomes for our clients.

• Variety: One month it's a fast-growing retailer, the next it's a healthcare provider or a local authority. No two clients are the same.

• Award-winning partner: We were the UK's first Zoom Contact Center partner in 2022, Zoom's CX Partner of the Year in 2024, and Solution Deployment Excellence Partner 2025.

• Integration at the core: You'll connect Zoom to clients' CRMs and line-of-business systems, using our own IntegrationHub for Zoom platform.

• First access to what's next: Zoom ships new CX and AI capability constantly. You'll be at the forefront of learning it, testing it and deploying it for clients early.

What You Will Be Doing
Most of your time is spent with clients, taking a project from kick-off to go-live, working with our internal teams to keep delivery on track and your product knowledge sharp.
Discovery & Requirements
• Take part in project kick-off meetings with the client and our Technical Delivery Leads.

• Lead discovery workshops to obtain and capture the client's requirements across contact centre, AI, and telephony.

• Demo Zoom capability so the clients understand the “art of the possible” to help shape what they need.

• Challenge requirements where there's a better way to solve the underlying problem.

Solution Design
• Design CX and AI solutions that solve the client's problems, documented clearly for them to sign off.

• Design IVR and call flows, queue and routing strategies, and agent and supervisor experiences.

Build & Configuration
• Implement and configure Zoom Contact Center, Zoom AI and Zoom Phone to the signed-off design.

• Configure Quality Management and Workforce Management to support how the client runs its operation.

• Build and refine Zoom AI agents iteratively: test, tune, retest, until they perform reliably.

Testing & User Acceptance
• Test everything you build end to end, including the unhappy paths, so every journey is robust when things go wrong.

• Support the client through User Acceptance Testing, making sure defects are triaged and resolved quickly.

Training & Enablement

• Deliver admin training and enablement sessions to the client's more technical staff, so they can run the platform day to day.

• Manage the number porting process with the client and Zoom's porting team.

• Attend weekly project calls with the client and contribute to weekly project status reports.

• Keep pace with Zoom's product roadmap, learning new features and capabilities as they launch.

• Present at our weekly internal Show & Tell on what you've been building.

AI Governance and Assurance - Senior Specialist

Role purpose
As our AI Governance and Assurance lead, you will run the day-to-day operation and continual improvement of Accelya's AI Management System, under the strategic direction of the SVP, Privacy, AI & Data Governance. You will translate regulatory obligations, approved policy and ISO/IEC 42001 requirements into practical governance activities, control testing, evidence and reporting. The successful candidate will need to ensure AI is governed and assured as it is designed, built and released across our products.

This position will be responsible for acting as the main governance partner to our Product and Technology teams, so that we remain compliant in how we integrate AI into our solutions. The focus will be on embedding governance into the product development lifecycle, assessing AI risk and impact, testing controls and getting Accelya ready for independent ISO/IEC 42001 assessment. • Run the day-to-day operation and continual improvement of Accelya's AI Management System, maintaining the control records, evidence library and action plan, and supporting readiness for internal review and independent ISO/IEC 42001 assessment

• Operate proportionate AI Governance by Design across customer-facing products and internal use cases, from intake and risk classification through design, development, testing, deployment, production monitoring and retirement

Company Overview

We are the better way to work in finance. As private equity’s value creation partner, we sit at the heart of PE—where sponsors and CFOs meet. Through financial consulting rooted in data, technology, and AI, we help clients drive value—supporting the office of the CFO to drive end-to-end value creation.

If you crave challenging work and are looking to grow, come solve complex problems alongside a team of finance and technology professionals in a supportive, collaborative environment.

Backed by leading private equity investors, we are a high-growth, entrepreneurial firm with a global presence. We are looking for people who want to help build something great and make a lasting impact.

Transactions 

Private equity sponsors are doing more carve-outs and integrations, on tighter timelines and with less room for slippage. For the CFO of a PE-backed company, a transaction lands on top of the day job: a finance function to stand up or combine, new reporting and control requirements to meet, and synergy commitments the sponsor’s value creation thesis depends on. The demands stretch across the wider CFO remit and are felt acutely in Europe, where regulatory and entity complexity varies country by country. Most finance teams haven’t done this before and can’t absorb it alongside business as usual, so the gap between the deal plan and what Finance can deliver is where value can be won or lost.

Accordion’s Transactions Practice is a dedicated team supporting PE-backed portfolio companies through carve-outs and integrations. On carve-outs, we support clients from pre-signing through to post-close, with our deepest involvement between signing and close, when readiness is built. On integrations, we help clients plan for the first 100 days ahead of completion and then execute them once the deal closes, including identifying and tracking synergies. What sets us apart is that we are hands-on and outcome-focused. We work alongside the finance team to get Finance rapidly ready for what the transaction demands. We are doers and problem solvers who stay accountable for results, not just the plan.

This role is based in our London office. Ideal candidates should be local to the desired location, with the flexibility to work remotely 1–2 days a week, blending the best of both worlds for efficiency and collaboration.

What You’ll Do:

• Lead client engagements and teams in planning and executing PE-backed carve-outs and merger integrations, through a Finance operating model lens, to include:

• Day 1 readiness and execution

• TSA scoping, costing and exit plans

• 100-day plans and execution

• Synergy identification, model development and tracking

• Interdependencies identification

• PE deal teams, Operating Partners and portfolio company CFO stakeholder management and reporting

• Lead the SMO/IMO for the Finance workstream, including development of functional carve-out and integration plans and execution activities, with heavy focus on cross-functional interdependencies by:

• Ensuring all Finance activities are captured and understood and completed timely

• Working alongside cross-functional teams (Operations, Commercial, HR, IT, Legal, and Tax, as well as other external advisors), to support separation, integration execution, strategic initiatives, and organisational alignment

• Support sell side readiness in terms of Finance Operating model, Finance Organisation structure, Reporting and Process’

• Manage multiple client engagements at the same time, ensure projects are on track, manage client expectations and perform course corrections when necessary

• Interact and build relationships with CFO and other C-suite personnel at portfolio company as well as representatives from Private Equity sponsors

• Assist in growing the firm by identifying and driving business development activities for both the Transactions team but for all the Services offered by the London office

• Regularly and extensively travel across Europe to work with clients in the relevant jurisdictions

• Identify and sponsor internal initiatives

• Identify follow-on opportunities for other Accordion teams to support

• Develop presentations for client proposals and thought leadership materials

• Contribute to the refinement of existing deliverables and approach documents, identifying opportunities to further leverage AI in our client delivery

• Mentor/coach our people

You Have: 

• 10+ years of relevant professional experience, specialising in Finance carve-outs and merger integration

• Buy-side Private Equity experience

• Functional subject matter expertise in Finance & Accounting and ideally one or more of the following:

• Information Technology

• Human Resources

• Operations

• Supply Chain / Procurement

• Communications planning

• Outstanding written and verbal communication skills to influence both internal and external relationships

• Superior problem-solving and analytical skills that can be utilised to translate disparate data into meaningful insights for our clients, leveraging AI and other available tooling

• Experience managing multiple projects at the same time, managing not only client/sponsor dynamics but internal team dynamics as well

• Willingness to get involved in implementation and working directly with the client to solve problems

• SMO / IMO experience

• Prior experience serving interim or permanent finance roles (i.e. VP Finance, Controller or CFO) helpful but not required

• ACA/CIMA preferred

You Are:

• Self-starter with a strong work ethic

• Leader of others; you lead by example

• Strong team player, able to work with team members across all levels

• Able to effectively communicate complex issues and solutions, and raise issues to senior team members when necessary

• Comfortable managing projects with multiple complex workstreams while also focused on managing and driving your own workstream.

• Excited to be part of a growing team, with a focus on driving future sustainable revenue

• Full of entrepreneurial spirit and comfortable in a fluid, flat organisation

• Knowledgeable about the relationship between Private Equity sponsors and their portfolio companies

• Passionate about delivering exceptional client service

• Willing to get your hands dirty in the details of a project while simultaneously seeing the whole picture

• Someone who enjoys coaching others and doing meaningful work

job_description:
PURPOSE OF THE ROLE

We are recruiting a Supervising Lawyer to support our growing Leeds Real Estate practice. This role will focus on supervising and developing junior lawyers in the Leeds office rather than managing a personal caseload.

The role will provide ad hoc supervision across live matters to improve the quality and consistency of work. You will play a key role in helping the partners to manage the training and development of more junior lawyers as well as supervising on complex client-facing work of our Tier 1 transactional real estate offering.

THE TEAM

The Real Estate Group is one of Addleshaw Goddard's largest practices. Within this, the Leeds Transactional Real Estate team is a substantial and growing team that forms a key part of the firm's national Tier 1 real estate offering.

The team advises on high-value investment, development, landlord and tenant, and portfolio transactions for a broad range of clients, including leading investors, developers, occupiers, funders, corporates and public sector bodies. It is recognised for combining technical excellence with a commercial, business-focused approach.

The team has built a high-performing yet collegiate culture, giving junior lawyers early responsibility within a genuinely supportive environment. A key differentiator is its commitment to structured supervision, training and knowledge management, reflected in this dedicated Supervising Lawyer role.

As a Supervising Lawyer, your primary clients will be the Leeds real estate lawyers you support and develop, and by extension the external clients they advise.

WHAT TO EXPECT IN THIS ROLE

In this role, you will:

- Provide supervision, teaching and coaching to junior lawyers (particularly those at 0–3 PQE) across landlord and tenant, property management, sales and purchases, development and client account work, reviewing drafts, providing feedback and helping build their legal judgement, commercial awareness and confidence.
- Support the delivery of high-quality legal work by providing targeted supervision across live matters, helping junior lawyers prioritise workloads, manage deadlines and understand their role within the wider transaction and providing constructive feedback without carrying a personal caseload.
- Support training and knowledge development initiatives by identifying and feeding back common themes from supervision to Senior/Principal Supervising Lawyers, assisting with the preparation and delivery of local office training, promoting knowledge sharing and continuous improvement within the team, and supporting Knowledge Lawyer (KL) initiatives.
- Undertake supplemental fee-earning work, where agreed on a case-by-case basis, including preparing title reports and lease reports, conducting legal research, completing discrete project-based tasks, responding to peer queries, as well as carrying out peer reviews.
- Help junior lawyers navigate the increasingly AI enabled legal services world; balancing the challenges of maintaining the integrity of legal advice whilst harnessing the productivity gain benefits. An in depth understanding of AI is not required but a willingness to learn about its application to our work and to be open minded about the benefits and challenges of embracing AI is welcome.

AREAS OF KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE

You will be:

- Experienced real estate lawyer, ideally with a minimum of seven years' current PQE gained in private practice or in-house, with strong experience in investment acquisitions and disposals, landlord and tenant matters, asset and estate management, and development work, together with a solid understanding of current market practice and commercially acceptable negotiation positions.
- Strong technical and communication skills, able to explain complex legal issues clearly and turn technical law into practical, commercial guidance.
- Passionate about developing others, with experience of supervision, coaching and providing constructive feedback, and the confidence to work effectively with stakeholders from trainees to partners.
- Committed to helping lawyers build the skills needed to deliver practical client solutions, manage competing priorities effectively, draft high-quality legal documents, and perform confidently under pressure.
- Inquisitive, enthusiastic, and committed to continuous learning, with a genuine interest in understanding clients' objectives and fostering a culture of quality, innovation, and collaboration.

Our story of international growth is built on a performance mindset, innovation and true collaboration. We believe results follow relationships, so we work closely with each other, and develop deep client connections to deliver.

Our award-winning culture balances high standards and hard work with genuine care – looking out for each other, supporting professional development, in a down to earth and inclusive environment. We do the right things in the right ways, combining commercial excellence and innovative thinking with teamwork. We are committed to supporting flexible working where possible and are happy to discuss how the role could be shaped to meet both business needs and the preferences of the successful candidate.

Leadership and Team Management: Providing direction and support to the HR Admin team, ensuring that all members are aligned with the firm's objectives and are working efficiently towards common goals. This involves mentoring team members, identifying training needs, and fostering a positive and collaborative team environment.
Operational Excellence: Overseeing the day-to-day HR administrative operations with a keen focus on optimising processes and ensuring the smooth execution of HR tasks. This includes managing the employee lifecycle, from onboarding to offboarding, and everything in between.

This requires excellent communication skills and the ability to understand and address the diverse needs of different departments and individuals.

Championing a culture and mindset to be a centre of excellence within the team and ensuring the highest standards at all times.
Supporting other HR Operations Managers as needed, representing the Admin team.

Proven experience in HR administration, as well as strong knowledge of HR processes and best practices.
Excellent leadership and people management skills, with a proven track record of leading a team.

job_description:
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced and forward-thinking Senior Manager, Labor Relations for the EMEA region. This role will help develop and deliver our approach to labor relations and social dialogue across the region. 

Working closely with the EMEA Director of Employee & Labor Relations, you will help set regional priorities, advise the business on complex labor relations matters, and build effective relationships with employee representatives. You will directly lead engagement with the Dutch Works Council and manage a small team of Labor Relations Consultants responsible for our German, French, and Spanish Works Councils.

We are looking for someone who brings strategic thinking, curiosity and sound judgment, with a natural ability to cut through complexity and offer clear, practical advice. You will be an expert at balancing business priorities with a genuine commitment to meaningful social dialogue.

What You'll Do
• Drive regional strategy: Partner with the Director of ELR to develop and implement our EMEA Labor Relations and social dialogue strategy, ensuring it reflects both business priorities and local requirements.
• Lead works council engagement: Directly manage the Dutch Works Council relationship while providing strategic oversight and guidance to the Labor Relations Consultants responsible for the German, French, and Spanish Works Councils.
• Enable the business: Partner with the business to understand their priorities, anticipate labor relations challenges, and develop practical solutions that support business objectives while respecting social dialogue obligations.
• Stay ahead: Anticipate emerging labor relations trends, risks, regulatory developments, and potential challenges, helping the business plan ahead and make informed decisions.
• Lead and develop the team: Manage, coach, and empower a small team of experienced Labor Relations Consultants, setting priorities and ensuring effective regional delivery.
• Drive operational excellence and insights: Evolve how Labor Relations operates across EMEA, strengthening intake, tracking, reporting, and governance to improve data quality, consistency, and visibility of key activities and risks, while providing meaningful insights to inform priorities and decision-making.

What You'll Bring
• Significant Labor Relations experience in a complex multinational environment, with deep knowledge of European works councils and social dialogue
• Hands-on experience engaging with works councils, particularly in the Netherlands, and navigating consultation processes across EMEA
• Proven experience advising complex organizational change and multi-country initiatives
• Strong business insight and good judgment, with the ability to influence, negotiate, and build trust with senior leaders and employee representatives. 
• An strong and articulate communicator who can simplify complex labor relations matters and translate them into clear, practical advice for different audiences.
• A natural problem solver who can navigate ambiguity, bring structure to complex situations, and identify practical ways forward.
• Proven experience managing and developing people, with a collaborative and empowering leadership style
• Proficiency in English

This role exists to make sure that doesn't happen, and to get us back on our feet quickly when it does.

As an Application Support Engineer, you'll be the technical owner for the health of the DevX platform in production. You'll provide Level 2 and Level 3 support for the DevX portal, its services and integrations, golden path pipelines and decorators, and the DevOps tooling estate we help run, including GitHub, Azure DevOps and its build agents, SonarQube, Snyk and Cloudsmith. job_description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

What you’ll do

- Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

- Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

- Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

- Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

- Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

- Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

What you'll bring

- Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

- Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

 - Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

 - NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

 - JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

- A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

- Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

- A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

- A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

- Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

- Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

- Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

- Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

- Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

- Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

- Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

- Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

- Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

- Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

##### Hello, we're Inovara

We help companies move from AI curiosity to AI capability. We embed in their leadership teams and leave behind the tools, habits and confidence they need to keep going after we leave. Our ethos is simple. Help, not hype. People before prompts.

##### What we’re looking for

An engineer who gets stuck in. You’ll embed with our clients, build AI agents that do real work inside a real business and get them into production.

This is one of the most important hires we’ll make this year. Every embedded partnership we sign has agents in the scope and client ambition is running well ahead of our capacity to build. We need someone who closes that gap by shipping, not by writing the strategy for someone else to ship.

You’ve done this before, more than once, on more than one stack. You know why an agent that demoed beautifully falls over in week three and you know it’s rarely the model’s fault.

We already have people in the team who are strong on n8n and Zapier. You’ll complement them, not duplicate them. When a workflow hits the limits of those tools, you’re the one who takes it further. When it needs a proper agent instead, you build that.

We’d rather be straight with you about the pace. We’re a small team running multiple live client projects, so you’ll have several builds on the go at once, real deadlines and a fair amount of time with clients and the team. If you want one project at a time and a fully async week, this isn’t the role. If you like a full plate and the judgement to sequence it, it probably is.

##### What you’ll be responsible for

- Build and ship AI agents into live client environments, on whichever harness or runtime fits, from Microsoft Foundry to Claude to open-source harnesses like OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. Live users and live data, which means it matters when something breaks.

- Work a real backlog across several clients at once. On a typical week that might be a list of ten-plus agents and automations for one partnership, rework on agents already running for another and a scoping session for a third. You’ll sequence it, say what’s realistic and tell us early when something has to give.

- Take over where n8n and Zapier run out of road. Custom code, self-hosting, error handling at volume and knowing when a workflow should move off a no-code tool and onto a proper agent runtime.

- Take over agents you didn’t build. Reverse-engineer what a client set up on a no-code platform, work out why it’s slow, expensive or unreliable, and rebuild it on something better where that’s the right call.

- Build on the Microsoft stack when that’s where the client lives. Several of our clients run on Azure and Microsoft 365, so you’ll build in Microsoft Foundry, register and govern agents through Microsoft Agent 365 and get them in front of people inside Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

- Run discovery. Sit with a client’s operations, sales, support or finance teams and work out which processes are worth automating and which agents are worth building. Plenty aren’t. Saying so early is part of the job.

- Work out the infrastructure and access an agent needs before you write anything: credentials, permissions, connectors into the client’s systems, data access, rate limits, service accounts, audit trails and where a human has to stay in the loop.

- Build everything around the agent that makes it dependable. Triggers, queues, error handling, retries, fallbacks and monitoring. An agent that fails quietly at 2am is worse than no agent at all.

- Pick the right harness for the job rather than the one you’re most comfortable with, and explain that choice to an engineer and to a CFO in the same week.

- Be the technical lead for how we build. Own our agent and automation delivery process end to end, from scoping and decision-making through to testing against live work and the feedback loop after launch, so the rest of the team and the hires after you can pick up a build and help rather than wait for you.

- Hand it over twice. Documentation and a working session for the client team so they can run it without us in the room, and the same again internally so nobody here is guessing how it works while you’re on holiday.

- Turn one-off client builds into reusable patterns in the Agents and Workflows areas of our platform, working with the business owner for those areas, so the second time is faster than the first.

- Keep us honest on new tooling. When a new agent builder lands from OpenAI, Anthropic or Microsoft, get hands-on with it and tell us whether it changes what we build for clients.

- Automate Inovara itself. We use AI heavily internally and there’s still plenty we do by hand that we shouldn’t.

##### A bit more about you

- You’re hands-on first. You’d rather show a working build on Friday than present a plan on Monday, and your best work is running in production somewhere right now.

- You’ve built and shipped real agents across several harnesses and runtimes, in production, not in a sandbox. We’re looking for direct experience with most of these, or equivalent experience on parallel platforms:

 - Microsoft: Microsoft Foundry and Foundry Agent Service, Microsoft Agent Framework (the successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel) and Microsoft Agent 365

 - Claude: Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, Skills and MCP servers

 - Open-source operational agents: OpenClaw and Hermes Agent

 - Code-first runtimes: LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and Letta or similar for persistent memory

 - Coding harnesses you use every day: Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot or Cline

- We care that you’ve made a considered choice between harnesses, not that you know one vendor deeply. Tell us which you’d pick for what, and why.

- Deep n8n and Zapier (or Make) experience, well beyond building flows. Code nodes, self-hosting, sub-workflows and error handling at volume, so you can take the team further when they hit a wall.

- You’ve built on the Microsoft stack in a real environment. Azure, Microsoft Foundry (including Foundry Agent Service) and Microsoft Agent 365, plus publishing agents into Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot with Entra ID permissions set up properly. This one isn’t optional.

- You’re comfortable with the unglamorous half of the work. Auth flows, scopes, secrets management, webhooks, logging, cost control and the API with the undocumented limit nobody warned you about.

- Solid engineering foundations. Python or TypeScript, confident with APIs and enough infrastructure knowledge to deploy and maintain what you build.

- You can hold a discovery conversation with someone non-technical and come out with a buildable spec. That means excellent spoken English and the judgement to leave the technical detail at the door when it isn’t helping the person in front of you.

- You can juggle several builds without dropping one, and you’re upfront when the plate’s full rather than quietly missing a deadline.

- You can show us your work. Two or three agents you’ve built, running live, with at least one on a code-first harness or runtime rather than a no-code tool, plus what happened to the business afterwards. Hours saved, error rate, cycle time, revenue touched, whatever the honest number is.

- Pragmatic. A simple thing that runs every day beats a clever thing that needs babysitting.

- Direct Selling experience is a plus, not a requirement. Learning a client’s world quickly matters more, and we’ll train you on the industry.

##### Nice to have

- Copilot Studio, Power Automate or the wider Power Platform

- Evals, observability or agent monitoring used in anger

- Retrieval-Augmented Generation and vector databases

- Enough frontend to put a usable interface on something

- Multi-agent orchestration, including a view on where it stops being worth the complexity

- Voice agents in production

- Security, data protection or compliance experience in a regulated environment

- Agency or consultancy background, working across several client environments at once

##### How this process works

We’re not hiring off a CV and a good conversation. Agent work is one of the easiest things in the world to talk convincingly about without having actually done it, so every stage after the first asks you to show rather than tell.

1. Intro call, 30 minutes

2. Live demo with our core team. Screen share, no slides. Run two or three agents you’ve built, at least one on a code-first harness or runtime, show us the guts of at least one and tell us what it was worth to the business.

3. The build. We’ll hand you a real problem, close to one we’ve hit with an actual client, and you’ll build something that works and walk us through it. Expect at least part of it to involve the Microsoft stack. We want to see the calls you made, the ones you rejected and the parts you’d rebuild given more time.

4. Handover to our core team, run the way you’d hand over to a client

5. Final conversation with Dan and Matt (founders)

We know that’s a fair amount of work and we don’t take it lightly. It’s also the best way for us both to find out whether this is the right fit.

##### What we’re offering

Ownership of the agent build inside a fast-growing AI consultancy, with client exposure from day one and real freedom over how we build.

A permanent, fully remote role with the potential to participate in our share option scheme.

Influence over our platform and our tooling. Build something good here and it goes into every partnership we run.

##### Interested? Get in touch

If this sounds like it was made for you, get in touch and tell us why.

If it doesn’t, but you still like the sound of Inovara, drop us a line anyway. We’re hiring in all sorts of positions across the business.

Alto Software Group powers more than half of all UK housing transactions each year. Estate and letting agents run their whole business on Alto, every day: winning instructions, marketing homes, agreeing sales, moving tenants in and managing properties for years after.
The platform behind that is large and proven, and we're investing in its next generation: moving it, one part at a time, onto a modern architecture while agents keep using it every day. The new platform is built for people and AI agents alike: anything a person can do, an AI agent can do safely on their behalf, with the same permissions, data protection and audit trail as a person. It's one of the hardest and most interesting engineering problems we have, and we want someone who'll love it.
The role in one line
You'll lead how Alto moves onto its next-generation platform: a platform ready for AI agents as much as for people. You'll decide how it should work, build the foundations yourself, and create the blueprint for other teams to follow.
What that looks like day to day
You'll own the target architecture: the key design decisions, the boundaries between the parts of the system, and the standards everything else is built to. You'll spend much of your time in the code, proving those decisions by building the platform and moving real features onto it. Then you'll guide the teams who build on it, reviewing their designs and removing what slows them down.
Nothing here is fully decided. We have an early direction and a working proof of concept, and we want you to challenge both. Once a decision is yours, it's yours end to end: the design, the build, the roll-out to real customers, and the plan for when something goes wrong.
Day to day you'll work across:
.NET and TypeScript: .NET for the core platform capabilities, where the business rules live once, and TypeScript for the workflows and AI agents built on top of them, with React micro-frontends on the front end, all on AWS. 
Core business capabilities come first, in .NET: carved out of the existing monolith rather than rewritten, so there's one source of truth for business logic and nothing drifts. 
The Jobs of Work layer, the end-to-end workflows people and AI agents run, is built in TypeScript on top of them. 
You'll be moving key production data to modern database services while it's in live use, and keeping every agency's data separate and safe the whole time.
AI agents are first-class users of what you build. That means clear, well-described capabilities they can call, permissions they can't step around, actions that are safe to retry, a full record of what an agent did and for whom, and a human sign-off wherever money or legal steps are involved.
We build with AI, not around it. AI coding assistants are standard kit here.
Who you are
You've moved a live system before. Old and new ran side by side for real customers, and you know what took the longest.
You see through technical debt. You understand the debt that comes with a long-lived codebase and business logic hidden deep in the data layer, and you lead how to displace it safely, keeping data correct while it moves.
You've built for AI agents, or want to. You understand what it takes for an agent to act safely in a real business system, and you design for it from the start rather than bolting it on.
You think in boundaries. You can say who should own which data and why, and you turn those rules into code, not wiki pages.
You set the technical strategy. You set a clear technical direction and get teams you don't manage to follow it, through clear written decisions, design reviews and pairing.
You'd rather show than tell. You share a proof of concept with confidence, not a polished plan, because early feedback beats being right alone.
You care about the people on the other end. A clever migration that disrupts an estate agent's day isn't a success.
You communicate clearly, whether it's a design note, a trade-off explained to a product lead, or an update for the business.
What success looks like in a year
The first part of Alto runs on the new platform in production, for real agencies, with a tested way back.
A second team has moved its part mostly on its own, using what you built.
The new platform measurably improves performance and scale.
AI agents are doing real work for agencies through the platform, with the same safeguards as people.
Engineers across Alto know how the platform works and why.

job_title: Associate Solutions Architect, Public Sector Solutions Architecture
job_description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive cloud platform, and
our Worldwide Public Sector team helps mission-driven organisations use the
cloud to scale their impact. Within Public Sector, our Regional Public Sector
team works with local authorities and not for profit organisations, from
councils delivering essential services for residents to charities supporting
vulnerable communities, humanitarian causes and the people who rely on them
every day.

As an Associate Solutions Architect supporting Local Government and Not for
Profit customers, you will work alongside experienced Solutions Architects,
Account Managers, Partners and Professional Services to help customers achieve
their mission outcomes with AWS. You will work directly with customer technical
teams, including IT managers, developers and engineers, to understand their
requirements and design and build solutions that meet them. That work includes
migrating workloads off ageing on-premises infrastructure, modernising resident
and supporter-facing services, transforming contact centres and engagement
channels with Amazon Connect, building generative AI prototypes that help
frontline staff and volunteers work more effectively, and setting up data
platforms that help organisations make better use of the information they
already hold. You will help deliver hands-on customer sessions such as Immersion
Days, workshops and build days, and you will grow your technical depth and
customer skills through mentoring, training and real customer work.

Local Government and Not for Profit customers deliver their missions with high
public expectations, often with tight budgets and small technology teams. They
answer to residents, donors, trustees and the communities they serve, so their
technology investments need to deliver clear outcomes. This role suits someone
early in their career who is curious, keen to learn and motivated by purpose.
You should enjoy getting hands-on with technology, explaining technical ideas
clearly, and seeing how the solutions you help build make a real difference to
people's lives.

Key job responsibilities
Support a portfolio of Local Government and Not for Profit customers as part of
an account team, providing technical guidance across migration, modernisation,
data and analytics, AI/ML and security, working alongside senior Solutions
Architects

Work with Account Managers on technical discovery and solution design, helping
customer opportunities progress from early conversations through to production
launch

Help deliver customer-facing technical sessions such as Immersion Days,
workshops, architecture deep dives and generative AI build days, and build
proofs of concept that show customers what is possible

Design and build solutions to customer requirements, including resident and
supporter-facing digital services, contact centre and engagement platforms built
on Amazon Connect, payment and donation systems, case management and grant
applications, and data platforms that bring together operational and service
data

Share what you learn by contributing to technical content such as blog posts,
sample code, reference architectures and workshops for the public sector and not
for profit community

Collaborate with specialist SAs, AWS service teams and Partners to deliver
solutions, and pass customer feedback and feature requests to AWS product teams

Build your skills through AWS certifications, training and mentoring, and
contribute to the wider SA community by sharing knowledge with peers

A day in the life
No two days look the same, but a typical one blends hands-on technical work with
customer time. You might spend the morning with a council's IT team, working
through how to move an ageing on-premises application to AWS. Later, you join a
charity's build day, helping their developers prototype a generative AI
assistant that answers supporter questions. Between customer sessions, you make
time to build a proof of concept, work towards your next AWS certification, or
pair with a teammate on a tricky technical problem. The balance shifts week to
week, but the thread running through it is the same: you are learning fast,
building things that work, and helping customers see what is possible for the
communities they serve.

About the team
The team you'll join covers mission-driven organisations across Education, Local
Government, Not for Profit and the United Nations. You will focus on Local
Government and Not for Profit, working with councils, charities and community
organisations that deliver essential services to residents and support some of
the most vulnerable people in society. Our customers are mission-driven and
accountable. They protect sensitive personal data about residents, service users
and supporters, run long-established systems alongside new digital services, and
answer to the communities, donors and trustees they serve.

We are a mix of early career and experienced Solutions Architects who build
strong technical relationships with our customers. We work closely with Account
Managers, AWS Professional Services and Partners, and we lean on one another for
peer review, whiteboarding and support on difficult problems. You will work
alongside senior SAs who will help you grow. Because the wider team covers such
a broad range of customers, from universities to UN agencies, you will have
plenty of chances to learn from different missions and technical challenges.

We value ownership, curiosity and a willingness to learn. Our customers bring us
real problems, from migrating core council systems to building generative AI
assistants for charity helplines, and we take pride in going deep to solve them.
We invest in your development through mentoring, training, AWS certifications
and hands-on customer work. We also invest heavily in AI-assisted workflows that
let us spend more time focusing on and collaborating with customers.

The role is based at one of our UK corporate offices and includes on-site time
with customers for engagements such as Immersion Days, workshops and build days.

If you want to start your career alongside people who genuinely care about their
customers' missions, hold themselves to a high technical standard, and treat
every engagement as a chance to make a real difference to communities, this is
the team for you. Basic Qualifications: - Experience in IT development or
implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries
- Experience in design, implementation, or consulting in applications and
infrastructures
- Experience within specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development,
cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data
& analytics). Preferred Qualifications: - Bachelor's degree or above in computer
science, computer engineering, or related field
- Experience migrating or transforming legacy customer solutions to the cloud
- Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools (CloudFormation, Terraform,
CDK).
- Experience of implementing AI solutions including Large Language Models
- Experience or knowledge of implementing Amazon Connect
- Experience with the AWS platform, web services, software development, or
related technologies

Operations is at the heart of everything Amazon does, and automation is one of
the ways we optimise our processes. As an Automation Engineer, you’ll make sure
that our automated systems are working at their best so that our customers get
their orders on time. By exploring data on everything from control systems to
sensors, you’ll maximise the availability of equipment at your sites. This role
puts you at the forefront of Amazon’s emerging technology to solve complex
productivity challenges.

Key job responsibilities
Monitor, troubleshoot and repair issues with key systems
Work with the EU Controls network to monitor Material Handling Equipment (MHE)
metrics
Provide data visualisations of troubleshooting to internal stakeholders
Own or actively participate in continuous improvement projects run by the EU
Controls network
Work with different departments to ensure all systems are correctly documented
and that accurate backup libraries are maintained
Work with global colleagues to install and commission new equipment
Support other sites in the EU Controls network as needed
Interpret mechanical and electrical drawings, and develop improvement strategies
for code conforming to IEC 61131-3

A day in the life
As an Automation Engineer, you’ll be the site expert when it comes to keeping
key automated systems running smoothly. You’ll be working with our automation
machinery, from conveyors to sortation systems, and ensuring they’re working
efficiently. If something has gone wrong or can be done better, you’ll take the
lead in coming up with and implementing a solution.

You’ll also share your expertise with your close colleagues. You’ll be keeping
your Engineering Technicians up to date with device troubleshooting and
preventative maintenance control training, so that your team can keep our
automation systems in order.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment
performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent
team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain,
troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment
centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on
exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general
maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles
most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally
compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum
efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME
team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations
sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late
hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts.
If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity
to develop and introduce completely new processes or advanced tech like Amazon
Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter. Basic Qualifications: - Experience with
PLC controlled automation and issue diagnosis in a continuous process or
production environment
- Experience supporting a wide range of different conveyors and sortation
systems
- Experience dealing with material handling, flow and capacity visualization and
monitoring
- Experience working with computer and web based tools
- Experience using MS Project, MS Office, and MS SharePoint
- Experience with Ladder Logic and structure programming from Siemens,
Allen-Bradley, or Codesys PLCs
- Experience with Ignition SCADA or a similar platform and Human Machine
Interface (HMI)
- Experience with HMI systems, Industrial Networks, VFDs, Servo Controllers,
etc.
- Experience in English-language communication skills, both written and verbal
- EthernetIP, Profinet, Profibus and AS-i or other fieldbus networks Preferred
Qualifications: - Bachelor's degree or above in computer science, electrical
engineering, or related field
- Experience leading change in a multiple site environments
- Experience working with Agile project management methodologies
- Experience with Six Sigma, or analytical and process improvement techniques
- Experience working within ISO 13849 and ISO 62061 frameworks

At eero, we pride ourselves on providing every customer an exceptional
experience. Our mission is to make technology in homes and businesses just work
— through fast, reliable, secure connectivity. Fixing connectivity in the home
is, however, just the start. We're working on the building blocks of small
business solutions and smart homes by designing our own hardware, enabling it
with seamless software, and tying it all together in the cloud.
We are seeking an Enterprise Network Support Specialist to join our growing
Enterprise Support team in London. You'll own complex network cases from first
contact to resolution, working directly with enterprise customers across
corporate, retail, ISP, and managed-service environments. You'll combine deep
networking expertise with customer partnership to solve multi-site deployment
challenges and shape the future of enterprise support at eero.
This role will be working out of our office in London, United Kingdom, providing
an opportunity to work with an amazing team of intelligent, motivated, and
supportive colleagues, and be part of a growing global company that offers a
range of career opportunities.


Key job responsibilities
As an Enterprise Network Support Specialist, you will:
• Own enterprise customer cases end-to-end, managing triage, troubleshooting,
resolution, and documentation whilst serving as the primary point of contact
throughout the customer journey.
• Diagnose and resolve complex multi-site eero deployments, applying advanced
networking knowledge to environments involving VLANs, routing, switching,
802.1X/RADIUS, captive portals, and WAN architecture.
• Configure and troubleshoot network devices, including routers, switches,
firewalls, managed switches, and wireless access points in high-density
enterprise environments.
• Collaborate with specialised teams by escalating to Network Support Engineers
(NSE) and engineering teams when cases require additional expertise, whilst
retaining overall case ownership and accountability.
• Document and share technical solutions from complex cases to build team
runbooks, identify trending issues, and communicate insights to product and
engineering teams.
• Participate in on-call support for enterprise incidents, including multi-site
outages and partner escalations, ensuring timely response and resolution.
• Provide guidance, mentoring, and on-the-job training to help junior team
members continuously learn and improve.


A day in the life
As an Enterprise Network Support Specialist, you'll be the primary point of
contact for enterprise customer cases, taking ownership from initial triage
through final resolution. Your day involves diagnosing complex multi-site eero
deployments, working with overlays and spokes, VLANs, 802.1X/RADIUS, captive
portals, managed switches, and high-density wireless environments. You'll
collaborate with our Network Support Engineers (NSE) and product teams via Slack
when cases require specialised depth, whilst maintaining accountability for
customer outcomes. You'll document each complex case to build our team's
knowledge base, identify trending issues, and inform product improvements.
You'll also participate in a shared on-call rotation to support enterprise
incidents, including multi-site outages and partner escalations. Occasionally,
you may travel within the UK and internationally (less than 15% of the time) to
support on-site enterprise deployments or partner escalations.

About the team
We're building eero's Enterprise Support function from the ground up, and you'll
be instrumental in establishing how we serve our most complex customers. Our
team partners closely with partner success, engineering, and product teams to
ensure customer success whilst feeding critical insights back into product
development. We serve customers across diverse industries, from retail and
corporate environments to ISPs and managed-service providers, each with unique
network architectures and business requirements. We're committed to doing the
engineering work to find the right answer, not just the fast one, and we value
technical depth paired with clear communication. As part of this founding team,
you'll help define our support culture, processes, and standards whilst directly
influencing how eero evolves to meet enterprise needs. Basic Qualifications: -
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, analytics, mathematics,
statistics, IT or equivalent, or experience in network and operating system
support
- Experience in managing and troublshooting network, or experience in technical
support
- CCNA or equivalent level networking certification, or High school or
equivalent diploma
- Experience in Network protocols like DNS/DHCP/TCP, or experience managing full
application stacks from the OS up through custom applications and experience
that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective
communication abilities
- Experience recognizing a challenge and working with a variety of teams and
data sources to diagnose the problem and recommend solutions
- Experience writing and publishing technical documents or equivalent
- Experience communicating clearly and concisely with leadership, stakeholders,
and cross-functional teams
- Advanced networking knowledge including VLANs, routing, switching, 802.1X,
RADIUS, captive portals, multi-site and multi-WAN architecture, and wireless
infrastructure (802.11). Preferred Qualifications: - Speak, write, and read
fluently in French, Spanish, German or Italian
- Experience with programming/scripting (Batch, VB, PowerShell, Java, C#, Chef,
Perl, Ruby and/or PHP), or experience with automation and any version control
tools and experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to
detail, and effective communication abilities
- CCNP or equivalent advanced networking certification.
- Experience with logging and monitoring platforms such as AWS CloudWatch,
Datadog, New Relic, Splunk, or similar tools.
- Knowledge of retail point-of-sale network requirements and PCI compliance
considerations.
- Experience managing or supporting Managed Service Provider relationships.
- Familiarity with multi-dwelling unit (MDU) or bulk deployments and their
associated topology challenges.
- Experience deploying and supporting high-density wireless environments with
100 or more concurrent clients per access point.
- Background supporting a product through early-stage launch or foundational
team phases.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare division’s Mission Command team builds, deploys, integrates, extends, and scales Anduril's software and hardware to deliver mission-critical capabilities to our customers. As the software engineers closest to Anduril customers and end-users, Mission Software Engineers solve technical challenges of operational scenarios while owning the end-to-end delivery of winning capabilities such as Lattice Mesh, Joint All Domain Command & Control, and Anduril's Menace Family-of-Systems.

As a Software Engineer on the Mission Command team, you will build the foundation for a first-of-its-kind platform designed for the tactical edge, solving novel problems across networking, autonomy, systems integration, robotics, and next-generation distributed data layers. Powering resilient, machine-speed decision-making for warfighters and allies—even in contested, disconnected environments—your work will ensure Anduril’s products seamlessly work together and with third parties to deliver customer value. Driven by a “Whatever It Takes” mindset, the Mission Command team balances intentional, long-term system design with the pragmatic tradeoffs needed to meet immediate customer needs. By keeping the mission top-of-mind, you will make sound, scalable engineering decisions to deliver high-quality, expedient software that preemptively addresses the national security challenges of the future.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Own software solutions spanning core mesh platforms, data interfaces, and release management deployed directly to customers to scale critical mission capabilities.

• Deliver well-architected systems using modern software engineering practices—including code and design reviews—while championing scalability, reliability, testability, portability, and maintainability.

• Drive software solutions end-to-end, partnering closely with end-users to translate complex needs into features while balancing user experience with engineering constraints.

• Collaborate across multiple teams to plan, build, and test complex, cross-functional functionality.

• Ensure system health and rapid resolution by creating and analyzing monitoring metrics, triaging production issues, root-causing failures, and coordinating next steps.

• Travel 10% – 30% of the time to meet customers wherever in the world they are, collaborate with teammates across the globe, understand real-world operating conditions, and build, test, and deploy capabilities directly in the field.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret Clearance

• Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Networking, Mathematics, or Physics

• At least 3-10+ years working with a variety of programming languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, etc.

• Experience building software solutions involving significant amounts of data processing and analysis

• Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and established code bases

• A desire to work on critical software that has a real-world impact

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience working with and designing distributed systems

• Proven ability to deliver high-quality results at pace, ideally within a startup or high-growth environment

• Deep networking experience, especially for distributed systems operating in non-standard networking conditions

• Familiarity with industry standard cloud platforms (AWS, Azure) and software infrastructure fundamentals (networking, security, distributed systems)

• A deep, demonstrated understanding of how computers and networks work, from a single desktop to a multi-cluster cloud node

• Professional software development lifecycle experience using tools such as version control, CICD systems, etc.

• Familiarity with industry standard monitoring, logging, and data management tools and best practices

$166,000—$253,000 USD

• Build the UK commercial function from the ground up – hiring, process, negotiating, deal structuring

• Act as player-coach: personally leading on marquee pursuits, and, when scale dictates, mobilise and develop a team to handle the growing pipeline.

• Navigate ambiguity and define your own path – the UK operation is scaling rapidly, and established playbooks may not exist yet.

• Credible engaging at SCS2 level and above with senior military and government stakeholders.

• Strong commercial judgement, able to balance risk, margin, and strategic value in deal decisions.

• Comfort working across a diverse range of disciplines including design, engineering, programme management, legal and contracts, supply chain, and finance.

• Ability to be local to or relocate to London, UK.

• SC cleared and eligible to obtain and maintain DV clearance.

• Familiarity with US defence contracting norms and FMS/DCS frameworks, enabling effective coordination with Anduril's US headquarters.

• Experience building a commercial function in a high-growth or start-up environment.

• Background in or exposure to industrial participation, offset, SSRO, innovative commercial deal structuring and sovereign capability development programmes.

• Advanced troubleshooting skills; able to resolve complex, non-routine issues at the interface of hardware, software, and networking. Linux command line and networking skills alongside familiarity with aircraft maintenance are highly desirable.
