About the role
We’re hiring a small group of founding Account Executives. We’ve already built incredible partnerships with our clients, but so far every sale has been led by the founders. Now we want to turn that success into a process: how we find the next buyer and how a deal moves from first conversation to signed contract. You’ll report directly to Patrick Sharpe, our co-founder and CPO.
You’ll carry a target and close new logos yourself, but this is not a full quota. Every element of the system you build is one future AEs will inherit: from sourcing leads, to qualification, closing, and handover.
If you want to decide how a new category gets sold, this is the role for you.
What you’ll do
• Source and close new logos. Own the full cycle: prospecting, discovery, negotiation and signature.
• Build the sales process. Turn what the founders have learned about our buyers into qualification criteria, pipeline stages and a clean handover from sale to delivery. Sharpen our ideal customer profile as we learn more.
• Write the playbook others follow. Document what works, from discovery questions and objection handling to pilot structure and proposal templates.
• Shape pricing and packaging. Work with the founders on how we price pilots, engagements and platform access, and how deals are structured.
• Shape the product through learnings. Understand what buyers need and feed this back to our product and research teams.
• Own the forecast. Keep a pipeline and forecast accurate enough that the founders can make hiring and investment decisions on it.
• Help build the team. As we hire more Account Executives, help define the profile, interview candidates and onboard them onto the process you built.
What we’re looking for
• 3+ years closing new business. Experience closing six-figure deals.
• Comfortable with ambiguity. We know our buyers, but there is no playbook, no enablement team and no formal sales process yet. You find that energising, not daunting.
• Self-sourcing. You can generate your own pipeline through outbound, your network and events.
• Credible with senior buyers. You can hold your own with a head of insight, a strategy director or a partner at an advisory firm, and you’re adept at navigating complex, multi-stakeholder cycles.
• Curious about the technology. You’ll be selling something new, so you’ll learn simulation well enough to explain what it can and cannot do.
• Ownership mentality. You don’t wait to be told. You see what needs to happen to win the deal, and you make it happen.
Nice to have
• You were one of the first commercial hires at an early-stage startup.
• You’ve sold AI, data, research or analytics products, where buyers weigh trust and accuracy before they buy.
• You’ve sold to insight, strategy, communications or consulting buyers.
• You’ve turned paid pilots into multi-year contracts.
Logistics
• Location: London or New York, in-office five days a week. We build better together, and this role is no exception.
• Compensation in London: £160,000–£200,000 OTE, split evenly between a £80,000–£100,000 base salary and commission at target.
• Compensation in New York: $260,000–$320,000 OTE, split evenly between a $130,000–$160,000 base salary and commission at target.
• Commission is uncapped.
• Plus equity.
Why join now
Simulation is a new market, and you’ll be one of the first people to sell it. You’ll sell to organisations whose decisions shape markets and policy, alongside engineers who can build what a client needs before the end of the call.
The demand is already there, and you’ll build the team that meets it. As that team grows, we intend to promote its leader from our founding Account Executives.

The problem
We simulate societies: how thousands of specific individuals influence each other and form opinions across a multiverse of scenarios.
The combinatorics are as hard as protein folding. Give 1,000 people a for-or-against position on 10 issues, and there are 103,000 possible group opinion states. DeepMind only has to model 10300 ways a protein can fold. Searching that space fast enough to provide answers in hours, not months, is a frontier machine learning problem.
To solve this, we are building a Societal World Model: an AlphaFold for societies. We are already informing strategies for clients with $3T+ in combined market cap. For a few seconds during one client simulation, we were 2% of Google’s global AI throughput.
About the role
We’re looking for a Member of Technical Staff to advance the frontier of our societal foundation models, working across the stack to improve their training, evaluation, and deployment.
You’ll design innovative methods to efficiently train models from real-world observations, reimagine how concepts like auto-regression and diffusion can capture human decision-making, and create the evaluation methodology that tells us how well our simulations match reality. You’ll work directly with our CEO and our growing research team, while partnering closely with product and forward-deployed engineers to move ideas from a research notebook into production.
This role is for someone who wants to do frontier research at the intersection of machine learning and social science and is motivated by applying their work to the world’s most consequential decisions.
What you’ll do
• Train large-scale models. Apply frontier ML methods in supervised learning and natural language processing to develop state-of-the-art simulations of individuals, subgroups, and populations.
• Ground models in data. Develop innovative methods to gather and learn from large-scale behavioural datasets.
• Own evaluation and calibration methodology. Design the evals, benchmarks, and validation studies that measure simulation fidelity against real-world decisions, and make the results interpretable to the team.
• Run experiments end-to-end. Hypothesis, infrastructure, training run, analysis, decision. Build the experimentation infrastructure that lets us iterate fast and trust the numbers.
• Push the frontier. Write, critique, and publish academic content to frame how the world understands and evaluates synthetic research.
What we’re looking for
• 5+ years of experience in an applied research or research engineering role.
• Experience in post-training and evaluating LLMs: RL, dataset and reward design, synthetic data, or related training methods.
• Demonstrated track record of success in deploying trained models in a commercial setting where they generated revenue.
• Research literacy to navigate and push forward the frontier of ML research and its applications in behavioural science.
• Python-strong: our simulation engine is Python-based, and this role lives in Python day-to-day.
Nice to have
• Interdisciplinary experience in behavioural science, computational social science, psychometrics, statistics, complexity science, or a related empirical field.
• AI-pilled: motivated to foster an environment where AI agents make meaningful contributions across the research, product-engineering, and commercial deployment stack.
• Experience scaling an ML research team in an industry setting.
Logistics
• Location: London (Holborn), in-office. We build better together, and this role is no exception.
• Salary: Competitive with lab market rates.
Why join now
If you want to work on something truly frontier, this is it. You’ll be working directly with some of the smartest people on the planet, on one of the hardest problems humanity has yet to solve. In a world on the brink of exponential, recursive change, there has never been a more important time to help society understand itself.

Hi 👋 I’m Colin, Director of Engineering, Europe. How do you feel about software engineers writing product specs, making product decisions, and not breaking down projects into individual tickets? If that sounds exciting (even if a bit scary), read on because I’m looking for an engineering manager to help us build a different type of engineering team and culture at Ashby.
To start, why do we need to be different? Time and again, I have witnessed engineers knowing what needs to be done yet being unable to get things done because of “the process” or because “more data is needed.” Some of the most effective projects have been skunkworks projects, where engineers have taken total ownership of a problem and driven it to completion. I want to normalize that at Ashby.
When we think about how these processes came about, we realize they carry a pessimistic mindset. They box people into smaller roles to minimize the chance of not meeting a certain standard. At Ashby. we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve and embraces the innovative engineers (and frankly, often stays out of their way).
To accomplish this, our engineering leaders need to think deeply about individual performance, process, and culture - not running sprint planning or driving product and technical decisions. You’ll focus on building your team, their skills to thrive with the ownership they’re given, and an environment that empowers them to do their best work consistently, with little distraction. For junior EMs we try to stay within 6 direct reports. This enables them to spend time with our teams observing, correcting, praising, and, yes, coding. We like our managers to be hands-on while also making sure they’re not on the critical path.
We’ve already gathered an experienced, talented, and collaborative team of 25+ engineers. You’ll help me manage the growing team of engineers in Europe.
In addition to working with engineers you’ll also get to work on projects yourselves. Some examples of work our engineering leaders have done:
 • Provide feedback on product and technical specs to help engineers identify where to cut scope or improve quality. You don’t make the final decisions, but you’ll influence and coach ICs to reach the right ones.

 • Grow engineers to the point where they can take large, loosely defined projects, and deliver them with little intervention. They still ask for help when needed - the difference is that they’re driving.

 • Jump into our systems and code to debug a customer issue, ship a small bug fix, or improve our developer experience. Engineering leaders at Ashby are great engineers and enjoy keeping their skills up-to-date (while staying off the critical path).

 • Improve how we generate and simulate data in demo accounts. It’s a project off the critical path, but it helps you keep up-to-date on our codebase while immensely impacting the business, from Engineering to QA to Sales.

 Why be a manager?
I had two experiences early in my career that set me on my path. I had a great manager who asked tonnes of questions about the decisions I was making and coached me without me realizing it. And I had a terrible manager - being told to work harder after a week of 3am finishes was not what I needed as a young engineer. The stark difference between these two experiences motivated me to become a manager: I wanted every engineer I worked with to have the support I had in the best case.
Since then, as I’ve learned more, I’ve realized that I love the kind of problems I get to solve as a manager. Deeply complex problems with long-term impact both on the company and on people’s lives. One of my proudest achievements is creating a fully transparent pay system, and on the day it was revealed, everybody was happy with it. Nobody stormed out. By spending time thinking deeply about everybody’s pay and ensuring the mechanics of promotion were clear, I put the team in a place where they could see a peer was paid more than them, and it not be a problem.
Despite all this, I love being technical. I sometimes indulge myself and spend a morning writing some code to improve tests or provide better abstractions. If I couldn’t be a manager, I’d be super happy to be an IC.
I’m looking for someone who is passionate. Passionate about both management and being technical. Someone who spots a pattern amongst their team, figures out a better way for us to operate, and then builds the automation that powers it. I introduced a new process that enables engineers to merge 30% of PRs without a human review beforehand. I also built the automation that approves these PRs. I also built that automation with abstractions that make it easy for the engineers to improve the automation themselves.
It can be hard to find seasoned engineering leaders who haven’t succumbed to the status quo in some way or another. We're committed to giving all our people a total and utter lack of terrible managers, and that means we're willing to take a chance on someone early in their leadership journey who's courageous, principled, and has the drive to build themselves into a great leader who can say “Yah I know everyone is doing that, but we won't because...”

What We’re Building
As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition (TA) software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.
Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.
As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!
As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply
Engineering leadership comes in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. I thought I’d outline some things I’m looking for to help you decide if this fits what you’re looking for:
 • You love being technical and can hold in-depth conversations with direct reports from infra to backend to frontend.

 • You enjoy management problems. We want people who get excited about driving people to be their best, giving difficult feedback, and building systems that make this easier

 • You hold your team to a high standard and don’t shy away from getting into the details and giving feedback, even to the best folks on your team.

 • You are an excellent and empathetic communicator. Facilitating change at both an individual and organization level requires understanding how to navigate the beliefs, opinions, and past experiences of engineers and figuring out how to both convince them of a new way of doing things while also leaving yourself open to feedback. 

 • You know what exceptional engineers look like. You’ve thought deeply about what makes them tick, how to recruit them, and how to grow folks into them. I want to see depth here, the industry often regurgitates a vanilla description, but the reality is more nuanced.

 • You’re good at thinking about product, business, and maybe even design, but you’re not interested in calling the shots and are more interested in building a team that can make the best decisions without you.

 • You thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments. We're a young startup where leaders wear multiple hats, and you'll build your own (high-speed) on-ramp through developing strong feedback loops.

 Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:
 • You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology.

 • You’ve gotten into management because it was the only growth path available

 • You want to make all the product decisions instead of empowering your team to make those calls.

 • You're happy with a team of engineers that are predominantly early-career, mid-career, or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. With enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

 • A staff or principal engineer to you is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews.

 • You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently than the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent product delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers.

Engineering Culture
Our engineering culture is motivated by Abhik and Benji’s (our co-founders) belief that a small talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:
 • Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 • Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 • Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

 • Putting effort into building a diverse team

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership
The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.
Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”
At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate
Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in here).

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size
We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:
 • Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

 • Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

 • AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.

Put Effort into Diversity
Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.
Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

Work-Life Balance: It’s A Marathon, Not a Sprint
The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.
Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. Interview Process
At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together. Our interview process is six interviews in the following order: 
 • Intro Call (30m) - Discuss your application questions, align on the responsibilities of the role, and answer questions about Ashby.

We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner).

About the Role and How We Work
Our engineering culture strives to recreate the environments where we did our best work as ICs – where we had the ownership and agency to impact our users with creative and innovative software.
I started my career building software for artists in the Visual Effects industry. It was a formative experience for me as a software engineer because success relied on my ability to be a product manager and designer. I talked to artists to understand their needs. I came up with ideas. I did industry research, designed interfaces, and prototyped ideas. I watched artists use what I built and decided what to tackle in the next iteration. No daily stand-ups, no t-shirt sizing, no planning meetings.
I studied computer science to solve problems, not tickets, and this felt exactly like that. I not only felt creative and fulfilled but the agency and ownership we were given as engineers powered an incredible amount of innovation.
Innovation came differently (or not at all) at technology startups beyond the seed stage, often through an engineer’s force of will and ability to push back against culture (rather than any encouragement from it). Engineering was narrowed to implementation and delivery, partly due to the influence of other departments and partly due to the influx of "Agile" processes like sprint planning. In those companies, I felt like a JIRA jockey. 
At Ashby, we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve. An environment that embraces innovative engineers, and, frankly, often stays out of their way. As a Product Engineer, you’ll take ownership over a large portion of one of our products and own projects end-to-end (wearing hats traditionally worn by product and design). You’ll research competitors, write product specs, make wireframes, and more. To ground it with examples, product engineers at Ashby have:
 • Designed and built automated interview scheduling. As we evolve from Oracle to Microsoft Dynamics, we’re reimagining how the business interacts with enterprise technology through modern automation, AI-enabled experiences and agentic workflows. This is a varied, fast-moving role spanning multiple business capabilities, from supplier onboarding and partner enablement through to inventory management, stock inbounding, fulfillment operations and ensuring the right products are available at the right time for our customers. 
Define the vision, strategy and roadmap for large-scale business capabilities and transformation initiatives. 
Drive simplification of complex business processes, identifying opportunities to remove friction, reduce manual effort and improve operational efficiency. 
Partner with Engineering, Architecture, Data, Operations, Commercial, Finance and wider Product teams to translate business outcomes into scalable product solutions. 
Shape how AI, automation and agentic experiences can improve productivity, decision-making and the way colleagues interact with enterprise platforms. 
Build strong relationships with senior stakeholders and influence decision-making across multiple business functions.

Comfortable operating across both strategic and technical domains, adapting your style and level of detail for different audiences.

Strong commercial awareness and an understanding of how business capabilities support growth, profitability, customer outcomes and operational resilience. 
Experience working with different marketplace, partner, fulfilment, wholesale, concession, dropship, third-party seller, or multi-channel selling models. 
Excellent stakeholder management skills, including influencing senior leaders and driving alignment across competing priorities. 
Demonstrated ability to use data and evidence to make decisions and measure business impact. 
Comfortable navigating ambiguity, creating clarity and leading teams through change.

Be an integral part of an agile team that's constantly pushing the envelope to enhance, build, and deliver top-notch technology products. If you are an experienced mobile engineer who enjoys building, solving difficult problems and helping others deliver better software, we have an opportunity for you.

 As a Senior Lead Mobile Software Engineer at JPMorganChase within Asset & Wealth Management's International Private Bank Technology organisation, based in Glasgow, you will design, build and improve the observability foundations of native iOS and Android applications for J.P. Morgan Online International. You will bring advanced technical expertise in mobile engineering and platform observability, own complex engineering solutions and make implementation decisions within the agreed technical direction.

 This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will contribute directly to production code across both mobile platforms, solve difficult design and operational problems related to app health, performance and reliability, and guide other engineers through substantive technical feedback. Working with engineering leadership, business and Product partners, you will translate client and financial workflows into reliable, observable mobile software, use enterprise-authorised coding agents effectively and demonstrate curiosity beyond routine delivery. You will lead through technical contribution and mentoring, rather than departmental resource or people-management ownership.

 Job Responsibilities

 • 

 Designs and develops secure, high-quality production code for native iOS and Android client applications, instrumenting them for crash reporting, performance monitoring, logging and telemetry; reviews, debugs and improves code written by others.

 • 

 Drives design and implementation decisions for mobile observability capabilities — including SLIs/SLOs, alerting thresholds, distributed tracing and real user monitoring (RUM) — balancing data integrity, performance, security, reliability, maintainability and operating cost within the agreed technical direction.

 • 

 Provides technical guidance to engineering and business partners, acting as a subject matter expert in native mobile development and mobile application performance management (APM).

 • 

 Leads the technical delivery of complex observability initiatives through implementation, testing, integration, controlled migration, release readiness and operational support, including triage and root-cause analysis of production incidents using crash and performance telemetry.

 • 

 Applies enterprise-authorised coding agents and automation across design, implementation, testing, review and troubleshooting for iOS and Android codebases, creating reusable context, tools and workflows.

 • 

 Drives effective team adoption of approved AI-assisted engineering practices, validating generated changes through peer review and independent tests for correctness, performance and security, and coaching others on safe use.

 • 

 Works closely with business, Product, Design and backend partners to clarify client needs, interpret financial workflows and translate agreed requirements into practical, observable mobile solutions.

 • 

 Improves engineering standards, instrumentation coverage, automation and resilience for owned mobile applications — establishing dashboards, alerting pipelines and performance baselines — and escalates material risks and cross-domain decisions to the appropriate engineering or control owner.

 • 

 Mentors engineers through code and design reviews, shares reusable observability patterns and knowledge, and contributes to a culture of curiosity, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

 Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

 • 

 Formal training or certification on software engineering concepts and advanced applied experience in native mobile development (Swift/SwiftUI or Objective-C for iOS, and Kotlin/Java with Jetpack libraries for Android).

 • 

 Advanced hands-on practical experience delivering system design, application development, testing and operational stability for scalable, client-facing native mobile applications.

 • 

 Strong practical experience with mobile observability tooling and practices — crash reporting and diagnostics, application performance monitoring, distributed tracing, real user monitoring, structured logging and telemetry pipelines — with the ability to define and operationalise SLIs/SLOs for mobile applications.

 • 

 Ability to solve complex design and functionality problems independently with limited oversight, explain technical trade-offs between observability coverage, performance overhead and battery/data cost, and recognise when wider decisions require alignment or escalation.

 • 

 Practical cloud native experience on AWS or a comparable platform supporting mobile backend services and telemetry ingestion, including automated delivery, testing and production support.

 • 

 Demonstrated effective use of enterprise-authorised coding agents beyond basic code completion, with concrete examples of implementation, review, test acceleration or troubleshooting applied to mobile codebases, and how outputs were verified.

 • 

 Strong understanding of responsible AI use in engineering, including sensitive-data handling, secure development, resiliency, human review and independent validation; ability to guide peers on compliant practices.

 • 

 Expertise in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field.

 • 

 Evidence of curiosity and self-directed learning beyond routine delivery, demonstrated through prototypes, open-source work, technical experiments or reusable mobile observability tooling.

 • 

 Effective technical leadership, mentoring and business communication, with the ability to understand client and financial workflows and work constructively across teams and locations.

 Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

 • 

 Experience in International Private Banking, wealth or asset management, digital banking, trading or other transaction-sensitive client platforms.

 • 

 Experience creating reusable coding-agent workflows, engineering skills, context libraries, test harnesses or evaluation tools that improve mobile observability and quality across a team.

 • 

 Experience with native platform-level performance diagnostics (e.g. Xcode Instruments, Android Profiler) and app-store level stability metrics, vitals and release-health reporting.

 • 

 Backend or full-stack experience — including API design, distributed systems and telemetry-ingestion services — that complements native mobile and observability expertise and reduces integration complexity and operational cost.

Join the Strategy Analytics Team to drive data governance, insights and change across platforms powering global data distribution.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail.
• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a team environment.

• Strong organisational, planning, and project management skills.
• Confidence challenging existing processes and influencing change through data-driven recommendations.

Introduction to role 
Are you ready to make a difference in the world of digital health? As a member of the Digital Strategy Team within Evinova you will partner with both AstraZeneca R&D, Top 10 pharmaceutical companies & biotechs to develop and implement AI and digital health strategies & solutions that accelerate clinical development and enhance patient outcomes. If you have significant experience in Clinical Development and the ability to work with a consulting mindset & problem solve with internal and external stakeholders, this is the opportunity for you!

Accountabilities
Strategic Partnering: Serve as a trusted advisor to both AZ and external organisations across clinical development, clinical operations, and medical. Shape digital strategies, develop operating models, and roadmaps that align with the development portfolio and individual assets.
Project Leadership: Lead project / engagement teams to develop & deliver digital health strategies
Digital Health Strategy & Solutioning: Define problem statements, solution options, vendor landscapes, and selection criteria for digital solutions including patient recruitment, remote data collection and monitoring, ePRO/eCOA, digital biomarkers, and patient engagement platforms.
AI leadership: Maintain a strong pulse on trends in AI tools transforming clinical development, operations and processes, bringing forward pragmatic, value-led innovations that deliver value across portfolios.
Business Case & Value Realization: Build robust business cases (benefits, costs, risks, scenarios) and define measurable value frameworks (cycle-time reduction, data quality, patient retention, site burden, cost avoidance). Track and report realized value post-implementation.
Protocol Development Support: Contribute to study protocol design where digital tools are used (e.g., endpoint rationale, sensor selection, sampling frequency, feasibility, burden, data flows, and risk management). Ensure alignment with therapeutic area strategy and regulatory expectations.
Protocol Feasibility and Execution: Utilize tools to support clinical development and operations teams in optimizing protocols through AI-driven solutions to minimize cost, accelerate timelines, improve patient and site experience, and minimize environmental impact without compromising scientific quality.
Implementation & Evaluation: Lead pilots and scaled implementations of digital health technologies, including feasibility studies, validation frameworks, vendor due diligence, interoperability planning, data governance, and change management. 

Essential Skills/Experience
- Experience: Substantial Clinical Development with a strong focus on application of digital health within healthcare (clinical development and/or clinical operations or biomarker strategy).
- AI in clinical development: Strong AI capabilities including demonstrated understanding of the role AI will play in drug discovery and development.
- Exceptional project management and communication skills, including demonstrated ability to build and maintain trusted relationships.- Therapeutic Area Exposure: Experience with one or more therapeutic area, across Oncology, CVRM, Respiratory/Immunology, Infectious Diseases and/or rare disease, where digital endpoints are emerging.
- Protocol Development: Hands-on involvement contributing to or reviewing clinical protocols and operational plans where digital tools inform endpoints, assessments, or data collection.- Business Case & Value Realization: Capability in financial modeling, benefits quantification, hypothesis-to-value tracking, and post-implementation value realization reporting.- Project Accountability: Demonstrated ownership of projects in clinical development teams, from initiation through delivery.
- Executive presence and leadership: Ability to interact and communicate effectively with senior executive teams, with demonstrated ability to lead and influence experienced professionals in a fast-paced, highly matrixed work environment- Education: Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, engineering, data science, or related field; advanced degree (MS, MPH, PhD, PharmD, MBA) preferred.

Desirable Skills/Experience
- Digital Health Delivery: Proven track record evaluating and implementing digital health solutions (e.g., wearables, sensors, ePRO/eCOA, DHT-enabled endpoints, trial delivery capabilities, patient apps/portals), including regulatory knowledge and technical fluency.
- Therapeutic Area Exposure: Experience with two or more therapeutic area, across Oncology, CVRM, Respiratory/Immunology, Infectious Diseases and/or rare disease, where digital endpoints are emerging.
- Consulting Experience: Experience in pharmaceutical / healthcare consulting, either as part of a dedicated consulting organisation (eg management consulting firm) or an internal pharmaceutical company consulting function.- Technical Landscape Expertise: Familiarity with eCOA, sensor/wearable trial design and delivery vendors; experience running RFPs and technical due diligence.- Validation & Qualification: Experience with analytical/clinical validation of digital measures, human factors engineering, and usability studies.- Product Mindset: Background in product management for digital tools or platforms used in trials or patient support.- Global Programs: Delivery experience across multi-country studies with an understanding of site/patient variability and localization needs.
- Regulatory experience: Understanding of global regulatory landscape and experience in global regulatory interactions and submissions

Why Evinova (AstraZeneca)?
Evinova draws on AstraZeneca’s deep experience developing novel therapeutics, informed by insights from thousands of patients and clinical researchers. Together, we can accelerate the delivery of life-changing medicines, improve the design and delivery of clinical trials for better patient experiences and outcomes, and think more holistically about patient care before, during, and after treatment. 

We know that regulators, healthcare professionals, and care teams at clinical trial sites do not want a fragmented approach. They do not want a future where every pharmaceutical company provides its own, different digital solutions. They want solutions that work across the sector, simplify their workload, and benefit patients broadly. By bringing our solutions to the wider healthcare community, we can help build more unified approaches to how we all develop and deploy digital technologies, better serving our teams, physicians, and ultimately patients. 

Evinova represents a unique opportunity to deliver meaningful outcomes with digital and AI to serve the wider healthcare community and create new standards for the sector. Join us on our journey of building a new kind of health tech business to reset expectations of what a bio-pharmaceutical company can be. This means we’re opening new ways to work, pioneering cutting-edge methods, and bringing unexpected teams together. Interested? Come and join our journey.

So, what’s next?
Are you already imagining yourself joining our team? Good, because we can’t wait to hear from you.

Where can I find out more?
Learn more about Evinova: www.evinova.com
Follow Evinova on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/evinova/

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. What you’ll be doing:

Job Title:                     Assistant Accountant
Location:                     Plymouth, Devon
Compensation:           £28,000 - £35,000 Depending on Experience + Benefits
Role Type:                   Full time / Permanent 
Role ID:                        SF76433
 
At Babcock we’re working to create a safe and secure world, together, and if you join us, you can play your part as an Assistant Accountant at our Devonport Royal Dockyard site.
 
The role
As an Assistant Accountant, you’ll play a key role in supporting financial control, operational reporting and business performance across the Engineering function. Working closely with Finance Managers, Project Managers and Engineering teams, you'll help ensure financial information is accurate, timely and meaningful, contributing directly to workforce planning, cost management and strategic decision-making.
 
Day-to-day, you’ll have an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their accounting career within a large, complex and highly respected organisation. You'll gain exposure to budgeting, forecasting, month-end reporting, labour cost management, invoicing and business analysis, while building relationships with a wide range of stakeholders across the business.
 

Preparing monthly financial reports, journals and balance sheet reconciliations to support accurate financial control.
Monitoring labour, headcount and contractor costs, providing analysis and insight to support workforce planning.
Managing invoicing and intercompany recharge activities while resolving stakeholder queries efficiently.
Producing dashboards, management information and performance reports for senior leaders.
Supporting budgeting, forecasting and continuous improvement activities across financial reporting processes.

 
This role is full time, 35 hours per week and is based on site at Devonport Royal Dockyard.
 
Essential experience of the Assistant Accountant

Experience supporting financial reporting activities including month-end processes, reconciliations, budgeting and forecasting.
Experience analysing financial and operational data to identify trends and support business decision-making.
Experience producing management information, dashboards and reports using advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Experience monitoring costs, resources or workforce data within a finance, project or operational environment.
Strong stakeholder management, communication and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.

 
Qualifications for the Assistant Accountant

AAT qualified or actively studying towards a recognised accounting qualification such as ACCA, CIMA or equivalent.

 
Security Clearance
The successful candidate must be able to achieve and maintain Security Check (SC) security clearance for this role.
 
Many of the positions within our company are subject to national security clearance and Trade Control restrictions. This means that your eligibility for certain roles may be affected by your place of birth, nationality, current or former citizenship, and any residency you hold or have held. Further details are available at United Kingdom Security Vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk).
 
What we offer 

Generous holiday allowance
Matched contribution pension scheme, with life assurance
Access to a Digital GP, annual health check, and nutritional consultations through Aviva DigiCare+
Employee shopping savings portal
Payment of Professional Fees
Reservists in the armed forces receive 10-days special paid leave
Holiday Trading is a benefit that allows UK Babcock employees to buy additional leave or to sell up to one working week of annual leave from their annual entitlement. This Window opens February through to March annually.
‘Be Kind Day’ enables employees to take one working day's paid leave a year (or equivalent hours) to undertake volunteering work with their chosen organisation or registered charity

 
Babcock
We’re Babcock — a global FTSE 100 organisation with over 29,000 people working together to make a difference.
Here, you’ll be part of something bigger. From initial design to final decommissioning, your work will contribute to products and services that are essential to national security and public infrastructure. Together, we’re building a future that lasts — not just through the impact we make, but through meaningful careers that respect your work-life balance.
 
We call that lifetime engineering.
Join us and see how far we can go, together.
 
We are a disability confident committed employer. If you have a disability or need any reasonable adjustments during the application and selection stages, please email careers@babcockinternational.com with the subject header ‘Reasonable adjustments requirement’. We’re committed to building an inclusive culture where everyone’s free to thrive. We are happy to talk about flexible working – please ask about alternative patterns of work at interview.
 
Closing date: 20/11/2026

Job Title:             Portfolio Risk Manager     
Location:             Bristol, Devonport or ClydeCompensation:   £55,800 DOE
Role Type:           Full time / Permanent  Role ID:                SF76898          
 
Do you want to help us in our mission, creating a safe and secure world together, whilst working on projects that are truly unique? 
 
The Royal Navy rely on our engineering, project management and digital teams to keep their submarines at sea and submariners safe. They Protect our Nation and we help to Protect them.
 
At Babcock we have a true culture of opportunity – with business contracts that last decades and structured career development pathways that can take you in all kinds of directions; you will grow, develop, and achieve more than you ever thought possible.  There has never been a better time for you to join Babcock Submarine Support and play your part in protecting the protectors.
 
The Role

Your customers are HR and benefits leaders running benefits for thousands to tens of thousands of people across multiple companies. • Stay ahead of your accounts: know your customers' key moments, from enrolment windows to renewals and payroll runs, and proactively raise risks and get ahead of things before they land

• Be the voice of the customer: take the patterns you see across your accounts to Product and Engineering, back them with the tickets and conversations behind them, and follow them through to what gets built

A few examples of your responsibilities
• Create exceptional visual assets across every touchpoint. From paid and organic social content to product visuals, brand assets, and presentation decks, create work that's effective, visually compelling, and delivered fast. Own the quality of every deliverable from brief to final output.

The generation of African leaders in office today, at this moment of tremendous demographic and
social change, has the potential to transform the continent’s future. These leaders’ priorities

partnerships. Our role is to act as a true partner, collaborating on design, providing resources and
support where they are needed, and sharing honest feedback.

additive and that have the potential to become “big wins”. Our goal is for our partners’ initiatives
to not only succeed on their own, but also to change norms and practices beyond their country’s or
region’s borders.

their transformation action plans and implementation strategies.

assessments through strategic program design, the creation of dashboards and data
systems, technical assistance, resource mobilization and delivery support to address
bottlenecks as they arise.

capacity and systems that leaders need to deliver on their visions.

•  We help our partners navigate the political environment, providing support with
communications, branding, and stakeholder engagement, among other areas.

•  We are committed to being responsive, working quickly to resolve emerging obstacles or
leveraging opportunities for greater impact as we pursue the broader strategic path.

Working at Big Win
At Big Win Philanthropy, we are committed to attracting and retaining exceptional, values driven
people who thrive in a dynamic, high-impact environment. You will join a strategic, agile team
dedicated to helping our government partners achieve “big wins” across the African continent. The
work is deeply ambitious, challenging, and profoundly rewarding. Here, you will gain hands-on
experience alongside inspiring peers both inside and outside the organization.

Associate Legal Officer to join our London office.

and the legal department. Your primary role will be ensuring operational details from our
programmatic initiatives are seamlessly and professionally integrated into our grant and service
agreements. This is an exceptional opportunity for a lawyer who has trained at a law firm or similar
institution and who is looking to transition into the international development and charitable
sector.

strategy, and goals of each program so that legal agreements facilitate the program’s
success. Partner directly with the relevant team to understand and extract the scope,
timelines, requirements and deliverables of initiatives that will be contracted.
Review proposals, workplans, budgets and payment schedules/conditions with the program teams
and clarify as necessary.

consistent, enforceable formats that reflect the shared intentions of the program team and
the partner. Ensure all milestones, deliverables schedules, and terms of reference are
professionally drafted and accurately reflect the intended charitable purpose of the
initiative.

seamless incorporation into the organization’s grant, contractor and vendor agreements.

agreements, requests for proposals, and vendor terms and conditions, including any
changes proposed by grantees or partners.

partner review to final execution, performance and close-out.

employment matters, immigration, and charity and company law compliance.

•  Qualified solicitor admitted to practice in England & Wales with 2+ years’ post-qualification

•  Strong analytical writing with the ability to simplify complex legal terms for non-legal teams.

•  Proven ability to undertake effective legal research.

•  Structured approach to work: excellent attention to detail and drafting ability.

workload, and meet deadlines.

translate them into contracting documents.

collaborate effectively with colleagues across Big Win Philanthropy and external partners.

•  Willingness to understand partners’ contexts and political constraints.

BlackRock is one of the world’s preeminent asset management firms and a premier provider of global investment management, risk management and advisory services to institutional, intermediary and individual investors around the world. About this role

Your team
The Aladdin Identity Engineering team builds and operates the identity platforms that enable secure authentication and access across Aladdin. We combine software and platform engineering to make identity capabilities reliable, scalable and straightforward for applications and clients to consume.
We care about building quality software, automating repetitive work and continuously improving the resilience and operability of our platforms. Identity is a broad engineering domain, so we value curiosity and people who are excited to learn. You do not need to arrive as an expert in every technology we use.

Your role and impact
As an Identity Engineer, you'll apply your software engineering skills to problems across authentication, authorisation and identity. You'll build and improve services that support Single Sign-On (SSO), federation, application integration and identity lifecycle capabilities.
This is an opportunity to develop deeper expertise in identity while continuing to grow as a software engineer. You'll work with technologies and standards including Okta, Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC), alongside application programming interfaces, automation and modern platform engineering practices.
We're particularly interested in engineers who enjoy understanding how systems work, are comfortable learning technologies they haven't used before, and take ownership of improving the software and services around them.

Your responsibilities
In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:
• Engineer, operate and improve identity platforms that provide reliable authentication and authorisation services.
• Build and support Single Sign-On and identity federation capabilities, including services built on Okta and open standards such as SAML, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC.
• Use software engineering and automation to simplify application onboarding, identity lifecycle and operational processes.
• Integrate applications and client identity providers with shared identity services, including supporting credential, secret and certificate lifecycles.
• Improve platform resilience, monitoring and observability, and investigate and resolve issues across authentication flows and identity services.
• Contribute to engineering designs, standards and the continued evolution of our Identity Engineering platforms and practices.

Your experience

Who are we?

Bloomberg onboards vast volumes of external data that ultimately power products such as the Bloomberg Terminal. Our team builds infrastructure that enables engineering teams and data management professionals to ingest, process, and operate those data flows reliably at scale.

DTP (Data Technologies Pipelines) is our Kubernetes-based platform for building and operating event-driven microservices at scale. Engineering teams and data management professionals use DTP to build data ingestion pipelines from small services that process billions of events per day. Built-in features such as traffic mirroring and observability help teams safely test changes in production-like environments and understand how their systems behave as incoming data changes.

We build systems that scale horizontally and are designed for reliability, usability, and operational simplicity. They are primarily written in Python and Go, built on top of Kubernetes, and leverage technologies such as Kafka, S3, Comdb2, and OpenTelemetry.

What’s in it for you?

You will work on a large-scale platform with wide impact across Bloomberg Engineering and Data. The role combines distributed systems, developer experience, production operations, and product-minded platform engineering.

You will have the opportunity to:

- Build features that scale Bloomberg’s data acquisition business.
- Own feature development start-to-finish, from design through rollout.
- Improve the reliability, scalability, and usability of systems processing billions of events per day.

Who are you?

You care about building reliable production systems that are intuitive for users and drive the business forward.

You are autonomous without being isolated: you can take a problem, explore the trade-offs, make a plan, communicate it clearly, and drive the work forward with your team.

You are comfortable with distributed systems, production debugging, and operational trade-offs. You expect failures to happen, and you think about redundancy, recovery, and graceful degradation when designing systems.

We’ll trust you to:

- Design, build, test, and operate infrastructure and platform features for event-driven data pipelines.

- Contribute to operational excellence through testing, monitoring, troubleshooting, incident response, and post-incident learning.

• Incorporate external labor-market data to provide context on talent availability, emerging skills, hiring demand, compensation, and areas where critical talent may be harder to attract or retain.
• Build on historical reporting by testing new metrics and leading indicators that can provide earlier visibility into emerging workforce trends and risks and develop scenario analyses that help leaders understand the potential implications of different workforce and talent choices.
• Leverage AI and emerging analytical tools to accelerate analysis, identify patterns and anomalies, test hypotheses, and explore new ways to make workforce insights more scalable and actionable.
• Prepare analyses, dashboards, decision-support tools, and leadership materials that clearly explain findings, supporting data, and areas that may warrant action or further analysis.

About us
Procentia, part of the Brightwell Group, is an award-winning software and technology company specialising in the Pensions and Pension Risk Transfer/Bulk Purchase Annuities market. Established in 2002, the business is renowned for its web-based pensions administration and management system, IntelliPen.
Procentia’s products and solutions help pension schemes and administrators of all types and sizes manage exceptional volumes of data, meet the demand for self-serve technology, and provide meaningful, consumer-like experiences that users expect from modern online financial platforms while minimising the need for administrator intervention and involvement.
With offices in the UK and North America, Procentia supports some of the largest pension schemes, insurers and retirement plans across the private and public sectors, including BP, British Airways Pension Scheme, BTPS, Chicago Transit Authority, Legal & General Retirement America, Retirement System City of Detroit, Rolls-Royce, Royal London, and Universities Superannuation Scheme.

The job: 

This is a senior, high-visibility role at the centre of the business, combining the focus of a Business Manager with practical operational leadership. The Business Manager will help the CEO and COO turn priorities into action, maintain an effective executive operating rhythm and ensure that key decisions, risks and commitments are followed through.
The role also leads health, safety and facilities management and manages the Executive Assistant team, creating a joined-up and professional service across the executive office and workplace operations.
Here's what you'll be doing:
• Act as the CEO and COO's trusted right-hand partner, managing priorities, preparing briefings, coordinating executive activities, and ensuring key decisions and actions are delivered.

• Lead Board and Executive Committee governance, including planning meetings, producing high-quality papers, tracking decisions, and maintaining effective communication between leadership and the Board.

• Drive strategic projects and business performance, coordinating cross-functional initiatives, monitoring KPIs, supporting budgeting and planning, and managing executive-level risks.

• Oversee Health & Safety, Facilities, and workplace projects, ensuring compliance, effective facilities management, and successful delivery of office-related initiatives.

• Lead and develop the Executive Assistant team, improving processes, service standards, workload management, and executive support operations across the business.

Key skills and experience:
· Proven experience in a Business Manager, Chief of Staff, executive office, strategy or senior operational role supporting C-suite leaders.
· Strong understanding of executive and Board governance, with experience drafting and quality-assuring senior-level papers.
· Demonstrable success leading cross-functional work through influence, coordination and constructive challenge.
· Strong financial and commercial literacy, with confidence interpreting budgets, forecasts, KPIs and performance information.
· Experience managing people and building a high-quality, customer-focused support service.
· Practical knowledge of workplace health, safety and facilities management, including risk management, supplier oversight and compliance monitoring.
· Excellent written and verbal communication, with the judgement and presence to work credibly with executives and Board members.

QA Automation Lead (AI-Driven Testing)
Engineering | Dublin, Ireland (Remote/Hybrid or Remote in EU)

Sim Local is a leading global travel eSIM provider, helping millions of travelers stay connected in over 200 destinations worldwide. Through a combination of local operator partnerships, innovative digital products, and omnichannel distribution, we deliver seamless connectivity experiences for international travelers.

We're looking for a QA Automation Lead to own quality across our products and lead test automation in a small, collaborative engineering team.

Quality is a shared responsibility here: you’ll own every release alongside the developers who build it, from the first conversation to production. You’ll lead with automation and AI, and you’ll also get hands-on, whether that’s testing eSIMs on real devices or setting up a sandbox for a partner.

What You'll Achieve

Every time a traveler lands in a new country and their eSIM just works, that's the quality you helped build. In this role, you'll shape Sim Local ships.

- Make shipping fast and safe. Turn releases into routine, low-risk events, so the team ships more often and knows quickly when something breaks.
- Protect the moments that matter most. Own end-to-end coverage of the journeys our customers and revenue depend on: eSIM purchase and checkout, installation and activation, top-ups, and partner orders through our Partner API.
- Build the foundation everyone runs on. Create the test identities, eSIM profiles and order data that every developer and partner sandbox uses, so partners can integrate with us faster and with confidence.
- Remove the blind spots. Run the full flow across our web store, mobile app, partner stores and the services behind them, on every release.
- Define what “ready to release” means. Give each release clear evidence of what it depends on and what has been tested and set the quality bar with the team.
- Shape how we test with AI. Find the AI tools and practices that work for us, and make them part of how the whole team tests.

Key Responsibilities

1. Test Automation Leadership

- Own and evolve our test automation strategy and frameworks across web, mobile app and APIs
- Write, maintain and run automated UI, API and integration tests in our CI/CD pipelines, steadily reducing manual regression

2. AI-Driven Testing

- Use AI tools to generate test cases, build and maintain self-healing automated tests, and create realistic test data
- Use AI to analyse code changes and risk, so we run the right tests at the right time
- Evaluate new AI testing tools and share what works with the team

3. Shift-Left Quality & Coaching

- Take part in feature discussions from day one, shaping acceptance criteria and risks before code is written
- Coach developers on test scenarios, test design and writing good automated tests
- Review test coverage in pull requests and set clear quality standards with the team

4. Hands-On Testing & Environments

- Test eSIM purchase, installation and activation on real iOS and Android devices across operators and destinations, including during network onboarding
- Set up and maintain sandbox and test environments for partners and clients integrating with our Partner API
- Run exploratory testing on new features, and investigate and reproduce issues reported by customers or partners

5. Documentation

- Write and maintain test plans, test cases, release checklists and QA processes
- Keep partner-facing sandbox and testing documentation up to date

What We're Looking For

Essential

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or other relevant discipline, or equivalent work experience
- 5+ years in QA or software testing, including at least 3 years building and maintaining test automation
- Strong programming skills in TypeScript/JavaScript or Java, and a track record of building test software other engineers keep using
- Extensive experience with modern automation frameworks such as Playwright, WebdriverIO, Cypress or Selenium
- Mobile test automation for iOS and Android (e.g. Appium), or testing hybrid/React Native apps
- Designing test strategies, test plans and test cases, including risk-based regression for frequent releases
- Hands-on use of AI in testing (AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, or AI testing tools) to write, maintain or prioritise tests, with real examples of its impact
- Testing journeys across APIs, services, web or mobile clients and third-party systems (e.g. network operators, payment providers), with sound judgement about what to test at which layer
- Creating reusable test data and environments, and running automated tests in CI/CD pipelines (e.g. GitHub Actions, AWS CodePipeline or similar)
- Investigating failures with logs, monitoring and crash reports, and explaining the risk plainly to engineers and non-engineers
- Solid manual and exploratory testing skills, and a willingness to get hands-on with devices and environments
- Working closely with developers in a cross-functional Agile team using Jira and Confluence, and coaching others on testing
- Clear, well-organised written documentation

Desirable

- Experience with multi-tenant or white-label products, and with onboarding new clients or brands
- Testing payment flows end to end using provider sandboxes
- Background in telecom, eSIM, travel or e-commerce
- Familiarity with AWS
- Performance, load, security or visual regression testing experience

Personal Qualities

- Strong quality focus — takes ownership of every release, from the first conversation through to production
- Proactive — spots gaps and risks early, and feels empowered to fix them
- Maintains and defends high-quality standards with good testing practices and habits
- Collaborative, clear communicator with developers, product and non-technical stakeholders
- Passionate about quality and eager to keep learning, especially new AI tools and smarter ways to test

What We Offer

- Fully remote or hybrid — join the team in our Dublin 16 office whenever you like, or skip the long commute
- Competitive salary, depending on experience

For full-time employees based in Ireland

- 21 days' annual leave, plus an extra day for each complete year worked, up to 25 days per year
- Summer Fridays — half days on Fridays throughout the summer
- Pension scheme
- Referral scheme
- Maternity benefit

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a company that cares about its people, likes to promote talent from within, and is continually growing in new markets. If you don't have all the requirements, but this could be the right role for your career, apply for this position. We are looking for the best cultural fit.

Candidates based outside Ireland will be engaged as independent contractors and will need to invoice Sim Local monthly (e.g. as a sole trader or through their own company).

To apply for this position please forward your CV to: Careers@simlocal.com with the subject "Sim Local - QA Automation Lead".

• Confidence reasoning about API contracts, authentication, transactions, concurrency, queues and idempotency.
• The ability to build and debug frontend features in TypeScript and a framework such as React.
• Evidence that you can explain your own technical decisions, validate assumptions and follow a problem across multiple layers of a system.
• Good judgment when using AI development tools, including reviewing generated code and checking its behaviour.

We are seeking a highly experienced IT - Business Platforms Solutions Expert - Digital Commerce to play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering world-class digital commerce solutions; with a deep expertise in Salesforce Commerce Cloud and/or Oracle Commerce Cloud you will drive the design, implementation, and governance of end-to-end eCommerce platforms that support business growth and innovation.
In this high-impact role, you will work at the intersection of business and technology, translating complex requirements into scalable, secure, and future-ready solutions. You will lead solution architecture and delivery, partner with senior stakeholders as a trusted advisor, and ensure seamless integration with critical enterprise systems. Along the way, you will champion best practices, optimise operational performance, and mentor colleagues to build technical capability across the team.
This is a fantastic opportunity to influence digital strategy, shape enterprise architecture, and deliver cutting-edge eCommerce experiences that make a measurable impact on the business.

Design and implement end-to-end eCommerce solutions using Oracle Commerce Cloud/Salesforce Commerce Cloud:
• Customise OCC storefronts, integrations, and APIs to meet business needs.
• Integrate OCC or Salesforce with third-party systems such as ERP, CRM, payment gateways, and marketing tools.
• Gather/produce business process requirements and convert these into solution requirements across Process, Data, and Technology. 
• Translate solution requirements into solution designs directed by Solution Control. 
• Assess the impact of the IT solution with the Business applications to provide and verify estimates on effort, costs and timelines for project proposals. 
• Translate the IT functional designs to IT solutions by the team. 
• Advice on any solution risks to direct related test plans. Follow and protect the design principles, such as no customizations, design for flexibility. 
• Drive the delivery and implementation of the resulting IT solutions in the business. 
• Act as Functional Solution Guardian – Manage functional template boundaries (data, process, technology) and agree deviations with Solution Control. 
• Advice stakeholders with expertise on best fitting process/IT solutions to guide requirement specifications and minimize package customizations. 
• Be recognised as technical and functional expert in their respective working area by business

Drive Change Management and Adoption to ensure benefits are realised:
• Leading change management/ user adoption of the solution, by providing expertise and good practices including good understanding of specific BU/function e2e business process. 
• Drive BU/ Function stakeholders to put in place key metrics (to be tracked by PMO) to give leadership visibility and insight into the usage and adoption of the platform. 
• End to end oversight to ensure that new features are adopted appropriately. 
• Highlight any early warning signs that could lead to lost value and work on mitigation actions with BU/function

Provide production support:
• With good understanding of domain business process - review and approve all application changes resulting from problem management assessing business risk and impact 
• Participate in incident analysis and problem resolution where expertise is required and / or where the issues are complex or impact multiple processes (3rd line consultancy and 4th line resolution). 
• Participate in trend analysis of all incidents and Root Cause Analysis of Major/Top incidents 
• Drive resulting improvements preventing reoccurrence by either technical refactoring that can be absorbed in project releases or propose changes for budget approval. 

Drive Compliancy controls for the delivery of applications with evidence: 
• Zero deficiency target. 
• Adhere to IT General Control (ITGC) & IT Application Control (ITAC) process / Execution. 
• Assess the materiality of any related Deficiency incident and ensure implementation of mitigation and remediation. Ensure the correct production and collation of evidence. 
• Apply data migration, release management, and SOD/UAM controls. 

Provide consultancy on the ownership of controls and support the testing of these controls to IT Operations as require: 
• Contribute and adhere to solutioning policies, principles and standards.
• Contribute to the Domains and Communities of Practice. Maintain the IT knowledge base of the Domain (baseline documentation). 
• Develop project leadership and management skills within team. 
• Serve as best practice/quality resource within Domain, guide team members in resolving complex issues, train/mentor junior team members.

• Education in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or related technical field. Masters Degree is a plus. 
• Significant experience in working with Oracle Commerce Cloud(OCC) or Salesforce Commerce Cloud (or similar eCommerce platforms).
• Excellent IT delivery skills. 
• Good knowledge and experience in IT Operations and Compliance 
• Working experience in managing business during change management and rollout of projects 
• Adept at creating and transforming business requirements into functional requirements and designs. 
• Exceptional problem solving and sound decision making capabilities, recognised by alternative solutions, and confident, accurate, decision-making coupled with excellent communication and interpersonal skills. 
• Understanding of and experience with best practice methodologies 
• Is recognized as an expert in own area within the organization. 
• Provides specialized depth and/or breadth of expertise. 
• Interprets internal or external business issues and recommends solutions/best practices. 
• Solves complex problems; takes a broad perspective to identify solutions. 
• Works independently, with guidance in only the most complex situations

Canon Core Behaviours
• Drive for results
• Focus on the customer
• Take ownership and accountability
• Act as a team player
• Show courage and conviction
• People orientated
• Care for self and others

Salary: £72,844 per annum, plus 10% bonus (dependent on experience)

This is an opportunity to kickstart your career by joining Canonical. You will be working from our Canonical London Office and will be accountable for delivering technical support to our employees and customers, as well as facilitating AV support for office conferences and events. From problem qualification to full resolution, you will own and manage your cases. When needed, you will transfer your cases to your colleagues or involve senior engineers. If you have an affinity for open source development and a passion for technology, then you will enjoy working with some of the best people in the industry at Canonical.

While our engineers regularly solve deeply interesting, complex technical problems - from triaging cloud environments to root-cause analysis on unseen Linux kernel crashes - this is fundamentally a role rooted in human connection. You will act as a trusted peer and technical guide to external engineering teams, translating intricate open-source challenges into clear, empathetic solutions. We are rapidly expanding and looking for brilliant problem solvers who are just as passionate about building strong, collaborative relationships with customers as they are about the next generation of Canonical solutions.

Location: Office Based in London, England.

The role entails

• 
Empathetic Engagement: Partner directly with customers across remote sessions, ticketing,, and live conversations to deeply understand and resolve their technical roadblocks.

• 
Collaborative Problem Solving: Work hand-in-hand with internal engineering teams and regional peer groups to bridge the gap between complex code fixes and real-world customer satisfaction.

• 
True Ownership: Manage your support cases with a strong sense of personal integrity, ensuring commitments are honored and customer expectations are communicated transparently and predictably.

• 
Ubuntu Lifecycle Guidance: Develop a rich understanding of the Ubuntu development process, empowering you to give customers clear, human context regarding timelines for engineering fixes.

• 
Knowledge Advocacy: Author and maintain accessible knowledge base articles, ensuring lessons learned are shared openly to elevate the entire open-source community.

• 
Operational Reliability: Participate in a regular weekend working rotation to maintain seamless, high-touch continuity of care for our global partners.

What are we looking for in you

• 
Communication Excellence: Exceptional written and spoken English, with a natural ability to convey technical complexity clearly, warmly, and compellingly.

• 
The Soft-Skill Edge: A genuine passion for helping people, paired with the emotional intelligence to navigate high-stakes technical situations with composure and empathy.

• 
Academic Dedication: Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university.

• 
Educational Background: An undergraduate degree in a technical subject or a compelling narrative about your alternative chosen path.

• 
On-Site Technical Leadership: Based in our state-of-the-art London, UK office, you will serve as a key technical support resource for our local teams and employees.

• 
Driven Mindset: A proven track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to deliver meaningful, outstanding results for teams or customers.

• 
Linux & Cloud Familiarity: Practical, hands-on experience supporting Linux systems, with an exposure to three or more of the following:

• 
Virtualization & Cloud: Using KVM or OpenStack.

• 
Containers: primarily Docker, LXD/LXC, or Kubernetes.

• 
Storage Ecosystems: Block, object, and network storage technologies.

• 
System Networking: Navigating bonding, firewalls, bridging, switching, or MTU tuning.

• 
Analytical Curiosity: A strong troubleshooting mindset—the ability to look into stack traces or logs, identify OS/application-level bugs, and strategically guide the customer through next steps.

• 
Development Fundamentals: Basic programming logic in any language to help parse code and collaborate effectively with Canonical Engineering teams.

We assess performance and revisit compensation twice annually to ensure we recognize outstanding colleagues. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission.
