#### About the role

We are looking for a Brand/Media Director to shape how Orpheus shows up in the world. The core of the role is designing and executing our content strategy across social channels, building an audience, and creating the materials that help people understand and trust the product.

You will work closely with the founders and the wider team to turn technical progress into compelling content — from launch videos and product demos to tutorials, blog posts, and community building.

#### Why you may want to join

- Own the voice and public presence of a company working at the frontier of voice and face AI
- Work directly with a small team where brand decisions can quickly shape company trajectory
- Translate genuinely novel technical progress into stories the market will remember
- Build the media engine, not just the campaigns, at an early-stage company

##### What matters

1. Creative taste. Knows what good content looks and feels like. Has a point of view. Can point to work they've made that proves it.
2. Audience-building. Has grown a following or helped grow one. Understands distribution, not just creation.
3. Output. Ships a lot, fast. Doesn't wait for permission or process.
4. Technical fluency. Can learn the product, use it, and show others how to use it well. Credible in technical conversations — doesn't need to be deep, needs to not be wrong.

##### The work

1. Launch videos for new models/languages, features, and partnerships
2. Social media — own the channels, post consistently, build the audience
3. Blogs, best-practice guides, and integration tutorials
4. Product demos and showcases — actually use Orpheus and show what it can do
5. Know the product cold. Know the competitors. Know why we're better and how to show it.

##### Channels

The Cyber   Security Manager is CAUK's hands-on lead of day-to-day cyber security. The role works directly in our security tools, such as Microsoft Defender, to   find and investigate issues rather than waiting for our managed service   provider (MSP) to raise them. It holds the MSP and suppliers to account, and   helps colleagues across the organisation stay safe online. It works closely with the Head of Data and Technology, the Technology Operations Manager, Risk, Compliance and Data to find control gaps, review evidence, track fixes   and turn cyber risks into practical actions. 
Privileged administration and technical execution sit with the MSP and relevant   suppliers. The role has full read access to the technology environment and   may be given elevated access in specific areas where agreed, but does not   hold global administrator rights. The Cyber Security Manager is accountable for internal ownership, challenge, follow-up and evidence of control   effectiveness, using reporting, assurance evidence, risk assessment, supplier   engagement and remediation tracking to validate that cyber risks are understood and addressed. The Technology Operations Manager owns the MSP   relationship and day-to-day technology operations; this role feeds security   challenge and requirements into those service reviews. 
The role   supports cyber resilience across the organisation by overseeing areas such as   the annual Cyber Essentials Plus renewal, vulnerability management, penetration testing follow-up, cyber insurance evidence, email security,   phishing awareness, incident response planning, identity and endpoint   security assurance, and cyber-related supplier actions. 
The role will also support the Head of Data and Technology in moving CAUK towards stronger formal security assurance, such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2, and in improving our NIST maturity score. The role is designed to grow with   CAUK: as our cyber maturity increases, so will its scope and responsibility. 

The role also   acts as a business partner within the IT function, working with Risk, Compliance, Projects, Change, Data and wider business teams to make cyber   security practical, proportionate and enabling. It helps unblock   cyber-related delivery issues, clarify control requirements, coordinate MSP   and supplier action, and ensure cyber security is embedded into operational  technology activity without becoming a blocker to business outcomes. 

We are   looking for a self-starter who lives and breathes cyber security and knows   what good looks like from hands-on experience. They will spot problems for   themselves, keep up to date with current threats and be confident challenging   the MSP and suppliers. They will also be articulate and engaging enough to help colleagues at all levels understand cyber risks and change their behaviour.

Role specific skills 

- Hands-on security experience: Practical experience securing Microsoft 365 and Azure environments, including Entra ID, Intune, Conditional Access and Defender, so they know what good looks like and can tell when it is not being done.
- MSP and supplier challenge: Confidence to challenge MSPs and suppliers firmly and constructively, and to keep pushing until actions are complete. Experience of working with an MSP is desirable.
- Security awareness and training: Experience of, or a strong interest in, running phishing simulations and awareness training, ideally using KnowBe4. Articulate and engaging, able to explain cyber risks in plain language and run sessions that change behaviour.
- Passion for cyber security: A self-starter who keeps up to date with current threats and attack techniques, acts without waiting to be asked, and is keen to keep learning and grow with CAUK.
- Vulnerability and remediation management: Ability to coordinate vulnerability findings, penetration test actions, insurer findings, audit issues and cyber control gaps through to resolution.
- Cyber Essentials Plus and assurance readiness: Practical understanding of Cyber Essentials Plus renewal, evidence gathering, technical verification, remediation tracking and supplier coordination.
- Email and identity security: Understanding of email security, phishing risk, DMARC, SPF, DKIM, MFA, identity lifecycle controls, privileged access risks and supplier-led remediation.
- Endpoint and cloud security: Practical understanding of endpoint compliance, patching, Defender or equivalent tooling, Microsoft 365, Azure and cloud security controls.
- Incident response and cyber resilience: Ability to support incident response planning, escalation routes, lessons learned, cyber recovery actions and coordination with MSPs and internal stakeholders.
- Cyber insurance and external assurance: Experience supporting cyber insurance requirements, security questionnaires, DDQs, insurer portals, rescans, evidence packs and remediation updates.
- Data governance and privacy awareness: Ability to work with Risk, Compliance and Data teams on privacy-related cyber findings, access controls, data protection risks and supplier-supported remediation.
- Qualifications: A relevant certification such as Microsoft SC-200, SC-300 or AZ-500, CompTIA Security+ or equivalent is desirable.
- Business partnering: Ability to work with Risk, Compliance, Projects, Change, Data and business teams to make cyber security practical, proportionate and outcome-focused.
- Evidence and reporting: Ability to maintain clear cyber risk reporting, remediation trackers, control evidence, supplier actions, awareness metrics and management information.
- Continuous improvement: Ability to identify recurring cyber control weaknesses, improve processes and support a more resilient and well-controlled technology environment.

Leadership at Cash Access UK 

- Build effective relationships across technology, Risk, Compliance, Data, business teams and suppliers, creating a constructive environment where cyber risks are raised and resolved early.
- Lead by influence, bringing clarity, pace and practical problem-solving to cyber-related activity across the organisation.
- Champion cyber security as an enabler of safe delivery, helping teams understand and manage risk without creating unnecessary blockers.
- Support colleagues with clear communication, pragmatic guidance and proportionate advice on cyber security requirements.
- Create confidence by following through on cyber actions, escalating when needed and maintaining transparent evidence of progress.

Establish psychological safety so colleagues feel confident to raise risks, near misses, control gaps and security concerns early.

- Provide internal oversight, challenge and assurance of cyber security controls across Microsoft 365, Azure, identity, endpoint, email, supplier-supported services and operational technology processes. This includes the joint security review with Risk of non-standard SaaS and AI tool requests under the AI and ML Policy.
- Be the day-to-day challenger of the MSP and relevant suppliers on cyber security: ask for evidence that controls work, push back on incomplete or poor-quality fixes, chase actions to completion and escalate when they are not done. This covers control effectiveness, incident response, vulnerability management, patching evidence and service follow-through, and includes establishing what is actually monitored across Microsoft Defender and the SOC.
- Monitor Microsoft Defender and our other security tools directly: review alerts, Secure Score, vulnerability findings and device compliance, investigate suspicious activity, and make sure the MSP acts on what is found.
- Own cyber risk and remediation tracking, ensuring findings from vulnerability scans, penetration tests, insurer assessments, the Cyber Essentials Plus renewal, the cyber audit and supplier reviews are logged, prioritised, followed up and evidenced.
- Lead the annual Cyber Essentials Plus renewal, including bringing the separate Azure tenant used for banking hub devices into scope, by coordinating evidence, tracking remediation activity, challenging gaps and ensuring MSP and supplier actions are completed before assessment.
- Support the Head of Data and Technology in developing a longer-term cyber assurance roadmap, including ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 readiness, by identifying control gaps, gathering evidence and helping assess future needs such as SIEM, XDR, logging, monitoring and incident response.

- Run CAUK's cyber security awareness programme using KnowBe4: plan and send phishing simulations, assign training, report results and follow up. Deliver engaging training sessions, including targeted sessions for colleagues who repeatedly fall for simulated phishing, so that risky behaviour improves over time.
- Support data governance and privacy-related cyber controls by working with Risk, Compliance, Data and suppliers on access controls, data protection risks, tracking technologies, privacy findings and remediation activity. #### About the Role

The purpose of the Community Housing Rights Lawyer is to strengthen CELC’s work on housing rights, early intervention and community-led change.

The role will act as a resource for colleagues across CELC and for community and VCSE partners. You will help non-housing specialists recognise housing issues earlier, provide appropriate initial advice and understand when specialist intervention is needed. You will also work with colleagues across different areas of law at CELC to identify intersecting issues and ensure people receive more joined-up, holistic support.

The postholder will build trusted relationships with community groups and partner organisations, helping them to understand housing rights, identify recurring problems and connect people to legal support. By bringing together insight from casework, enquiries, partner knowledge and the experiences of affected communities, you will help CELC identify unmet legal need, spot patterns of systemic injustice and with communities develop practical and legal responses that improve access to rights and contribute to wider change.

#### Key Responsibilities

**Housing rights advice**

- Act as CELC’s internal housing resource for our frontline projects, supporting and supervising non-housing specialist caseworkers to identify housing issues, undertake appropriate initial advice and casework, and recognise when they can progress a matter themselves and when a specialist referral is required.
- Work with colleagues across CELC to identify intersecting legal issues and provide coordinated, holistic support for clients.
- Provide some specialist housing advice, casework and court representation through telephone, face-to-face and community-based appointments.
- Provide specialist housing input to CELC’s community partnerships and projects, including advice sessions, legal health checks and providing accessible legal information where appropriate.
- Maintain high standards of case management, recording and client care in accordance with CELC’s quality requirements, Lexcel and Legal Aid Agency requirements.

**Creating systemic change in partnership with communities**

- Build trusted relationships with community groups and VCSE organisations, spending time in community settings to understand the housing and related rights issues people are experiencing.
- Build partners’ capability to recognise housing rights issues, identify recurring or systemic problems and connect people with appropriate legal support.
- Help analyse evidence from individual cases, organisational data including insight from colleagues and experiences and priorities of affected communities to identify patterns and emerging problems.
- Work with colleagues, communities and partners to develop ideas for using legal expertise and legal interventions to address identified systemic issues and achieve strategic change.
- Represent CELC at relevant housing, community and partnership networks and forums and bring a legal and rights-based perspective to wider conversations about housing, homelessness, poverty and inequality.

#### What We Are Looking For (Please see the recruitment pack for full details)

- Senior Caseworker with 5+ years’ housing casework experience, **or** a Qualified Solicitor with 3+ years’ PQE in housing law.
- Deep understanding of housing and homelessness law.
- Proven ability to supervise others and handle a complex caseload.
- Strong dedication to social justice, client confidentiality, and non-judgemental client care.

#### How to Apply

Please submit:

1. An up-to-date **CV**.
2. A **Covering Letter** (maximum two sides of A4) detailing your suitability and how you would use law and community participation to bring about positive change.
3. A completed **Equality and Diversity Monitoring Form**.

Send your completed applications to: **[recruitment@celc.org.uk](mailto:recruitment@celc.org.uk) by 23rd November 2026**

We warmly welcome applications from diverse and lived-experience backgrounds.

**About the role**

You’ll build and ship production software in a cross-functional team. You don't just take specs; you grasp the why behind a feature and push for a smarter, faster way to deliver it.

Because AI agents write most of our code, your technical bar needs to be high. You can’t spot a subtle bug in code you didn't write unless you know how to build it from scratch, from underlying data structures and algorithms to transaction boundaries, service architecture, and failure points. What ships to production hinges on your review of its security, performance, and correctness.

Expect to rotate through different domains roughly every six months. This gives you enough runway to build real domain expertise while staying close to the business. You’ll tackle high-value engineering challenges like our longitudinal client health platform for early patient frailty detection, or our automated matching engine that connects carers with available shifts. Across every project, our core goal remains the same: automate away manual data entry so care workers can focus 100% on delivering care.

We cut out bureaucratic handoffs entirely: the engineer who understands the problem designs it, checks it, and ships it in small, fast iterations. If a process step feels like slow overhead without adding real safety, speak up.

- **Deep engineering skill** to guide and evaluate AI-generated code.

- **Domain knowledge** in home healthcare or care operations.

- **Clear, direct communication** with any team across the company.

- **True ownership** of the business metrics your code is built to improve.

Think of this as a traditional T-shaped role. Engineering is your core depth, but product intuition, UX design, and communication cross the top. Engineers help shape the product vision and anyone building client-facing software is shaping the user experience with the design judgement that comes with that.

**Responsibilities**

- **Run the complete cycle:** understand business problems, communicate directly with stakeholders, map out a solution, guide the build, verify it end-to-end, and measure real-world impact.

- **Architect before building:** Define data models, API schemas, and the failure handling strategies before handing work off to AI agents.

- **Guide AI development:** Prompt agents, audit their output against intent, security, and performance constraints, and make the final call on what is shipped to production.

- **Maintain quality & testing:** Write automated tests tailored to risk, use feature flags to test safely in production, and take full ownership of system reliability. Quality is your responsibility.

- **Security:** Meet the security competencies expected of every engineer, and complete information security and information governance training before you touch production.

- **Stay close to users:** Work directly alongside branch staff, care teams, and business teams to ensure the software you built solves their actual daily work challenges.

- **Own the outcome, not just the deploy:** Track the metrics your feature was designed to impact. If the numbers don't move post-launch, investigate and fix it.

- **Drive product thinking:** Talk to the people you build for, form a view on what's worth building, and bring proposals to the team before anyone asks for them.

- **Elevate team tooling:** Continually tweak prompts, CI/CD pipelines, and test scaffolding so the entire engineering team benefits.Small improvements compound across everyone who uses them after you.

- **Collaborate actively:** Participate in architecture discussions, code reviews, and technical architecture decisions across the platform.

**Qualifications and skills**

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer with a focus on backend who simplifies, ships, and owns their work. Someone who is equally comfortable navigating new platforms and legacy systems within an organisation such as ours in the care domain.

We are looking for someone with experience in e-commerce, logistics (companies with a strong physical operational component) or SaaS companies.

**Core technical foundations**

- **Data structures & algorithms:** Deep core understanding to review and evaluate code effectively.

- **Databases at scale:** Deep knowledge of database modeling, indexes, query plans, transactions, and multi-tenant isolation patterns, specifically with Postgres at scale.

- **Concurrency & failure patterns:** Mastery of concurrency, race conditions, and distributed systems failure patterns (idempotency, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, outbox, event sourcing, eventual consistency).

- **Architecture & design:** Strong background in API design, integration, common design patterns, and Domain-Driven Design (DDD) to slice complex systems into clear domain boundaries.

- **Infrastructure:** Understanding underlying infrastructure, including connection pools, caching, queues, and container limit behaviors.

We now need a senior reward specialist to strengthen them, fill the gaps and shape them into a framework that grows with the firm. We want reward that reflects how Unity actually works: Partner-led client teams, Functional Leader-led enablement teams, and a culture built on trust, direct feedback and progress over process. We don’t want a generic framework lifted from a larger, more traditional firm.

You’ll take what we have, judge what’s working and what isn’t, and build it out where it needs to go next. You’ll also run it: pay reviews, benefits renewals, and the data and reporting that keep it trusted. You’ll refine it each cycle and make sure the framework is well documented and easy for others to work with.

It suits someone who gets energy from building and improving, and who knows that reward only proves itself once it’s live. You’ll be comfortable with ambiguity and confident making judgement calls. You’ll respect what’s already been done while being willing to challenge it. You’ll also take satisfaction in the steady work of keeping a system accurate, fair and well-run.

This is a role where one expert can own reward end to end, without needing a full-time seat. It will suit an experienced reward specialist who wants a senior, high-impact role with a bounded commitment, including people with a fractional or portfolio background who now want a permanent home.


What you’ll own

 - Reward strategy and philosophy: build on and evolve Unity’s approach to pay. That covers how we position against the market, how pay works across client-facing and enablement tracks, and how reward reinforces Unity’s “progress over process” culture rather than working against it.

 - Pay structure and benchmarking: develop and maintain salary bands and grading across roles and levels, benchmarked against relevant professional services and advisory market data.

 - Pay review cycles: design and run the annual (or biannual) pay and bonus review. That includes timelines, guidance for Partners and Functional Leaders, calibration support, and sign-off with the Management Team / Partners Group.

 - Benefits: own the benefits offering end to end, including provider relationships, renewals, flexible benefits design and clear communication of value to employees.

 - Pay equity and compliance: run regular pay equity analysis (including gender pay gap reporting where applicable), keep Unity compliant with UK reward-related employment law, and flag risk to the CPO early.

 - Reward governance and data: keep reward data accurate and current in our people systems, and produce clear reporting for the Management Team on pay spend, equity and market position.

 - Advisory support: partner directly with Partners and Functional Leaders on individual pay decisions, such as new hire offers, promotions and retention cases. Your recommendations will be clear, defensible and grounded in the framework, not one-off improvisation.

 - The future of reward at Unity: work with the CPO to shape how reward evolves as the firm grows, including the capability, capacity and structure we’ll need over time.


What success looks like in your first 12 months

 - A refined, published pay and grading framework that Partners and Functional Leaders trust and actually use

 - A clean, well-governed annual pay review with no surprises for the Management Team

 - Reward decisions that are consistent, benchmarked and easy to explain, in keeping with Unity’s “trust and accountability” and “no surprises” principles

 - Reward documented and embedded, so that the framework is understood, easy to work with and keeps improving with each cycle


What we’re looking for

 - Senior reward / compensation and benefits experience, ideally including time in professional services, consulting or another partnership-style environment

 - Equally at home developing and extending an existing framework and running it well day to day, from benchmarking data and banding mechanics to benefits contracts and review timelines

 - Confident advising Partners and senior leaders directly, with recommendations grounded in evidence rather than precedent alone

The Cyber security Risk Manager has a global remit and is an integral member of the Cyber security team. The role is responsible for providing clear, evidence-based cyber security risk insight that informs strategy, supports investment decisions and enables projects and business change to adopt appropriate security controls.

The role delivers core Cyber security risk services, including third-party supplier security assessments, cyber risk reviews, maintenance of the cyber risk register, governance support and input to the annual Cyber security Risk Assessment report. The role is expected to plan and prioritise its workload, maintain consistent quality, escalate material issues promptly and ensure agreed actions are followed through to closure.

Success in the role means that decision-makers understand the cyber risks relevant to them, risk decisions are recorded and supported by clear analysis, and security requirements are embedded into projects, procurement and supplier relationships in a proportionate and practical way.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Delivery planning and coordination: Own and maintain delivery plans for assigned risk services, prioritise activities, monitor progress and quality, and identify delivery risks or capacity constraints. Coordinate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders to ensure required outputs are completed to the expected standard and within agreed timescales.
- Third-party and vendor oversight: Oversee third-party security due diligence and the work of external security vendors. Ensure assessments are risk-based, conclusions are supported by evidence, material gaps are clearly recorded, and remediation or risk acceptance is assigned to an accountable owner. Play a key role in procurement by helping stakeholders understand security implications before contractual commitment.
- Cyber risk identification and assessment: Identify, assess and clearly describe cyber risks arising from technology, business change, suppliers and control weaknesses. Evaluate likelihood, impact and existing controls using the agreed risk methodology, and recommend pragmatic treatment options that reflect business context and risk appetite.
- Risk treatment and follow-through: Work with risk and action owners to define proportionate remediation plans, clear milestones and target dates. Monitor progress, challenge overdue or insufficient responses, validate closure evidence where appropriate and escalate material exposure or stalled remediation through the relevant governance route.
- Risk register management: Maintain an accurate and current cyber risk register that provides a reliable view of material exposure, ownership, treatment status and decisions. Apply consistent risk language and quality standards, avoid duplication, and ensure changes in exposure are reflected promptly.
- Stakeholder communication and executive reporting: Translate complex technical matters into concise business risk language for technical and non-technical audiences. Prepare decision-ready materials for senior leaders, Executives and the Board, clearly setting out the issue, potential business impact, current controls, recommended action, accountable owner and decision required.
- Cyber security governance: Perform Cyber security governance activities, including business-as-usual cyber risk assessments, policy and standards development, contract reviews and third-party security due diligence. Ensure outputs are consistent, traceable and aligned to the organisation’s governance requirements.
- Policy and standards: Author and maintain clear, practical Cyber security policies and standards. Engage relevant stakeholders during development, convert requirements into implementable expectations and support teams in understanding how the requirements apply to their services, projects and suppliers.
- Risk culture and awareness: Build understanding of cyber security risk across IT and the wider business. Constructively challenge decisions where risk is not adequately considered, explain the rationale for required controls and promote accountable, risk-informed decision-making rather than compliance as a tick-box exercise.
- Continuous improvement: Use findings from risk assessments, incidents, assurance activity and stakeholder feedback to identify recurring themes and improve risk processes, templates, reporting and service quality. Promote consistency and reduce avoidable delay or rework.

PERSONAL PROFILE

- Operate with sufficient independence to provide objective risk advice, while working collaboratively with technology, procurement, legal, project and business stakeholders.

- Managing production accounts, acting as the main day-to-day point of contact and ensuring timely responses to clients across all communication channels.

- Developing and maintaining good customer and crew relationships.

- Creating and managing customer quotes by utilizing kit lists and schedules to ensure equipment availability.

- Researching and updating customer databases and asset management systems.

- Attending networking events.

Previous Experience

Essential

Experience working within a production office, broadcast or production company.

- Managing multiple productions and deadlines simultaneously.

- Being accountable for client projects.

- Building relationships with Production Managers, Producers, Production Coordinators and Heads of Department or similar position.

- Managing enquiries and converting opportunities into confirmed bookings.

- Handling client issues professionally and finding practical solutions.

- Liaising with other departments to ensure smooth project delivery.

- Knowledge of production workflows in your relevant experience.

- Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain strong relationships and customer rapport.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

- Self-motivated and capable of using initiative working independently under pressure.

- Positive, can-do attitude with a conscientious and dependable work ethic.

- Highly organised with strong time management and prioritisation skills.

- Quick learner with the ability to adapt to new systems and processes efficiently.

Desirable

- Knowledge of production crew structures and departmental requirements.

- Apple OS with ability to learn new programs quickly   

- Previous experience of CMS tools would be beneficial

- Interest in film

The person who will thrive in this role will have strong planning skills and enjoy juggling multiple, ever-changing tasks. ## Brief Role Description

We are seeking an experienced Production Network and Communications Engineer to join our team. In this full-time, primarily field-based role, you will work on-location on major feature film and high-end TV productions, ensuring on-set connectivity and communications run smoothly. You will be responsible for rigging, configuring, and supporting mobile network, internet and comms systems (including Starlink satellite internet, bonded 4G/5G solutions, network, RF & comms infrastructure). If you are passionate about networking technology and excited by the film/TV production environment, this role offers a unique opportunity to apply your skills on some of the biggest productions in the industry.

## Role and Responsibilities

- Deploy On-Set Internet Connectivity: rig and configure mobile internet solutions (Starlink satellite units and bonded 4G/5G cellular routers) to provide dependable high-speed connectivity on set.
- Network Infrastructure Setup: set up and manage on-set network infrastructure including switches, wireless access points, and VLAN configurations, with proper IP addressing and network segmentation.
- RF Systems (training provided): assist with the deployment and support of RF systems including COFDM for wireless video transmission and mesh networking; set up antennas, receivers and associated infrastructure; monitor spectrum usage and troubleshoot interference.
- Comms Systems (training provided): deploy and maintain wireless crew communication systems including Riedel Bolero; ensure base stations, antennas and belt packs are configured and tested; provide technical support and troubleshoot dropouts.
- On-Set Support: act as the point of contact on set for connectivity, streaming and communications support, working closely with DIT, Editorial, VFX, Camera and other departments.
- Troubleshooting: monitor network performance and swiftly resolve connectivity or communication issues to minimise downtime.
- Cross-Team Coordination: liaise with production IT, service providers, or off-site support teams to maintain robust service.
- Equipment Maintenance: prep and test equipment at CineArk HQ before it goes to set, and perform routine maintenance; document configurations.
- Unit Moves: assist with relocating equipment between production locations, which can take place overnight or on weekends.
- CineArk Culture: demonstrate CineArk's values in all daily tasks and interactions.

## Candidate Requirements

### Essential

- Strong Networking Knowledge: deep understanding of networking principles and protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, switching). VLAN configuration and IP addressing skills are absolutely essential.
- Hands-On Experience: proven experience setting up and supporting network infrastructure; comfortable configuring routers, switches and Wi-Fi access points.
- Flexibility & Adaptability: willingness to travel to filming locations and adapt to dynamic production schedules.
- Client-Facing Skills: professional, service-oriented attitude; able to translate tech talk into plain language.
- Problem-Solving Under Pressure: strong analytical and troubleshooting abilities in high-pressure situations.
- Driving Licence: full UK manual driving licence – required.
- Work Ethic: self-motivated and reliable, with excellent organisational skills.
- Discretion: trusted to handle sensitive information in highly sensitive areas of film production.

### Preferred

- Firewall and security experience (VPNs, access control lists).
- RF & communications knowledge; Riedel Bolero or similar a plus.
- Networking certifications (CCNA Wireless, CCNA Security, MCSA, Cisco, CompTIA).
- Exposure to media-over-IP standards (SMPTE ST 2110, AES67, PTPv2).
- Prior experience in film, TV, or broadcast environments.

## Working Conditions

- Field-based at production sites — a mix of outdoor and indoor environments.
- Travel is part of the job; productions film across the UK and occasionally abroad (travel/accommodation arranged or reimbursed).
- Standard hours approx. 8:00am – 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, but flexibility is essential (early starts, late wraps, night and occasional weekend work). Overtime is paid.
- May assist with unit moves (overnight or weekends), scheduled in advance and compensated.
- Office/warehouse prep days at CineArk HQ when not on set.
- Physical demands: lifting and rigging equipment, sometimes at height or in variable weather.
- Holiday – 23 days per year plus UK bank holidays.

## Perks and Benefits

- Employee Assistance Program.
- Additional holiday day after 2 years' service.
- Employee of the Month Award.
- 2 unpaid days annually for volunteering.
- Regular staff socials and celebrations.
- Company Discount Program

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Circle is building its enterprise business across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Your role will be to design and execute a strategy to help our partners implement, launch and grow their stablecoin strategy.

Your portfolio is 10 to 15 strategic partnerships: household-name corporations, and the platforms and institutions that serve them, from the Nordics and DACH to the Gulf and Sub-Saharan Africa.

Own the partnership

• Own each partnership from contract signature as the partner’s primary contact at Circle, accountable for time to value and for the go-live dates you agreed.

Leverage automation and AI-assisted reporting to keep the plan current and visible.
• Carry the partner’s blockers to Product, Legal, Compliance, Risk and Operations, and come back with an answer rather than a status.
Turn launches into adoption
• Own the work that turns an integrated partner into a transacting one.

Grow the relationship
• Expand each partnership step by step into further products, currencies, markets and entities, and structure agreements so that growth does not mean reopening them.
• Create expansion and monetization opportunities, which drive value to live partners and work them to close with Business Development.
• Know what each partner is worth to Circle and how much of their business is still available to us, and feed that back to Product, Marketing and regional leadership in a form they can act on. Apply analytical models and AI-enabled forecasting to surface opportunities and risk.
Build the model the segment runs on
• Define the post-signature lifecycle, its stages and its gates, and make it the way the segment operates rather than a document it refers to.
• Set reliable baselines and reporting for the portfolio, then own the targets built on them. Automate reporting where appropriate and use AI-enabled analytics to maintain accuracy and surface insights.
• Codify what works into a model that scales beyond the partnerships you personally manage.
• Build a mechanism to facilitate data-driven portfolio prioritization, partner-health assessment and recovery plans.

What you’ll bring to Circle

• 12+ years managing enterprise partnerships or strategic accounts across the full lifecycle: implementation, adoption, expansion and renewal.
• A record of turning signed agreements into live, growing usage, with the numbers to show it: time to launch, adoption against plan, growth within the account, additional revenue generated by upsell opportunities.
• Deep experience in complex, matrixed organizations, with credibility in the boardroom and with operational teams.
• Proven ability to lead cross-functional execution across Product, Legal, Compliance, Risk, Marketing and Operations without formal authority over any of them.
• Strong commercial and analytical judgment. You measure what you own, keep one source of truth, and bring a number to every conversation.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, including material built for executive audiences.
• Fluency with AI-enabled productivity and automation tools (e.g., large language model interfaces, workflow automation, knowledge retrieval) to synthesize partner data, accelerate reporting, build playbooks, and improve go-to-market speed. Familiarity with core AI/ML concepts and the ability to evaluate AI-driven features in product and provide practical feedback.

• Background in treasury, payments, financial services, enterprise software or digital assets, with practical fluency of how large organizations move money across borders.
• Experience building early-stage programs or partnerships where the process did not exist yet.

We've recently built a new platform from the ground up, a multi-tenant, multi-region distributed microservices platform that serves as the foundation for all of our products. The platform was purpose-built to remove engineering as the bottleneck in product development: it provides a workflow and agent execution engine, a provider framework, and a tooling layer that allows our product teams to ship new agents, workflows, and products in days or weeks, not months.

Because of this, the core engineering focus isn't building individual product features on repeat. It's building and maintaining the engine itself, extending its capabilities, expanding its toolsets, and ensuring the platform gives product teams and customers the flexibility they need to build on top of it without waiting for engineering cycles.

Role Overview

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to join as one of the first hires on this platform. You'll work across the full backend, from database schema design and API implementation through to workflow orchestration, AI integrations, and infrastructure. This isn't maintenance work. It's building.

The platform has genuine depth: multi-region deployments with data residency compliance, a durable workflow execution engine, autonomous AI agents, and a 3-tier database architecture with physical tenant isolation. You'll encounter hard problems regularly, and you'll have the room to solve them properly.

Critically, this is a high-traffic, low-latency, high-availability platform. We're building toward handling millions of requests per day across multiple regions, and non-functional requirements such as scalability, data storage optimisation, latency, availability, cost optimisation are first-class concerns, not afterthoughts. Every feature you build needs to be designed with these considerations from the start.

We service global financial institutions and are subject to some of the strictest regulatory requirements around data residency, data transfer, and information security. Security isn't bolted on, it's a foundational layer. Data isolation, encryption in transit and at rest, GDPR compliance, and jurisdictional data storage and processing are built into the architecture from the ground up, and you'll be expected to maintain and extend that standard in everything you build.

What You'll Do

- Build and extend the platform engine — new workflow node types, control flow improvements, human-in-the-loop infrastructure, provider capabilities, and tooling that product teams consume
- Design for scale and performance — optimise data storage patterns, manage connection pooling across a large number of tenant databases, reduce latency in high concurrency multi-tier data access and in workflow / agent orchestration, and ensure the platform handles high throughput withoutdegradation
- Build event-driven integrations — services that subscribe to workflow and agent completion events and trigger downstream actions, extending the platform's reactive capabilities
- Integrate AI/LLM capabilities — Multi modal, tool calling / MCP, semantic routing, provider management, agent orchestration including A2A, token and cost tracking, streaming patterns
- Uphold security and compliance standards — tenant data isolation, encryption, access control patterns, credential management, and audit logging in a regulated financial services context
- Work across the data layer — schema evolution across multiple database tiers, migration tooling, tenant provisioning, query optimisation, and caching strategies
- Contribute to infrastructure— Terraform modules, Docker builds, CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, monitoring and observability
- Maintain platform quality — comprehensive testing, strict TypeScript, shared library architecture, structured error handling, performance benchmarking

Who You Are

End-to-end owner — you take problems from understanding through to deployment and monitoring. You don't wait to be told what to do next

- Platform thinker — you understand the difference between building a feature and building a capability. You design with product teams and customers in mind.
- Performance-minded — you instinctively consider how things behave under load. It's part of how you think, not a box you tick before release.
- Security-conscious — you treat security as a responsibility, not a checklist. You care about getting it right because the data matters
- Strong communicator — remote work demands clear writing. You're effective in PRs, documentation, and async conversations
- Pragmatic about quality — you care about code quality as a tool for moving faster, not as an abstract ideal. You write tests because they help, not because someone told you to.
- Collaborative and open — you bring strong ideas to the table and you're happy to debate them, but you're equally comfortable being convinced otherwise

Skills & Experience

Must Have

Strong TypeScript / Node.js — you write strict, type-safe code and are comfortable with generics, decorators, and advanced patterns

- Backend framework experience — Express, NestJS, Fastify or similar structured MVC or modular frameworks with dependency injection, middleware, and guard patterns
- Relational database proficiency — schema design, migrations, indexing, query optimisation, transactions, and connection management at scale
- Containerisation — building, running, and debugging containerised services in local and production environments
- API design — RESTful services with proper authentication, authorisation, pagination, error handling, and rate limiting
- Performance and scalability — you've built systems that handle significant traffic. Caching strategies, connection pooling, query optimisation, and low-latency design are second nature
- Security fundamentals — encryption, secrets management, data access boundaries, audit logging. Experience in regulated industries is a strong plus
- Testing — unit and integration testing, mocking strategies, high coverage targets CI/CD and Git — automated pipelines, branching strategies, PR-based workflows

Strongly Preferred

Distributed systems experience — services communicating across network boundaries, consistency trade-offs, multi-region deployment challenges

- Event-driven patterns — pub/sub, message queues, event subscriptions, async processing
- Durable workflow / orchestration engines — experience with systems that guarantee execution completion across failures and long-running processes
- Cloud infrastructure — deploying and managing services, databases, caching layers, and storage on a major cloud provider
- Infrastructure-as-code — managing infrastructure declaratively with version-control led tooling
- Multi-tenant architecture — database-per-tenant patterns, tenant isolation, data residency compliance
- AI/LLM integration — working with LLM provider APIs, function/tool calling, agent patterns, prompt engineering
- ORM tooling — type-safe database access with migration management
- Monorepo management — build orchestration, affected detection, shared library architecture

Nice to Have

NoSQL databases — single-table design patterns, global replication

- RegTech, FinTech, or compliance domain experience
- Enterprise authentication providers — SSO, OIDC, SAML, directory sync, JWKS validation
- Real-time streaming — server-push patterns for live data delivery
- Workflow graph interpretation — topological sorting, branching logic, loop execution

What We Offer

Shape Our Future, Together: You'll be one of the earliest engineering hires. You'll have a direct hand in shaping not just the product, but how we build software and what kind of engineering team we become.

- Build the Engine, Not the Features: Your work empowers product teams and customers to move fast. You're building capabilities and tooling, not grinding through feature tickets. It's platform engineering with real leverage.
- Technical Depth: Multi-region infrastructure, durable workflow execution, AI agent orchestration, and a data architecture with real complexity. The problems here are interesting and the codebase is well-structured.
- Flexible Hours: We have core hours for alignment, but we trust you to manage your time. Get the work done, pick the schedule that works for you.
- Unlimited PTO: Take what you need to stay sharp and healthy.
- We trust you.Direct Impact: In a small team, your work ships and matters immediately. You'll see the results of your contributions every day.
- A Culture of Trust and Collaboration: Kanban-style workflow with minimal ceremony transitioning to full Agile / Scrum as we scale our team. Open and frequent communication, mutual respect, and a shared commitment to building something that matters.

How to Apply

Attach your CV and a brief note about what caught your interest. If you have a GitHub profile, side project, or writing that shows how you think about software, we'd love to hear about it, but it's not required.

Our process is a conversation about your experience, a practical technical discussion about real problems, and a short take-home exercise that reflects the kind of work you'd actually do here.

Company Description
Who we are
As a global law firm our work spans jurisdictions, cultures, and languages – and so do our people.
Our culture is collaborative and inclusive — where diverse perspectives are recognised and valued. Where performing to your highest ability, unlocks equal access to opportunities to learn, thrive and grow. 
We combine deep legal expertise and commercial intelligence to grow, transform, protect, and defend our clients' businesses, across every critical moment.
We operate in the sectors and regions that matter to our clients. With forward-thinking insights and innovative, tech-enabled solutions that combine deep knowledge of their sectors and markets.
Join us to build connections and work with colleagues as one global team – empowering each other to be exceptional and create advantage for our clients.
Job Description
The role
This is a senior opportunity to join and lead the London Corporate Transactions & Advisory (CT&A) Product Group's existing Knowledge & Training and Thought Leadership team (K&T and TL team), consisting of experienced Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists.
Our London CT&A Product Group advises on some of the world's largest and most complex M&A transactions, including private M&A, joint ventures, restructurings and corporate advisory work.
Our K&T and TL team is focused on delivering practical and insightful knowhow and advice to lawyers, predominantly in London but also across our global network. Key to achieving this goal is the need to keep abreast of legal and regulatory developments and work closely with our lawyers in order to ensure that deal and advisory knowhow and insights are collated, analysed and shared across the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.
In summary, you will be responsible for ensuring that the London CT&A K&T and TL team delivers on ensuring that lawyers have legal and regulatory knowledge and knowhow at their fingertips, whether that is internal knowhow or knowledge on legal and regulatory developments. 
In addition, your particular area of expertise will be company law and corporate governance. You will keep up to date with, and analyse, all legal and regulatory developments in respect of these areas. You will also be the "go to" resource for legal and regulatory developments, template maintenance and production, knowledge sharing, training, thought leadership, client communications and AI and innovation in respect of company law and corporate governance. 
Your role will also play an important part by ensuring our collective experience is captured and utilised for the benefit of all across the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.
You will provide valuable support to the Chair of the CLLS Company Law Committee and any partner on the Company Law Committee of the Law Society, which will involve taking part in working groups, alongside members of these Committees, formed to respond to Government and regulatory body consultations that impact the work of the CT&A Product Group, with a particular focus on company law and corporate governance. 
You will also help drive the adoption of legal technology, including the firm's AI tools, by fee earners. By combining this focus with your legal expertise, you will support the delivery of more efficient, consistent and client-focused legal services.
Who you will work with
You will work in our leading, world-class CT&A Global Product Group, alongside the partners and lawyers.
What makes us one of the most respected Corporate Transactions & Advisory practices globally is our client base, the mandates we win, our industry expertise and commercial approach, and our people and their intellectual capability. We are consistently retained as lead international counsel on cross-border mandates and our team has a diverse client base that includes a number of FTSE350 and Fortune 500 listed corporations. 
You will work within the London CT&A Product Group and also be part of our London and global K&T and TL teams. This means you will work collaboratively with Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in other Product Groups in the London office (including Private Equity, Debt Finance, Employment, Incentives and Real Estate) and in our offices across the globe.
The role more generally and the work supporting the partners involved with the CLLS and Law Society Company Law Committees will provide opportunities to interact with other City law firms, Government departments such as the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) and industry bodies/regulators such as the FCA, the Takeover Panel, Companies House and the FRC.
You will also collaborate with our Corporate Governance Team, Business Development Team, Transformation Team and Legal Technology Advisors. Clifford Chance's Transformation Team and Legal Technology Advisors work collaboratively with fee earners and Knowledge Lawyers to deliver the highest-quality, efficient and cost-effective client service, including by leveraging developments in AI and legal technology. 
What you will be responsible for
Leading London CT&A K&T and TL team
Managing the CT&A Knowledge Lawyer team, with responsibility for appraisal reviews, objective setting, performance management and monitoring progress against strategic priorities.
Leading CT&A K&T and TL business planning, including setting the strategic direction for the CT&A K&T and TL team and overseeing implementation of the business plan.
Leading on ensuring effective collaboration with the Corporate Governance Team on relevant legal and regulatory developments. 
Running the London Corporate Knowhow Committee, including liaising with Knowledge Lawyers and the Corporate Governance Team, preparing and circulating agenda and supporting information, facilitating meetings and ensuring appropriate follow-up. 
Legal/regulatory 
Analysing forthcoming legal/regulatory developments in respect of company law and corporate governance in order to update lawyers and clients on their impact (including supporting the team, led by our Corporate Governance specialists, that prepares a corporate governance update emailed to clients on a weekly basis and preparing other client communications and client presentation materials) and to update internal resources e.g. templates/practice notes/Topic Guides.
Responding to fee earner queries on legal/regulatory matters in respect of company law and corporate governance, including on legal/regulatory developments.
Contributing to legal/regulatory consultation responses relevant to company law and corporate governance.
Supporting Clifford Chance partners on work relating to external legal committees, such as the Company Law Committees of the CLLS and the Law Society.
Preparing and presenting summaries on legal/regulatory developments in respect of company law and corporate governance at London Corporate Knowhow Committee meetings.
Knowledge management and sharing 
Maintaining an up-to-date knowledge database, ensuring content is well curated, structured and optimised for effective use with the firm’s AI tools.
Encouraging fee earners to share and submit knowhow to the firm's knowledge database.
Assisting with the development and maintenance of any relevant bespoke knowhow collections.
Identifying improved ways to capture, organise and share knowhow.
Templates
Maintaining, reviewing and updating existing company law and corporate governance templates to ensure they remain accurate, current and aligned with legal, regulatory and market developments.
Identifying and creating new company law and corporate governance templates as required.
Improving the accessibility and ease of use of company law and corporate governance templates, including through template automation and optimisation for effective use with the firm’s AI tools.
Training
Preparing and/or delivering training on company law and corporate governance, including legal/regulatory developments in these areas.
Delivering knowledge updates on company law and corporate governance to the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.
AI and innovation
Supporting the development, adoption and effective use of legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, across the London office and globally, helping to share best practice and embed new ways of working.
Promoting and assisting fee earners with the use of legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, and helping to identify and develop appropriate use cases to improve matter delivery and lawyer productivity.
Supporting the responsible use of the firm's legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, in line with firm policies, client requirements and confidentiality obligations.
Collaboration
Collaborating with Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in Product Groups that deliver M&A and corporate advisory client work to ensure activities are co-ordinated in respect of legal, regulatory and market practice developments, knowledge management, training, thought leadership and AI/innovation.
Collaborating with other Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in London and globally to ensure knowledge is shared and activities are co-ordinated within Product Groups globally and across other relevant Product Groups within the firm, particularly in respect of company law and corporate governance.
Participating in external Knowledge Lawyer community discussions to share knowledge and information on legal and regulatory topics as well as market practice.
Qualifications
Your experience

What You’ll Get

• Partner collaboratively with peer engineers and cross-divisional squads to ensure alignment between security controls and modern cloud-native architectures.

• Hands-on proficiency deploying, configuring, and securing workloads in public cloud environments, with an emphasis on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or AWS.

• Practical experience embedding automated security gates within CI/CD platforms, particularly Jenkins, Git, and Maven.
• Proven scripting and coding abilities in languages such as Python, Bash, Go, or Groovy to automate complex pipeline actions.
• Working familiarity with containerization and orchestration platforms, including Docker and Kubernetes (GKE/EKS).
• Familiarity with cloud-native monitoring and telemetry suites such as GCP Cloud Operations/Logging, AWS CloudWatch, or Splunk.
• Working knowledge of industry security baselines and regulatory frameworks (e.g., CIS Benchmarks, NIST 800 series, PCI-DSS).
• Clear, collaborative technical communication skills with a mindset geared toward enablement rather than friction.
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related discipline; or equivalent practical experience.
• Relevant cloud or security certifications are advantageous (e.g., GCP Associate Cloud Engineer, GCP Professional Cloud Security Engineer, CKA, or CSSLP).

job_description:
## About Us

Jointly is a creative agency working with the UK construction supply chain. We help building product manufacturers, distributors and tool hire companies look sharp and stand out through branding, web, copy, email and print.

We're looking for a freelance email designer to help deliver email work for our clients on a flexible basis.

## About the role

You'll design email campaigns for our clients, taking them from concept through to polished, responsive, on-brand layouts. Work comes in waves depending on client demand, so we're after someone reliable and flexible rather than tied to fixed hours. Some weeks will be busy and others quiet, and we'll always give you as much notice as we can.

## What you'll do

- Design email campaigns in Figma, from layout and hierarchy through to a clean, build-ready handoff

- Create responsive layouts that hold up across the major clients and devices

- Work within each client's brand guidelines whilst keeping things clear and effective

- Design around the real-world quirks of email, so your work renders properly in Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail and everything in between

- Work with our team on briefs, feedback and revisions

## What we're looking for

- Excellent Figma skills, since this is where you'll do your design work

- A strong grasp of email responsiveness and how layouts behave across different screen sizes

- Real knowledge of email client limitations and how to design around them, particularly Outlook's rendering and the differences between clients like Gmail and Apple Mail

- A sharp eye for clean design that serves the message rather than fighting it

- Clear communication and reliability, which matter all the more with freelance, demand-led work

- Based in the UK time zone, or close enough to overlap comfortably with our working day

## Nice to have

- Email coding capabilities: being able to hand-code your designs into responsive HTML and CSS. It isn't essential, but it's a real plus.

- Experience designing for B2B, trade or industrial brands

## How we work

This is a freelance role that flexes with client demand, so there's no fixed weekly commitment. It's fully remote, and we just ask that you're in or near the UK time zone so collaboration stays easy.

## How to apply

You'll need to be happy to take on a short test task as part of our process, so we can see how you work and you can get a feel for us. It's paid and capped at four hours. From there, we'll talk through how we'd work together. Use the form below to apply today.

The primary function of the Account Manager Continence Care is to deliver sustainable territory growth through effective engagement with clinical and commercial stakeholders across community and acute care settings. The role is responsible for driving product adoption through education, training, formulary implementation, pathway development, and the successful pull-through of approved initiatives.

The Account Manager Continence Care works closely with, and under the strategic direction of the Strategic Partnership Manager across targeted ICBs to support formulary wins, drive product adoption and oversee clinical evaluations, delivering sustainable Convatec product growth.

This is a field-based role with a company car and approximately 90% customer facing. 4 days per week in the field at a minimum with overnight requirements.

Territory: North UK/Scotland

ABOUT THE ROLE:
• Develop and maintain strong relationships with key prescribing and clinical stakeholders across acute and community care settings, including Continence Nurses, Urology Nurses and other specialist healthcare professionals.
• Initiate and support product evaluations within hospital and community settings in partnership with the Clinical Development Manager.
• Drive product uptake and utilisation following formulary approval and inclusion within local guidelines.
• Maximise commercial opportunities by ensuring effective pull-through of approved formularies, pathways, and clinical initiatives.
• Increase access to key Convatec brands through successful formulary inclusion, guideline development, and stakeholder engagement.
• Demonstrate a high level of clinical, product, and market knowledge across key therapy areas.
• Develop and execute robust account plans aligned to Strategic Partnership Managers regional & ICB / HB strategies
• Protect and grow existing business through effective stakeholder management and partnership working.
• Deliver training to ensure the safe, effective and appropriate use of Convatec products.
• Support the Clinical Development Manager in the delivery of audits and the collection of real-world evidence and outcomes data.
• Plan and implement local educational initiatives, service improvement projects, and clinical activities that support business growth and customer objectives.
• Achieve agreed performance metrics and Sales Force Effectiveness (SFE) standards while maintaining full compliance with company policies, the Standards of Business Conduct and Ethics, and all relevant industry regulations.
• Utilise CRM systems effectively, ensuring all customer interactions, opportunities and activities are recorded accurately and in line with company KPIs.

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams to achieve shared business objectives.

• Highly motivated, resilient, and results-oriented, with a strong desire to achieve and exceed objectives.

job_title: Head of IT Delivery Excellence & Automation
job_description:
Position Overview:

Help shape the future of IT delivery at Convatec, a global medical technology company focused on improving outcomes for people living with chronic conditions. In this global leadership role, you will drive delivery excellence, strengthen performance management and accelerate automation across our business application landscape. Bringing together people, processes and technology, you will turn insights into action and apply workflow automation, analytics and AI to improve service quality, reliability and efficiency across SAP and non-SAP applications. You will establish consistent governance, KPIs and dashboards; identify performance trends, risks and improvement opportunities; and support the stabilization and transformation of business-critical application services. Working closely with IT leaders, delivery teams, business partners and strategic vendors, you will translate complex challenges into practical recommendations and measurable improvements. This is an opportunity to shape how we work, influence strategic partners and deliver trusted business solutions that create measurable value across the organization.

Key Responsibilities:
• Cross Functional Service Delivery: Ensure reliable and efficient delivery of cross functional services across IT Delivery Business Applications. Define and continuously improve common processes, governance and delivery standards.
• Performance Management: Establish and maintain consistent KPIs, dashboards and reporting across application operations and the delivery portfolio. Identify performance trends, risks and improvement opportunities and initiate preventive actions and corrections.
• Automation and Continuous Improvement: Identify, prioritize and implement opportunities to automate recurring service requests, technical operations, delivery processes and reporting activities across SAP and non-SAP applications.
• Application Service Stabilization: Support the stabilization and transformation of business-critical application services through appropriate governance, delivery models, partner arrangements and improvement roadmaps.
• Stakeholder Engagement: Maintain effective relationships with IT leadership, Delivery Leads, business partners and other key stakeholders. Ensure transparent communication of performance, progress, risks, decisions and outcomes.
• Partner and Vendor Management: Manage strategic delivery partners and external resources, ensuring alignment with agreed objectives, performance expectations, quality standards and commercial commitments.
• Risk and Quality Management: Proactively identify and manage operational and delivery risks. Ensure that services and deliverables meet agreed quality, compliance and business requirements.
• Technology Enablement: Monitor relevant technology developments and promote the appropriate use of workflow automation, analytics, artificial intelligence and agentic capabilities to improve delivery efficiency and quality.

Skills & Experience:
• Minimum of 5 years of experience in consulting, project delivery or application operations, with a focus on industrialized service delivery.
• IT delivery leadership: Proven experience in global IT service delivery and application operations across SAP and non-SAP environments.
• Consulting experience: A strong consulting background, with the ability to assess complex challenges, develop practical recommendations and translate strategy into measurable results.
• Automation and innovation: Experience identifying and implementing workflow automation, analytics and AI opportunities to improve efficiency and service quality.
• Performance management: Ability to establish meaningful KPIs, dashboards and actionable insights that drive accountability and continuous improvement.
• Operational excellence: A track record of standardising processes, strengthening governance and stabilising business-critical application services.
• Stakeholder and partner management: Strong communication and influencing skills, with experience aligning senior stakeholders, cross-functional teams and strategic delivery partners.
• Change leadership: Ability to build engagement, challenge established ways of working and embed sustainable improvements across a global organisation.
• MedTech and regulated environments: Experience in medical technology, life sciences or another regulated industry is highly desirable, with an understanding of quality and compliance requirements.

Education & Qualifications:
• A bachelor's degree in business, information technology, or a related field. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus.
• ITIL 4, PRINCE2 or SAFe CSP certification is a plus.

Travel Requirements:
• Position may involve travel up to 10% of the time, mostly within Europe, Asia Pacific, and Americas. Most trips will include overnight travel.

Working Conditions:
• Remote working, with flexibility to travel when required by business needs.

job_description:
About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Implementation Manager to lead the global rollout of Convatec’s background screening programme. This role will be responsible for driving the successful implementation of a new global background check process across multiple countries, ensuring consistent execution, stakeholder readiness, and a controlled transition into business-as-usual operations.

Working in partnership with HR, Talent Acquisition, Workday, Employee Relations, Legal, Risk Management, Procurement, country stakeholders, and an external screening provider, you will coordinate all aspects of implementation from process design and requirements gathering through to testing, go-live, stabilisation, and operational handover.

This is a highly visible role requiring strong programme delivery skills, global stakeholder management experience, and hands-on expertise implementing enterprise background screening solutions across complex, multi-country environments.

Success in this role will be measured through on-time country launches, effective risk management, audit-ready documentation, stakeholder adoption, and a seamless transition to operational ownership.

This is a 6 months fixed-term contract.

Key Responsibilities

Implementation & Programme Delivery
• Lead the end-to-end implementation and global rollout of Convatec’s background screening programme across multiple countries and regions.
• Develop and manage implementation plans, governance forums, milestones, dependencies, risks, and delivery timelines.
• Coordinate implementation activities across internal teams, country stakeholders, Workday teams, and the selected screening provider.
• Ensure all countries are operationally ready for launch, with appropriate processes, controls, and support mechanisms in place.

Process Design & Operational Readiness
• Define, document, and maintain end-to-end operating processes, including workflows, roles and responsibilities, decision points, escalation paths, and exception handling.
• Facilitate implementation workshops and requirements sessions with global and local stakeholders.
• Translate business requirements into clearly documented build and configuration requirements for vendor and technology teams.
• Establish readiness criteria and support testing, validation, and deployment activities across participating countries.

Stakeholder Management
• Build strong partnerships across HR, Talent Acquisition, Employee Relations, Legal, Risk Management, Procurement, Workday, and regional leadership teams.
• Partner closely with the CBS Process Owner to ensure operational readiness and sustainable long-term ownership.
• Drive alignment on process decisions, country requirements, policy interpretation, and implementation priorities.
• Provide regular updates on programme status, readiness, risks, issues, and key decisions to project leadership and governance forums.

Vendor & Risk Management
• Act as the primary day-to-day implementation lead for the background screening vendor.
• Monitor vendor deliverables, timelines, testing outcomes, and issue resolution activities.
• Identify and proactively manage implementation risks, process gaps, defects, and country-specific challenges.
• Escalate unresolved issues and critical decisions to programme sponsors and workstream leaders where required.

Go-Live & Transition
• Coordinate go-live activities and post-launch stabilisation support across all participating markets.
• Oversee defect triage, issue resolution, and readiness tracking during deployment.
• Support knowledge transfer, documentation, and transition plans to ensure successful handover into business-as-usual operations.
• Partner with change and communications stakeholders to support training, adoption, and stakeholder readiness activities.

Authority
• Recommend process improvements, implementation approaches, readiness activities, and risk mitigation actions for approval by business owners.
• Coordinate delivery across multiple workstreams and stakeholder groups to achieve programme milestones.
• Escalate implementation risks, unresolved issues, and decision requirements through appropriate governance channels.
• Contribute to programme reporting, leadership updates, and go-live readiness assessments.

Position Overview:

Help shape the future of IT delivery at Convatec, a global medical technology company focused on improving outcomes for people living with chronic conditions. In this global leadership role, you will drive delivery excellence, strengthen performance management and accelerate automation across our business application landscape. Bringing together people, processes and technology, you will turn insights into action and apply workflow automation, analytics and AI to improve service quality, reliability and efficiency across SAP and non-SAP applications. You will establish consistent governance, KPIs and dashboards; identify performance trends, risks and improvement opportunities; and support the stabilization and transformation of business-critical application services. Working closely with IT leaders, delivery teams, business partners and strategic vendors, you will translate complex challenges into practical recommendations and measurable improvements. This is an opportunity to shape how we work, influence strategic partners and deliver trusted business solutions that create measurable value across the organization.

Key Responsibilities:
• Cross Functional Service Delivery: Ensure reliable and efficient delivery of cross functional services across IT Delivery Business Applications. Define and continuously improve common processes, governance and delivery standards.
• Performance Management: Establish and maintain consistent KPIs, dashboards and reporting across application operations and the delivery portfolio. Identify performance trends, risks and improvement opportunities and initiate preventive actions and corrections.
• Automation and Continuous Improvement: Identify, prioritize and implement opportunities to automate recurring service requests, technical operations, delivery processes and reporting activities across SAP and non-SAP applications.
• Application Service Stabilization: Support the stabilization and transformation of business-critical application services through appropriate governance, delivery models, partner arrangements and improvement roadmaps.
• Stakeholder Engagement: Maintain effective relationships with IT leadership, Delivery Leads, business partners and other key stakeholders. Ensure transparent communication of performance, progress, risks, decisions and outcomes.
• Partner and Vendor Management: Manage strategic delivery partners and external resources, ensuring alignment with agreed objectives, performance expectations, quality standards and commercial commitments.
• Risk and Quality Management: Proactively identify and manage operational and delivery risks. Ensure that services and deliverables meet agreed quality, compliance and business requirements.
• Technology Enablement: Monitor relevant technology developments and promote the appropriate use of workflow automation, analytics, artificial intelligence and agentic capabilities to improve delivery efficiency and quality.

Skills & Experience:
• Minimum of 5 years of experience in consulting, project delivery or application operations, with a focus on industrialized service delivery.
• IT delivery leadership: Proven experience in global IT service delivery and application operations across SAP and non-SAP environments.
• Consulting experience: A strong consulting background, with the ability to assess complex challenges, develop practical recommendations and translate strategy into measurable results.
• Automation and innovation: Experience identifying and implementing workflow automation, analytics and AI opportunities to improve efficiency and service quality.
• Performance management: Ability to establish meaningful KPIs, dashboards and actionable insights that drive accountability and continuous improvement.
• Operational excellence: A track record of standardising processes, strengthening governance and stabilising business-critical application services.
• Stakeholder and partner management: Strong communication and influencing skills, with experience aligning senior stakeholders, cross-functional teams and strategic delivery partners.
• Change leadership: Ability to build engagement, challenge established ways of working and embed sustainable improvements across a global organisation.
• MedTech and regulated environments: Experience in medical technology, life sciences or another regulated industry is highly desirable, with an understanding of quality and compliance requirements.

Education & Qualifications:
• A bachelor's degree in business, information technology, or a related field. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus.
• ITIL 4, PRINCE2 or SAFe CSP certification is a plus.

Travel Requirements:
• Position may involve travel up to 10% of the time, mostly within Europe, Asia Pacific, and Americas. Most trips will include overnight travel.

Working Conditions:
• Remote working, with flexibility to travel when required by business needs.

As an Applied AI Product Director at JPMorganChase within J.P. Morgan Personal Investing (JPM PI), you will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for AI-powered solutions across the business spanning large language models, agentic systems, intelligent automation, AI assistants, and rapid prototyping infrastructure. This is not a role that simply manages a backlog. You will define what AI can do for JPM PI, translate emerging capabilities into applied tools that deliver measurable results, and lead cross-functional teams to build and deploy them at scale.

This role requires a leader who delivers measurable results for sophisticated AI products under ambiguous conditions in a fast-paced environment someone who is as comfortable discussing an API spec or an auth flow with an engineering team as they are presenting an AI strategy to senior management.
