Job responsibilities:

 • Develops and articulates a clear Applied AI product strategy and roadmap that delivers meaningful value across JPM PI, covering LLMs, agentic capabilities, AI assistants, intelligent automation, and rapid prototyping, while setting team goals, success metrics, and priorities aligned with broader business objectives.

job_title: Compensation Manager, Digital & Platform Services, Executive Director
job_description:
The Commercial and Investment Bank (CIB) Compensation Team provides compensation analysis, insights, and advisory support to recruiters, HR Business Advisors, business leaders, and managers across JPMorgan Chase’s CIB.
As a Compensation Manager in the CIB Compensation Team, you will lead compensation planning for Digital & Platform Services, encompassing the Operations, Technology, and CDAO businesses within CIB. You will partner closely with senior HR stakeholders and business leaders on compensation pool planning and pay-for-performance decisions. The role also includes co-managing a team of six Compensation Managers and Associates.
You will work closely with functional segment leads to ensure compensation strategies align with the firmwide Technology and Operations agenda. Bringing strong analytical capabilities, sound judgment in handling highly confidential information, and the ability to translate complex data into clear, executive-ready insights for senior stakeholders.
Job Responsibilities
• Partner with senior Compensation and HR leaders on compensation pool decisions, pay-for-performance frameworks, market data reviews, and the regulatory agenda across Digital & Platform Services and the Technology, Data & Product / Operations segment.
• Lead end-to-end compensation planning for a global population, including scenario modeling, outcomes analysis, and executive-ready materials for governance and decision forums.
• Co-manage, develop, and coach a team of six compensation professionals. Set priorities, maintain quality-control standards across analyses and deliverables, and ensure high-quality advisory support.
• Provide guidance and analytical support to global business heads to inform strategic business decisions.
• Collaborate with Compensation leaders and HR partners across lines of business, functions, and regions to understand stakeholder needs and deliver consistent, well-governed compensation recommendations.
• Monitor external compensation trends and competitive intelligence, translating insights into actionable recommendations that support competitiveness and retention.
• Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, including engagement up to Operating Committee –1.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience, with strong analytical and data and information management skills.
• Significant compensation experience, ideally in financial services.
• Experience leading compensation planning for global populations.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong PowerPoint skills, including the ability to produce executive-level communications and materials.
• Experience using AI tools to support day-to-day work, including Copilot across the Microsoft suite; familiarity with using large language models to improve efficiency.
• Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, exceptional attention to detail, and strong quality-control discipline.
• Proven ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment while delivering accurate, timely results.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to explain the story behind the data to senior audiences.
• High integrity and sound judgment when handling sensitive and highly confidential information.

Preferred qualifications, skills, and capabilities
• Prior people-management experience, including coaching and developing high-performing teams.
• Familiarity with compensation governance, regulatory considerations, and market-data methodologies relevant to financial services.

job_title: Global Screening Operations – Transaction Screening Escalations Analyst
job_description:
If you demonstrate strong organizational skills that enable effective work prioritization, ensuring trust and safety of the bank is at the forefront of your priorities, then this role is for you! In collaboration with compliance and escalations teams take an active role and be accountable for delivering the firm’s financial crime objective. Perform an assessment of alerts for potential Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing or Sanctions related activity based on system and manually sourced alerts, consistent with global and local standards. 

As a Transaction Screening Escalations – Analyst in the Global Screening Operations (GSO) team, you will be part of a the EMEA transaction screening team, investigating live transactions which present potential Internal, AML (“Anti Money Laundering”) and Sanctions concerns. You will work in a team environment and will adapt to a rapidly changing business and regulatory environment.

Job responsibilities

 • Conduct a comprehensive review of production transactions across globally booked business, which are escalated to Sanctions Escalations daily as suspect items against OFAC, HMT, EU, or other sanctions programs, utilizing in-house and publicly available information to identify concerns.

 • Review and analyze the underlying data to accurately support decision-making, which may result in escalation in line with Sanctions programs and/or law enforcement/SAR filing.

 • Summarize and fully document all transactions within the Global Sanctions Manager system within expected timeframes, in line with currency cut-offs.

 • Understand upstream and downstream processes and identify client impact when reviewing transactions.

 • Develop and maintain knowledge of the ever-changing Sanctions landscape through knowledge, research, and training.

 • Participate in ad-hoc projects related to technology enhancements, procedural updates, and thematic reviews.

 • Maintain and review current controls for effectiveness, in close partnership with internal functions and in accordance with company policies and regulatory changes.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

 • Ability to deliver strong business results against internal and market cut offs in a fluid and ever-changing sanctions environment. 

 • Advanced analytical and written skills, enabling clear and accurate summarization of your decision making.

 • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build effective relationships with other teams. 

 • Ability to follow procedures, maintain quality standards, understand regulatory requirements while adhering to the appropriate controls. 

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

 • Previous experience of Sanctions, financial crimes compliance or a related position.

 • Proactive and resourceful mindset. 

 • MS Office skills including intermediate Excel skills.

 • Developing experience using AI-powered analytics, workflow automation, or intelligent process tools to drive efficiency gains, reduce manual effort, or improve accuracy in operational processes.

Principal Engineer

About this role

The bar has moved. Five years ago a strong engineer was measured by what they could build and how well they could mentor others to build it. Today, with Claude Code and agents, we produce quality work at a speed that would have looked superhuman in 2022 (Podium, PayPoint, Zuto, RL, OAG Analyser and others).

What separates exceptional from good is no longer typing speed or local craftsmanship. It is the complete package: architecture, deep engineering foundations, communication, system thinking, and the judgement to direct both your own intelligence and AI toward outcomes that matter. 

Exceptional people at this level are not the best implementer in the room; they are the person whose specifications, decisions, and review judgement compound into systems that work in production and that others (and agents) can build on. They are a force multiplier, they hold a room at the highest levels, and clients treat them as the SME by default.

Your mindset

The mindset is the engine, and it is almost impossible to teach retrospectively. You are outcome obsessed, not output obsessed and you care whether the problem was actually solved - you resist the ego instinct to admire a clever solution and ask whether it was needed at all.

You are intellectually honest about uncertainty, taking a trust-but-verify approach and assuming the surprising bug is the one that will burn. You are deeply pragmatic, which matters at CreateFuture where pace counts: you have outgrown the religious wars about platforms, languages and patterns, you hold opinions loosely, and you decide for the systems in front of you, not the ones you wish you had.

You have a bias toward delivery: the smallest thing that works, then iterate, treating documents and meetings as means to that end. 

And you are relentlessly curious beyond any immediate need, wanting to know how the database actually stores things or why a Claude Opus inference call costs what it does, which keeps you several layers ahead while the rest of the team is still reading the API docs.

AI as the accelerant

For a Principal to be truly exceptional, this is now already a first-class competency in your arsenal, not a side skill. An engineer who is brilliant by last year's standards but not fluent with AI is not exceptional in 2026. In practice that means:

• Setting AI up to succeed. You treat context engineering as a craft (the right files, specs, examples and constraints), and you architect systems with clean interfaces, good naming, machine-readable specs and knowledge bases so the codebase is a quality baseline AI can work on later. No separate ivory-tower architect required.
Reviewing and choosing well. You read far more code than you write, and your value is in the quality of review: catching the silent assumption, the security flaw, the architectural drift, knowing where models fail and looking there first. You pick the right tool for the job (Claude Code for a deep refactor, an inline assistant when that is enough, a sub-agent for parallel work, the right model for analysis versus generation) and you know the constraints differ by client, an enterprise like PayPoint or Natwest versus a scale-up type business like Zuto or OAG.
Working with non-determinism. You see where AI moves the bottleneck and help people left and right of you unblock the value stream. You build with AI components but know success is no longer a binary, reaching for evals, golden datasets, structured outputs and fallback paths as naturally as you reach for unit tests.

Technical breadth across the full stack

Exceptional means depth in at least one area but competence everywhere the system reaches.

• Backend: an instinct for distributed systems (what fails, what is eventually consistent, where queues back up), APIs that age well, thoughtful data modelling, and an understanding that languages are mostly syntax differences you can close with AI.
Cloud: cost-aware and security-aware by default, reaching for IaC, composing the primitives rather than stitching together managed services and hoping it works.
Data: modern pipelines, governance and lineage, increasingly vector stores and embeddings, with data quality treated as seriously as production code because garbage in, garbage out is far worse once AI features depend on it.
Web and mobile: past the framework arguments, with a clear view on what you would pick today, and able to build "good enough" front ends yourself with AI.

Full-stack here means seeing the platform as one system and knowing which levers matter most. It does not mean front-end work with a few Node.js servers.

System thinking, consulting and commercial judgement

At CreateFuture we work in a consultancy context, where many otherwise excellent IC engineers can struggle. 

You know technology is roughly 30% of the picture; the rest is design, argument and reasoning, commercial and political acumen, and the clarity to frame outcomes for a COO, CTO, CIO or CEO in their own language.

You know when gold-plating is wasteful, you can name when a project's real problem is not technical and say so even when it is awkward, and you have a strong sense of what is durable versus what is fashion. 

You are not the engineer who introduced the team to seven new technologies last year; you are the one who removed three and quietly made the remaining stack stronger.

Leadership mentality

Technical work is necessary but no longer sufficient. By default you raise the level of everyone around you, regardless of discipline.

• Communicate clearly and frequently (documents, decisions, post-mortems, design notes); the written artefact is the machine-readable context we can feed to AI later.

• Make decisions and own them. You don't escalate everything or hoard control, and you are willing to be the benevolent dictator when it is your turn.

• Mentor in AI fluency, not just code: tooling, prompting and review discipline, so your team is twice as productive a year from now.

• Need little line management. You communicate upwards, raise by exception, self-resolve, and can be trusted with financial controls.

• Disagree well. You tell people they are wrong with evidence and no ego, and you change your own mind when you are shown to be wrong.

What we're not looking for

• The gifted engineer who sits in a silo. This is a team game.

• The one who is fluent with AI but ships without the guardrails and quality gates enterprise clients expect.

• The one with strong technical opinions who cannot justify them commercially and gets defensive when challenged.

• The pure manager who wants to orchestrate teams rather than get involved. This is about setting a new standard, not coordinating it.

• The engineer who will not immerse in a client environment. This role will mean on-site work and trusted relationships built in person. We are not going back to working away from the client and being bypassed.

The Role
Every clinical trial depends on a commitment to the people who take part: their rights, safety and wellbeing come first, and the data they help generate can be trusted. Once a product reaches patients, that commitment continues through the monitoring of its safety and benefit-risk. This role holds the organisation to both. As Head of Patient-Facing Quality Assurance, you will lead an integrated QA organisation covering Good Clinical Practice and Good Pharmacovigilance Practice, reporting to the Head of Global R&D Quality. Your team will include PV System and Process Leads, Therapeutic Area Quality Leads, and a Head of Clinical QA or of PV and Regulatory QA, depending on which complements your own background.

Hybrid (3 days a week on site), based in Maidenhead, UK, or King of Prussia, PA, with other global locations open to discussion

Why it matters
Bringing clinical and pharmacovigilance quality under one leader is a deliberate choice. Some of the most consequential risks sit at the interfaces between them: serious adverse event reconciliation, expedited reporting, and the safety information that reaches investigators and regulators. A single function can see these clearly and act on them. The role is also a chance to shape how quality is done, not just police it. With ICH E6(R3) moving the industry toward Quality by Design and risk-based quality management, you will set the strategy, operating model and standards for how the company protects participants and patients. You will keep the specialist depth that GCP and GVP each need while making the approach consistent worldwide.

What You’ll Be Responsible For
You will provide independent, risk-based QA oversight from trial design through close-out, and across the global pharmacovigilance system. You will be the consistent quality voice in governance and a constructive challenger to the functions that own operational delivery.
Setting the strategy, operating model, governance, capabilities and global resource model for Clinical QA and PV QA, harmonising approaches without diluting specialist expertise
Embedding Quality by Design, critical-to-quality factors and risk-based quality management, and making sure risks to participant safety, patient safety and data integrity are escalated in time
Assuring the quality systems behind clinical development and pharmacovigilance, including their integration with the enterprise QMS and accurate representation in the Pharmacovigilance System Master File
Overseeing the clinical safety interfaces: SAE collection and reconciliation, SUSAR and expedited reporting, investigator safety reporting, safety data exchange agreements and signal escalation
Running a globally consistent framework for significant quality issues, serious breaches, critical deviations and CAPAs, backed by rigorous root-cause analysis and reportability assessment
Leading GCP and GVP inspection readiness and health-authority inspections, owning the patient-facing audit plan, and giving senior leadership an integrated view of quality risk, trends and regulatory intelligence

Experience Required
At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in pharma, biotech or regulated life sciences, with a degree in life sciences, pharmacy, medicine, nursing or a related discipline (an advanced degree or professional certification in Quality, GCP, GVP or auditing is an advantage)
Significant QA leadership in clinical quality, PV quality or both, including leading global teams in a complex matrix; experience across both GCP and GVP is strongly preferred
Expert knowledge of GCP and GVP regulation and inspection expectations, including ICH E6(R3) and the EU GVP framework
A track record with health-authority inspections, serious breaches, investigations, CAPAs and inspection remediation
Hands-on experience of Quality by Design, risk-based quality management, quality metrics, data integrity and computerised systems, as well as oversight of CROs, vendors, affiliates and partners
Experience managing budgets, consultants, workforce plans and talent, and building a team of trusted strategic advisers

Note on travel
This is a global role. Expect some out-of-hours meetings across time zones and periodic international travel.

CuspAI is the frontier AI company on a mission to solve the breakthrough materials needed to power human progress. While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering.

We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock.

We invite you to be part of a diverse, innovative team at the intersection of AI and materials science, working to create impactful partnerships that drive innovation, scalability, and industry collaboration. This work matters. Your work matters.

We’re on the cusp of the on-demand materials era. Join us.

The Role
We are seeking a Scientific Software Engineer to build and run the systems that connect our AI platform to physical laboratories around the world. Together with the team, you will shape the software layer of our closed-loop discovery workflow: our agents propose experiments, partner labs execute them, and the results feed back into our models to guide the next set of experiments.
This role sits between lab automation and production engineering. You will bring hands-on experience with scientific or lab automation, and the engineering discipline to make those integrations secure, reliable and scalable across many partners.
You will be part of a small team of materials scientists, ML engineers and software engineers, working closely with each other and with our partner labs. You will help define how our AI platform connects to the physical world and shape the tools and practices that link external partner labs to our platform. You will thrive here if you enjoy collaborating across disciplines and learning from people whose expertise differs from your own.

• Help shape how we connect to partner labs around the world, accounting for different levels of automation and AI-readiness, then design, build and operate the services that send experiment requests from our AI agents and reliably bring results back.

• Integrate with lab instruments, robotic platforms, LIMS/ELN systems and scheduling software, translating between disparate formats and CuspAI's data platform.

• Make integrations reliable at scale: idempotency, retries, queueing, monitoring and alerting across many partners and time zones.

• Assist with the technical onboarding of new lab partners, assessing their systems and setting up integrations quickly and repeatedly.

• Collaborate day to day with experimental materials scientists, optimisation experts and engineers on the team, co-designing workflows and feeding lab realities back into platform design.

• Deploy and run containerised services on cloud infrastructure, with testing and CI/CD as standard.

Bonus Points

• Drive data contract and schema evolution practices so that breaking and non breaking changes are managed predictably across lab domains.

About Kubos Semiconductors
Kubos Semiconductors is developing and commercialising its patented technology in cubic gallium nitride (GaN) which has the potential to significantly increase the energy efficiency and switch speed of LEDs across the visible wavelength spectrum. Kubos’ technology can provide fundamental advantages across multiple markets, namely, next generation displays (including AR/VR), high-efficiency LED lighting and optical communications.
Kubos has a small team of its own but is fabless, with all its development carried out at third party facilities including both academic institutions and commercial manufacturing facilities. From its office in Cardiff, Kubos is ideally situated in the South Wales semiconductor cluster with ease of access to the wider UK semiconductor eco-system. On completion of development, Kubos plans to license its technology to existing large OEMs and LED manufacturers, providing low barrier to entry to developers wishing to take advantage of cubic-GaN technology.
The Opportunity
Kubos runs experimental campaigns that produce large amounts of research data. This is an exciting chance to shape how a deep-tech company manages and analyses that data, so its scientists and engineers can spend less time processing results and more time understanding what the experiments are telling them. Working closely with the team, you will review how data is handled today, recommend the right tools, including AI-powered options, and show what is possible using Kubos’ real experimental data. You will have the freedom to shape your own solutions and see the impact of your work on a growing research team.
What You Will Do
Data review and discovery
Review Kubos’ current data management and analysis processes, mapping the sources of experimental data and how they are handled
Work with engineers to understand what results they need to see, and how they want to compare results across experiments and over time
Tools and automation
Work with staff to define a standard report template for experimental campaigns
Build and demonstrate automated data processing and reporting using real data, reducing manual copy-and-paste work
Explore how AI and data tools could support design of experiments, helping the team decide what to test next
Adoption and responsible use
Deliver training to the team on new tools and ways of working, so they can use them with confidence

DEPT® is a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. About the job

Global AI Strategy & Solutions defines how DEPT®’s clients respond as AI agents become the primary layer between customers and brands. The Future of the Customer Journey (FCJ) is the team’s flagship offer: it maps how AI systems intermediate customer journeys, diagnoses where a brand’s product reality diverges from what AI systems say about it, and directs investment accordingly. Growth and strategy teams across markets are selling and delivering it now.

As a GTM Engineer, you are an embedded builder inside that motion. You will sit with growth and strategy teams, understand the problem in front of them, and answer with working software rather than documentation. You will convert FCJ methodology into agentic components, prototypes, and internal tools, and integrate with infrastructure that lets new prototypes appear in days. When needed, you will work across global client projects on a partially billable basis, making sure the firm-wide strategy is captured and implemented properly rather than reinvented market by market. As components mature, you will collaborate with product and craft teams to keep everything compatible with the long-term platform and hand over cleanly. 

You will be given broad problem statements to help collaborate and solve, not specific product ideas and features to create. We are not looking for someone to lead on devops or CICID, this is about having great ideas that are sensitive to our clients’ real challenges, and shipping prototypes and strategic tools rapidly. 

Your most important collaboration is with the FCJ core team on the global growth strategy: deciding what gets built next, for which market, to unlock which engagement. The toolchain will keep changing underneath you, new models, new vendor products, new technology-partner platforms, and that is the point. This role suits an engineer who learns by shipping and treats every new AI product as something to master in the field.

• Work with the FCJ core team on the global growth strategy, converting methodology into working agentic components, prototypes, and internal tools.

• Collaborate closely with growth and strategy teams to understand their problems and provide working solutions at prototype pace.

• Work across global client projects on a partially billable basis, ensuring the firm-wide FCJ strategy is captured and implemented consistently across markets.

• Collaborate with product and craft teams where necessary to document integration paths, maintain platform compatibility, and hand over validated components.

• Work with technology partners to evaluate, adopt, and integrate new AI products; maintain an AI-native toolchain and share what works across markets.

• Experience developing agentic systems with orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or equivalent.

• AI-native way of working: AI tooling is the default across coding, research, and delivery, with comfort spanning the tools in use across different markets.

Reporting To: Ed Haynes
Compensation: £60,000 - £70,000 / year

Description
DeterTech's purpose is giving greater peace of mind to people and communities, every day – and for our alarm signalling customers, that promise depends on hardware and software working together flawlessly. This role owns IoT and alarm signalling hardware integrations and device connectivity for DT ARC, bridging the gap between hardware and software to support new engineering requests as well as repair and manufacturing workflows.

Given the safety-critical nature of alarm signalling, this role needs a security-conscious approach and the confidence to troubleshoot issues that span both hardware and software.

As a specialist within the ARC development team who brings dedicated IoT experience, you will bridge the gap between physical hardware engineering and our operational monitoring platforms. Working alongside embedded firmware engineers, product managers, and software peers, you will ingest and map device telemetry, sensor feeds, and remote MQTT commands into our central Alarm Receiving Centre (ARC) platform and DTCommand client portal.

You will translate device-level hardware capabilities (such as geolocation) into intuitive, dependable controls and visual states for our 24/7 ARC operators. Furthermore, you will drive the iterative evolution of device features—progressing capabilities from basic on/off toggles and timed schedules through to smart, telemetry-driven automations and workflows.

ABOUT DETERTECH

DeterTech is a security technology company operating across six countries, with principal UK sites in Prestwick and Telford. We predict, deter and detect risk on behalf of the people and communities we serve. Our values – Committed, Inclusive and Ambitious – shape how we work every day: we are accountable and deliver excellence; we collaborate and build trust; and we never stop learning while winning in the right way.

This is a remote role, with the flexibility to work from home. We also value face-to-face collaboration and would ask for some flexibility to attend occasional in-person meetings or team sessions.

Key Responsibilities

1. IoT and hardware integration

• Build and maintain software integrations with IoT and hardware devices, including alarm signalling equipment, sensors and gateways.

• Apply relevant signalling protocols and standards used in the alarm/ARC industry (for example SIA, Contact ID, IP signalling).

• Ingest, decode, and process device telemetry and command topics (via MQTT, WebSockets, and TCP/UDP sockets) published by embedded hardware and firmware engineering teams.

• Map raw device states, diagnostic health metrics, and sensor data into operational database schemas and real-time ARC monitoring views.

• Implement resilient bidirectional messaging pipelines to dispatch remote control commands, configuration updates, and firmware state synchronisations over cellular and IoT networks.

2. Application development & iterative feature engineering

• Build the software side of device integrations, APIs and monitoring using strong Laravel/PHP skills.

• Use MQTT or similar messaging protocols for device connectivity where appropriate.

• Implement responsive operator interfaces and control panels within the ARC platform and DTCommand, translating UI/UX wireframes, interactive prototypes, and design specs provided by the Lead Digital Product Designer into functional frontend components and backend APIs

• Drive the phased, iterative evolution of hardware features in close alignment with the Head of Product and Lead Digital Product Designer—progressing device commands from simple manual toggles to rule-based timed intervals, telemetry-driven thresholds, and machine-learning assisted automations.

• Architect and scale background queue consumers to process high-frequency device heartbeats, pings, and alarm events with minimal latency.

• Build and maintain secure RESTful and event-driven APIs connecting device management services with the core ARC platform, DTCommand client portal, and mobile applications.

3. Troubleshooting and support

• Troubleshoot issues across the hardware/software boundary, working with engineering, repair and manufacturing colleagues as needed.

• Partner closely with hardware and embedded firmware engineers to define clear interface contracts, payload schemas, and MQTT topic structures for emerging device revisions and product features.

• Develop diagnostic utilities and device provisioning scripts to empower manufacturing and repair technicians to test, flash, configure, and certify equipment efficiently.

• Investigate complex telemetry anomalies, packet dropouts, and handshake timeouts in collaboration with relevant teams.

• Provide tier-3 technical escalation support for live signalling faults, identifying whether root causes stem from firmware bugs, cellular network carriers, protocol decoding, or backend application logic and work with relevant teams to support and fix. 

4. Security, compliance and reliability

• Apply a security-conscious approach to device connectivity, reflecting the critical, safety-related nature of alarm signalling.

• Implement strict security standards across all device communications, including transport encryption (TLS/mTLS), secure token/credential rotation, and mutual authentication.

• Ensure signalling architectures comply with alarm industry standards (such as BS EN 50131 / BS 5979 / PD 6662) and data privacy regulations (GDPR).

• Establish monitoring, synthetic health checks, and alerting on device listener sockets and broker connections to detect dropouts or network degradation proactively.

5. Sprint delivery and platform collaboration

• Participate actively in Agile sprint meeting with the Technical Delivery Manager, delivering predictable milestones on product engineering initiatives.

• Partner with the Lead Full Stack Developer for architectural guidance, code reviews, and API schema design to ensure IoT components integrate cleanly into the wider Laravel ecosystem.

• Collaborate closely with the Lead Digital Product Designer to review user interaction models, technical feasibility of UI components, and stateful feedback loops.

• Liaise with the MuleSoft / Integration team to ensure device information from manufacturing and repair configurations can be synchronised.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

Essential

• Experience integrating software with IoT/hardware devices (for example alarm signalling equipment, sensors, gateways).

• Understanding of relevant signalling protocols/standards used in the alarm/ARC industry (for example SIA, Contact ID, IP signalling).

• Strong Laravel/PHP skills to build the software side of device integrations, APIs and monitoring.

• Comfortable troubleshooting issues across the hardware/software boundary.

• A security-conscious approach to device connectivity, given the critical nature of alarm signalling.

• Background developing web applications, microservices, or daemons in modern PHP/Laravel (including queue workers, and event broadcasting).

• Practical experience working with MQTT, WebSockets, or publish/subscribe messaging architectures for device connectivity and telemetry ingestion.

• Demonstrated ability to translate raw hardware sensor data (telemetry, environmental inputs, battery budgets) into functional software applications and clear visual states.

• Familiarity with appropriate databases and caching/queue technologies for high-volume event processing.

• Collaborative team player, comfortable working across disciplines with embedded firmware engineers, product managers, digital designers, and manufacturing/repair technicians.

Desirable

• Experience with MQTT or similar messaging protocols for device connectivity.

• Experience in the security, alarm or IoT hardware industry.

• Familiarity with frontend technologies commonly used in the Laravel ecosystem (such as Livewire or React).

• Familiarity with cellular IoT connectivity (e.g. roaming M2M SIMs, APNs, bandwidth budgets, and AT commands).

• Practical experience using hardware diagnostic tools to debug issues.

• Familiarity with AWS cloud services (such as EC2, ECS, Lambda, or IoT Core).

• Exposure to manufacturing workflows, hardware provisioning tools.

Why Plumery exists
Our mission is to enable financial companies of any size globally to launch composable digital and AI banking experiences fast without giving up control, so they can adapt freely as banking changes and their vision grows.

Who are we?
Our name is derived from Plumeria, a tropical flower that is considered sacred in some cultures, symbolising new beginnings, dedication, and beauty.
It’s a contrast to how ugly digital banking can get. We know where the industry's compromises came from because we once worked for the companies that built them. We were in escalation meetings when banks discovered their vendors’ technology was more limited than they anticipated. And we were powerless to offer more than license concessions as a consolation.
This was a situation we didn’t want to continue. So we launched a new beginning for banks: Plumery.

What will you be working on?
We are looking for curious and passionate engineers to join us in building our developer-centric platform from the ground up.
• You will be part of an exciting journey, creating a financial platform from scratch that will impact hundreds of financial institutions and millions of end users.

• You will help to solve complex problems and mentor more junior team members.

• You should have a good understanding of Secure SDLC and OWASP concepts and be able to implement them in the code.

• You have solid experience building, operating, and distributing backend services in production.

FAQ
Questions that may be on your mind

Here we lay out some of what you can expect if you apply to a role or join our team.

What does your hiring process look like?

Our hiring process is designed to learn as much as we can about you in as little time as possible, so you’re not committing too much effort before we hire you.
A typical process looks like (Note: this may vary depending on the team and the role you’re applying for):
• A 30-minute initial interview. Depending on the role, this could be with the hiring manager or founder, Ben Goldin.
• A personality assessment, such as the Hogan Assessment. This gives us an idea of what it might be like to work with you over time.
• A second interview. Depending on the role, this could be with the hiring manager or founder, Ben Goldin.
• An interview with a peer, for instance, with our Head of Growth or Product or Chief of Staff.
• Finally we ask you to complete an assignment designed to test your thinking in a real world situation. It’s usually designed so it doesn’t require you to set aside much time (if any) to prepare.
If you’re talented, don’t count yourself out. We hire the best people from any background. The diversity of our senior team is evidence of this.

How long does the recruitment process usually take?

The recruitment process varies in length, depending on the role. However we usually wish to make a hire as soon as possible, so the process is rarely longer than between two and four weeks.

Do you offer remote, hybrid, or in office work?

We’re a remote-first company. We have a head office in Amsterdam, but many of our colleagues work remotely in a number of locations around the world. This is a high priority in our culture, so don’t expect any mandates to return to the office.

What does onboarding look like for new employees?

There is no formal onboarding path for our employees. Instead, you can expect your first few days to feel like diving in the deep end, with support from us.
You’ll meet the founder, the hiring manager, and you’ll get a number of vital recordings and write-ups to look through. But you’ll also get straight into the action, offering your expertise and your input. But we’re also realistic about what to expect: no one’s going to blame you if you get anything wrong in the first week.
We want you to prioritise the outcomes you can bring, not the tasks you can complete. So you’ll have autonomy and you’ll be defining your own personal strategy to achieve results. No one will be directing you, but we’ll be on hand to help.
You’ll likely need to commit to discovery at first, figuring out what’s already working and what’s not. That way you can build your own plan to move an area of the company forward.

What is your company culture like?

In our culture there is autonomy and ownership. We work to give financial institutions, and our team members, the independence to pursue their own strategies. If you like micromanagement or corporate directives, look elsewhere. We trust each of our people to set their own direction, to find and solve problems, and stay outcome-oriented.
There is openness and new ideas. It’s a startup cliche to say we need people to be adaptable, curious and able to think outside the box, but that’s exactly what we need. We can’t afford to rely on what’s worked in the past.
There is a team at your back. If you get stuck, you can always ask for help. And you can be brutally honest about how your day is going. We require no fake smiles.
There is willingness to find a way. Things will go wrong, but we believe in taking ownership when they do. We’ll trust you to stay motivated and to keep working on a problem.
There is one missing piece. Our culture isn’t complete and locked in stone. We’re looking for people to add to our culture, not just fit in, and we want people to bring themselves and all of their qualities to the table.

What does work-life balance look like?

Work-life balance is protected at Plumery. We want people to have families and hobbies, and we believe overworking is taking a credit you have to pay back. The last thing we need is for our people to be drained on a Monday morning because they worked the weekend. To stay rested and energised, we generally don’t work beyond 9–5 or 9–6, five days a week.
Our working hours aren’t rigid, so there’s some flexibility to set your own hours around family commitments or personal needs.

What opportunities are there for learning and career growth?

This isn’t a company to join if you’re looking for a formal learning and career path, but you’ll have plenty of opportunities to learn and step up as new challenges arise for the company. As a startup we’re growing rapidly, so if you do your best work with us, you can expect opportunities to move upwards (or horizontally) as the company changes.

Why Plumery exists
Our mission is to enable financial companies of any size globally to launch composable digital and AI banking experiences fast without giving up control, so they can adapt freely as banking changes and their vision grows.

Who are we?
Our name is derived from Plumeria, a tropical flower that is considered sacred in some cultures, symbolising new beginnings, dedication, and beauty.
It’s a contrast to how ugly digital banking can get. We know where the industry's compromises came from because we once worked for the companies that built them. We were in escalation meetings when banks discovered their vendors’ technology was more limited than they anticipated. And we were powerless to offer more than license concessions as a consolation.
This was a situation we didn’t want to continue. So we launched a new beginning for banks: Plumery.

About the Platform Team
We are the backbone of Plumery, providing a robust and reliable platform that empowers our product teams to build and deploy amazing things. We’re obsessed with automation, performance, and security, and we believe in the power of cloud-native technologies to drive innovation.

Your Mission
As a Platform Engineer, you will be a key player in building and maintaining the foundation upon which Plumery’s success is built. Your mission is to:
• Ensure Plumery’s platform is a rock: You’ll be responsible for the availability, performance, and scalability of our infrastructure, ensuring zero downtime and seamless scaling.
• Champion a culture of collaboration: You’ll work closely with product teams, understanding their needs and enabling them to deliver features faster and more efficiently.
• Automate everything: You’ll embrace Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and GitOps practices to automate infrastructure changes, ensuring consistency and repeatability.
• Be a knowledge leader: You’ll continuously learn and share your expertise with the team and the wider organisation, promoting best practices and improving our collective knowledge.

What You Bring to the Table
• Platform building expertise: You have a proven track record of designing, building, securing, and supporting platforms at scale for both product and infrastructure.
• IaC and GitOps mastery: Terraform is your weapon of choice, and you’re fluent in the language of IaC and GitOps.
• Cloud-native expert: You have a deep understanding of cloud-native applications, distributed systems, and microservices architectures.
• Public cloud proficiency: You’re comfortable navigating multiple public cloud providers (AWS,Azure,GCP), with experience in managed Kubernetes services.
• Automation enthusiast: You can automate tasks effectively using Go and/or Python.
• Kubernetes expert: You have hands-on experience managing applications on Kubernetes.
• Networking specialist: You have a strong grasp of public cloud networking concepts, with a focus on security and Kubernetes service meshes.
• Data management: You have experience managing databases, streaming, and messaging services.
• Security advocate: You have a deep understanding of public cloud security and Kubernetes security, including best practices for securing infrastructure, applications, and data. You have experience with security tools and technologies such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, encryption, and identity and access management.You are familiar with Well-Architected Frameworks and compliance frameworks like ISO27001, SOC2.
• Observability expert: You have a deep understanding of observability practices and tools, including monitoring, alerting, tracing, and logging.

What Your Colleagues Would Say About You
• Team player: You thrive in a collaborative environment and are passionate about fostering technical excellence.
• Adaptable and open to change: You embrace new challenges and are always willing to learn and grow.
• Driven to make a difference: You’re motivated to make a real impact and are always looking for ways to improve.
• Innovative and curious: You’re not afraid to experiment with new technologies and challenge the status quo.

Why should you join Plumery?
• Work with a team of highly passionate people where every person is appreciated and respected.
• Be part of changing how banking is done globally.
• Enjoy a unique opportunity to influence and shape the trajectory of Plumery, making a substantial impact on our future growth and development.
• Maintain work-life balance as we prioritize efficiency over long working hours.
• Gain significant equity upside as one of Plumery’s foundational team members.
In addition, we are proud to offer full remote work flexibility. We believe that remote work fosters greater productivity, work-life balance, and employee well-being.
Join us and help build the future of Plumery!

FAQ
Questions that may be on your mind

Here we lay out some of what you can expect if you apply to a role or join our team.

What does your hiring process look like?

Our hiring process is designed to learn as much as we can about you in as little time as possible, so you’re not committing too much effort before we hire you.
A typical process looks like (Note: this may vary depending on the team and the role you’re applying for):
• A 30-minute initial interview. Depending on the role, this could be with the hiring manager or founder, Ben Goldin.
• A personality assessment, such as the Hogan Assessment. This gives us an idea of what it might be like to work with you over time.
• A second interview. Depending on the role, this could be with the hiring manager or founder, Ben Goldin.
• An interview with a peer, for instance, with our Head of Growth or Product or Chief of Staff.
• Finally we ask you to complete an assignment designed to test your thinking in a real world situation. It’s usually designed so it doesn’t require you to set aside much time (if any) to prepare.
If you’re talented, don’t count yourself out. We hire the best people from any background. The diversity of our senior team is evidence of this.

How long does the recruitment process usually take?

The recruitment process varies in length, depending on the role. However we usually wish to make a hire as soon as possible, so the process is rarely longer than between two and four weeks.

Do you offer remote, hybrid, or in office work?

We’re a remote-first company. We have a head office in Amsterdam, but many of our colleagues work remotely in a number of locations around the world. This is a high priority in our culture, so don’t expect any mandates to return to the office.

What does onboarding look like for new employees?

There is no formal onboarding path for our employees. Instead, you can expect your first few days to feel like diving in the deep end, with support from us.
You’ll meet the founder, the hiring manager, and you’ll get a number of vital recordings and write-ups to look through. But you’ll also get straight into the action, offering your expertise and your input. But we’re also realistic about what to expect: no one’s going to blame you if you get anything wrong in the first week.
We want you to prioritise the outcomes you can bring, not the tasks you can complete. So you’ll have autonomy and you’ll be defining your own personal strategy to achieve results. No one will be directing you, but we’ll be on hand to help.
You’ll likely need to commit to discovery at first, figuring out what’s already working and what’s not. That way you can build your own plan to move an area of the company forward.

What is your company culture like?

In our culture there is autonomy and ownership. We work to give financial institutions, and our team members, the independence to pursue their own strategies. If you like micromanagement or corporate directives, look elsewhere. We trust each of our people to set their own direction, to find and solve problems, and stay outcome-oriented.
There is openness and new ideas. It’s a startup cliche to say we need people to be adaptable, curious and able to think outside the box, but that’s exactly what we need. We can’t afford to rely on what’s worked in the past.
There is a team at your back. If you get stuck, you can always ask for help. And you can be brutally honest about how your day is going. We require no fake smiles.
There is willingness to find a way. Things will go wrong, but we believe in taking ownership when they do. We’ll trust you to stay motivated and to keep working on a problem.
There is one missing piece. Our culture isn’t complete and locked in stone. We’re looking for people to add to our culture, not just fit in, and we want people to bring themselves and all of their qualities to the table.

What does work-life balance look like?

Work-life balance is protected at Plumery. We want people to have families and hobbies, and we believe overworking is taking a credit you have to pay back. The last thing we need is for our people to be drained on a Monday morning because they worked the weekend. To stay rested and energised, we generally don’t work beyond 9–5 or 9–6, five days a week.
Our working hours aren’t rigid, so there’s some flexibility to set your own hours around family commitments or personal needs.

What opportunities are there for learning and career growth?

This isn’t a company to join if you’re looking for a formal learning and career path, but you’ll have plenty of opportunities to learn and step up as new challenges arise for the company. As a startup we’re growing rapidly, so if you do your best work with us, you can expect opportunities to move upwards (or horizontally) as the company changes.

job_description:
Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.
A Day in the Life

Medtronic Digital Technologies is building the future of connected intelligent surgery through the Touch Surgery™ ecosystem. As our portfolio evolves, artificial intelligence and data will play an increasingly important role in supporting surgical teams with clinically grounded insights before, during and after procedures. We are looking for a Global Marketing Manager to own the development and communication of our commercial AI and data story, demonstrating how connected surgical data can be transformed into meaningful insights and new capabilities for customers. 

About the Position

The central purpose of this downstream marketing role is to create and communicate a clear, credible and differentiated story about Medtronic’s role in AI and data-enabled surgery.
The role leads global promotion of AI and data-enabled capabilities within the Touch Surgery™ ecosystem, connecting individual product launches into a compelling overarching narrative. It translates complex technology, clinical evidence and customer needs into value propositions, launch strategies and commercial tools that build understanding, confidence and demand.
Working closely with Upstream Marketing, which leads portfolio strategy, product roadmaps and requirements, the role ensures future capabilities are grounded in customer needs and positioned for successful commercialisation.
In partnership with Product, R&D, Clinical, Medical Affairs, Regulatory, Privacy and regional commercial teams, it ensures a consistent, evidence-led AI and data story that resonates across markets and customer touchpoints.
Success is measured through the strength and adoption of the AI and data narrative, launch readiness, commercial execution and customer adoption of new capabilities.

Primary Responsibilities:
• Own, develop and continually evolve the commercial AI and data story for Medtronic Digital Technologies and the Touch Surgery™ ecosystem. 
• Partner closely with Upstream Marketing to translate portfolio strategy and product roadmaps into clear, compelling and differentiated commercial narratives. 
• Articulate Medtronic’s surgical data advantage and the role of data in powering insights, AI applications and the connected ecosystem. 
• Lead global promotion and go-to-market planning for individual AI and data-enabled capabilities. 
• Connect individual applications to the wider Touch Surgery™ ecosystem story, creating a consistent narrative across the portfolio. 
• Translate technical capabilities and clinical evidence into relevant customer benefits, proof points and commercial messages. 
• Partner with Regulatory, Legal, Clinical, Medical Affairs, Privacy and technical teams to develop accurate, differentiated and compliant claims. 
• Build launch plans, campaigns, sales tools, training and customer-facing content for global and regional teams. 
• Provide customer, competitive and commercial insight to Upstream Marketing to support roadmap, product-development and evidence-planning decisions. 
• Develop customer segmentation and engagement strategies for surgeons, surgical teams, hospital executives and technology stakeholders. 
• Monitor the evolving AI, data and digital surgery landscape, identifying competitive threats, market trends and opportunities for differentiation.
• Support congresses, thought-leadership initiatives and clinical partnerships that strengthen Medtronic’s position in AI and data-enabled surgery. 
• Establish launch and adoption metrics, monitor performance and adapt plans based on customer and commercial feedback. 

Required Qualifications:

About the role
We are seeking an ambitious, highly organised, and commercially minded Deal Desk Coordinator to support our sales organisation in structuring, coordinating, and closing complex deals. Supporting our EMEA and APAC regions while working London hours, this role acts as a central hub between Sales and key internal teams (Legal, Procurement, Operations, Finance, and Systems) to ensure deals are accurately quoted, approved, enabled, and smoothly handed over for execution.

The ideal candidate is an ambitious individual who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic, and cross-functional environment, bringing strong attention to detail, process discipline, commercial acumen, and a collaborative mindset to support deal velocity and quality.

Why This Role Is Interesting
This role offers a unique opportunity to sit at the high-impact intersection of Sales, Legal, Finance, and Operations within an Emmy award-winning visual technology leader. Supporting complex, high-value deals ($200k+) across the dynamic EMEA and APAC regions, the Deal Desk Coordinator acts as a strategic business partner driving deal velocity, structuring innovative commercial terms, and gaining broad cross-functional visibility in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment.

What you will do 

• Support Sales with deal structuring, pricing configurations, and quote creation for complex opportunities across the EMEA and APAC regions.

• Ensure deal terms, pricing, and commercial assumptions align with internal policies and approval frameworks.

• Prepare and maintain accurate deal documentation within Salesforce, tracking deal progress, approvals, escalations, and timelines.

• Act as the primary point of coordination between Sales and internal teams throughout the deal lifecycle.

• Partner with Legal to route, track, and finalise contracts, NDAs, Statements of Work, and non-standard terms.

• Work closely with Finance on pricing approvals, billing setup, credit checks, and revenue recognition requirements.

• Liaise with Operations on service readiness, delivery alignment, customer onboarding, third-party dependencies, and smooth post-signature handover.

• Ensure all required internal approvals are obtained prior to deal close, preparing clear deal summaries and handover packages for delivery teams.

• Maintain data accuracy across Salesforce, CPQ, and contract management systems, identifying opportunities to streamline deal workflows, reduce cycle time, and improve cross-functional collaboration.

• Support the regional forecasting cadence by keeping opportunity stages, close dates and deal values current and accurate in Salesforce, giving Sales and Finance leadership a number they can trust.

• Drive system and process enablement initiatives, including training sales teams on new processes and workflows to enhance tool adoption and optimize commercial operations.

Experience we are looking for 

Required

• 3-5 years experience in a Deal Desk, Sales Operations, Sales Support, or Commercial Operations role.

• 3-5 years experience supporting complex ($200k+ and cross territories) or non-standard deals in a B2B, SaaS, or services environment.

• Strong understanding of sales processes, deal structuring, quoting, approval workflows, and cross-functional deal coordination.

• 3-5 years hands-on experience using CRM systems (ideally Salesforce), CPQ tools, and contract management systems.

Preferred

• Experience supporting or contributing to forecast calls or pipeline reviews, with the confidence to flag risk on a deal to a Sales Manager directly.

• 1-2 years managing multi-regional stakeholders (supporting EMEA and APAC regions while working London hours).

Skills, behaviours and values we are looking for

• Strong Interpersonal Skills: Builds rapport quickly across very different personality types, from assertive Sales Managers to detail-focused Finance and Legal contacts. Comfortable holding a firm line on process with a senior stakeholder who is pushing back, without the relationship souring.

• Dynamic & Resilient: Excel in a dynamic, cross-functional environment alongside diverse teams and priorities, collaboratively adapting your approach to support different stakeholders and meet key deal goals.

• High Level of Attention to Detail: Able to keep reports, Salesforce data, quotes, and contract documentation meticulous and up to date.

• Collaborative & Dependable: Both a team player and an autonomous agent who builds strong, trust-based working relationships across Legal, Finance, Operations, and Sales.

• Excellent Communication: Strong written, verbal, and diplomatic communication skills with the confidence to interact with cross-functional stakeholders.

• No Ego: Approachable, authentic, and humble.

Disguise is the industry-leading platform sitting at the heart of a new era of visual experiences. One powerful integrated system of software, hardware and services to help create the next dimension of real-time spectacle.
We partner with the biggest entertainment brands and companies in the world to deliver the A-list of live music events, live TV broadcasts, immersive experiences, installations, theatre, film and TV production, corporate communications and brand product launches. Working with Disney, Snapchat, Netflix, ESPN, the Burj Khalifa, and Adele, Disguise is the number one partner delivering the next dimension of entertainment.

Don’t Disguise your differences.

Innovation comes from everyone. We strive to create a workplace that reflects our diverse audience. We celebrate our people for their full authentic selves, and embrace uniqueness. Inclusion and Equity matter at Disguise. We create together and we create everywhere. 

 

Our values

• Honest. We are real with ourselves and our clients and share our ideas with openness and transparency. 

• Evolutionary. We innovate using our user’s ever-changing needs so our technology remains ahead-of-the-game.

• Fearless. We take the best path, not the easiest, and innovate where it’s right, not where it’s simplest.

• Resilience. We don’t give up until we find the right solution, even if it means going outside our remit.

• Belong.  We create an environment where everyone feels like they belong and is empowered to do their best work.

• We have a suite of globally relevant competitive benefits packages as we want to make sure we retain the best talent out there. Our benefits for every perm hire, globally include:

• Unlimited Paid Time Off - with minimum time you must take set at 20% above statutory

• Hybrid working between home and our offices (dependent on role and location)

• Training, coaching & mentoring

Doodle is a B2B SaaS platform used by millions of professionals to coordinate meetings and collaboration across teams and companies. We are building the future of scheduling and productivity, and trusted data has become one of our most valuable products. You are more than an Analytics Engineer. You are a builder who cares about getting the numbers right, and you love helping people make better decisions with them.
The Role
In this role, you’ll co-own a share of the analytics layer that powers decisions across Doodle. You’ll turn raw product data into trusted, scalable datasets for experimentation, reporting and product innovation. Our transformations are built in dbt on top of Amazon Redshift, with Athena alongside it, and teams explore and report on data in Power BI, Hex and our own internal AI tools.
You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Finance and Leadership. Some days that means defining the metrics the whole company runs on. Other days it means helping a Growth Manager design an A/B test, or showing a team how to answer their own questions without waiting on anyone. If you get excited by clean models, well-defined metrics and data people actually trust, you’ll find a stimulating environment here.
AI is at the heart of how we work. We expect you to use AI coding tools to move faster on modelling, testing and documentation, and to help the rest of Doodle get more out of AI in their daily work with data.
What You’ll Actually Do
• Model the Data: Design, build and maintain scalable analytics data models in dbt, following analytics engineering best practices.

• Own Data Quality: Build reliable transformations from raw product data to business-ready datasets, with testing, validation and documentation across the analytics layer.

• Define the Metrics: Define, document and maintain the trusted business metrics used across the company, and keep definitions aligned across teams.

• Build the Semantic Layer: Evolve a scalable semantic layer that makes consistent reporting and self-service analytics possible.

• Power Experimentation: Partner with Product and Growth Managers on A/B tests, funnels, retention and customer insights, through high-quality event modelling and instrumentation. Then help teams read the results and decide what to do next.

• Lead with AI: Build AI-enabled analytics workflows and help teams across Doodle adopt AI in how they work with data.

• The Warehouse: Experience with cloud data warehouses such as Amazon Redshift.

• The BI Toolkit: Experience building dashboards and self-service reports in Power BI or similar BI tools.

• The Product Lens: Familiarity with experimentation frameworks and product analytics.

• The AI Mindset: Hands-on experience with Claude or similar AI assistants, including setting up MCPs and using AI coding tools. You’ve helped drive AI adoption in a team or organisation.

• Good Python skills for data processing and automation, for example with pandas.

• Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow, and experience with Athena.

• Experience with tools such as Google Analytics 4, GrowthBook (A/B testing) or Avo (tracking plan design and data governance).

• The SaaS Background: Experience working in a modern B2B SaaS environment.

Who we are

We’re doxy.me (doc-see-me), the world's most loved telemedicine solution, and we're on a mission to connect the world to the future of healthcare.

We believe that cost and complexity should never be a barrier to telemedicine. That’s why we created a simple, free, and secure telemedicine platform. Since 2013, we’ve grown to more than 1 million healthcare providers from 180+ countries who have clocked over 8 billion minutes of telemedicine sessions to date.

Our goal is to deliver the future of healthcare to every patient and healthcare professional on earth. Help us get there by joining our team of innovators, dreamers, and doers.

We’re a remote-first company with regional hubs for in-person collaboration (Charleston, SC, Salt Lake City, UT & London, UK).

The role

This is a software engineering role with security as the domain, not a security role with some scripting attached.

We are building internal security platforms, such as SecurityOS and our Trust Engine, that run the security program for our product, with AI doing much of the work that used to be manual. SecurityOS is in production today, Trust Engine is next, and there is more to come.

The security team at doxy.me is becoming an engineering team. We build and run these platforms, we build and govern the AI agents that operate inside them, and we ship the product security work for doxy.me's telehealth platform as part of the same practice. You would be an early engineer on that team with a direct hand in what these platforms become.

We are looking for someone with a founder mindset: you see what should exist, you design it, you build it, and you ship it. You can own a problem end to end without a spec handed to you. You have taste about what makes software good and opinions about how security should be done, and you can back both with working code.

What you'll build and do

• Design and build core SecurityOS capabilities: domain modules, integrations with the systems that feed the platform (identity, endpoints, cloud, code, ticketing), the event model that connects them, and the reporting and console layer on top. Production TypeScript and Node, shipped to real users on the security team.

• Build and govern AI agents that operate inside the platform: define what they can do, what context they get, how their actions are controlled and audited, and how they go through the same front door as a human user.

• Own product security for doxy.me's telehealth platform as an embedded engineer: threat modeling with product teams, design and code review, and fixing or building the thing yourself when that is the fastest path.

• Build the security tooling and guardrails that make the right thing the default in our stack, as code our engineers actually use, not as policy documents.

• Automate the security SDLC. You know how to threat model, review a design, review code for security flaws, and run security testing by hand. Your job is to build the platform and automation that does that work at scale, so it is not done by hand.

• Shape the roadmap. You will have real influence over what SecurityOS becomes and how the security function at doxy.me operates.

Who you are

Must-haves

• You can build and ship software. You have taken something from an idea to running in production, maintained it, and had other people depend on it, in TypeScript and Node or a comparable stack. We care that you can design a system from the data model up and get it live, not how many years you have been doing it. If AI tools are a big part of how you build, good. That is how we build too.

• You have real depth in application and product security: secure SDLC, threat modeling, secure design and code review, OWASP and how vulnerabilities actually get authored and designed out. You need this to be able to build software that does it. Knowing it is table stakes; building it is the job.

• You have built things nobody asked you to build because you saw they were needed, and they got used.

• You can take an ambiguous problem, form a point of view, and drive it to working software without a spec or a ticket.

• You have opinions about how a security program should run and you are not attached to the way it has always been done.

• You are comfortable building with and around AI: using it as a core part of how you work, and designing systems where agents are first-class actors with controls on what they can do.

• You can talk to product engineers as a peer. They should see you as one of them who happens to know security deeply.

Nice-to-haves

• Experience building a platform, internal product, or developer tool from zero to adopted.

• Startup or founding experience, or a side project you took seriously enough to ship.

• Healthcare, HIPAA, or other regulated-industry context.

• AWS, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code. Useful, but we are not hiring for this.

Your skills

• Staff or principal level expected. Years matter less than what you have built and what you can show us.

• Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience. A strong portfolio of shipped work counts for more than the degree.

• Experience with remote, globally distributed teams. English is the language of all internal communication.

To lead and strengthen accounting operations across multiple legal entities. TEAM
· At easyJet, we are transforming Airline Operations through modern product-led technology, operational excellence, automation, data and AI-enabled capabilities.

· Coordinate the platform squads against mission sprints, owning delivery cadence across the allocated portfolio.
· Own the commitment position with the missions: what Platform has committed to each sprint, what has changed, and what is at risk.
· Track and manage vendor commitments as external dependencies, surfacing the vendor critical path before it becomes a delay.
· Own dependency, risk and issue management across products, missions, suppliers and enterprise platforms.
· Ensure work entering a sprint is sized, understood and free of unresolved dependencies.
· Support the demand rhythm through triage, sizing and the reuse-first challenge, keeping the single backlog credible and current.
· Ensure change reaches the operation safely, with readiness, supportability, documentation and cover agreed before release.
· Define and report delivery metrics that give visibility of flow, predictability and delivery health.
· Champion Product and Platform ways of working, treating the missions as customers of the Platform.
· Provide clear, early communication on progress, risk and change to mission and Platform leadership.
· Drive continuous improvement in how the Platform delivers, removing repeated impediments rather than working around them.
JOB ACCOUNTABILITIES
Delivery Cadence & Squad Coordination
· Coordinate platform squads across the capability chapters — Data Availability, API & Integration; Proactive App Management; Automation — against mission sprint commitments.
· Own the delivery cadence: backlog refinement, sprint planning, stand-ups, reviews and release planning, run consistently rather than when there is time.
· Maintain one backlog and one plan for the allocated portfolio, so squad members working across several missions have a single view of priority.
· Sequence work so that run and support, mission demand and improvement work coexist rather than compete, protecting the agreed capacity allocation.
· Keep the plan honest: reflect actual progress and capacity, not the plan as originally committed.
Mission Interface & Commitment Management
· Run the per-sprint interface sync with the Mission Product Managers for the allocated missions: what Platform commits to that sprint, and what has changed since the last one.
· Own the commitment record, so a mission always knows what it is getting, when, and what it depends on.
· Surface changes to commitment early, with the reason and the option set, rather than reporting a miss after the fact.
· Ensure missions are not building platform capability that is already coming, by making the Platform roadmap and backlog visible to them.
· Escalate to the Platform Lead – Demand & Capability where commitments and capacity diverge, with the trade-off articulated.
Demand Support, Sizing & Dependencies
· Support daily triage and the weekly demand review, contributing sizing, dependency mapping and the reuse-first challenge.
· Ensure nothing enters a sprint unsized, without dependencies mapped, or without the vendor critical path named in the commitment.
· Own dependency management across products, missions, suppliers, enterprise data, architecture and I&O, coordinating resolution rather than reporting the blockage.
· Maintain and work the risk and issue log for the allocated portfolio, with mitigations owned, monitored and escalated where required.
· Identify where the same dependency or impediment recurs, and work with the Platform Leads and Architects to remove the cause.
Vendor & Supplier Delivery
· Track vendor commitments — releases, fixes, roadmap items, API and integration changes — as external dependencies with dates, owners and evidence.
· Hold suppliers to their delivery commitments day to day, escalating to the Supplier Management Specialist where contractual leverage is needed.
· Ensure vendor-driven change is sequenced through the same route as internal work, and impact assessed before it is accepted.
· Feed delivery evidence — missed dates, repeated defects, performance under load — into supplier performance management.
· Coordinate vendor activity around the operational calendar, so third-party change does not land at the wrong moment for the operation.
Release, Readiness & Transition into Support
· Coordinate release planning and deployment across products, suppliers and operational stakeholders.
· Ensure every release meets agreed readiness criteria before it goes live: testing and quality gates with the QE function, monitoring, documentation, training, supportability and named cover.
· Work with the Technical Specialists and Service Support Lead so support and callout arrangements are in place before change reaches the operation, not after.
· Coordinate the delivery and readiness elements of applications transitioning between the Platform and the missions.
· Run lessons learned after significant releases and major incidents with a delivery cause, and feed the outcome into how the next one is planned.
Delivery Performance & Continuous Improvement
· Define and maintain delivery metrics and flow measures for the allocated portfolio, including predictability, throughput, unplanned work and time to triage.
· Provide reporting that gives mission and Platform leadership a true view of delivery health rather than a reassuring one.

The Trade Operations IT Delivery Team is one of the teams of EDF Trading IT Delivery function. The team provides comprehensive IT custom development and support for the EDFT Operational teams (Trade Capture/Controls, Scheduling, Nominations, Confirmations and Settlements). Working on one of the key interfaces between the business and IT, a good understanding of the commodity trading business context in which the applications are used, as well as solid IT software engineering practices are both of paramount importance.

Position purpose
The team designs, develops and supports (when required) custom-built, multi-asset class applications and tools in a variety of technologies, primarily using a Microsoft toolset.

The team currently has a flat structure with an emphasis on getting the job done, regardless of job title. As such, developers must be prepared to do their own analysis and testing in some situations, however they will be supported by Senior Developers and Business Analysts (BA) in the team. A BA will typically be involved in most cases, especially for larger items.

In addition, developers are expected to contribute to improving EDF Trading development processes, as well as participate in evolving the architectural road map. Emphasis is more on a Senior developer to do this, while developers are encouraged to push in this direction.

The solutions built by the team are expected to last many years and hence robustness and supportability is absolutely key. 

The team needs a Junior Developer who can enhance and fix existing applications and write new ones with Angular front end (React is considered) and C# .Net backend.

Development

• Adhere to the company’s standards and best practices, including, but not limited to, documentation, testing and peer reviews.
• Ensure maintenance of the development infrastructure required by the above tools. Maintenance of the source code repository, continuous build and deployment facilities.

Support to the Business

Engagement with IT

• Keep abreast of industry technological developments and identify opportunities to implement new frameworks, technologies, and tools to provide a more efficient and effective service to the Business.

• Previous experience in a development role working closely with both IT and business customers.

• Experience with deploying changes all the way to production.
• Experience in assisting with the analysis, planning and design of the new applications and enhancements to existing ones.

Technical requirements

• Experience in designing and building distributed systems using Microsoft C#, .NET Core and Web API.
• Experience working with relational databases such as Oracle or SQL Server
• Basic front end web development experience or keenness to learn Angular, Typescript, JavaScript, HTML/CSS.
