job_title: Attestations and Client Audit Manager D&A (DORA)
job_description:
About Us

LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group) is more than a diversified global financial markets infrastructure and data business. We are dedicated, open-access partners with a dedication to excellence in delivering the services our customers expect from us. With extensive experience, deep knowledge and worldwide presence across financial markets, we enable businesses and economies around the world to fund innovation, manage risk and create jobs. It’s how we’ve contributed to supporting the financial stability and growth of communities and economies globally for more than 300 years. Through a comprehensive suite of trusted financial market infrastructure services – and our open-access model – we provide the flexibility, stability and trust that enable our customers to pursue their ambitions with confidence and clarity.
LSEG is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with significant operations in 70 countries across EMEA, North America, Latin America and Asia Pacific. We employ 25,000 people globally, more than half located in Asia Pacific.

Role Summary

This is a high-impact leadership role within the Data & Analytics (D&A) assurance function.
As the Attestations and Client Audit Manager, you will lead the delivery of key D&A DORA client audit and attestation programmes.

You will lead complex client assurance engagements, including DORA client audits and ISAE 3000 attestations, working directly with clients, external auditors and senior partners across Technology, Product, Risk, Information Security, Legal and Compliance.

Beyond delivering audits and attestations, you will drive audit readiness, strengthen controls, oversee remediation and continuously improve how assurance is delivered across D&A. 
This is an opportunity to combine people leadership, client engagement, risk and controls expertise and assurance delivery within a complex global technology environment!

What You’ll Be Doing

Leadership & Team Management
• Lead, coach and develop a team of assurance professionals based in India, creating a high-performing and collaborative culture focused on quality, accountability and continuous improvement.
• Set clear priorities and objectives, oversee delivery and support team development through coaching, feedback and career development.
• Drive automation, standardisation and continuous improvement to enhance the quality, efficiency and scalability of assurance delivery.

Client Audit & Attestation Management
• Own the end-to-end development and delivery of ISAE 3000 attestations, including scoping, control and evidence coordination, management review and engagement with the external assessor through to final issuance.
• Lead the DORA client audit programme, coordinating planning, stakeholder engagement, evidence collection, client responses and remediation activities.
• Act as a senior point of contact for clients, account teams and external auditors throughout assurance engagements.
• Coordinate collaborators and domain experts to deliver accurate, timely and well-evidenced responses, identifying recurring themes and opportunities to improve audit readiness.

 Risk, Controls & Governance
• Drive DORA client audit readiness across Data & Analytics, partnering with Product, Engineering, Technology, Risk and other control functions to strengthen controls, evidence and supporting documentation.
• Maintain oversight of key assurance documentation, including control narratives, process flows, risk and control matrices and supporting evidence.
• Track audit observations and remediation actions, working with accountable partners to support timely and sustainable resolution.
• Represent the Attestations and Client Audit function at relevant working groups and governance forums, providing assurance updates, highlighting emerging risks and themes, and driving actions and decisions where required.
• Apply risk-based judgement to assurance matters, bringing up material risks or control gaps appropriately.
• Produce clear assurance metrics and reporting, providing collaborators with visibility of audit activity, remediation and emerging themes.

Client & Stakeholder Engagement
• Build trusted relationships with clients, external auditors and various collaborators.
• Partner with Legal, Compliance, Information Security, Technology, Product and customer-facing teams to address evolving client, contractual and regulatory assurance requirements.
• Lead complex discussions, constructively challenge where appropriate and translate technical, risk and regulatory matters into clear, actionable insights.

What We’re Looking For

Experience
• Significant experience within Risk Assurance, Technology Audit, IT Risk, Information Security, Controls or Internal Audit, ideally within financial services, technology, consulting or another regulated environment.
• Demonstrable experience leading, coaching and developing teams.
• Experience managing complex client audits, external assurance reviews or attestation programmes from planning through to completion.
• Experience engaging directly with external auditors, financial institutions or other sophisticated clients.
• Practical understanding of DORA, technology risk and control requirements.
• Solid understanding of relevant assurance standards and frameworks such as ISAE 3000/3402, SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT or equivalent.
• Experience working across complex technology environments and geographically distributed teams, including driving remediation and sustainable control improvements.

Skills & Leadership
• Strong people leadership, coaching and team development capabilities.
• Excellent stakeholder management, influencing and negotiation skills.
• Solid understanding of technology risk, information security and control principles.
• Excellent analytical, critical-thinking and problem-solving skills.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to engage directly with clients, auditors and senior partners.
• Ability to translate complex technical, risk and regulatory matters into clear, actionable business insights.
• Ability to handle challenging priorities, exercise good judgement and work effectively with a high degree of autonomy.

Desirable
• Professional qualification such as CISA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, CIA or equivalent.
• Degree or equivalent professional experience in Information Security, Technology, Risk, Audit, Business or a related field.
• Experience supporting DORA, FCA, SEC, ESMA or other regulatory or client assurance reviews.
• Experience across Operational Resilience, Technology Risk, Control Assurance or Technology Governance.

o Ensure understanding of applicable Group Risk policies.
o Draft Daily Credit Monitoring Reports summarising:
§ Key financial and other market data releases
§ Significant changes in market data information including external ratings and share price fluctuations
§ Breaches of clearing activity thresholds/limits
o Ensure appropriate escalation of any breaches and significant news stories to senior management.

· Analyse and interpret data to provide regular reports for stakeholders, identifying risks outside appetite

We are looking for a Development Manager to lead the Software Development and Quality Engineering teams responsible for our FX Exchange applications across FX Spot, Swaps and NDF. You will have overall accountability for the people, technology, delivery and quality of the product area.

You will work closely with Product to shape the roadmap, assess technical feasibility and turn business and customer priorities into secure, resilient and scalable solutions. This is a senior People Leader role that requires technical credibility. You will guide architecture and key engineering decisions while enabling teams to own detailed design, development, testing and production support. You will also build an inclusive environment where engineers can grow, collaborate and deliver their best work.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:
Lead the engineering organisation
Lead Software Development and Quality Engineering teams with shared accountability for delivery and product quality.
• Lead Software Development and Quality Engineering teams with shared accountability for delivery and product quality.
• Set clear technical direction, engineering standards and delivery expectations.
• Coach engineers, support career development and build future technical and people leaders.
• Plan the skills, capacity, hiring and organisational structure needed to deliver the product roadmap.
• Create an inclusive environment that values different perspectives, open communication and continuous learning.
• Lead distributed teams and work effectively with external technology partners.
Partner with Product
• Share accountability with Product for translating business strategy, customer needs and market opportunities into an achievable product roadmap.
• Assess technical feasibility, dependencies, delivery options and engineering investment before roadmap commitments are made.
• Balance functional delivery with resilience, security, regulatory obligations, technical debt and platform modernisation.
• Provide clear estimates, delivery choices and trade-offs so Product can make informed priority decisions.
• Use customer, operational and engineering data to measure outcomes and guide future investment.
Own engineering delivery and quality
• Be accountable for delivery from requirements and design through development, testing, deployment and production operation.
• Establish a modern software development lifecycle based on automation, continuous integration and delivery, peer review, continuous testing, security, observability and operational readiness.
• Make quality a shared responsibility across Development and Quality Engineering.
• Lead functional, integration, performance, resilience and security testing for business-critical trading services.
• Improve release confidence by automating repeatable checks, reducing manual hand-offs and addressing defects earlier.
• Ensure technical debt, engineering risks and dependencies are visible, prioritised and managed.
Provide technical leadership
• Guide architecture and design for high-volume, low-latency and highly available trading systems.
• Ensure solutions are scalable, secure, observable, supportable and aligned with the wider FX technology strategy.
• Lead technical reviews and challenge designs constructively, while enabling teams to own implementation decisions.
• Drive modernisation of legacy platforms, including modularisation, simplification and the adoption of reusable engineering patterns.
• Maintain a strong understanding of Java, C++, Linux, event-driven architectures, distributed systems, messaging and performance engineering.
• Lead the response to complex production issues and ensure learning is converted into lasting improvements.
Embed AI and automation across engineering
• Set expectations for responsible use of AI throughout the software development lifecycle, from requirements and design to coding, testing, documentation and production support.
• Encourage teams to create and reuse AI skills and agents that automate repeatable engineering activities.
• Use AI-assisted analysis and automation to improve quality, delivery speed and developer experience while protecting security, data and intellectual property.
• Measure adoption and outcomes, share effective patterns and ensure appropriate human review and governance.
Measure and improve performance
• Define meaningful measures for delivery flow, quality, reliability and engineering effectiveness.
• Use measures such as lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, recovery time, escaped defects, automation coverage, service availability and performance trends to identify improvements.
• Build a culture of evidence-based decisions, experimentation and continuous learning rather than using metrics as individual performance targets.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:
• Experience leading Software Development and Quality Engineering teams responsible for business-critical products.
• Technical leadership experience in high-volume, low-latency or distributed systems, preferably within electronic trading or financial markets.
• Depth in modern software architecture, Java engineering and performance optimisation, with a working understanding of C++ and Linux environments.
• Experience leading large-scale technology transformation, modernising legacy platforms and improving engineering practices while sustaining live services.
• Experience partnering with Product to shape roadmaps, evaluate options, prioritise investment and deliver customer and business outcomes.
• Experience establishing modern SDLC, automated testing, CI/CD, secure engineering, observability and operational readiness practices.
• Practical experience applying AI-assisted engineering, reusable skills or agents across requirements, development and testing.
• Experience using engineering and operational measures to improve delivery, quality and service reliability.
• Knowledge of FX Spot, Swaps or NDF, matching engines, FIX or comparable electronic trading platforms.
• Ability to communicate clearly, influence senior stakeholders and lead teams through ambiguity and change.

WHY JOIN US:
You will lead a product area at the heart of global financial markets and help shape the next generation of FX trading technology. You will have the opportunity to develop people, influence product and technical direction, and improve how software is designed, built, tested and operated.

We believe different perspectives strengthen our decisions and help us innovate. You will join an environment that values collaboration, learning, responsible experimentation and meaningful engineering outcomes.

ROLE SUMMARY:

This is a highly technical and critical role which is accountable for defining, directing and execution of LSEG’s Sustainability Reporting and Accounting Strategy, to ensure compliance with all existing and future regulatory requirements and investor expectations. As the Director or Sustainability Reporting you will be LSEG’s most senior technical expert on this topic, as well as designing and leading the execution of LSEG’s Sustainability Reporting and Accounting Strategy.

You will be accountable for the design and delivery of complex, enterprise-wide regulatory change programmes related to new corporate reporting requirements that have a direct bearing on LSEG’s regulatory compliance, reputation with regulators, shareholders and the market more widely. 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING; 

• Define and lead the execution of LSEG’s sustainability reporting and accounting strategy. This involves being the recognised lead technical expert on sustainability reporting regulatory requirements, including emerging regulation including the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), country-specific adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Reporting Standards , UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (SRS) and all other existing applicable reporting requirements. Lead technical impact assessment and implementation programmes to meet all new sustainability reporting requirements. (see end notes) 
• Lead the multi-year, multi-stakeholder programme for delivery of key CSRD and UK SRS workstreams to ensure compliance with incoming regulation from FY27. This requires the introduction of substantial new capabilities, processes, controls and systems across the business. 
• Manage the design and implementation of new sustainability reporting technology solution (Workiva) and embed as new way of working from FY27, ensuring users across the Group have the appropriate skills, experience and training to use the system effectively. 
• Manage relationship with key vendors including the corporate reporting agency and technology partners. 
• Ensure effective and timely delivery of all in-year (half year to quarterly) and annual reporting processes, effective controls, document production with external design agency across annual report and accounts, and stand-alone reports and online content. 
• Define all basis of preparation and reporting for all LSEG sustainability disclosures, including the definition of appropriate calculation methodologies, model/estimate approaches, assumptions, judgements, uncertainties 
• Lead LSEG’s programme of work to gain limited assurance of LSEG’s sustainability disclosures, representing LSEG to the external auditor (Deloitte)

Role purpose
The Market Data Compliance Manager leads the delivery of the market data audit and compliance programme, ensuring that client and vendor use of LSEG venue and index data is assessed against applicable agreements, commercial policies and reporting obligations. The role provides leadership across audit planning, complex case management, client engagement, remediation, revenue recovery, governance and process improvement.
The role holder combines deep market data licensing knowledge with sound judgement, ensuring that findings are evidence-led, commercially consistent and capable of withstanding internal, client and legal review. The role also develops the audit team, strengthens stakeholder alignment and drives automation and data-led improvements across the audit lifecycle.

Key accountabilities
· Own the global audit plan and prioritisation process, setting a risk-based pipeline across end clients, vendors, datafeeds, applications and redistribution models.
· Lead and develop market data auditors and audit support colleagues through clear objectives, work allocation, coaching, quality review, regular progress tracking and timely escalation.
· Oversee complex on-site and remote compliance reviews covering display, datafeed, redistribution, delayed, end-of-day, derived, manipulated, non-display and automated usage.
· Ensure audit findings, reconciliations, calculations, draft reports, client correspondence and closure documentation are accurate, complete and supported by a clear evidence trail.
· Provide management direction on contractual interpretation, commercial policy, entitlement, reporting and licensing issues, engaging Legal, Policy, Finance, Sales, Account Management and Product teams where specialist input is required.
· Manage client challenges, negotiation strategy, settlement discussions and escalations, maintaining a fair, consistent and audit-defensible position while supporting constructive closure.
· Drive remediation of identified gaps, including corrected reporting, appropriate go-forward licensing, historical revenue recovery and closure of control weaknesses.
· Maintain visibility of the pipeline, case status, financial exposure, forecast revenue, overdue actions and key risks through dashboards, trackers and senior management reporting.
· Govern audit-related Salesforce records and related compliance reporting so that opportunities, status and ownership are reflected consistently.
· Lead continuous improvement and automation of audit planning, allocation, document management, workflow, templates, reminders, dashboards and audit analysis capabilities.
· Partner with reporting and platform teams on migration and system-change requirements, ensuring that audit controls, data access, reporting evidence and client obligations remain effective.
· Ensure Restricted Customer Information (RCI) is handled correctly in accordance with applicable information-barrier and access-control requirements, including the timely onboarding and offboarding of members of RCI Ringfenced Teams and appropriate review, evidence and escalation.
· Promote responsible use of AI and analytical tools to improve audit quality, reduce manual effort and strengthen decision-making, in line with organisational policy and information-handling requirements.

Leadership and stakeholder responsibilities
· Set clear expectations, priorities and quality standards for the audit team, balancing workload against case complexity, client responsiveness and business risk.
· Coach auditors on policy application, investigative methodology, data analysis, client communication, negotiation and report writing.
· Provide senior oversight for high-value, sensitive or disputed audits and act as an escalation point for clients and internal stakeholders.
· Build effective relationships with senior stakeholders and communicate complex compliance matters clearly through concise written updates, presentations and decision papers.
· Create a collaborative culture that encourages challenge, knowledge sharing, continuous learning and consistent application of policy.

Decision-making and controls
· Approve audit scope, material findings, evidence requirements, calculation methodology, remediation approach and readiness for client issue or closure.
· Determine when a matter requires policy clarification, legal review, commercial approval, additional evidence or senior escalation.
· Ensure concessions, reduced settlement fees and closure decisions are appropriately authorised and documented.
· Protect the integrity and confidentiality of client, contractual and ring-fenced information throughout the audit lifecycle.
· Monitor adherence to agreed standards, service levels, record-keeping requirements and control obligations.

Measures of success
· Risk-based audit plan delivered with transparent allocation, active pipeline management and timely completion.
· High-quality, evidence-led audit outputs with clear contractual and policy rationale.
· Identified non-compliance is remediated through accurate reporting, appropriate licensing and historical recovery where applicable.
· Complex client matters are progressed with disciplined follow-up, proportionate escalation and documented decisions.
· Reliable management information covering delivery, exposure, revenue, ageing, risks and actions.
· Measurable reduction in manual activity through workflow, dashboard, automation and AI-enabled improvements.
· Capable, engaged team with strong market data knowledge, analytical rigour and consistent client communication.

Candidate profile
· Significant experience in market data compliance, audit, licensing, reporting, commercial policy, vendor management or a closely related financial services discipline.
· Deep understanding of how market data is sourced, entitled, consumed, displayed, redistributed, stored and used within buy-side, sell-side, trading, technology and vendor environments.
· Strong knowledge of exchange and index data licensing, including display and non-display use, datafeeds, redistribution, automated applications, derived or manipulated data, delayed data and end-of-day use cases.
· Demonstrated experience leading people and delivering a portfolio of complex audits, investigations, compliance reviews or commercial remediation cases.
· Ability to interpret agreements and policy, test client assertions against evidence, identify inconsistencies and reach balanced, defensible conclusions.
· Experience of working with Legal, Finance, Sales, Product, Account Management, Reporting and Technology stakeholders.
· Advanced analytical capability, including data manipulation, reconciliation and confident use of Microsoft Excel and Word; experience with BI, workflow or automation tools is beneficial.

• Work with Fogsphere’s API-driven platform for automation and reporting.
• Configure publish/subscribe messaging patterns (e.g. MQTT, Kafka, or similar technologies).

4) Customer & Partner Enablement
• Support customer and partner deployments across EMEA.
• Participate in technical onboarding, training sessions, and workshops.
• Provide clear, empathetic technical support to customers with varying levels of technical maturity.
• Contribute to technical documentation and deployment guides.

Required Skills & Experience

• 4+ years of experience in Linux systems administration and DevOps.
• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production environments.
• Strong understanding of containers and container orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes).
• Working knowledge of JavaScript for scripting, automation, or integrations.
• Experience working with REST APIs and external systems.
• Basic understanding of distributed systems and cloud infrastructure.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
• A customer-focused mindset with patience and empathy when supporting users.

Nice to Have

• Experience with Azure AKS or other managed Kubernetes services.
• Exposure to computer vision or AI-based workflows.
• Familiarity with MQTT, Kafka, or event-driven architectures.
• Experience with edge computing, IoT platforms, or sensors.
• Knowledge of LoRaWAN networks and devices.
• Additional languages such as Italian, Spanish, or Arabic.
• Proven experience in customer-facing delivery or partner enablement roles 

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
• 3+ years in Linux, DevOps, and distributed infrastructure deployment.
• 3+ years of production Kubernetes experience.

Why Join Fogsphere

You’ll be at the forefront of AI, computer vision, and IoT innovation, working with global partners and leading enterprises in oil & gas, energy, manufacturing, smart cities, transportation & logistics, and retail. This role combines deep technical challenges with the opportunity to make a real impact by training and supporting partners in deploying AI to transform safety, security, and operations across EMEA.

Selection Process

After submitting your application, you will be contacted by our HR team to schedule an initial interview, subject to a positive CV screening.
The first interview will focus on getting to know you, your background, and your career path, and will include a small number of light technical questions.
If the outcome is positive, you will be invited to one or two technical interview rounds (depending on both your availability and the team’s schedule), aimed at assessing your technical skills and problem-solving approach.
Following a successful technical evaluation, you will have a final conversation with members of the management team. At that stage, you will be ready to move forward and start your journey with Fogsphere.

This helps organizations across industries—from manufacturing, construction, oil & gas, and healthcare to smart cities—reduce workplace accidents by up to 90%, ensure regulatory compliance (EHS), and gain powerful operational insights. Description
As a QA Engineer, you will design, automate, and execute tests that ensure the reliability, security, and performance of Fogsphere’s AI platform. You’ll work hands‑on across UI, API, integration, and security testing, collaborating closely with Engineering, Product, and DevOps to embed quality throughout the development lifecycle. This role reports to the QA Lead Engineer.
Responsibilities
• Implement, maintain, and optimize automated tests across UI, API/backend, integration, and regression suites.
• Contribute to robust testing pipelines in CI/CD (Azure DevOps), including gating policies and quality metrics.
• Apply Test‑Driven Development (TDD) and Behavior‑Driven Development (BDD) practices using Behave and related frameworks.
• Execute and manage test plans and test cases in Atlassian X‑Ray or TestQube testing platforms, with clear traceability to requirements and defects.
• Build scalable GUI test automation with Playwright and/or Selenium; stabilize flaky tests and improve runtime.
• Collaborate with engineers to reproduce, triage, and root‑cause defects; champion preventive fixes.
• Integrate and monitor security checks in the pipeline (static analysis, dependency scanning, basic runtime checks).
• Contribute to test data management and maintain test environments aligned with microservices and Kubernetes deployments.
• Track and report quality signals (coverage, pass/fail trends, defect leakage) to the QA Lead and stakeholders.
• Document test strategies, fixtures, and utilities; share knowledge through reviews and pairing.

• Software Development: 3+ years in software testing/engineering; solid Python proficiency (tests are Python‑based).
• Quality Assurance: 1+ years hands‑on QA for enterprise or high‑availability platforms; practical use of TDD/BDD.

• • Behave for BDD (or equivalent).

• Atlassian X‑Ray (1+ years) for test management and traceability.
• Azure DevOps pipelines and ecosystem for CI/CD.

• Familiarity with compliance frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2).
• Exposure to container ecosystems, IoT, or AI‑enabled tooling.

• Competitive salary: £35,000, gross per year.
• Bespoke benefits, negotiated per candidate profile.
• Opportunity to shape QA strategy in a fast‑scaling, tech‑centric startup.

• Professional growth: training, conferences, certifications, and career progression.
• A collaborative, inclusive environment with a high innovation pulse.

job_title: Senior Financial Reporting and General Ledger Accountant
job_description:
About the job
Fold makes it easy to earn, buy, sell, and live off of Bitcoin. Fold takes established consumer financial products and optimizes them for a Bitcoin future. Fold also offers an FDIC-insured checking account, a Bitcoin exchange and wallet, thousands of merchant offers, and more.In 2020, we partnered with Visa to launch the first-ever bitcoin-rewards debit card. We've since launched our bitcoin-rewards credit card, and we continue to launch new products at regular intervals. In February 2025, Fold became the first publicly listed bitcoin financial services company. We're growing quickly with a passionate and loyal community.
Location: Remote, USA
Reports to: Accounting Manager
Department: Finance & Accounting
As our Senior Financial Reporting and General Ledger Accountant, you'll be a hands-on contributor to Fold's financial reporting program and day-to-day accounting operations, helping keep our books accurate and audit-ready as we grow as a public company.On a quarterly basis, you will assist in the preparation of the Company's Quarterly and Annual Reports on Forms 10-Q and 10-K, respectively, and work in DFIN to develop our financial statements, footnotes, and disclosures. Company profile

Role profile:

The Senior Network Engineer is responsible for the technical design, implementation, configuration, optimisation and ongoing support of secure enterprise networking solutions across customer environments.

The role combines Professional Services project delivery with Tier 3 technical escalation, providing advanced technical expertise across LAN, WLAN, SD-WAN, network security, SASE, data centre and cloud networking technologies.

The engineer will work closely with Technical Design, Project Management, Service Operations, Security and customer technical teams to translate approved designs and Low-Level Designs (LLDs) into secure, supportable and production-ready solutions.

A key part of the position is providing subject matter expertise for complex incidents and escalations, including root cause analysis, vendor engagement and the identification of long-term technical improvements.

The role will have a strong focus on Cisco and Meraki secure networking technologies, while requiring an understanding of wider enterprise networking and security principles.

The position is primarily remote, with UK-wide travel required for customer workshops, implementation activities, site surveys, migrations, technical whiteboard sessions and vendor training.

Key Responsibilities:

• Deliver customer-facing network and security projects from approved technical designs and Statements of Work.

• Review High-Level Designs (HLDs), Low-Level Designs (LLDs) and implementation documentation prior to deployment.

• Configure, deploy and migrate enterprise network and security infrastructure.

• Participate in customer workshops, technical discovery sessions and implementation planning.

• Produce implementation plans, Methods of Procedure (MOPs), change documentation and rollback plans.

• Undertake pre-deployment validation and identify technical risks, dependencies and prerequisites.

• Execute customer changes within agreed change-control processes and maintenance windows.

• Support transition of completed Professional Services projects into BAU and managed service operations.

• Act as a senior technical escalation point for complex networking and security incidents.

• Provide advanced troubleshooting for issues that cannot be resolved by first- and second-line operational teams.

• Troubleshoot complex LAN, WLAN, WAN, SD-WAN and security problems across multi-vendor customer environments.

• Identify recurring incidents and recommend permanent fixes, architectural improvements or automation opportunities.

• Capture technical knowledge from complex escalations and feed this into internal documentation and operational teams.

Technical Profile

The Senior Network Engineer is expected to have experience of the following technologies:

• Cisco Enterprise

• Excellent routing and switching experience

• Catalyst switching including 9000 series

• Cisco Nexus series

• Cisco Wireless

• Cisco ISR

• Cisco Secure Firewall FTD

• Cisco Secure Network Analytics

• DNA Center, ISE, ACI, SD-Access

• Secure access and Secure connect

• Cisco Secure Access, Umbrella, Duo, Cisco Secure Endpoint.

• Meraki

• MX series (Security & SD-WAN), MS series (Switching), MR (Wireless)

• Meraki Dashboard

• Meraki Adaptive Policy and integration with ISE.

• Meraki cloud APIs for automation and reporting.

• General

• Micro and macro segmentation best practice

• Use of zoning and VRFs

• Zero Trust Network Access

• SD-WAN application band steering policy and management

Technical capabilities

Fournet will provide continual development and training, both within the direct vendor domain and across supplementary disciples and frameworks. The following technical capabilities are highly desired:

• Cisco Certified Network Professional; Enterprise (CCNP) (Required)

• Cisco Meraki Solutions Specialist (Required)

• Cisco Certified Network Professional; Security (CCNP) (Desired)

• Cisco Certified Specialist Enterprise Design (Desired)

Our Values and Behaviours

- Strong understanding of APIs, system integrations and software development lifecycles.
- Experience managing third-party software integrations and external technology partnerships.
- Ability to translate business requirements into clear technical specifications.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
- Commercially aware with the ability to balance customer needs, technical feasibility and business priorities.
- Experience working within agile delivery environments.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.

- Experience working with EPOS, ticketing and eCommerce applications.
- Familiarity with payment gateways, acquiring services and merchant services.
- Experience working with SaaS products and cloud-based platforms.

- Background in fintech or payment processing environments.

Product & Integration Management

- Work closely with engineering and technical teams to deliver robust, scalable and secure payment integrations.
- Ensure integrations align with business objectives, customer needs and operational requirements.
- Collaborate with payment gateways, POS providers, ticketing systems and digital platforms to create seamless customer experiences.
- Monitor integration performance, identify optimisation opportunities and drive continuous improvement.

Stakeholder & Partner Management

job_title: Paralegal (Agricultural Real Estate Team - Non-qualifying Role) - Oxford
job_description:
Role Overview
We are seeking a diligent and organised Paralegal to support our agricultural property/real estate team. The successful candidate will play a key role in legal drafting, client liaison, title investigation and lease review, under the supervision of a solicitor or other supervising fee earner. This role would suit someone with strong analytical and organisational skills who can work independently within agreed limits while managing multiple deadlines.

N.B. This is a non-qualifying role, not a trainee solicitor position or an offer of a training contract. Administrative and post-completion work are excluded, including Land Registry applications and requisitions, file administration and billing. These tasks are allocated elsewhere.

Key Responsibilities
• Review leases and prepare draft lease summaries, transaction documents and substantive correspondence using approved precedents, for review by a supervising fee earner
• Liaise directly with clients to gather information, provide updates, and respond to queries in a professional and timely manner
• Obtain and review title information and property search results, identify legal issues and draft enquiries and title summaries for review by a supervising fee earner
• Monitor substantive pre-completion legal deadlines and outstanding legal issues on allocated matters, and escalate concerns promptly to the supervising fee earner; routine diary administration is excluded
• Support fee earners with legal research, due diligence and the preparation of draft legal reports and advice for retail clients, within delegated authority and subject to supervising fee earner review
• Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and procedural requirements throughout all tasks
• Assist with pre-completion legal readiness by checking the consistency and completeness of draft transaction documents and identifying outstanding legal requirements, without undertaking administrative completion arrangements or post-completion tasks

Skills and Experience Required
• Ideally, proven experience in a paralegal or legal support role, ideally within property/real estate law
• Practical understanding of commercial leases and legal drafting; specific job training will be provided
• Ability to analyse legal documents, identify material issues and produce clear, accurate first drafts and summaries under supervision.
• Ability to review title information and property search results and undertake focused legal research, with appropriate training and supervision.
• Strong organisational skills in managing substantive legal work and maintaining clear records of legal analysis and client instructions.
• Good legal research, analytical and organisational skills
• Strong time management skills with the ability to prioritise a varied workload
• High level of accuracy and attention to detail
• Confidence working with numerical provisions in leases, including rent and service charge figures, and identifying points requiring specialist input.
• Ability to use initiative and progress allocated legal tasks within agreed parameters, recognising when to seek guidance or escalate an issue.
• Confident and professional communication skills, both written and verbal, for liaising with clients and internal teams

Desirable
• Previous paralegal experience in commercial real estate.
• Experience of agricultural property transactions and lease review
• Prior experience working with both external clients and in-house legal teams
• Experience of IT systems, document management software, and dataroom platforms

Personal Attributes
• Self-motivated with a proactive approach to problem-solving
• Reliable and trustworthy when handling confidential client information
• Team player who can also work effectively without close supervision
• Calm and methodical under pressure, particularly when managing competing deadlines

The role

We are looking for an experienced Data Engineer to join our IT team and play a key role in the development of our firmwide data capability.

This is a newly created position and our first dedicated Data Engineering hire, joining at an important stage in the development of Gateley’s wider data strategy. We are building the foundations that will allow us to bring together data that currently sits across different systems and areas of the business, improve its quality and governance, and make it easier to use for insight, reporting, analytics and emerging AI capabilities.

You will have the opportunity to get involved at the ground level of that journey. Working predominantly within Microsoft Fabric, you will help us unlock data from existing sources, bring it into our developing data platform and engineer the pipelines and structures needed to cleanse, consolidate and transform it into trusted, reusable data products. A key part of this will be helping us develop reliable "golden records" and stronger master data practices, providing a trusted foundation for dashboards, analytics and future AI-enabled use cases.  

The scope is deliberately broad. You will combine hands-on engineering with problem solving, technical advisory work and stakeholder engagement, working across IT, Change and different business areas to understand their data, identify priorities and turn requirements into practical solutions.

As the first Data Engineer in a growing capability, you will also have the opportunity to influence how we do things. You will help establish repeatable engineering patterns, standards and ways of working that can support the Data Programme as it develops.

Responsibilities:

- Design, build and maintain data pipelines using Microsoft Fabric, creating reliable ingestion and transformation processes that move data from source systems into governed, reusable data products.
- Develop our Fabric data architecture, creating scalable lakehouse, warehouse and medallion-style structures in line with agreed architecture, governance and security standards.
- Onboard and integrate data from across the business, working with structured and semi-structured information held within core business applications, SaaS platforms, databases, files and approved APIs.
- Build appropriate batch and near-real-time integrations, selecting the right engineering approach based on the underlying business requirement rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach.
- Help unlock and consolidate data that currently sits across different systems and areas of Gateley, cleansing, transforming and structuring it so that it can be used more effectively for reporting, analytics, decision-making and future AI use cases.
- Ensure production data services are reliable and supportable, implementing appropriate monitoring, logging, exception handling, data lineage and operational support.
- Work directly with application owners, suppliers and internal stakeholders to identify and resolve issues relating to source data, connectivity, schemas, data quality and performance.
- Support the development of master and reference data capabilities, including data matching, entity resolution, identifiers, survivorship and golden-record processes, helping Gateley establish more trusted and consistent information across the organisation.
- Turn data governance and stewardship requirements into practical engineering solutions, including validation rules, quality controls, remediation processes and appropriate workflows.
- Create clear technical and operational documentation, including data definitions, mappings and lineage, ensuring the solutions you develop can be understood and supported by data stewards, technical teams and business stakeholders.
- Provide technical guidance on analytics and Power BI, advising on semantic models, measures, dashboard structure, visual selection, accessibility and performance.
- Help establish consistent definitions and trusted sources of data, ensuring Power BI outputs and other reporting products make use of governed data products rather than recreating business rules and logic locally.
- Challenge requirements constructively, working with stakeholders to understand the problem they are trying to solve and identifying whether a dashboard, metric, alert, workflow or another data product offers the most effective solution.
- Support the development of Fabric agents and AI-enabled data experiences, helping establish the data products, grounding approaches, permissions and access controls required to use these technologies responsibly.
- Assess whether data is ready for AI and agent-based use cases, considering data quality, metadata, access permissions, semantic consistency, governance and traceability before solutions are progressed.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues responsible for AI and data governance, ensuring experimentation remains controlled, transparent and aligned with Gateley’s wider governance and security requirements.
- Apply strong engineering and DevOps practices, including source control, peer review, automated testing, deployment pipelines and appropriate separation of development, test and production environments.
- Work closely with technical and non-technical stakeholders across Gateley, translating complex engineering concepts into straightforward language and helping colleagues understand how data can address their business challenges.
- Take ownership of data engineering solutions from requirement through to delivery, balancing pace with data quality, security, reliability, scalability and long-term maintainability.
- Help establish the standards and ways of working for Gateley’s developing data capability, contributing reusable engineering patterns, templates and best practice that can be adopted as the Data Programme grows. As the first dedicated Data Engineer hire, the successful person will have the opportunity to influence how this capability develops rather than simply inheriting an established engineering model.

The team

Gateley have a dynamic and collaborative IT team, bringing together specialists across IT Service, Infrastructure, Architecture, Security, Change Management, Technology Innovation & Delivery and other technology disciplines.

Our team works across the business to deliver secure, practical and forward-thinking technology solutions that support how our people work today, while helping Gateley prepare for the future.

As our data capability continues to develop, this role will work closely with colleagues across IT and the wider business, providing the opportunity to collaborate with a broad range of technical and non-technical stakeholders.

The person

We are looking for a hands-on Data Engineer who combines strong technical capability with a pragmatic and curious approach to problem solving.

You will be comfortable taking a requirement from initial conversation through to a working technical solution, taking ownership of delivery along the way. You will understand that effective data engineering goes beyond moving data between systems, with a strong focus on data quality, governance, security, scalability and maintainability, as well as how the end product will ultimately be used.

As our data capability continues to develop, you will be comfortable working in an evolving environment and helping to establish effective engineering practices, standards and ways of working. You will enjoy the opportunity to help shape a growing capability rather than stepping into something that is already fully established.

Strong communication skills will be equally important. You will work with both technical and non-technical stakeholders across the business, so you will need to be able to translate complex data and engineering concepts into clear, straightforward language and build effective relationships with people at all levels.

We are open-minded about sector background. You do not need previous legal-sector experience, although experience gained within a corporate, professional services or similarly complex environment would be beneficial.

Essential:

- Strong, hands-on data engineering experience, including building and operating production-grade data pipelines, transformations and curated data products.
- Practical experience with Microsoft Fabric or closely related Microsoft Azure data services, with the ability to quickly become productive across Fabric workloads.
- Strong SQL skills and practical experience with at least one engineering language, typically Python or PySpark.
- Experience integrating data from a range of sources, including enterprise applications, APIs, databases and file-based sources.
- A good understanding of lakehouse, warehouse and dimensional modelling patterns, alongside semantic models and data quality controls.
- Experience applying effective DataOps and DevOps practices, including Git/source control, automated testing, deployment pipelines and environment management.
- Experience designing and delivering data solutions with quality, reliability, security, scalability and maintainability in mind.
- The ability to work with data owners and business stakeholders to translate governance and stewardship requirements into practical engineering controls.
- Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to take ownership of technical challenges from initial requirement through to delivery.
- Excellent stakeholder communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and confidently to non-technical audiences.
- A collaborative approach and the confidence to work across multiple teams and business areas, building effective relationships with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Desirable:

It would be advantageous if you have:

- Hands-on experience with Microsoft Fabric, including Data Factory, notebooks, lakehouses, warehouses, Real-Time Intelligence or Fabric agents.
- Experience implementing master data management, entity resolution, reference data or golden-record capabilities.
- Power BI experience, including semantic modelling, DAX, dashboard performance and effective data visualisation.
- Knowledge of Microsoft Purview, including data lineage, metadata, sensitivity classification and data access controls.
- Experience working with established data governance, stewardship or data ownership frameworks.
- Exposure to AI-enabled data products or agents, particularly where data quality, permissions, grounding, traceability and governance are important.
- Experience working within a corporate, professional services, financial services or other information-intensive or regulated environment.
- A relevant Microsoft certification, such as Fabric Data Engineer Associate, or equivalent demonstrable technical expertise.

As a Senior Product Owner, you'll own the product side of two or three client projects at once. The Project Manager looks after delivery, timescales and commercials, so your focus is the product itself. 

You'll sit with the client, work out what they actually need rather than what they've asked for, and shape it into work the team can build. You're involved from the first discovery workshop through to release and beyond, and you're the client's main contact on product.

- Helping grow our product practice, sharing approaches and supporting less experienced POs

- You're happy moving across different clients and domains rather than settling into one product

About GiveDirectly 

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

• Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.

• Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.

• Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

• Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.

• Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.

• Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.

• Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.

• Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

Reports to: Head of People

Level: Director

About this role

We are currently planning for a significant increase in scale, and we are building the People function that can carry it.

This is our first senior talent management role. Today we have pieces of talent management programs and processes in place, but not yet a function. You will build one: an intentional approach to how we onboard, develop, and retain our people. That covers performance management and its link to pay, manager and leadership development, learning, onboarding, talent planning and succession, employee listening and engagement, and culture and values.

The first year is weighted toward four priorities: joining the redesign of our performance system early, alongside the Head of People, and owning it as it moves into execution, as we move to pay for performance, revamping onboarding ahead of our next wave of hiring, planning our values retreat for senior leaders, and getting a read on employee listening and engagement. As those take shape, the balance shifts toward the longer-term build: the vision and roadmap for the function, a foundational manager program, talent planning and succession, and the team around you.

The reason for this weight: the performance system and onboarding are our most acute gaps today, but they should not be construed as a ceiling of the job. We are hiring a senior talent management leader who can shape the whole function over several years, not the owner of one or two programs. If your instinct on reading this is that the performance redesign is the whole job, this role probably isn’t the right fit, and the reverse is also true: if you want to set strategy but not build the first versions yourself, year one will frustrate you.

Build the talent management function

• Set the vision and multi-year roadmap for talent management across the areas it covers, and sequence the work against the People roadmap.

• Propose the team around it, and decide what we build in-house and what we buy or borrow.

• Connect talent management to workforce planning, compensation, and recruitment, in partnership with the Head of People, Finance, and function leaders.

• Build an approach to talent and succession planning, starting with critical roles: work with leaders to identify succession gaps, assess potential successors, and put development plans in place to prepare people for future opportunities.

Own the performance system

• Join the performance system redesign early, alongside the Head of People, and own it as it moves into execution: a system that produces reliable, calibrated outputs to inform merit increases, connected to our new salary bands.

• Make the system worth using, not a check-the-box exercise: one that helps managers hold better performance and development conversations and gives employees clarity on expectations, feedback, and growth.

• Build calibration and the data around it so ratings and merit decisions stay consistent and fair across countries, currencies, and manager quality.

• Set a clear global standard for handling low performance that doesn’t default to a misconduct process, and equip managers to use it.

• Ensure the performance system helps managers identify and support sustained high performance, connecting it to recognition, development, and career growth opportunities.

• Iterate the system through multiple cycles, using calibration, outcome data, and feedback from managers and employees to improve it.

Build how people join, learn, and are led

• Revamp onboarding ahead of our next wave of hiring: own the content and experience for new hires and their managers, working with People Ops on process and systems.

About GiveDirectly 

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. - Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R

- Analytical thinking and problem-solving mindset
- Strong attention to detail and data accuracy

 2. Our goal is to maximize intelligence per joule. We work across model behavior, software, systems, and silicon to find better ways to run models.

 3. We start by thinking about the model as a mathematical function, and map that out onto hardware and then build software on top of that which is custom to each model. This maximises performance and removes wasted abstractions.

 4. We are early. You will help set the technical direction and the way the company works.


WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

 1. We are building an inference research team to find where current hardware and software waste time, memory, and energy when serving open-weight models.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 3. Change runtimes, schedulers, distributed execution, and serving paths when they limit the system.

 4. Test latency, throughput, energy use, model quality, correctness, and reliability on real workloads.

 5. Turn research results into production services.

 6. Share research publicly so that others can learn about how inference research is done.

 7. Work with the silicon team to identify hardware bottlenecks and design opportunities.


PROBLEMS YOU MAY WORK ON

 1. Kernels and fused execution paths for exact model shapes.

HR & People Trustee

 HR & People Trustee

Purpose of the HR & People Trustee role

Alongside the responsibilities held by all Greener & Cleaner Trustees, the HR & People Trustee will provide specialist expertise, oversight and practical support on employment, people management and organisational culture.

Greener & Cleaner is a relatively small charity with a committed and diverse team. We employ a significant number of part-time staff and seek to create an inclusive and supportive workplace, including for colleagues managing disabilities, long-term health conditions and caring responsibilities. This can create people-management situations that require thoughtful, flexible and sometimes complex approaches alongside sound employment practice.

A particularly important part of this role is therefore to be a trusted advisor and confidential sounding board to the CEO, a second brain to help navigate complex or sensitive people issues, while maintaining the appropriate distinction between Trustee oversight and the CEO’s responsibility for day-to-day management.

Duties of all Trustees

• Contribute to setting the charity’s strategic goals and monitoring performance through active participation in Board discussions and decision-making.

• Help ensure that Greener & Cleaner complies with its governing document, charity law and other relevant legal and regulatory requirements.

• Demonstrate a commitment to Greener & Cleaner’s charitable objectives, values and activities.

• Help identify strategic and organisational risks and ensure appropriate controls and mitigations are in place.

• Help the Board make sound decisions by contributing personal knowledge, professional experience and independent judgement.

• Support the Chair in the appointment and appraisal of senior leadership as appropriate.

• Make all reasonable efforts to attend Board meetings, away-days, development meetings and other key events as requested.

• Where possible, help the charity build useful connections, partnerships and opportunities that support its goals and financial sustainability.

• Ensure that equality, diversity, inclusion and accessibility remain central to the charity’s strategy, governance and delivery.

Specialist HR & People responsibilities

• CEO advice and support. Provide practical HR advice and support to the CEO, particularly where employee situations are complex, sensitive or higher risk.

• Trusted sounding board. Act as a confidential sounding board for the CEO, helping them think through options, risks, proportionality and appropriate approaches to people-management issues.

• Complex needs and adjustments. Talk through matters involving disability, long-term health conditions, reasonable adjustments, flexible working, caring responsibilities, attendance and capability, balancing individual needs with the charity’s operational requirements and responsibilities.

• Employee relations. Provide guidance, where required, on performance management, grievances, disciplinary matters, absence management, workplace conflict, difficult conversations and other employee-relations issues.

• Escalation and external advice. Help the CEO identify when an issue can appropriately be managed internally and if external specialist HR, occupational health or employment-law advice should be sought.

• Workforce strategy. Support the Board and CEO on organisational structure, workforce planning, recruitment, induction, retention, succession and staff development as the charity evolves.

• Reward and remuneration. Advise the Board and CEO on fair and proportionate approaches to staff remuneration, benefits and reward, supporting the charity’s ability to attract and retain employees within its financial resources.

• Policies and compliance. Provide oversight and advice on employment contracts, the staff handbook and HR policies and procedures, helping ensure they remain proportionate, practical and compliant with current UK employment law and good practice.

• People-related risks and reporting. Ensure the Board maintains appropriate oversight of people-related risks, including staff turnover, key-person dependencies and employment disputes, and receives relevant reporting to support informed decision-making.

• Organisational development and change. Advise the CEO and Board on organisational development and significant organisational change, including restructuring, changes to staffing arrangements and the people-related implications of organisational growth or change.

• Culture and wellbeing. Support the development of a positive organisational culture that promotes wellbeing, inclusion, fairness, good management, accountability and sustainable ways of working.

• Equality, diversity and inclusion. Champion inclusive employment and volunteering practices and help the charity consider the needs of a diverse workforce in its people decisions.

• CEO employment matters. Support the Chair and Board, as appropriate, in relation to CEO objectives, appraisal, remuneration, development and succession planning.

• Safeguarding and duty of care. Provide oversight and advice on people-related safeguarding arrangements, helping ensure that appropriate policies, procedures and practices are in place to protect staff and volunteers.

• Volunteers. Provide strategic advice on the charity’s approach to volunteers where this overlaps with people management, organisational culture, safeguarding or organisational risk

What this role is – and is not

This is a Trustee role with a specialist advisory component. We are looking for someone who is willing to make their HR expertise genuinely accessible to the CEO rather than limiting their contribution to periodic policy or compliance review.

The HR & People Trustee will not become the charity’s operational HR manager, line-manage staff on behalf of the CEO, or take management decisions that properly sit with employed leadership. Instead, they will help the CEO and Board reach sound, fair and well-informed decisions, and provide additional expertise and challenge where people issues are difficult or carry material risk.

Person specification

Essential experience and knowledge

• Significant professional experience in HR/People management, ideally at senior HR Business Partner, Head of HR/People, People Director or equivalent level.

• Strong and current knowledge of UK employment law and good employment practice.

• Hands-on employee-relations experience, including advising managers or senior leaders through complex individual cases.

• Experience of supporting employees with disabilities and/or long-term health conditions, including reasonable adjustments, alongside flexible working and caring responsibilities.

• Experience of performance, capability, absence, grievance, disciplinary and conflict-management processes.

• Ability to give practical and proportionate advice in a small organisation where there may not be a dedicated internal HR function or extensive management infrastructure.

• Confidence in advising and constructively challenging a CEO while respecting the distinction between governance, specialist advice and executive decision-making.

• Excellent judgement and the ability to handle highly sensitive and confidential information appropriately.

• Ability to combine empathy and flexibility with clarity, fairness, accountability and the operational needs of the organisation.

• Ability to translate HR legislation and good practice into straightforward, workable advice for non-HR colleagues and Trustees.

Desirable experience

• CIPD qualification or equivalent professional experience.

• Experience within a charity, voluntary-sector organisation, SME or similarly resource-constrained organisation.

• Experience of organisations employing significant numbers of part-time, flexible or non-standard-hours workers.

• Experience of volunteer management or organisations with blended staff and volunteer teams.

• Experience of organisational development, culture change, management development or workforce planning.

The Trustee role

The primary role of every Trustee is, together with the other Trustees, to accept ultimate responsibility for the affairs of Greener & Cleaner and to ensure that the charity is solvent, well run and delivering the charitable outcomes for which it has been established.

Trustees contribute to the charity’s strategy, governance, growth and sustainability, bringing their individual knowledge, experience and judgement to Board discussions and decisions.

Attributes expected of all Trustees

• A strong commitment to Greener & Cleaner’s objectives and activities.

• A willingness to devote the necessary time and effort to the role.

• Strategic vision, the ability to think creatively and an appropriate level of financial literacy.

• Understanding and acceptance of the legal duties, responsibilities and liabilities of trusteeship.

• Good independent judgement and willingness to challenge constructively.

• Ability to work effectively as part of a team and support collective Board decision-making.

• Commitment to the Nolan Principles of selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability, openness, honesty and leadership.

• Respect for the delegated authority of employees and willingness to allow staff to make reasonable decisions within the limits set by the Board.

Time commitment and ways of working

Trustees are expected to make all reasonable efforts to attend scheduled Board meetings and relevant away-days or development sessions. Because of the specialist nature of this position, the HR & People Trustee will also need to be willing to provide occasional advice to the CEO between meetings when significant or time-sensitive people issues arise.

The frequency of this support will vary. The intention is not to create an operational HR role, but candidates should be comfortable with a role that involves meaningful engagement between Board meetings rather than Board attendance alone.

Tenure and conduct

• Trustees are normally expected to commit to at least one three-year term, subject to the charity’s governing document and Board arrangements.

• Trustees participate in periodic review or appraisal with the Chair to support effective contribution and development.

• Trustees are expected to undertake training appropriate to the charity’s activities and their responsibilities, including safeguarding where required.

• Trustees are expected to maintain appropriate confidentiality, declare conflicts of interest and act at all times in the best interests of the charity.

• Trustees who are persistently unable or unwilling to fulfil their duties may be subject to the processes set out in the charity’s governing document.

Our approach to inclusion

Greener & Cleaner is committed to equality, diversity, inclusion and accessibility. We value different perspectives and experiences and want our governance and workforce to reflect and understand the communities we work with. We welcome applications from people with a wide range of backgrounds and lived experiences.

If you would like an informal chat first about the role, please drop us a line at the same email address and we will arrange this. Also, if this method of application or recruitment does not work for you, please get in touch to discuss alternative options.

We look forward to hearing from you.

About the role

Can you be the friendly face of Greener and Cleaner? As we continue to grow, we’re looking for more volunteers to make people feel at ease and explain in simple terms how The Hub can help them make small changes in their lives to help fight climate change.

What will you be doing?

We’ve created a supportive, judgement free and engaging experience for visitors in our Hub where they can find out about climate change and what they can do about it. There is so much information out there that it’s really important to have a place people trust which can help them make informed decisions much more easily and less overwhelmingly.

Much of your time at The Hub will be spent chatting and pointing people in the right direction to get more information or support, helping make sure our events and workshops run smoothly, and there will be a chance to get involved in or lead other local projects should you wish.

No past experience or in-depth knowledge of sustainable living or community support is required. Job training and Carbon Literacy training is provided to all volunteers and there will be a host of other information you will have access to, such as the most common questions, concerns and materials that we and other sustainability groups have created. You will be supported by a network of people who share a passion for all things green.

A regular weekly 3-6 hour commitment would make a huge difference to The Hub, practical and cultural changes we are aiming to facilitate across south east London. If The Hub pilot is a success, it has the potential to be rolled out across the rest of the UK – and you will have been part of an amazing achievement!

Much like volunteering in a charity shop, animal sanctuary or church group etc, cover will be arranged fo

We’re a group of proactive and friendly locals sharing information and resources to reduce our environmental impact at home, at work and in our wider communities to fight the climate crisis.

We firmly believe we’re all in this together. Across the team we’re all at different stages of trying to be greener and cleaner, reducing our own carbon footprint and helping you to do the same.

We are looking for more friendly local people who are interested in supporting the work of Greener and Cleaner, working in The Hub and fighting the climate crisis together.
