About the Role
GSK’s Enterprise AI team translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across drug discovery, development, manufacturing, and commercial. Forward deployed engineers (FDEs) and full-stack engineers embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes.
We are hiring a Product Manager II, AI Product Manager to support our forward deployed teams working with GSK’s manufacturing sites. This is an individual contributor role for someone early- to mid-career who is hungry to do the analytical, hands-on, and stakeholder-facing work that makes AI engagements succeed: opportunity discovery, value sizing, scoping, hands-on prototyping, delivery, and ongoing measurement. You will be supported by senior team members, but the work — the briefs, the analyses, the value cases, the scoping docs, and getting things over the line — will be yours to drive.
This role is execution first. You will work directly with site teams in production, planning, quality, and training, and iterate with them on the data, the model outputs, and the workflow until the solution works on the floor. You are comfortable rolling up your sleeves: pulling and checking data, testing outputs, running user sessions, and closing the loop between the site and the engineers.

Why This Role Exists
Forward deployed teams are most powerful when paired with sharp opportunity selection and disciplined execution. This role closes that gap at this level by ensuring the engineers we deploy are working on the right things, and that what they build lands with the people at the site who will use it.
In this role you will be the person who:
• Drives opportunity discovery and value-case work on specific manufacturing engagements, supported by senior team members.
• Acts as a working partner to FDE pods on day-to-day scoping, delivery, and measurement.
• Works hands-on with site stakeholders, iterating on data, model outputs, and workflows until solutions are fit for use.
• Builds the analytical artefacts (briefs, value models, scoping docs, early prototypes) the team relies on.

Key Responsibilities
Opportunity Identification & Value Sizing
• Run opportunity discovery with site and business stakeholders — interviews, workflow walk-throughs, time on the production floor, light data analysis — to surface AI-shaped problems worth pursuing.
• Build first-cut value cases with clear assumptions, rough sizing, and a credible path to validation, using manufacturing metrics such as throughput, schedule adherence, right-first-time, labour productivity, and training cycle time.
• Document opportunities in a consistent, comparable format so they can be ranked and prioritized.
Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping
• Help senior team members prioritize by gathering the evidence, building the comparison views, and pressure-testing assumptions.
• Track the opportunity backlog and keep it tidy, current, and decision-ready.
Execution & Hands-On Delivery
• Own the execution of your assigned workstreams: plans, actions, dependencies, and follow-through, so engagements keep moving from prototype to production.
• Get hands-on when needed: pull, explore, and sanity-check site data; build quick analyses or low-code prototypes; test model outputs against what the site expects.
• Iterate with site stakeholders on data quality, model outputs, and user feedback. Run review and user-testing sessions, capture what is wrong or missing, and turn it into clear asks for the engineers.
• Support site rollout and adoption: user guides, training sessions, feedback loops, and tracking whether the solution is actually being used.
Engineering Partnership & Enablement
• Be a working partner to FDE pods. Sit close to the work, capture decisions, surface blockers, and turn them into clear asks for stakeholders.
• Maintain engagement scoping documents and keep them current as scope evolves.
• Take great notes that synthesize into great artefacts — scoping briefs, decision logs, value memos.
Stakeholder Alignment & Communication
• Run productive working-level meetings with site and business stakeholders, from operators and supervisors to site leads.
• Communicate clearly in writing — short, structured updates that respect stakeholders’ time.
Measurement, Learning & Iteration
• Track engagement outcomes against the value case and flag drift early.
• Capture lessons learned in a consistent format the team can search and reuse.

What You Bring
Required Experience
• 5+ years of experience in some combination of manufacturing, operations, strategy/consulting, product management, AI/ML product, or analytical roles in pharma, healthcare, or other regulated or technology-led organisations.
• An understanding of the manufacturing business — how production, planning, workforce, quality, and training work at a site — ideally gained through working at or closely with a manufacturing site.
• A track record of execution: getting projects delivered, not just planned, in a fast-moving, hands-on environment.
• Willingness and ability to get hands-on with data and tools (for example Excel, SQL, Python, or low-code tools) to explore data, check model outputs, and prototype quickly.
• Strong analytical and structured-thinking skills — you can take a fuzzy ask and produce a tight, well-reasoned brief.
• Comfortable technical fluency in modern AI/ML — enough to participate credibly in engineering scoping conversations and to explain model outputs to site users.
• Excellent written and verbal communication; you produce artefacts senior people will read and act on, and you can work just as well with operators on the floor.
• Automate daily tasks using skills, plugins, and markdown.
• High agency: you take work to a finished state without needing to be chased.

How You Operate
• You think in terms of value, not activity.
• You are execution focused: you get things done and close the loop.
• You roll up your sleeves when needed, and you go to the site to see the work for yourself.
• You convert ambiguity into clarity engineers can act on.
• You bias toward small, sharp documents and decisions over slideware and process.
• You hold strong views, loosely held, and welcome being proven wrong by data.
• You take the long view on patient impact while caring deeply about shipping things this quarter.

Skills Profile
The following skills define what strong performance looks like in this role across seven domains. Each descriptor reflects the scope, autonomy, and impact expected at this level.

AI Opportunity Identification

AI Product & Engagement Strategy

Measurement, Learning & Iteration

The CSO PMO is the governance and portfolio management authority for the Cyber Security Office project portfolio. • Govern portfolio intake, prioritisation, sequencing and roadmap integration so that investment and resource decisions align with CSO strategy, risk priorities and available capacity. 
• Set expectations for project planning and control across scope, milestones, dependencies, resources, financials, risks, issues, change, quality, benefits and closure.

• Own the integrated CSO delivery plan and executive governance reporting, providing a single, reliable view of progress, forecast, capacity, dependencies, risk and benefits. 
• Advance automation of PMO workflows, controls, data collection, reporting and management insight to improve accuracy, timeliness and scalability. 
• Drive simplification and process improvement, removing unnecessary bureaucracy while retaining proportionate controls appropriate to cyber security and a regulated environment. 
• Define portfolio data standards and performance measures, strengthen data quality and use analysis and visualisation to enable evidence-based governance decisions. 
• Lead, coach and develop PMO governance capability, ensuring practitioners and delivery resources understand and consistently apply the CSO Delivery Framework. 
• Build trusted relationships with CSO leaders, finance, risk, quality, technology and delivery partners, resolving cross-portfolio issues and improving interfaces across organisational boundaries. 

Why you?

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience. 
• Substantial experience leading portfolio, programme or enterprise PMO governance in a complex global organisation. 
• Demonstrated ownership of a delivery framework, methodology or governance operating model, including standards, controls, assurance and adoption. 
• Strong portfolio and programme management acumen across prioritisation, integrated planning, financial management, resource and capacity planning, risk, dependency, change and benefits governance.

Working with business stakeholders, Product Managers, Solution Architects, Engineers and Product Analysts, you'll help ensure our products are intuitive, secure, compliant and supportable. We manufacture and supply reliable, high-quality medicines and vaccines to meet patients’ needs and drive our performance.
Our network of 37 medicines and vaccines manufacturing sites delivered 1.7 billion packs of medicines and 409 million vaccine doses in 2024 to help make a positive impact on the health of millions of people.

Working across Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, MSAT and Technical functions, the role coordinates day-to-day performance to achieve Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and People objectives, strengthen capacity and capability, and ensure reliable product supply.

The job holder deputises for the Value Stream Operations Manager when required, ensuring continuity of leadership, supporting governance and escalation, and translating value stream priorities into effective operational execution.

• Balance immediate delivery needs with compliance, reliability and long-term capability.

• Experience using performance data, governance routines and structured escalation to drive action.
• Capability to influence stakeholders, lead teams and coach others without relying solely on direct authority.
• Working knowledge/ experience of cGMP, quality systems, supply planning and production-system principles.

• Advanced qualification in, Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Manufacturing Leadership, or Operations Management.
• Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt or equivalent improvement experience.
• Experience in sterile or aseptic manufacturing is strongly preferred.
• Experience deputising for a senior operations leader or leading through delegated authority.

Opportunities to join Hakluyt
Our firm is growing, and we are currently seeking expressions of interest from well-qualified candidates for an editor and risk manager role in our Quality Control and Compliance (QCC) team, starting in London. 

 What we do
Hakluyt advises leaders of the world’s largest companies and investment firms on the opportunities and risks facing their businesses. Over the last 30 years, our clients have turned to us for the judgement and insight we provide on their most important and sensitive commercial issues. 
Our advice is delivered by our in-house team of experienced professionals, and informed by high-quality conversations held by well-connected individuals in our global network. Our connectivity is unique in its scale, reach and seniority, and allows us to access the thinking of relevant stakeholders without revealing our clients’ interests. Few other business models depend on human relationships as much as ours: this, above all, is what makes us different.
We hold ourselves to exacting ethical standards, and we take on work only once we are confident that we can provide value. We are discerning about whom we work for and with. This approach to doing business has helped us build a blue-chip client base that includes many of the world’s most prestigious companies, successful private equity and infrastructure funds, and reputable institutional investors. Our clients value our discretion and independence of thought. The range of issues we work on is extraordinary: M&A, shareholder activism, regulatory and policy issues, disputes, senior hires, sustainability, and more.
Requirements
The role
The QCC team plays a crucial role at the heart of Hakluyt. Our written and oral work for clients undergoes rigorous editing by QCC so that it meets our high standards. The team also ensures that the firm’s commercial and risk-management policies are applied to all the work we undertake – from decision-making over client acceptance and the drafting of proposals, through to final reporting and the provision of advice. In doing so, the QCC team works seamlessly with our general counsel and legal colleagues, ensuring we maintain the highest standards of ethics and compliance. 
As with the wider Hakluyt team, QCC is made up of people from a variety of professional backgrounds. There is no ‘one size fits all’ profile. However, we are looking for a candidate with strong commercial awareness, superb editing and writing skills, a sharp eye for detail and accuracy, excellent judgment, and an understanding of – and interest in – the management of risk. The successful candidate is likely to have an enquiring mind, confidence and clarity of expression, and a proven ability to work collegially in a fast-paced environment. Strong EQ is essential – the candidate will need to build trusted relationships with colleagues across all Hakluyt offices, working with client-facing teams to enable their business development and project delivery. 
Day to day, the successful candidate will review and edit client work; help colleagues identify and manage a range of risks; and provide practical guidance on developing client relationships and running projects. As they gain experience, they may also take on wider responsibilities alongside client-facing colleagues, including delivery of written and oral reporting and client management. They are likely to advise colleagues across the company on a range of issues, with a focus on quality, compliance and risk management. There are also opportunities to contribute more widely to the development of the firm, for example by building our senior connectivity and running differentiated client and marketing events. 
Benefits
What we offer 
The successful candidate will start as an executive, and there is a pathway within the team for promotion to director and then election to the partnership, depending on performance. Responsibilities grow with experience and capability. Compensation is competitive and in line with other leading professional services firms, comprising a base salary and an annual performance-related bonus. We also offer a generous range of benefits including pension, health insurance, and 25 days’ holiday per annum (plus the days between Christmas and New Year).
The team is expanding internationally. After spending time in London, the successful candidate may be expected to move to an office in North America or Asia, subject to personal preference and the needs of the business.

job_description:
Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. In just three years since our launch, we’ve grown, evolved and are now entering an exciting new chapter – one filled with bold ambitions and enormous opportunity.

Our trusted portfolio of brands – including Sensodyne®, Panadol®, Advil®, Voltaren®, Theraflu®, Otrivin®, and Centrum® – lead in resilient and growing categories. What sets us apart is our unique blend of deep human understanding and trusted science.

It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture.

 The Enterprise Transformation Programme is a multi-year journey focused on transforming the Haleon business building an organisation that is wired for excellence to be able to deliver our ‘Win as One’ strategy and drive growth through continuous improvement. The programme aims to strengthen the heartbeat of our business enabling us to become more agile, efficient, and innovative and is enabled through SAP S/4HANA. The Business Process Expert partners with Business Process Owners and functional teams to design, govern, and continuously improve end-to-end business processes.

Detailed Responsibilities 
Business Process Experts (BPE) are responsible for shaping, measuring and continuously improving process elements to deliver business value. The role partners with the Business Process Owner (BPO) and other BPEs to manage the current process (including ensuring proposed changes are aligned to the intended future state), define the future end‑to‑end process vision and roadmap, ensuring high‑quality, well‑controlled and user‑centric processes are created, and drive the transition from current state to future state through disciplined execution, strong governance and effective change delivery. They support the BPO in maximising value delivery through rigorous performance management, adoption oversight and continuous improvement activities, to ensuring that committed benefits are realised and sustained. 

Responsibilities specific to the BPE – IBP E2E Planning:
• Partner closely with the SAP IBP APS programme to align process, data, and governance outcomes. 
• Ensure the evolving end-to-end planning operating model remains coherent across programmes, recognising that elements of “to be” design are already defined and focusing effort on gap closure, standardisation, and usability rather than redesigning from scratch. 
• Drive clarity on how the E2E Planning and IBP processes integrate across Supply Chain, Commercial, and Finance and how these processes are enabled by the combined landscape of SAP S/4 (ERP) and SAP IBP (APS). 
• Own the process-led definition of critical integration touchpoints between SAP S/4 and SAP IBP (e.g., planning master data, product/location hierarchies, calendars, key figures, and inbound/outbound interfaces), ensuring they support planning accuracy, timeliness, and auditability. 

Design Plan and Coordination: 
• Collaborate with the BPO and the relevant function(s)/operating units to ensure design meets requirements and strategic objectives. 
• Facilitate workshops to gather input, feedback, and socialise recommendations made with the functions/operating units to refine and finalise process design in partnership with the BPO and other BPEs. 
• Collaborate with the BPO to document “to be” processes; and support evaluation of “as is” processes identifying bottle necks, inefficiencies, and duplication. 
• Drive decisions through relevant governance forums, ensuring decisions are communicated to stakeholders in a timely manner. 
• Align designs with programme timelines and milestones, ensuring coordination with other functional areas and interdependent programmes. 
• Review and validate existing process design outputs from the SAP IBP APS implementation programme (process flows, design decisions, templates, roles), and translate them into the Plan to Forecast value stream standards and documentation set. 
• Lead identification and resolution of process/design gaps created by running multiple change initiatives (e.g., differences in planning calendars, hierarchy definitions, roles/RACI, and KPI calculations) and drive alignment through agreed governance. 
• Define and document the end-to-end process steps and controls that depend on S/4 ↔ IBP integration, including ownership of data objects and decision points across systems (what is planned in IBP vs executed/recorded in S/4). 
• Coordinate cross-functional agreement on standard demand planning concepts that must be consistently implemented in IBP (e.g., baseline vs uplift logic, event assumptions, forecast versioning, bias management, and exception rules). 
• Ensure process design includes explicit requirements for integration performance (timing/latency, cut-off times, error handling, and reconciliation steps) so that planning outputs flow reliably into execution. 

Readiness for Delivery:
• Support the Functional Leader in evaluating the preparedness of their functional area for programme delivery, identifying any gaps and proposing solutions. 
• Support the business change team in understanding people implications for the change and defining and delivering relevant interventions to create conditions for successful adoption. 
• Create appropriate documentation for new processes; partnering with Training & Adoption team to develop appropriate training/upskilling for colleagues to support adoption and benefit realisation. 
• Define readiness criteria that reflect a dual-landscape transition, including minimum standards for S/4 and IBP master data readiness, interface readiness, and planning calendar alignment before cutover. 
• Partner with the SAP IBP APS programme to ensure training and adoption materials cover not only “how to use IBP”, but also how planning actions in IBP translate into execution in S/4 (and what users must check/reconcile). 
• Support definition and execution of end-user readiness activities that target integration points (e.g., reconciliation checks, interface monitoring, exception management, and cut-off adherence). 
• Ensure process documentation and standard work include “what to do when it goes wrong” guidance (e.g., interface failures, master data mismatches, version conflicts) to protect continuity and enable rapid issue resolution. 

Managing Transition phases:
• Partner with the Business Continuity Manager to establish and manage interim operating states to support business continuity during the change. 
• Collaborate with operational teams to design and implement interim processes, ensuring minimal disruption to existing operations. 
• Ensure that plans are in place to transition from interim states to permanent processes in a sustainable way. 
• Define interim operating procedures where S/4 and IBP deployments are not fully synchronised (e.g., phased rollouts by market/category), ensuring continuity of forecast to supply signal and decision forums. 
• Establish interim and permanent reconciliation routines between S/4 and IBP (e.g., master data alignment checks, interface validation, key figure sanity checks) to maintain trust in the numbers during transition. 
• Drive clear entry/exit criteria for decommissioning legacy planning workarounds (spreadsheets/local tools), aligned to confirmed IBP stability, interface performance, and user adoption. 

Stakeholder Engagement:
• Foster effective relationships with stakeholders, ensuring alignment and collaboration. 
• Communicate effectively, adapting messaging for different audiences to ensure clarity and engagement in the programme objectives. 
• Champion the interest of the process vision, ensuring priorities are reflected in programme decision-making, and feedback loops are effective. 
• Serve as the key process interface between the Plan to Forecast value stream and the SAP IBP APS programme, ensuring design decisions, constraints, and impacts are transparently communicated both ways. 
• Align stakeholders on what is “global standard” vs “local flex” specifically in the context of SAP IBP configuration and S/4 integration constraints. 
• Facilitate cross-functional resolution of integration-driven issues (e.g., ownership of hierarchies, calendars, and key planning assumptions) to prevent fragmentation and protect the single set of numbers. 
• Maintain a strong end-user voice in design decisions, ensuring that new SAP-enabled processes are practical, efficient, and do not introduce avoidable manual reconciliation burdens. 

Experience and Key Competencies: 
• Experience working in complex, global organisations, ideally within Consumer Health, or FMCG sectors. 
• Strong analytical skills; ability to analyse complex processes, understand workflow patterns, and identify inefficiencies. 
• Knowledge of process modelling software, data analysis tools, and familiarity with automation technologies is essential. 
• Project Management Skills: Ability to plan, manage, and execute process improvement initiatives. 
• Proven experience operating in a transformation landscape with parallel programmes, able to leverage existing design artefacts and drive pragmatic alignment rather than duplicating work. 
• Strong understanding of end-to-end planning processes and the enabling architecture across ERP (SAP S/4) and APS (SAP IBP), including implications for data, controls, and operational execution. 
• Experience defining and governing system integration requirements (interfaces, cut-offs, reconciliations, data ownership) and translating these into robust business process controls and standard work. 
• Demonstrated ability to drive KPI-based performance management in a system-enabled planning environment (e.g., forecast accuracy/bias, adherence to IBP cadence, and issue resolution effectiveness). 
• Ability to influence senior stakeholders and technical teams to resolve cross-programme dependencies and deliver a seamless, user-centric planning experience. 
• Inspiring and motivating – strong leader with the power to inspire, energize, and motivate their team to work together to achieve shared goals. 
• Building strong relationships – skilled at developing ability to build strong collaborative team connections relationships with their team.  
• Making informed decisions – Evaluates challenges Considering problems and challenges from multiple different perspectives, analyse potential outcomes, takes calculated risks, and make decisions that drive help propel the organization forward. 
• Navigating and driving change –identifying the need for change, executing structured change management strategies, guiding teams through managing periods of uncertainty and disruption, and ensuring operational maintaining stability and continuity throughout the transformation. for the organization.

In good company

Hamilton (NYSE: HG) underwrites specialty insurance and reinsurance risks on a global basis through its wholly owned subsidiaries. Its three underwriting platforms: Hamilton Global Specialty, Hamilton Select and Hamilton Re, each with dedicated and experienced leadership, provide access to diversified and profitable business around the world.

Headquartered in Bermuda, Hamilton has over 600 employees with key underwriting operations in London, Bermuda, the US and Dublin. We work collaboratively, we share a passion for the service and results we deliver, and we know that what we do each day is meaningful – to our customers and our business. We believe we are ‘In good company.’ with everyone we interact with.

We’re looking for an Employee Communications Manager

Based in London, reporting directly to Group Head of Human Resources, Communications & Culture.  You will plan and deliver Group-wide and local employee communications and engagement initiatives that support Hamilton’s strategy, business priorities, performance and culture. Partnering with senior leaders, HR, functional teams and colleagues across our international offices, you will bring together trusted communications advice and commercial awareness with creative, hands-on delivery.

- Develop and deliver communications strategies and campaigns that build employee understanding of Hamilton’s strategy, business imperatives, performance and key initiatives
- Lead the end-to-end delivery of Group and local Town Halls, including shaping agendas and messaging, writing scripts and developing presentations
- Own Group HR communications, including performance management, compensation and benefits, wellbeing, learning and development, policy updates, inclusion initiatives and organisational change
- Support communications for Group functions, including IT, Finance and Legal, and lead employee communication and engagement for Group-wide AI initiatives
- Lead the twice-yearly employee engagement survey, from launch and communications through to analysis and action planning
- Develop and distribute Group-wide and local communications through the digital employee email platform, using engagement data to evaluate and improve performance
- Provide strategic advice and hands-on communications support to senior leaders, functional teams and offices across Hamilton’s international operations
- Work in close alignment with the Marketing & Corporate Communications Lead to ensure employee and external communications are consistent and coordinated

What you require for the role

- Significant employee or internal communications experience, ideally within insurance, reinsurance or financial services
- A proven ability to provide strategic communications counsel while remaining highly hands-on and delivery focused. 
- Exceptional writing and editing skills, including executive scripts, business updates and employee communications. 
- Advanced PowerPoint skills and extensive experience developing senior-level presentations
- Proficiency in a digital employee email platform, including campaign development, distribution, audience management, analytics and reporting
- Experience in leading employee engagement surveys and interpreting results
- A creative mindset and strong visual judgement, with the ability to translate complex business, technology and HR topics into engaging content
- Strong stakeholder and project management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships and deliver consistently across international teams

What you can expect from us

At Hamilton, we offer a vibrant, entrepreneurial and collaborative workplace shaped by our values: Be Smart, Be Sensible, Be Open and Be More.

Our employees consistently say they would recommend Hamilton as a great place to work — a testament to the inclusive, supportive, and empowering culture we’ve built together. We embrace individuality, value diverse perspectives, and recognise the unique contribution each person makes to our continued success.

job_title: Head of Investment and Market Risk Oversight
job_description:
Help us shape the future!

There’s never been a more exciting time to join HL. We’re looking for a Head of Investment and Market Risk Oversight to support our bold ambition to become the UK’s premier investment and savings platform, all in service of our purpose to help Britain build wealth with confidence.

We’re transforming how we support our clients through personalised guidance, distinctive products and trusted expertise, and our people are at the heart of making that happen.

Join us and you’ll have the opportunity to think boldly, do brilliant work and make a purposeful difference, while growing your career and helping to shape the next chapter of HL.

About the role
Reporting to the Chief Risk Officer, you’ll lead HL’s independent second-line oversight of investment and market risk across our funds, products, investment solutions and own balance sheet. You’ll set the direction for our Investment Risk Framework, provide authoritative challenge to senior leaders and Boards, and ensure material risks are understood and managed within appetite. Combining deep technical expertise with commercial judgement, you’ll build a forward-looking capability that protects clients, informs strategic decisions and helps HL respond confidently to changing markets, regulation and emerging macro trends.

What you’ll be doing
• Set the strategy for, own and continually develop HL’s Investment Risk Framework, methodologies, standards and analytical toolkit.
• Lead independent second-line oversight and evidence-based challenge across investment, market, liquidity, treasury, counterparty, credit and concentration risk.
• Shape risk appetite, limits, metrics and stress-testing approaches, ensuring breaches, concentrations and emerging trends are identified and escalated clearly.
• Provide proactive risk oversight for new and changing funds, products and investment solutions before launch.
• Advise the Chief Risk Officer, Chief Investment Officer, senior executives, governance committees and Boards through clear, decision-useful reporting and insight.
• Track market and macroeconomic developments, translating complex quantitative analysis into practical implications for clients, portfolios and HL’s balance sheet.
• Lead and develop a high-performing team of investment-risk specialists while strengthening data, technology and automation across the capability.

About you
Essential
• Significant senior-level experience in investment, portfolio or quantitative risk within asset management, investment management or a comparable regulated financial-services environment.
• Deep knowledge of multi-asset investment-risk methodologies, including market and liquidity risk, portfolio construction, asset allocation, performance and portfolio risk drivers.
• Practical expertise in scenario analysis, stress testing, quantitative risk measurement and risk appetite, limits and monitoring frameworks.
• Strong understanding of funds, fund-of-funds structures, underlying holdings, derivatives and the relationship between investment risk and performance.
• Experience of firm-level market, treasury and balance-sheet risk, including counterparty, credit and concentration risk.
• Detailed knowledge of the investment-risk regulatory environment, including UCITS and AIFMD requirements.
• A strong record of influencing senior stakeholders, constructively challenging decisions and translating complex analysis for executive and Board audiences.
• Proven experience leading and developing specialist risk professionals.

Desirable
• CFA, FRM, PRM or a comparable professional qualification.
• Experience with institutional risk platforms such as MSCI BarraOne, LiquidityMetrics or comparable analytical tools.
• Experience of investment-risk governance involving Boards, investment committees or regulated fund-management entities, and of developing analytics, dashboards or automation.

We know great candidates don’t always meet every requirement. If this opportunity excites you and you have many of the skills and experiences we’re looking for, we encourage you to apply.

Hybrid / office expectations: Hybrid working, with regular office presence to support senior stakeholder engagement and team leadership.

Interview process
A 3-stage process consisting of technical, behavioural and presentation-based interviews

• Flexible working options, including hybrid working

• Income protection and life insurance (four times salary at core cover level)
• Private medical insurance*
• Healthcare cash plans, including optical, dental and outpatient care
• Health screening programme
• Help@hand, including confidential mental health counselling and remote GP support
• Free on-site gym including classes
• Wellhub access to fitness providers and wellness coaching
• Travel-to-work schemes, bike storage and shower facilities
• In-house barista and deli with subsidised coffee and sandwiches
• Two paid volunteering days each year
* Dependent on role level.
** Available for selection during the annual benefits window in November.

Belonging at HL
HL is an inclusive employer and we value the different perspectives and experiences people bring. We welcome applications from everyone and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you need an adjustment at any stage, please let the Recruitment & Onboarding team know.
Flexible working: This role may be available on a flexible-working or part-time basis. Please ask the Talent Acquisition team for more information.

Introduction

At IBM Global Sales, we bring together innovation, collaboration, and expertise to help clients solve their most complex business challenges. Working across industries and geographies, you'll partner with colleagues, clients, and partners to co-create solutions that drive digital transformation and lasting impact.Success in Global Sales is built on curiosity, empathy, and collaboration. With world-class onboarding, continuous learning, and a supportive culture, IBM offers the tools and opportunities to grow your career. Join us and be part of a global team that's passionate about driving innovation and making a difference.

Your role and responsibilities

As a Brand Sales Specialist, you will be responsible for selling HashiCorp automation solutions. This role involves enabling secure infrastructure provisioning, lifecycle management, and cloud agility through solution delivery.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Solution Selling: Sells HashiCorp automation solutions to enable secure infrastructure provisioning and lifecycle management.

• Client Engagement: Engages with clients to understand their needs and deliver solutions that provide cloud agility.

• Sales Delivery: Delivers sales solutions that meet client requirements, leveraging HashiCorp automation capabilities.

Bachelor's Degree

Bachelor's Degree

• Automation Expertise: Experience in automation technologies, specifically in enabling secure infrastructure provisioning and managing lifecycles, to deliver cloud agility solutions.

• Cloud Agility: Experience with solutions that provide cloud agility, leveraging HashiCorp automation capabilities to meet client requirements and deliver sales solutions.

• Infrastructure Management: Experience with infrastructure management, including provisioning and lifecycle management, to enable secure and efficient operations.

• Sales Delivery: Experience in delivering sales solutions that meet client requirements, utilizing HashiCorp automation capabilities to drive business outcomes.

Preferred technical and professional experience

- A strong track record of exceeding enterprise software sales targets within financial services, winning new customers and expanding strategic accounts.

- Demonstrated ability to hunt for new business and generate your own pipeline through targeted prospecting, account research, networking and creative outreach.

- Confidence engaging C-suite executives, understanding their priorities and building relationships across business, technology and security leadership.

- Experience creating compelling, value-based proposals that connect technical capabilities to measurable customer outcomes, supported by clear business cases and return-on-investment analysis.

- Success leading complex enterprise sales cycles, building customer champions and navigating procurement, commercial negotiations and competing stakeholder priorities.

- Self-motivation, high energy and a strong sense of ownership, with the initiative to create opportunities and the discipline to progress them through to close.

- Curiosity about customers’ businesses, the ability to ask thoughtful questions and a commitment to helping customers achieve meaningful outcomes.

- Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, automation or platform engineering, with the ability to translate technical concepts into business value.

- A collaborative approach to bringing together technical specialists, partners and customer success teams to win business and deliver lasting customer value.

### ABOUT BUSINESS UNIT

IBM has a global presence, operating in more than 175 countries with a broad-based geographic distribution of revenue. The company’s Global Markets organization is a strategic sales business unit that manages IBM’s global footprint, working closely with dedicated country-based operating units to serve clients locally. These country teams have client relationship managers who lead integrated teams of consultants, solution specialists and delivery professionals to enable clients’ growth and innovation. By complementing local expertise with global experience and digital capabilities, IBM builds deep and broad-based client relationships. This local management focus fosters speed in supporting clients, addressing new markets and making investments in emerging opportunities. Additionally, the Global Markets organization serves clients with expertise in their industry as well as through the products and services that IBM and partners supply. IBM is also expanding its reach to new and existing clients through digital marketplaces.

### YOUR LIFE @ IBM

In a world where technology never stands still, we understand that, dedication to our clients success, innovation that matters, and trust and personal responsibility in all our relationships, lives in what we do as IBMers as we strive to be the catalyst that makes the world work better.

Being an IBMer means you’ll be able to learn and develop yourself and your career, you’ll be encouraged to be courageous and experiment everyday, all whilst having continuous trust and support in an environment where everyone can thrive whatever their personal or professional background.

Our IBMers are growth minded, always staying curious, open to feedback and learning new information and skills to constantly transform themselves and our company. They are trusted to provide on-going feedback to help other IBMers grow, as well as collaborate with colleagues keeping in mind a team focused approach to include different perspectives to drive exceptional outcomes for our customers. The courage our IBMers have to make critical decisions everyday is essential to IBM becoming the catalyst for progress, always embracing challenges with resources they have to hand, a can-do attitude and always striving for an outcome focused approach within everything that they do.

Are you ready to be an IBMer?

### ABOUT IBM

IBM’s greatest invention is the IBMer. We believe that through the application of intelligence, reason and science, we can improve business, society and the human condition, bringing the power of an open hybrid cloud and AI strategy to life for our clients and partners around the world.

Restlessly reinventing since 1911, we are not only one of the largest corporate organizations in the world, we’re also one of the biggest technology and consulting employers, with many of the Fortune 500 companies relying on the IBM Cloud to run their business. 

At IBM, we pride ourselves on being an early adopter of artificial intelligence, quantum computing and blockchain. Now it’s time for you to join us on our journey to being a responsible technology innovator and a force for good in the world.

Hiscox is delivering change across the Group. This role helps a defined cluster of transformation workstreams deliver their plans and achieve their intended outcomes.

Each Programme Manager partners with a different cluster of workstreams. You will build a clear view of delivery across your cluster, test whether plans are realistic and help leaders deal with risks, dependencies and resource pressures early.

This is not a reporting-only PMO role. You will provide independent delivery assurance, practical support and focused intervention when a workstream is at risk. You will work closely with workstream leads and sponsors, while keeping clear accountability: business sponsors own outcomes, benefits and adoption; workstream leads own day-to-day delivery; you provide oversight, challenge and help to unblock delivery.

What You'll Be Doing

1. Partner with your workstream cluster
· Build strong working relationships with the sponsors and leads across your assigned cluster.
· Understand each workstream’s objectives, key outcomes, delivery plan and main challenges.
· Provide constructive challenge and practical support without taking day-to-day ownership away from the workstream lead.
· Connect workstreams to the right support across Finance, Technology, People, Risk, Procurement and other teams.

2. Assess delivery health
· Regularly test whether scope, milestones, resources, risks and dependencies are clear and realistic.
· Give the Transformation Office Director an honest, evidence-based view of delivery confidence.
· Identify issues early, explain their likely impact and agree clear actions with owners and dates.
· Follow actions through until the issue is resolved or formally escalated.

3. Manage dependencies and capacity
· Maintain the dependency and capacity view for your cluster.
· Agree clear owners and dates for hand-offs between workstreams.
· Work with the other Programme Managers and the TO Planning & Operations Manager to resolve cross-cluster dependencies and shared resource conflicts.
· Escalate unresolved conflicts to the Transformation Office Director with clear options and a recommendation.

4. Lead targeted intervention and recovery
· Step in when delivery confidence falls or when a workstream needs focused help.
· Agree a short, clear recovery or acceleration plan with the sponsor, workstream lead and Transformation Office Director.
· Bring together the right people to remove blockers and restore delivery momentum.
· Track recovery measures and exit the intervention once delivery is stable.
· Use a peer Programme Manager for independent assurance when you are directly leading a recovery.

5. Support clear decisions
· Write concise cluster updates that explain progress, risks, dependencies, options and decisions needed.
· Make sure governance discussions focus on decisions and action, rather than status reporting alone.
· Provide timely plan updates to the TO Planning & Operations Manager.
· Provide delivery evidence and forecasts to the Transformation Strategy Manager and Finance Transformation Office for enterprise reporting and value tracking.

6. Support readiness and lasting outcomes
· Check that workstreams have clear plans for business readiness, adoption and transition into business as usual.
· Surface gaps in readiness and make sure they have owners and actions.
· Keep attention on intended customer, colleague, control, operational and financial outcomes, not activity alone.
· Capture recurring delivery issues and lessons, and share them with the Head of Transformation Practice & Capability.

Person Specification
· Strong experience leading, assuring or recovering large and complex programmes.
· Able to judge whether plans are realistic and identify the real causes of delivery risk.
· Confident working with senior sponsors and workstream leads, including giving clear and respectful challenge.
· Strong planning, dependency management and problem-solving skills.
· Able to turn complex information into simple choices, recommendations and actions.
· Good understanding of business cases, financial control, benefits, readiness and adoption.
· Comfortable working across different delivery approaches, including programme, project, product, agile and hybrid delivery.
· Collaborative, practical and calm under pressure, with strong ownership and follow-through.
· Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Clear Role Boundaries
· Workstream leads own day-to-day delivery. Business sponsors own outcomes, benefits and adoption.
· Programme Managers own cluster-level assurance, dependencies, capacity oversight and targeted intervention.
· The TO Planning & Operations Manager maintains the integrated delivery plan and runs TO operations.

Job Description

Location:
London, GB

Condé Nast is a global media company, home to iconic brands including Vogue, The New Yorker, GQ, Glamour, AD, Vanity Fair and Wired, among many others. The company's award-winning content reaches 84 million consumers in print, 367 million in digital and 379 million across social platforms, and generates more than 1 billion video views each month. 

The company is headquartered in New York and London, and operates in 32 markets worldwide, including China, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico & Latin America, Spain, Taiwan, the U.K. and the U.S., with local license partners across the globe. 

Condé Nast thrives on collaboration, and our teams come together in the office four days a week (Monday - Thursday).

We value diversity of background, views and cultures. We celebrate people for their personal qualities, skills and contributions, recognising the power our brands have to influence and shape culture. 

The purpose of this role is to support the General Counsel by leading and overseeing the full range of Employment law (including pensions, incentives and immigration), in all of our international markets. 

The role involves close working with senior leaders across the business and directly advising C-Suite colleagues on sensitive people-related matters, up to and including the CEO. The role involves becoming a close partner of the global People Team community and a trusted advisor to the Chief People Officer and the People Leadership team in all international markets.

The role involves providing strategic, cross border employment law advice to enable CN to achieve its business goals.

Specific Responsibilities

• Partnering with Conde Nast People Team colleagues (both in HQ and in our wholly owned international markets) to ensure internal legal best practices for managing employee relations.
• To lead on all non-US employment law work, working closely with People Team colleagues to ensure the provision of advice and support as necessary and to partner closely with US legal colleagues on global matters.

· Planned preventative maintenance (PPM) visits.

Essential Requirements
· Experience working with automated gates, barriers, doors, shutters or similar automation systems.
· Strong electrical competency and fault-finding ability.
· Good understanding of relevant safety standards and industry best practices.
· Ability to work independently and manage workload effectively.
· Full UK driving licence.
· Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

Experience & Qualifications
· DHF Level 2 qualification.
· Gate Safe IOSH certification.
· Manufacturer training with leading automation providers.
· Commercial awareness and the ability to identify opportunities for improvement and growth.
· Proactive and self-motivated.
· Reliable and professional.
· Well organised with excellent time management skills.
· Customer focused and commercially aware.
· Ambitious, with aspirations to progress and take on further responsibility.
· Committed to continuous learning and professional development.
· Full and clean driving license

What We Offer

· 25 days holiday, with buy and sell schemes
· Genuine career growth opportunities
· Access to prestigious clients and high-end systems
· Supportive work environment focused on teamwork and success

About the Role

Main Responsibilities

As a Commercial Finance Manager, you will provide strategic financial insight, challenge, and guidance to support business performance and value creation across forecasting, budgeting, and long-range planning processes. You will deliver accurate and actionable financial reporting and analysis, identifying risks and opportunities while recommending corrective actions to influence key business decisions. Partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Development teams, you will help develop and execute plans to meet and exceed budget and P&L targets, ensuring commercial decisions are supported by robust financial analysis.

The role includes leading and supporting finance transformation initiatives such as acquisitions, systems enhancements, process simplification, and technology improvements. You will provide high-quality financial modelling, scenario planning, and decision support for strategic opportunities and investments. As a people leader, you will develop, coach, and support the Commercial Finance Analyst, strengthening analytical capability and financial business partnering across the team while maintaining strong financial governance and compliance with internal controls and company policies.

The position acts as a key link between FBC business teams, IT, external partners, and Ferrero, ensuring alignment, effective governance, stakeholder engagement, and successful adoption of change.

Main Responsibilities

1. Lead Delivery of Strategic Technology Projects & Programmes

Manage the successful delivery of large, complex, cross-functional projects and programmes that support FBC's business strategy, ensuring agreed scope, timelines, quality, costs, and benefits are achieved.

2. Own Programme Governance and Portfolio Reporting

Establish and maintain effective governance across the portfolio, including project plans, steering committees, status reporting, RAID management, decision logs, and executive updates to ensure informed decision-making and successful delivery. Coordinate the local delivery across FBC of Ferrero-led initiatives, ensuring business resource availability, local requirements are represented, UK activities are completed on time, stakeholders remain engaged, and dependencies between global and local teams are effectively managed.

Proactively identify, track, and resolve project and programme risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies, escalating where required to prevent delays, protect business outcomes, and maintain delivery momentum

Bring together business, IT, external partners, and Ferrero teams to ensure resources are available and aligned, responsibilities are clear, and all workstreams are coordinated towards common objectives.

7. Ensure Benefits Realisation and Business Value

Work with business leaders to define expected outcomes, measure benefits, and ensure technology investments deliver tangible improvements in reporting, decision-making, efficiency, resilience, compliance, and business performance.

8. Develop and Mature Project & Programme Management Practices

Champion consistent methodologies, standards, tools, templates, and reporting across FBC IT, working with Ferrero to establish repeatable delivery practices and improve organisational project delivery capability.

About the role

Our understanding of the audiences who consume our products, the contributors who shape them, and the landscape in which we operate is fundamental to the success of our products.

Reporting to the UX Research Director, the Lead UX Researcher leads complex research across brands including Vogue, GQ and Condé Nast Traveller. The role takes accountability for research priorities, approach and delivery, using customer evidence to inform product direction and improve audience experiences.

As the strategic research partner to the portfolio’s Design and Product leadership, the Lead works closely with Editorial, Engineering and Brand Leadership to inform decisions from discovery through ongoing improvement.

Alongside portfolio responsibilities, the role supports the UX Research Director in evolving UX Research at Condé Nast through innovation, experimentation and emerging AI-native approaches. This includes developing self-serve tools, guidance and capability that help teams access customer insight and apply it confidently in everyday decisions.

Responsibilities of the role

Lead strategic customer research across the brand portfolio

• Own the research agenda, aligning priorities around the decisions where customer understanding matters most.
• Lead qualitative and quantitative research across the product lifecycle, uncovering needs and opportunities while ensuring quality, inclusion and clear actions.
• Turn insight into recommendations that shape product direction and roadmap priorities, sharing learning across brands while respecting their distinct audiences.
• Focus human expertise on high-stakes questions requiring depth and judgement, enabling appropriate self-serve research for tactical needs.

Build cross-functional alignment and influence

• Partner across Product, Design, Engineering and Editorial to bring customer evidence into decisions early.
• Translate complex findings into clear narratives that build alignment and help teams act.
• Work with the UX Research Director to balance priorities and contribute to wider strategic initiatives.

Advance innovation and future research practice

• Help the UX Research Director evolve the team’s skills and methods as technology, customer expectations and business needs change.
• Pilot emerging methods and AI-enabled workflows, turning successful experiments into shared practices that improve research quality, pace and impact.
• Explore how AI changes content discovery and engagement to anticipate customer needs and future research opportunities.
• Apply human judgement and research rigour to business strategy, testing AI-generated insights and hypotheses against customer evidence.

Scale customer understanding and build capability

• Develop shared tools, playbooks and standards with the UX Research Director and fellow Lead to enable effective self-serve research.
• Make customer intelligence accessible and reusable through shared repositories, AI-enabled tools and knowledge distribution programmes. 
• Mentor researchers and coach colleagues through practical guidance, workshops and shared learning, building research confidence and AI fluency.

About you

• You’re relentlessly customer-obsessed, curious about people and driven to make their experiences better. 
• You ask good questions, challenge assumptions and take initiative to turn learning into action. 
• You’re comfortable with ambiguity, move fast and stay focused on what matters most, using customer feedback to guide decisions without compromising quality.
• You take ownership of outcomes and stay involved from start to finish. 
• An AI-native mindset is part of how you work: you experiment, apply sound judgement and share what you learn. 
• You reach beyond your role, build new skills and work across disciplines to help the team succeed. 
• You care about cultural brands and bringing audience needs, editorial ambition and business goals together.

Experience and capabilities

• 7+ years in applied research, with a track record of shaping product and experience decisions.
• Strong qualitative and quantitative expertise, choosing methods to suit the question, risk and time available.
• Experience leading complex research independently, balancing priorities and adapting across teams.
• Strong synthesis and storytelling, turning research and analytics into clear recommendations that influence Product, Design and senior stakeholders.
• Experience mentoring researchers and coaching colleagues to use research effectively.
• Practical knowledge of research platforms, repositories and AI-assisted workflows, including their limitations and appropriate use.

Additional relevant experience

• Research across media, publishing, subscription products or other content-led digital experiences.
• Global or multi-market research and collaboration with distributed teams.
• Experience developing research assistants, experimenting with emerging methods or making research knowledge more accessible across an organisation.

What success looks like

Success means teams understand their customers well enough to make confident choices about what to prioritise, build and improve. Through strong research and trusted partnerships, the Lead turns that understanding into practical direction and helps colleagues build the confidence to act on it. Coaching, shared knowledge and AI-enabled self-serve tools extend this work across the organisation, helping more teams learn from customers and put that learning into practice.

Condé Nast is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own how consent and privacy preferences are collected, managed, stored, and honoured across our global digital ecosystem. Consent sits at a critical intersection of customer trust, regulatory compliance, data collection, advertising, marketing, analytics, and the digital experience. This role will ensure that Condé Nast has a consistent, scalable, and well-governed approach to consent while understanding and managing the broader business implications of the decisions we make.

You will own the consent product strategy, roadmap, and end-to-end operating model across brands, markets, web, and app. Working closely with Legal, Data Governance, Engineering, Product, Advertising, Marketing, Analytics, and other stakeholders, you will translate evolving privacy requirements into clear product decisions and durable capabilities, while ensuring material changes are tested, monitored, and understood across the business.

Based in London, this is a highly cross-functional role requiring close partnership with the teams shaping privacy and consent requirements, alongside a strong operating cadence with Engineering teams responsible for implementation.

What You will be doing:

Own consent & compliance end to end
• Own the product strategy, roadmap, and operating model for consent and preference management across Condé Nast's digital products and platforms.
• Be accountable for how consent requirements move from regulatory interpretation through product definition, implementation, validation, release, monitoring, and continuous improvement, with clear decision rights and ownership across teams.
• Establish consistent approaches to consent collection, storage, propagation, and enforcement across brands, markets, web, and app, including marketing preference management.
• Own the business relationship with our Consent Management Platform provider, ensuring the platform and partnership support our product, regulatory, and business needs.

Translate privacy requirements into scalable products
• Partner closely with Legal and Data Governance to translate evolving privacy regulations - including GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other global requirements - into clear product requirements and scalable capabilities.
• Own product decisions and trade-offs while Legal and Data Governance remain accountable for regulatory interpretation and privacy policy.
• Maintain a strong understanding of the data collection ecosystem, including cookies, tags, SDKs, identifiers, vendor integrations, and downstream systems that depend on consent and preference signals.

Build trust, controls, and operational rigor
• Establish strong testing, monitoring, auditing, and release-management practices so material consent changes are validated before and after launch.
• Own Product acceptance and release readiness, including appropriate staging, UAT, stakeholder approvals, production validation, and clear escalation paths when issues arise.
• Monitor the health and effectiveness of the consent ecosystem and use incidents, audit findings, and recurring support patterns to identify systemic improvements rather than one-off fixes.

Balance compliance, customer experience, and business outcomes
• Understand how consent decisions and changes affect customer experience and critical business outcomes, including advertising, analytics, marketing, audience engagement, and data quality.
• Establish monitoring of relevant business KPIs alongside consent and platform-health metrics, particularly when significant consent or configuration changes are introduced.
• Partner with stakeholders to assess and communicate trade-offs between regulatory requirements, customer experience, technical feasibility, data quality, and business impact.
• Ensure stakeholders understand the expected impact of material consent changes and that unexpected business impacts are quickly identified, investigated, and addressed.

What You Bring
• 6+ years of product management experience, with meaningful experience in consent, privacy technology, data governance, identity, customer data, advertising technology, or another highly regulated technical domain.
• Strong understanding of consent-management concepts and preference-management technologies, including consent experiences, notices, purposes, vendors, jurisdictions, downstream signaling, and the role of a Consent Management Platform (CMP).
• Experience with CMP platforms; direct familiarity with Ethyca/Fides is a strong plus.
• Working knowledge of global privacy regulations and digital-consent requirements, including GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and evolving US state privacy laws; able to translate approved legal and privacy guidance into product decisions.
• Understanding of digital advertising technology, including how ad delivery, cookies, tracking technologies, and consent signals interact across the advertising ecosystem.
• Strong familiarity with digital data collection and the marketing consent ecosystem, including marketing preferences, opt-in/opt-out management, cookies, tags, SDKs, identifiers, APIs, and integrations with marketing and customer-data platforms.
• Working knowledge of SQL, with the ability to query data, investigate consent and preference signals, validate implementations, and assess downstream business impact.
• Experience working with technically complex, multi-system products and partnering closely with Engineering teams on requirements, configuration, testing, monitoring, and release quality.
• Strong business judgment and an understanding of how consent and data-collection decisions can affect advertising, analytics, marketing, customer experience, and other business outcomes; able to identify, communicate, and manage trade-offs across stakeholders.
• Strong stakeholder-management skills and the ability to build alignment across Legal, Governance, Engineering, Marketing, Advertising, Product, Analytics, and other business teams.
• Experience managing technology vendors or platforms and holding partners accountable for roadmap alignment, delivery commitments, support quality, and business outcomes.
• A pragmatic product leader who brings structure and clarity to complex, highly regulated environments and is comfortable making decisions when technical, regulatory, customer, and business considerations compete.

HOW WE WORK

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 5, that looks like this.

An AI-first approach to web development
AI isn't a side project at ICAAL. It's changing how we build.

You'll take ownership of website builds and ongoing development across a varied portfolio of client sites, with AI coding agents at the heart of how you work. You'll be responsible for understanding what each site needs to achieve, turning that into a clear technical plan, and delivering it to a high standard.

The expectation isn't that you paste a ticket into an agent and ship whatever comes back. It's the opposite.

You'll need to know when the AI is right, when it's wrong, what it's missing, and what to do next.
That means using your experience and engineering judgement to:

• Plan builds and features with clear specs, acceptance criteria and boundaries before the agent starts

• Keep project context, conventions and rules files up to date so agents produce consistent, maintainable code

• Review AI-generated code line by line on critical paths, and catch hallucinated functions, logic errors and security gaps

Building on mature platforms

We're particularly interested in people who understand that AI makes good engineering practice more important, not less. Version control, code review, testing, sensible architecture and documentation are what make AI-assisted development safe to put in front of clients.

More than shipping code
We're not looking for someone who simply knows how to get an AI to produce a website.
You'll become the developer that both our clients and Account Managers trust. That means being able to explain what you built, why you built it that way, what the trade-offs are, and what you'd recommend next.

You'll bring a test-and-learn mindset, challenge assumptions, and look beyond "it works on my machine" to whether a site loads quickly, converts visitors and is easy to maintain.

Overall purpose of role :

The Site Quality Manager and Global Compliance Lead provides leadership for the site quality function and owns the effectiveness of the local quality management system, while leading global product and regulatory-systems compliance governance. The role has particular emphasis on equipment and solutions used in food, pharmaceutical, and nutraceutical applications. It ensures that products, processes, suppliers, technical documentation, validation activities, FAT protocol preparation and governance, and shipment release meet applicable customer, regulatory, industry, and internal requirements. Working across quality, engineering, operations, supply chain, project management, commercial, and service, the role reduces risk, strengthens customer confidence, improves first-pass quality, and builds a consistent culture of compliance and continuous improvement.

Key responsibilities:

Site quality responsibilities

- Lead the site quality function, including quality engineering, inspection and test, metrology, document control, nonconformance management, supplier quality, and quality-system administration.
- Own the site quality management system and ensure compliance with applicable ISO standards, customer requirements, regulatory obligations, industry expectations, and internal policies.
- Establish and manage site quality objectives, management reviews, improvement plans, and performance measures, including FAT first-pass success, on-time FAT readiness, punch-list closure, customer complaint recurrence, cost of poor quality, supplier defects, audit-action closure, and overdue compliance actions.
- Lead containment, root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and effectiveness verification for significant product, process, supplier, field, and customer quality issues.
- Ensure inspection and test methods, acceptance criteria, calibration controls, quality records, and product-release processes are accurate, controlled, risk-based, and effective.

- Verify FAT protocol readiness before execution, review completed test records and deviations for conformity to the approved protocol, ensure punch-list items are assigned and closed, and withhold or escalate quality approval for product release or shipment where product, documentation, compliance, or acceptance requirements remain unmet.
- Own customer-quality planning and documentation, including pre-FAT agreement of protocol content and acceptance criteria, qualification support, complaint and field-quality escalation, and quality input to recovery plans for critical customer projects.
- Lead supplier quality controls, including supplier qualification and monitoring, audits, first-article and incoming inspection requirements, supplier corrective action, and traceability and certification for critical components and product-contact materials.
- Lead site internal, customer, supplier, and registrar audits and ensure findings and associated actions are closed effectively and on time.
- Partner with operations, engineering, supply chain, project management, commercial, and service teams to embed quality requirements into new product introduction, design and process changes, supplier management, production, FAT protocol development, installation, and field support.
- Develop the site quality team through clear accountability, coaching, training, performance management, capability building, and succession planning.

Global compliance responsibilities

- Establish and maintain the global product and regulatory-compliance framework, including policies, standards, governance, risk assessments, controls, reporting, and minimum requirements across applicable sites and business units.
- Monitor changes in applicable product, market, regulatory, industry, and management-system requirements; assess business impact; assign accountable owners; and coordinate timely implementation.

- Define common compliance processes and minimum controls while partnering with site and functional leaders to ensure effective local execution and documented evidence of conformity.
- Lead or coordinate global compliance audits, assessments, and reviews; maintain visibility of findings and risks; and drive remediation actions through verified closure.
- Maintain global compliance dashboards and provide concise updates to senior leadership on regulatory changes, material risks, control effectiveness, trends, and overdue actions.
- Serve as the escalation point for significant product and compliance concerns, coordinating cross-functional containment, risk assessment, decision-making, documentation, customer communication, and lessons learned.
- Build global compliance capability through standardized training, guidance, tools, templates, and communities of practice.
- Demonstrated ability to lead a site quality organization while influencing global teams and senior stakeholders in a matrixed environment.
- Proficiency in FAT protocol preparation, document control, acceptance-criteria definition, and completed-record review, together with root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, process validation, change control, supplier quality, customer-quality planning, and quality performance analytics.
- Working knowledge of quality and compliance considerations for Food, Pharmaceutical, and Nutraceutical equipment, including hygienic design, cleanability, product-contact materials, traceability, qualification documentation, CE marking, ATEX conformity requirements, GMP expectations, and data integrity where applicable.
- Ability to interpret regulations, standards, specifications, customer requirements, and technical documentation and translate them into practical, scalable business controls.
- Strong judgement and decision-making, with the confidence to escalate risk, withhold quality approval, and drive timely accountability when requirements are not met.
- Clear, credible communication with employees, customers, suppliers, auditors, regulators, and senior leaders, combined with the ability to manage multiple priorities and lead cross-functional initiatives.
- Global product-compliance governance and risk management.
- Quality Management System ownership, auditing, and management review.
- FAT protocol preparation and governance, customer-requirement alignment, completed-record review, and quality-release decision-making.
- Customer, supplier, field, and regulatory issue management.
- Root-cause analysis, corrective action, and recurrence prevention.
- Continuous improvement and data-driven performance management.
- Cross-functional influence, sound judgement, and executive communication.

Knowledge:

- Strong working knowledge of quality management systems, product and regulatory compliance, risk management, audit practices, document control, validation, and product release.
- Strong progressive quality and compliance knowledge and experience in a regulated or highly controlled manufacturing environment, including evidence of experience leading people or a quality function.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience preparing, controlling, and approving FAT protocols and reviewing completed FAT documentation, making product- or shipment-release decisions, managing customer and supplier quality, and supporting equipment used in Food, Pharmaceutical, or Nutraceutical applications is strongly preferred. Practical experience with CE marking, technical documentation, Declarations of Conformity, and ATEX compliance for applicable equipment is preferred.
- Experience working across multiple sites, regions, or global compliance process is also preferred.

job_title: Contract and Revenue Accountant | OTC Team
job_description:

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring that customer contracts are accurately translated into billing and accounting outcomes. You will work across the contract lifecycle, from reviewing commercial terms and setting up contracts through to invoicing, revenue recognition, accruals, reconciliations, and financial analysis.
This is an opportunity to combine strong accounting expertise with commercial understanding in an international, subscription-based environment. You will work closely with Sales, Consulting, Finance, and Market Unit teams to ensure that contractual arrangements are accurately reflected in our financial systems and reporting.

What you'll bring

• At least three years of relevant experience in revenue accounting, contract accounting, financial accounting, invoicing, or a related area.

• Experience using business intelligence or financial reporting tools.

What will make you successful
You bring together strong accounting fundamentals, analytical thinking, and commercial curiosity. You are comfortable working with contracts and financial data, investigating discrepancies, and taking ownership through to resolution.

A standing weekly cadence with Sales leadership — not quarterly check-ins. Direct support on competitive and enterprise deals: RFPs, security and technical evaluations, displacement plays.

We are also global AWS, Microsoft and Databricks partners and Databricks Ventures has invested in our business and holds a seat on our board. We are deploying production AI systems into the world's most complex organisations across Financial Services, Energy, and Healthcare. We exist to make AI a genuine competitive advantage for our clients, not in a presentation but in production.

We invest seriously in our people. Every FDE at Indicium AI has access to Anthropic training, and a flexible learning budget to go with it.
