The Role

This is a role for an engineer who wants to lead an engagement end to end, from helping design the solution through to deploying in production with real users depending on it, and you will be accountable for your team getting it there.

As a Lead FDE, you are the person the team routes its hardest problems to. You design the systems and make architecture calls. You set the delivery quality bar through reviews and standards, and you make sure it stays high when a deadline starts pressing on it.

You will deliver through other people: planning and prioritising, managing dependencies and risk, shaping who is on the team, and having the honest conversations that keep a delivery on track. Knowing which of these to do yourself and which to hand over is an important part of the job.  You understand enterprise environments and how to get a system through to production inside one, working with internal review and security teams from day one rather than leaving it too late.

You will own the client relationship day to day and be the person they call when they need advice. That includes bringing bad news early with a plan attached, in a way that builds trust instead of triggering an escalation. 

This is an engineering role, which is worth being explicit about. A Lead FDE is not a delivery management role with a technical flavour. You will be in the codebase every week. You will make architecture decisions and be accountable for them. You will be the person the team escalates the genuinely hard technical problem to, and you will need to be able to solve it.

What you will do

• Lead AI engineering engagements end to end, from solution design through to production deployment, in complex enterprise environments

• Design and build production agentic AI systems: multi-agent orchestration, autonomous agent workflows, tool-use patterns, and the reliability layer that makes agents trustworthy in regulated environments

• Build advanced RAG pipelines — retrieval architectures, embedding strategies, reranking, hybrid search, and the evaluation frameworks that prove they work at scale

• Develop and deploy MCP servers and tool ecosystem integrations that give agents real-world capability within enterprise infrastructure

• Design evaluation and observability frameworks for non-deterministic systems, ensuring production AI applications are measurable, debuggable, and continuously improving

About the role:
This is a hands-on, technically grounded accounting role within one of our Financial Accounting sub-teams. The Senior Accountant is responsible for producing accurate, timely and well-evidenced month-end journals, balance sheet reconciliations and management accounting outputs for their assigned area — with the level of skill, judgement and autonomy expected from a qualified or nearly qualified accountant. The role sits one level below the Financial Controller and plays a pivotal part in making the close run smoothly every month.
What you’ll be doing:
Month-End Close
• Own the month-end journals, accruals, prepayments and reclassifications for your assigned area — ensuring all entries are accurately calculated, clearly supported by evidence and posted within the close timetable.

• Take the lead on close activities for your sub-area without needing to be directed at each step — managing your own workload against the close calendar and flagging blockers or issues to the Financial Controller promptly.

• Prepare and review accruals for your cost or revenue area, including identifying missing invoices or accruals from operational data, and ensuring the P&L reflects the correct position at period end.

• Provide clear, well-documented close workings for all journals posted — so that entries can be understood, reviewed and recreated by any member of the team.

Balance Sheet Reconciliations
• Own and maintain balance sheet reconciliations for all accounts within your assigned scope — completing them to timetable, investigating and resolving all reconciling items promptly, and ensuring your reconciliation pack is always audit-ready.

• Proactively identify and clear aged or unresolved items from your balance sheet accounts — escalating items that require cross-functional resolution and following through until they are closed.

• Support the Financial Controller in the monthly review of the balance sheet pack — providing clear commentary on movements and ensuring any areas of risk or uncertainty are clearly flagged.

Management Accounting & Reporting
• Prepare accurate, well-presented monthly reporting schedules for your assigned area — including cost centre analysis, variance commentary and any other regular outputs required by the Financial Controller or management accounting team.

• Write clear, concise variance commentary that explains movements in your area against budget, forecast and prior period — going beyond describing the number to identifying the underlying cause.

• Support the Financial Controller in the preparation of the management accounts pack — ensuring your area's numbers are accurate, submitted on time and clearly cross-referenced.

Technical Accounting & Standards
• Apply relevant accounting standards (IFRS and UK GAAP as applicable) to transactions within your assigned area — making appropriate accounting judgements and documenting your rationale clearly.

• Identify and escalate any transactions or events that may require technical accounting consideration beyond your authority level — working with the Financial Controller or Head of Financial Accounting to ensure the correct treatment is applied.

• Stay current on developments in accounting standards relevant to your area, flagging any potential impact on InPost's accounting to the Financial Controller.

Audit Support & Controls
• Prepare audit-ready working papers and schedules for your assigned area — ensuring all positions are fully evidenced, clearly cross-referenced and provided to auditors promptly.

• Respond to auditor queries relating to your area accurately and in a timely manner — managing the resolution of any findings and implementing agreed recommendations.

• Maintain year-round audit readiness — keeping reconciliations current, working papers up to date and controls evidenced throughout the year rather than only at year-end.

Supporting the Team
• Provide guidance and on-the-job support to Management Accountants and Trainee Accountants within the team — reviewing their work, answering technical questions and helping them develop their accounting skills and understanding of the ledger.

• Identify opportunities for process improvement within your area — proposing practical enhancements and working with the Financial Controller and Finance Transformation team to implement them.

• Cover other areas of the ledger when colleagues are absent — maintaining continuity of the close process and demonstrating the breadth of accounting knowledge expected at Senior Accountant level.

We’re looking for people who are ready for a fast paced environment, get their kicks out of problem solving and can balance getting today's stuff done, whilst building for the future. We’re looking for people with drive and natural curiosity – who want to do things differently. And do them brilliantly.

Qualifications & Experience
• Qualified or nearly qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent, or in the final stages of qualification) with demonstrable experience of managing your own area of a month-end close process.

• Strong working knowledge of balance sheet reconciliation, accruals accounting and management account preparation — with a track record of producing accurate, timetabled outputs independently.

• Experience of working within a multi-entity, ERP-based accounting environment — SAP, Unit4, SAGE or similar.

• Demonstrable ability to apply accounting standards to practical transactions and to document your judgements clearly and concisely.

• Experience of supporting or mentoring more junior team members is desirable.

Skills & Competencies
• Technically capable and intellectually curious — applies accounting standards with confidence, asks the right questions when uncertain, and takes pride in getting the numbers right. Self-sufficient and organised — manages their own close workload without needing to be chased, meets deadlines consistently and knows when to escalate.

• Accurate and detail-oriented — takes genuine ownership of the quality of their area of the ledger and their reconciliations.

Senior Integrity Engineer, Europe

An inspection shows a client what is wrong. You show them what to do about it.

Are you the integrity engineer people turn to when the inspection data is in and a decision has to be made? Do you enjoy combining fracture mechanics, corrosion growth and sound engineering judgment into advice an operator can actually act on? Then we would like to meet you. We are growing our Integrity team and are looking for our first Senior Integrity Engineer based in Europe.

About Intero

Intero Integrity Services helps pipeline operators and industrial companies keep their assets safe, compliant and running. With our own in-line inspection technology (including MFL and UT) we inspect pipelines and installations all over the world and tell clients exactly what condition their assets are in. Headquartered in Tricht, the Netherlands, we have over 40 years of experience and 650+ professionals from 25+ nationalities.
Learn more about our Inspection service line in this video: Intero - The Power of Integrity.

Your team

You join a close-knit Integrity team of five, including you: a Principal Integrity Engineer and Team Lead in Vancouver, an Integrity Engineer in Mexico City and two Junior Integrity Engineers in Toronto and Calgary. The team is part of our Data Analysis (DA) department.
Together the team delivers integrity reports for clients around the globe. You will be in daily contact with your teammates. The atmosphere is informal, communication is clear and transparent, and the pace follows the workload: some weeks are calm, others are full on. As the first team member in Europe, you strengthen our coverage of European time zones and clients.Why this role matters

An inspection delivers a list of findings. For our clients, especially in highly regulated markets, a list of problems without a solution is not enough. That is where you come in. The Integrity team turns inspection results into a complete solution package: assessments, remaining life, and clear recommendations that help operators make well-founded decisions about the continued operation of their systems. In this role you raise the quality and consistency of that package, review the work of junior engineers, and help develop the tools and methods the team relies on.

What your week looks like

Part of your week goes to performing integrity assessments on pipelines, piping, heaters and boilers. The other part goes to supporting business development, developing methods and giving technical support. From day one you will work on Corrosion Growth (CG) reports and Fitness-for-Service (FFS) assessments.

· Perform Level 1 and Level 2 FFS assessments and advanced Corrosion Growth Analysis (CGA); review or prepare Level 3 FFS assessments where projects require it.

· Review the work of junior engineers, such as Run Comparison reports, dent strain and bending strain analyses, against the applicable codes and standards.

· Act as the technical point of contact for project managers and clients on structural integrity questions, and support proposals and client-facing technical activities.

· Align recommendations with local and national regulations, and build knowledge of codes and standards across jurisdictions.

· Validate and help develop our in-house engineering tools, and write Python or VBA scripts to automate evaluations based on MFL and UT inspection data.

· Set up and maintain internal procedures, technical questionnaires and quality checklists so every deliverable meets client and internal standards.

· Manage several projects at the same time, and flag risks and priorities early.

What you bring

Must-haves

· A degree in Mechanical and/or Materials (or Metallurgical) Engineering, ideally a combination of both. A Master's degree is a strong plus.

· At least 5 years of relevant experience in the structural integrity of pressurised equipment, preferably pipelines, including independently performing and reviewing FFS assessments and remaining life calculations.

· Strong working knowledge of fracture mechanics and corrosion and fatigue damage mechanisms.

· Working knowledge of API 579 / ASME FFS-1, API 530, ASME B31G, DNV-RP-F101, API 1183, ASME VIII Div. 2 and ASME PCC-2, and of the international regulations for pipeline and pressure equipment integrity.

· Experience with risk assessments and turning results into clear, actionable recommendations.

· Strong mathematics and statistics, including probabilistic methods.

· Programming skills to solve engineering problems, preferably in Python, VBA or MATLAB.

· Mid to advanced-level training in integrity assessment methods.

· You write clear, professional technical reports and explain complex topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.

· You work independently with minimal supervision, keep your agreements, and are flexible with working hours to collaborate with colleagues in Canada and Mexico.

· You are curious, proactive and a team player who suggests improvements to help the team work better and avoid rework.

Nice-to-haves

· Hands-on experience with finite element analysis (FEA), preferably ABAQUS.

· Experience with creep assessment of boilers and heaters.

· Exposure to Level 3 FFS assessments.

· Experience with pipeline ILI data analysis (MFL/UT).

· Experience with client-facing technical activities or proposals.

· Experience in highly regulated industries.

Why Intero

· Work that makes a difference. Your recommendations directly determine whether critical pipelines and installations can keep operating safely.

· Variety. Pipelines, piping, heaters and boilers; FFS Level 1 to 3, corrosion growth, dent strain and more, for clients all over the world.

· Real influence. You help shape the team's methods, procedures and in-house tools, and see your ideas put into practice.

· International team, flexible set-up. Daily collaboration with colleagues in Canada and Mexico, remote working from Europe, and once or twice a year a visit to our HQ in Tricht.

· Growth. Within one to three years you can take on a larger share of Run Comparison and FFS reviews and expand into dent strain analysis.

What we offer

· A contract for 32-40 hours per week.

· A competitive salary and benefits package, tailored to the country you're based in. Because pay and conditions vary by location, we'll discuss the details with you personally during the process.

· Remote working from Europe, or hybrid if you live near one of our offices with available space.

· Flexible start of the day between 6:00 and 10:00, with occasional early or late meetings to overlap with our North American team.

Application process

1. Introductory interview with our recruiter.
2. Technical interview with our Principal Integrity Engineer and Team Lead.
3. Final interview with Manager and Business Director.
4. Job offer.

# Careers

We are a focused team of specialists using AI to do better work for large, complex clients, and we are always looking for people who take their craft seriously.

We hire specialists, not generalists. People who are serious about their craft, energised by complex client challenges, and ready to work at the frontier of AI and enterprise technology.

## Why Invoka?

At most firms, AI is a slide in a deck. At Invoka, it is how we work. Every day, across every engagement.

You will use the latest AI tools as a matter of course. Not as a novelty, and not because we told you to, but because they genuinely make you more effective. Less time on admin. More time doing the work that matters.

Our clients are large, complex organisations: global pharma companies, sports governing bodies, manufacturers, and professional services firms. The problems are real, the stakes are high, and the relationships run deep. You will not be handed a script. You will be trusted to think.

We are a focused team, which means the work is visible and the contribution is tangible. What you do here will be seen by clients, by leadership, and in the results.

## What it is actually like here?

We are client-immersed. That means spending time in the room with the people we are helping, understanding how their business works, not just what they asked us to deliver.

It is demanding work. Enterprise transformation does not follow a neat schedule, and our clients operate in high-pressure environments. We hold ourselves to the same standard we ask of them: accountable, rigorous, and calm under pressure.

What people consistently say they value here: the calibre of the work, the trust placed in them early, and the fact that AI tools are treated as genuine professional assets, not perks.

We do not have layers of bureaucracy. If you have a better way of doing something, say so. If a client needs something we have not done before, we figure it out.

## What we believe

### Client Obsession

Our clients do not need another vendor. They need someone who cares about the outcome as much as they do. We stay accountable long after the initial delivery.

### Excellence in Delivery

Good enough is not. We hold high standards on every engagement, not because someone is watching, but because we care about the work.

### Innovation Mindset

We do not use technology for its own sake. We use it because it makes us sharper, faster, and more useful to the people we work with. We stay close to what is changing and apply it with judgement.

### Partnership Approach

We work with clients, not at them. The best outcomes come from genuine collaboration, where we are honest about what we see, and they are honest about what they need.

### Integrity

Transparent with clients. Transparent with each other. No spin, no politics.

## The kind of people who thrive here

The common thread is not a specific background. It is a specific attitude. The people who do well here are:

- Specialists who take their craft seriously
- Comfortable working directly with senior client stakeholders
- Self-directed. They do not wait to be told what to do next
- Curious about AI and already using it in their working practice
- Honest when something is not working, and proactive about fixing it

If you are at a larger firm and frustrated by the gap between what is promised and what is delivered, you will find a different pace here.

- Continuous learning and certification
- Access to the best AI tools
- Career progression from day one
- Flexibility

Tell us what you are looking for and why Invoka. No covering letter template, just say what matters to you.

A direct conversation about your experience, how you work, and what you would bring. We will also tell you honestly what the role looks like in practice.

A short, practical exercise relevant to the role. Not a trick, a real indication of how you think and how you approach problems. We will share what we are looking for in advance.

If it is a fit on both sides, we move quickly.

Job Description

The Core Engineering builds and operates the platforms, applications, data solutions, models, and analytics that power critical processes for The Core divisions of the firm (e.g., Risk, responsible for the risk profile of firm activities; Controllers, responsible for the financial control and reporting obligations; Compliance, responsible for the firm's compliance, regulatory, and reputational risks; Corporate Treasury, responsible for the firm's liquidity, funding, balance sheet, etc.; and Human Capital Management, responsible for attracting, developing, and managing a global workforce). A centralized engineering structure in support of The Core enables a common platform model and operating framework that promotes consistent governance and scalable solutions, leveraging cloud, AI, and machine learning for innovation and efficiency. The Core Engineering's 2,000+ engineers and strats deliver engineering, data, analytics, and quantitative capabilities within six business units:

- Metrics & Analytics Platforms: responsible for the measurement and management of the firm's risk, capital, and liquidity for The Core functions

- The Core Strats: responsible for the development and implementation of models and other quantitative methodologies, including the accuracy and attribution of modeled metrics

- Financials & Reporting: responsible for facilitating the production of the firm's financials and a wide range of reporting functions

- Non-Financial Risk & Controls: responsible for non-financial risk and control processes

- Enterprise Platforms: responsible for platforms and applications that support critical operational processes across The Core such as payments, people processes, and procurement

- Shared Services: responsible for driving the adoption of consistent engineering strategy, including data platforms, cloud, and AI enablement, as well as the management of technology risk

Summary

The Core Engineering Shared Services AI team operates as an internal forward-deployed AI engineering function, embedding with The Core business teams to identify priority workflows, prototype agentic AI solutions, and productionize cloud-native applications that deliver measurable business impact. This hands-on role combines client-facing problem discovery, rapid engineering execution, production AI architecture, and structured transition to receiving teams that will operate and extend the solutions over time.

As an AI Application Engineer, you will work directly with internal business and engineering partners to convert ambiguous operating problems into secure, reliable AI products. You will define where agents should act, where they should assist, and where human approval or control gates are required, then design and deliver solutions that are adopted in real workflows and can be supported in production.

Key Responsibilities

- Rapid Prototyping & Application Delivery: Lead the design, build, deployment, and operationalization of cloud-native AI applications, using modern software engineering practices, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing to accelerate reliable delivery.

- Business Partnership & Solution Architecture: Partner with business and engineering teams to identify high-impact AI opportunities, translate requirements into cloud-optimized architectures, and define scalable data models and technical specifications.

- Forward-Deployed AI Engineering: Embed with The Core business teams to map workflows, identify pain points, assess agentic automation opportunities, define control and approval boundaries, iterate with users, and drive adoption through pilots, feedback loops, and measurable outcomes.

Our team is looking for an Applications Engineer who will enjoy taking the lead on our customer-facing technical work – from first conversations, bids and proposals through to benchmarking and project delivery – and growing within our world-class team.
This is a brand-new role at IONATE. As our Hybrid Intelligent Transformer moves from the lab into utilities, renewables, industrial sites and data centres, you will be the engineer customers turn to first – and you will help shape how applications engineering works here.
This role will suit someone who thrives in a fast-moving, ever-changing environment, where no two days are the same. 
Reporting to the Chief of Staff as part of our Hardware Operations team, and requiring extensive knowledge and experience in power systems and power electronics applications, you will play a key role as the technical bridge between our customers and our engineering teams – supporting sales through bids and proposals, capturing customer requirements, benchmarking the HIT against alternative solutions, and helping carry projects from proposal through to delivery.
What you will do:
Customer-facing technical lead: Act as IONATE's technical voice with utilities, developers, EPCs, industrial and data centre customers – explaining the HIT's capabilities, how it integrates into their systems, and the value it delivers.

A degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).

Hands-on experience contributing technical content to bids, tenders or proposals, including specifications and compliance responses.
Experience gathering and documenting customer requirements and working across sales, engineering and project teams to deliver against them.
The ability to turn complex technical concepts into a clear value proposition for both engineers and commercial decision-makers, in writing and in person.
Familiarity with relevant standards and grid codes.
Strong organisation skills, with the ability to prioritise and juggle several bids and projects at once in a fast-paced environment.
Willingness to travel to customer sites and industry events in the UK and internationally.

job_description:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Role Overview

Role:

IonQ is hiring a Senior Quantum Sales Director to drive new and expansion revenue for Capella Data as a Service (DaaS) and satellite systems across EMEA. You will own a portfolio of strategic enterprise, defence and government accounts, selling SAR imagery and analytics subscriptions, tasking capacity and complete satellite systems, and you will report to Garrick Ballantine.

This is a quota carrying, hunter oriented role for a seller who can run long cycle capital programmes alongside faster moving data subscriptions, and who can translate space based sensing into mission and business outcomes. The role is remote, employed through an IonQ entity in the UK (Oxford) or Switzerland, with travel of up to 20%.

Responsibilities:

You will own an annual new business and expansion quota across Capella DaaS subscriptions, tasking capacity and satellite system sales within an assigned enterprise, defence and civil government territory in EMEA. You will build and execute account plans for a named portfolio, mapping stakeholders across mission, programme, procurement and technical functions and building executive relationships at several levels in each account.

You will sell the full value chain, from SAR data and analytics subscriptions and recurring tasking commitments to ground segment integration and dedicated or jointly owned satellite systems. Working with product, engineering and mission solutions teams, you will bring customer requirements back into the roadmap and represent IonQ at industry, defence and geospatial conferences.

Key responsibilities include:

• Run complex, consultative sales cycles from prospecting through to close, including discovery, technical validation with solutions engineering, pricing, contracting and negotiation of subscription and system purchase agreements.

• Respond to RFIs, RFPs and government tenders in partnership with capture, proposal and contracts teams, and support prime and subcontractor teaming strategies.

• Forecast accurately in CRM, keep disciplined pipeline hygiene and deliver reliable monthly and quarterly commits.

• Develop executive relationships across mission, programme, procurement and technical stakeholders in each account.

• Represent IonQ at industry, defence and geospatial events across EMEA, and feed customer requirements back to product and engineering.

Requirements:

You will bring substantial enterprise sales experience in geospatial data, earth observation, satellite systems, defence technology or adjacent data and SaaS markets, with a consistent record of exceeding quota. You will have closed both recurring data or subscription contracts and large capital or programme based hardware sales, and you will have sold to EMEA and allied government, defence and security customers, with a working knowledge of their procurement frameworks and contracting cycles.

You will have command of a structured sales methodology such as MEDDICC or Challenger, with disciplined CRM and forecasting rigour, and the ability to engage credibly with technical and mission stakeholders on remote sensing, SAR, tasking and data delivery workflows. A bachelor's degree in business, engineering or a related field, and willingness to travel up to 20%, are also required.

You’d be a great fit with:

• Direct experience selling SAR, optical imagery or RF sensing data and analytics.

• A background in satellite systems, ground segment or space mission integration.

• Experience in early market development or category creation for an emerging technology.

• The ability to obtain the relevant national security clearance in your country of employment, such as UK SC or NATO clearance.

• Established relationships with EMEA government, defence or security customers, including NATO and allied programmes.

The total compensation package includes base salary, bonus, equity, and a range of benefits available on our career site.
Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment. 

At IonQ, we believe in fair treatment, access, opportunity, and advancement for all while striving to identify and eliminate barriers. We empower employees to thrive by fostering a culture of autonomy, productivity, and respect. We are dedicated to creating an environment where individuals can feel welcomed, respected, supported, and valued.
 
We are committed to equity and justice. We welcome different voices and viewpoints and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, ancestry, physical and/or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

 

US Technical Jobs. The position you are applying for will require access to technology that is subject to U.S. export control and government contract restrictions.  Employment with IonQ is contingent on either verifying “U.S. Person” (e.g., U.S. citizen, U.S. national, U.S. permanent resident, or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum) status for export controls and government contracts work, obtaining any necessary license, and/or confirming the availability of a license exception under U.S. export controls.  Please note that in the absence of confirming you are a U.S. Person for export control and government contracts work purposes, IonQ may choose not to apply for a license or decline to use a license exception (if available) for you to access export-controlled technology that may require authorization, and similarly, you may not qualify for government contracts work that requires U.S. Persons, and IonQ may decline to proceed with your application on those bases alone.  Accordingly, we will have some additional questions regarding your immigration status that will be used for export control and compliance purposes, and the answers will be reviewed by compliance personnel to ensure compliance with federal law.  

US Non-Technical Jobs. Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Accordingly, we will have some additional questions regarding your immigration status that will be used for export control and compliance purposes, and the answers will be reviewed by compliance personnel to ensure compliance with federal law.

 

If you are interested in being a part of our team and mission, we encourage you to apply!

At IP House, we empower brands, legal professionals, and rights holders to manage and protect intellectual property—both online and offline—on a truly global scale. Through cutting-edge technology and deep cross-border expertise, we deliver scalable, end-to-end solutions for IP portfolio management, enforcement, and content and brand protection.

With over 700 experts operating across five continents, we are trusted by some of the world’s most recognized brands to combat counterfeiting, piracy, and IP infringement at scale. From digital platforms to physical marketplaces, we help clients safeguard what matters most—everywhere it matters.

Overview of the Role:

The IT Administrator manages day-to-day IT operations for IP House’s highly distributed workforce and will work as part of a team with IT Administrators in different regions to together provide coverage across time zones. Working alongside our managed service provider (MSP), the IT Administrator handles escalations, manages the employee technology lifecycle, administers our Microsoft 365 environment and other business applications, and carries out recurring security and compliance work. Participation in a shared on-call rotation is required.

While there is some opportunity for remote work, the IT Administrator is expected to be on-site in our Derby, UK office. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
• Own employee onboarding and offboarding with HR, coordinating accounts, access, and equipment with remote employees across time zones
• Serve as the escalation point and day-to-day contact for our MSP, holding them accountable to agreed service levels
• Administer Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Intune, and other business systems; including access control, MFA, SSO
• Management of Windows and macOS end-user devices, as well as shared technology resources and networks
• Procure, deploy, inventory, and retire hardware, and manage warranty repairs
• Monitor security alerts and apply best practices to protect client and company data
• Complete recurring compliance work such as partner and client security assessments, audit evidence, and incident response testing, and keep IT policies and documentation current
• Identify opportunities for improvement and work with team to standardize and improve IT processes
• Manage licenses, subscriptions, and IT spend, and research new tools and vendors

What You’ll Bring:
• Associate or bachelor’s degree in IT or a related field, or equivalent experience
• At least 3 years of IT administration experience, ideally supporting a distributed workforce
• Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Intune
• Proficiency supporting both Windows and macOS users
• Working knowledge of networking and security fundamentals (e.g., DNS, VPNs, firewalls, MFA, SSO)
• Experience working with MSPs and other IT vendors
• Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work across time zones
• Microsoft certifications, Azure or AWS experience, or PowerShell scripting are a plus
• Ability to lift IT equipment up to 50 pounds and support occasional after-hours or weekend work
We hire qualified candidates who are legally eligible to work in the UK. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.

Why IP House:

IP House is redefining how the world combats illicit trade and intellectual property theft—delivering scalable, end-to-end solutions that empower global brands and rights holders through innovation, strategic expertise, and a relentless commitment to global enforcement.

Achieving this ambitious mission requires the collaboration of an exceptionally talented team. We believe our people are the foundation of everything we do—and we invest accordingly. From day one, we foster a culture rooted in continuous learning, professional growth, and shared excellence.

We also understand that meaningful work begins with a strong foundation. That’s why we offer a flexible work environment and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees and their families.

Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape a fast-scaling organization with a strong reputation for results—and room to grow with it. Join us in safeguarding the brands, content, and innovations that shape our world.

IP House is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to fostering a respectful, collaborative, and inclusive work environment.

QA Analyst
Location: Derby, UK (Hybrid - 5 days per week, minimum 2 days in office)

Position Overview
The QA Analyst supports the Quality Assurance function by reviewing evidential materials produced by the Revenue Recovery investigations team.
Working closely with Investigators and the QA Manager, the role helps ensure evidence generated through test purchases and investigative activities is accurate, complete, and suitable for inclusion within litigation-focused case builds. The position requires strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, and a commitment to maintaining high-quality standards.

Key Responsibilities
Evidence Review and Quality Assurance
• Review evidence generated by Investigators to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
• Verify that evidence packages comply with internal procedures, evidential requirements, and quality standards.
• Review exhibits, screenshots, test purchase documentation, and supporting materials for completeness and accuracy.
• Identify errors, omissions, inconsistencies, or evidential gaps and provide clear feedback to Investigators.
• Ensure evidential materials are appropriately documented and suitable for inclusion within litigation-focused case builds.
• Support the QA Manager in maintaining high evidential standards across the Revenue Recovery function.

Collaboration and Development
• Work closely with Investigators to improve the quality and consistency of evidential submissions.
• Escalate recurring quality issues and observations to the QA Manager.
• Support the implementation of QA processes, procedures, and quality standards.
• Build knowledge of case build processes, evidential requirements, and stakeholder engagement activities to support future progression within the Quality Assurance function.
• Maintain awareness of developments in online enforcement, litigation support, and intellectual property protection.

Administration and Compliance
• Maintain accurate records of QA reviews and findings.
• Assist with reporting and administrative activities where required.
• Ensure all work is completed in accordance with company policies, procedures, and quality standards.

What You'll Bring
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Excellent attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies within large volumes of information.
• Strong written communication skills and ability to provide constructive feedback.
• Good organisational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities.
• Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues across different teams and locations.
• Previous experience in quality assurance, investigations, compliance, legal support, or analytical work.

Why IP House:

IP House is redefining how the world combats illicit trade and intellectual property theft—delivering scalable, end-to-end solutions that empower global brands and rights holders through innovation, strategic expertise, and a relentless commitment to global enforcement.

Achieving this ambitious mission requires the collaboration of an exceptionally talented team. We believe our people are the foundation of everything we do—and we invest accordingly. From day one, we foster a culture rooted in continuous learning, professional growth, and shared excellence.

We also understand that meaningful work begins with a strong foundation. That’s why we offer a flexible work environment and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees and their families.

Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape a fast-scaling organization with a strong reputation for results—and room to grow with it. Join us in safeguarding the brands, content, and innovations that shape our world.

IP House is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to fostering a respectful, collaborative, and inclusive work environment.

Responsibilities
The Advisory Software Architect is a senior strategic leader responsible for defining and driving the enterprise-wide architectural vision across software systems and applications. This role ensures that technology solutions align with business needs while maintaining the highest standards of security, performance, scalability, and quality.
As a trusted advisor to senior leadership, the role influences long-term technology strategy, leads complex transformation initiatives (e.g., Micro Service Architecture and SaaS transformation, cloud adoption, AI integration, technical stack modernisation), and governs architectural consistency across the enterprise and partner ecosystems. The position also plays a key role in shaping industry best practices and representing the organisation externally. 
Enterprise & Ecosystem Architecture
Design and oversee the implementation of enterprise-wide software architecture, spanning internal platforms, cloud environments, and external partner ecosystems
Develop “big picture” architectural frameworks to guide engineering teams and ensure alignment with business strategy
Ensure architectural consistency, scalability, performance, and maintainability across all systems
Strategic Technology Leadership
Influence executive-level decision-making by aligning architectural strategy with evolving business and market needs
Evaluate and recommend emerging tools, technologies, and processes to enhance platform capability and innovation
Define development standards, including technology choices, workflows, and coding practices
Transformation & Modernisation
Lead large-scale technology transformations such as:
Cloud migration and hybrid architecture strategies
Monolith-to-microservices evolution
AI, analytics, and data platform integration
Drive innovation in digital customer experiences within fintech and insurtech domains
Architecture Governance & Risk Management
Establish and lead enterprise architectural governance frameworks
Ensure adherence to security, compliance, regulatory, and quality standards
Identify and mitigate long-term architectural risks (e.g., vendor lock-in, scalability constraints, regulatory exposure)
Technical Design & Solution Development
Conduct research, analyse data, gather requirements, and define end-to-end solutions
Create architectural artefacts representing system functions, integrations, and user interfaces
Provide expert technical guidance and oversight to development teams
Integration & Interoperability
Lead enterprise and ecosystem-wide integration strategies, including APIs, partner platforms, and third-party systems
Ensure seamless interoperability across internal systems and external stakeholders
External Representation & Industry Influence
Represent the organisation at industry forums, regulatory groups, and technical consortiums
Contribute to shaping broader industry architecture standards and best practices
Leadership & Mentorship
Coach and mentor architects and senior engineering leaders across the organisation
Develop internal architectural frameworks, standards, and talent strategies
Foster a strong engineering culture focused on excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement
Product & Platform Initiatives 
Microservice/SaaS Transformation: Lead the transition from monolith and on‑premise solutions to scalable, resilient SaaS platforms, defining tenancy, deployment models, and operational patterns. 
Cloud Modernisation (AWS): Architect and govern migrations to AWS using native services (e.g., serverless, managed databases, API Gateway), ensuring security, performance, and cost efficiency. 
AI Enablement: Enable responsible adoption of AI and GenAI capabilities across the SDLC, including code generation, review, testing, documentation, and deployment automation. Take the technical ownership on implementing AI solutions for product enhancements. 
Cost of Ownership Optimisation: Drive architectural decisions that reduce TCO through right‑sizing, service selection, automation, and platform standardisation. 
Architecture & Governance Processes 
Central Change Governance: Contribute to and lead architecture forums to assess change impact, manage technical risk, and ensure alignment with enterprise strategy.
Technical Design Authority (TDA): Act as a design authority for complex initiatives, reviewing and approving architectures, patterns, and non‑functional requirements.
Security & Compliance by Design: Embed global security best practices into architecture and delivery, ensuring compliance with regulatory and organisational standards.
Pre‑Sales Enablement: Provide architectural leadership for RFI/RFP responses and Proofs of Concept, shaping credible, scalable, and secure technical propositions. 
Qualifications
Core Engineering: .NET Framework and C#, SQL, MVC, REST and SOAP APIs, with strong experience in designing maintainable, testable systems. 
AI‑Assisted Engineering: Practical use of GenAI to accelerate development while maintaining quality, security, and governance standards. 
API & Integration: Headless API design, event‑driven and service‑oriented architectures, and secure integration across distributed systems. 
Cloud & DevOps: AWS‑native architectures, CI/CD automation using GitHub Actions, infrastructure and deployment optimisation. 
Security Engineering: Security‑by‑design mindset with applied knowledge of OWASP Top 10, WCAG, OAuth2, MFA, and secure identity patterns. 
Quality & Assurance: Proficient in unit testing frameworks; governance and execution of SAST, DAST, SCA, and penetration testing processes. 
Benefits
We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, opportunities for career growth, Pension plan with company-matched contributions, generous time off and flexible work/life balance, an employee wellness program, and an awards and recognition program – all in a creative, fast-growing, and innovative company.

As an Associate Director in the Market Strategy & Execution Client Success Team, you will lead strategic research programmes for global clients, helping them make confident decisions about growth, positioning and portfolio strategy.
You will be responsible for leading large multi-market studies, particularly segmentations, demand spaces, usage & attitudes, shopper and brand strategy programmes. Acting as a senior client lead, you will build strong relationships with global and local stakeholders, oversee project delivery in partnership with our Delivery Excellence teams, and ensure insights are translated into clear, actionable business recommendations.
You will also contribute to business growth through proposal development, thought leadership and identifying opportunities within existing client relationships
This role is offered on a hybrid basis with 3 days in our London office and the rest from home.
Your Day to Day
These are the types of things you can expect to be doing during your day to day, although as Ipsos is a dynamic organisation, this may vary as different opportunities arise:
• Lead complex multi-market research programmes from design through to debrief.
• Act as the primary contact for senior client stakeholders.
• Design bespoke research approaches that address strategic business questions.
• Partner with Delivery Excellence teams to ensure smooth and efficient project delivery.
• Develop questionnaires, analytical frameworks and insight development processes.
• Translate data into compelling stories and strategic recommendations.
• Lead reporting, presentations and client workshops.
• Identify opportunities to grow client relationships and support new business.
• Line manage, coach and develop junior team members.
• Collaborate with specialist teams to bring the best of Ipsos capabilities to clients.

Essential Criteria:
To be successful in this role you will need the following skills and experience:
• Significant experience in quantitative market research.
• Strong expertise in market understanding and strategy research, in one or more of segmentation, demand spaces, shopper, brand and usage & attitudes studies.
• Proven experience leading large, multi-country research programmes.
• Strong client leadership and stakeholder management skills.
• Excellent research design, insight generation and storytelling capabilities.
• Experience presenting to and influencing senior client audiences.
• Commercial awareness and experience contributing to proposals and business development.
• Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills.

Desirable Criteria:
These are the skills that would add value to the role but are not critical. If you have them, we’d love to hear about them:
• Experience working on global segmentation and demand space studies.
• Experience across multiple sectors and international markets.
• Familiarity with advanced analytics approaches commonly used in strategic research programmes.

At Iris.ai, we’re building an agentic AI platform that scales expert-level domain knowledge across entire organizations.

For more than a decade, we’ve worked at the intersection of scientific research, industrial data, and applied AI, helping researchers, engineers, and business teams reason over complex technical knowledge.

Our products - Neuralith, Axion, and RSpace - span the full GenAI lifecycle:

- Data ingestion across text, tables, figures, and technical formats
- Advanced RAG and indexing pipelines
- Agentic orchestration and reasoning
- Rigorous LLM evaluation and governance

What makes us different: we care deeply about accuracy, evaluation, and responsibility. We don’t optimize for demos and proof-of-concepts we optimize for systems that experts trust and use.

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior/Lead LLM Researcher to lead Iris.ai’s research around LLM evaluation, model interpretability, and mechanistic interpretation of LLMs.

You’ll define and drive research into how we evaluate, understand, and measure the reliability of LLMs - from answer quality and groundedness to uncertainty, confidence, and model behaviour.

This is a research and leadership role with a strong applied focus. You’ll shape research directions, lead experimentation, and work closely with our engineering and product teams to turn research into products used within the Iris.ai platform.

You’ll also participate in shaping projects for EU and national research funding, leading and co-authoring grant proposals such as Horizon Europe and EIC.

What You’ll Research:

You’ll work on a focused set of high‑impact research directions that sit at the core of modern applied NLP\ML\LLM and agentic systems. You will be making LLM-based systems measurable, interpretable, and trustworthy. The core aspects include:

- LLM evaluation — model grounding (in context, following instructions, following domain knowledge), faithfulness, and task adherence.
- Mechanistic interpretation \- analyzing model behaviour during inference. All our metrics are focused on real-time analysis so they require model analysis during inference, not another LLM call.
- Model interpretability — understanding and explaining model behaviour and outputs.
- Uncertainty & confidence — identifying when outputs can be trusted and when they cannot.
- Evaluation frameworks — developing scalable methods for comparing models, prompts, agents, and whole agentic systems
- Agentic reasoning & control — understanding when models should reason, stop reasoning, or act, including inference‑time steering
- Translation & multilingual NLP — evaluation and system design for modern LLM‑based translation, including low‑resource languages

Your goal will be turning rigorous research into capabilities that real users can trust and use.

What You’ll Do:

- Lead Iris.ai’s research direction around LLM evaluation and interpretability
- Design novel evaluation methods, metrics, and experimental frameworks
- Run rigorous experiments, benchmarking, and ablation studies
- Translate research into prototypes and production capabilities
- Provide scientific guidance to researchers and engineers
- Collaborate closely with product and engineering teams
- Publish research and engage with the AI research community
- Lead and co-author EU and national research grant proposals
- Write and publish research articles
- Supervise interns and master thesis students

Our Tech Stack

- Languages: Python (strong OOP practices)
- ML: PyTorch, Transformers, TensorFlow
- LLMs: Hugging Face, OpenAI, custom and fine‑tuned models
- Systems: RAG pipelines, Multi-agent frameworks, Evaluation tools
- Infra: AWS, Docker, HPC
- Practices: Git, CI/CD, reproducible research workflows

What We’re Looking For:

- PhD in ML, NLP, Computer Science, or a related field

At the same time, you will modernise how HR is delivered in the region. As a key client of our global HR Shared Services, you will own the successful move of transactional and operational work out of the region and keep finding more that can move. You will also champion an AI-enabled way of working, so our team spends its time where it adds the most value: talent, leadership, organisational effectiveness and change.

As a member of the HR Leadership Team, you will help shape global HR strategy, not just execute it regionally. You will represent a key area of transformation for the company and are expected to be a significant contributor and team player.

Responsibilities

Regional leadership, employee relations and compliance
• Act as the senior point of escalation for HR in the region, with high-risk matters escalating to the CHRO, ensuring practices comply with local employment law and global policies.
• Lead, develop and inspire the EMEA HR team (approximately 15 people), and partner with regional specialists such as Talent Acquisition, building a business-focused team with strong succession.
• Manage day-to-day relationships with Works Councils, unions and employee representative bodies, and run consultation processes, with CHRO and Legal oversight on significant changes.
• Manage complex employee relations matters, balancing risk, fairness and business needs, working with Legal and external counsel as appropriate.
• Deliver annual performance, promotion and compensation cycles effectively in the region, in partnership with global Centres of Expertise and Shared Services.
• Design and lead change management for restructuring and integration, making sure change is well planned, well communicated and lands appropriately with employees.
• Help leaders build a high-performing, accountable culture aligned with our values, using engagement and culture insights to drive targeted action.
• Lead the people elements of mergers and acquisitions (M&A) across the region, including due diligence and post-deal integration.

Strategic business partnership
• Serve as the senior HR thought partner to an ELT member, bringing an independent, constructive point of view on people, organisation and culture.
• Help the client organisation operate more effectively and at greater pace, strengthening how it works with commercial and client-facing teams so solutions reach clients faster.
• Understand how the business makes money, its value streams, clients and priorities, and translate these into a clear people plan that the business owns.
• Coach and counsel senior leaders on leadership effectiveness, team dynamics, difficult decisions and how they shape our culture.
• Use people data (engagement, attrition, capability, productivity, cost) to diagnose issues early and recommend practical, evidence-based solutions.

job_description:
## About the role

We are looking for an IT Technician / Helpdesk and Desktop Support to act as the first point of contact for IT issues across TAC Healthcare and deliver the day-to-day IT support that keeps our staff working.

The role supports internal and external stakeholders and works with the organisation’s security and support teams to provide a good service in compliance with ISO standards.

You will support the business’s hardware, software, network, data and communications across its sites, working with third-party providers to deliver quality services to staff and customers.

## What you will do

- Provide first-line helpdesk and desktop support to staff, logging, prioritising and resolving incidents and requests within agreed SLAs.
- Diagnose and troubleshoot software and hardware issues, escalating complex or unresolved problems to the Senior IT Engineer or CTO with clear notes on actions already taken.
- Set up, configure, deploy and maintain desktops, laptops, mobile devices, printers and peripherals.
- Carry out new starter, mover and leaver tasks, including account set-up, access permissions and the issue and return of equipment.
- Support users of Microsoft 365 and key business software, including account, access and multi-factor authentication requests.
- Apply software updates and security patches, and keep device and licence records accurate and up to date.
- Work with third-party providers when incidents or requests need their support, tracking their response to ensure SLAs are met.
- Source and order software and hardware in line with approved budgets and procedures.
- Record fixes and maintain knowledge base articles so that repeat issues are resolved quickly.
- Identify recurring incidents and recommend improvements to the Senior IT Engineer or CTO.
- Support internal audits and compliance checks of IT systems, and help implement agreed actions.
- Handle company, customer and health data in line with company policy and data protection law.
- Report suspected security incidents, such as phishing or lost devices, immediately.
- Help end users reduce avoidable IT incidents and outages through how they use IT equipment.
- Represent TAC Healthcare IT professionally at all times, providing excellent customer service.

This is not an exhaustive list of duties. All members of TAC Healthcare IT may be required to carry out additional reasonable tasks appropriate to their role and capability.

All members of staff are required to participate in appraisals, self-development, and mandatory and statutory training.

## About you

### Essential

You will have:

- A degree or professional qualification in Information Technology or Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
- A minimum of 2 years’ experience in an IT helpdesk, desktop support or similar role.
- Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and common desktop operating systems.
- Good knowledge of computer hardware and software.
- Knowledge of structured troubleshooting practices.
- Experience using an IT service management or ticketing system and working to SLAs.

### Desirable

- Relevant certifications, for example CompTIA A+, ITIL Foundation or Microsoft 365 Fundamentals.
- Experience with mobile device and endpoint management tools.
- Awareness of information security standards such as ISO 27001 and data protection requirements.
- Experience working within a healthcare or other regulated environment.

## Skills and attributes

You will have:

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with a patient and clear approach when helping non-technical users.
- A strong customer service focus.
- Strong prioritisation and organisational skills, with the ability to manage a busy queue of competing requests.
- Strong attention to detail and thoroughness, including accurate record keeping.
- A logical and analytical approach to problem-solving.
- A flexible and adaptable approach, with an interest in learning new technologies.
- The ability to act independently and proactively, while knowing when to escalate.
- A professional, tactful and discreet approach, particularly when handling confidential information.
- A commitment to high standards and to the quality and impact of the service provided.

## What’s in it for you

- Private Medical Insurance.
- Company Pension Scheme.
- Enhanced Annual Leave.
- Parental Leave.
- On-site Parking.
- Employee Assistance Programme, including health, wellbeing and financial support.
- Company Sick Pay Scheme.
- Enhanced Maternity Leave.
- Family and Friends discount on TAC Healthcare services.
- Opportunities for ongoing professional development and progression within occupational health.

The Head of Technology GRC is accountable for the delivery, capability and operational effectiveness of the function.

• Translate the Technology Risk, Governance & Assurance strategy into an effective and sustainable operating model, services, processes and capabilities that are consistently applied across the Group.

• Lead the operation and continuous improvement of technology risk management processes, ensuring technology risks are identified, assessed, reported and managed consistently across the Group.

Area Operations Manager (AOM)
Regional cleaning operations leadership across multiple sites
The Role
The AOM is the person regional cleaning delivery runs on. Rather than being anchored to a single building, you hold a portfolio of contracts – moving between sites, understanding each one's budget and client relationship, and stepping in wherever standards need lifting. When a Site Manager hits something they can't resolve alone – a client escalation, a sudden gap in cover, a KPI slipping – you're the person they call, and you bring the regional mobile team with you when extra hands are needed.
You're responsible for implementing the strategic direction of cleaning operations across your patch, and for making sure every site under your remit reflects an engaged, positive team culture in line with JLL's vision and values.
Key Responsibilities
Leadership
You lead the cleaning teams across your sites, working to create a positive, motivational and supportive working environment wherever you go. That means advanced planning of all cleaning operations – including periodic tasks with clear schedules and sign-off – so nothing falls through the cracks between sites. You put real focus into training and developing teams, building good working practices with a vision that covers both the cleaning operation itself and the customer experience it creates. Excellence has to show up consistently: security, health and safety, compliance, cleaning standard, colleague appearance and presentation (a full, clean uniform, every time), and the everyday courtesy of guest and staff interaction.
Best Practice and Innovation
You're the professional point of support for the business on service-related and contractual matters, holding high standards while staying flexible enough to meet changing operational needs – and you're expected to suggest new initiatives that keep improvement and best practice moving. Cleaning feedback and complaints are yours to own through to conclusion, and you work closely with stakeholders and departments across the business to add value and promote teamwork throughout.
On the operational side, you manage and report on cleaning budgets across your sites with full transparency, including forecasting, and you control the delivery of colleagues' rosters to ensure compliance is always maintained. You lead the team in managing absence and holiday records – sickness and annual leave included – organising non-agency cover wherever possible to avoid staff and qualitative shortfalls. Monthly audits are run to keep cleanliness and safety standards high, and you manage recruitment, induction, development and retention so that good people stay.
Quality and compliance sit at the centre of the role: adequate performance measures (KPIs and SLAs) are adhered to, with any failures resolved professionally and clear next steps made visible to all; quality audits are conducted to ISO9001 requirements; and strict compliance with the Data Protection Act, GDPR and associated regulations is non-negotiable. Day to day, that means delivering excellent leadership, communication and motivation to each site-based team, communicating daily so a sound channel exists for team goals to be achieved – and making sure each on-site Supervision Team is fully conversant with their individual tasks and responsibilities, even when you're not physically there.
Team Management
You lead and support your direct reports in an engaged, positive manner, and hold them to delivering exceptional operational standards alongside genuinely meaningful building user interaction. Working with the Senior Leadership Team and Operations Management, you forward-plan staffing to ensure capacity is met – paying particular attention to how the service scales during peak periods without sacrificing SLAs. Every team member should feel valued: annual job chats identify who wants to progress their career, and you work with HR and L&D to put development plans in place where possible. You also work alongside HR and L&D to deliver Customer Experience training for colleagues, participating yourself where necessary, and identify training needs for your direct reports so the SLT can shape training plans for the wider cleaning and operational team.
Communication
Effective operational communication – meetings, handovers, reporting – has to run smoothly across every site you cover. You attend daily, weekly and monthly business progress meetings and team meetings as required, and deliver concise, clear written reports that aid company communication both internally and externally. Confidentiality is absolute: when communicating with a client, you make sure internal JLL information is never shared.
Brand Enhancement
You ensure your own behaviour and your team's reflects the JLL Brand and Culture, and you actively look for opportunities to drive a more sustainable service. The aim throughout is to consistently exceed customer expectations and deliver long-term, sustainable customer satisfaction.

• Staff attrition rate below the National/Company standard

• Number of client compliments and complaints
• All mandatory training up to date
• Monthly Toolbox talks delivered and evidenced
• H&S tours up to date
• Agency targets adhered to
• Contract KPIs achieved

## About the role

#### JUMPSEC is building a specialist Continuous Recon capability to help clients understand and reduce the security risks visible across their external digital footprint.

This is not a traditional vulnerability scanning role, and it is not a dashboard-watching role. Continuous Recon is about seeing organisations from an attacker’s perspective, investigating what is exposed, validating what matters, and turning ambiguous external signals into clear, actionable security insight.

As a Recon Engineer, you will work at the intersection of external attack surface discovery, vulnerability validation, OSINT, threat intelligence, and exposure analysis. You will investigate internet-facing assets, identify unknown or unmanaged infrastructure, validate potential weaknesses, and help clients understand which issues create meaningful risk.

You will be joining the service at an important stage in its growth. That means you will not simply inherit a static operating model. You will help shape how Continuous Recon works, how we investigate findings, how we validate exposure, how we report to clients, and how we build scalable research-led capability over time.

This role is well suited to someone who enjoys recon, external attack surface analysis, bug bounty methodologies, exposure research, internet infrastructure, and the process of turning scattered technical clues into a coherent picture. If you spend time thinking about how attackers enumerate targets, how exposed services can be chained together, how forgotten assets become initial access opportunities, or how to validate findings safely and defensibly, you will likely feel at home in this team.

The right person will combine technical curiosity with operational discipline. You will need to be comfortable with ambiguity, able to investigate independently, and capable of communicating findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

## About Continuous Recon

Continuous Recon is JUMPSEC’s managed external reconnaissance and exposure reduction service.

The service gives clients a continuously maintained attacker’s-eye view of their external estate. It combines asset discovery, exposure monitoring, vulnerability validation, dark web and open-source intelligence, and analyst-led investigation to help clients reduce externally visible risk before it becomes an incident.

Continuous Recon helps clients answer questions such as:

- What can attackers see from the outside?
- Which assets are unknown, unmanaged, or unexpected?
- Which exposures are genuinely meaningful?
- Which findings require urgent action?
- Where are we seeing recurring exposure patterns?
- Is our external risk reducing over time?

The service is designed to go beyond raw scanner output. Our focus is on validation, prioritisation, evidence, and actionable client outcomes.

A successful Recon Engineer will:

- Identify meaningful external exposure that clients may not otherwise have seen.
- Validate findings carefully and avoid creating noise.
- Produce clear evidence that supports technical conclusions.
- Help clients understand what matters and what to do next.
- Improve the quality, consistency, and scalability of the Continuous Recon service.
- Contribute to external threat hunts, research-led investigation, and reusable validation capability.
- Build trust with colleagues and clients through strong judgement, clear communication, and reliable delivery.

Quality Assurance Engineer
Engineering · India · Full-time, remote
Why this role exists
Every day, thousands of people in the UAE and Saudi Arabia rely on Justlife to get things done at home—cleanings booked, maintenance sorted, life simplified. Behind that simplicity is a quality promise: the service they book works, the app doesn't break, the experience is seamless. When a bug slips to production, someone's day gets harder. When quality breaks down, trust breaks down.
This is a hands-on QA role that sits at the heart of scaling Justlife's engineering organisation. We're growing our development team and launching new product lines, which means testing complexity is rising fast. You'll own the quality gate across mobile, web, and backend systems—catching bugs before customers do, working shoulder-to-shoulder with developers to fix root causes, and building the AI-driven testing practices that let us scale without compromise. Your headline metric: “minimising defects that escape to production while identifying and resolving bugs faster as engineering capacity grows.”
You'll love this role if you...
• You think like a detective—you don't just run test cases, you ask "why would this break?" and find the edge cases nobody else sees
• You're genuinely curious about AI and automation, and you actively use these tools to work smarter, not just faster
• You thrive in startup chaos and actually enjoy changing priorities, evolving processes, and building things that didn't exist before
• You believe quality is everyone's job—you push back constructively on vague requirements, challenge assumptions, and help developers ship better code
• You measure yourself by outcomes (bugs caught, speed to resolution, process improvements shipped) not just activity
What you'll own
• “Drive defect escape rates down and resolution velocity up” by mastering Justlife's products, designing test scenarios across mobile/web/backend, and investigating root causes that developers can actually fix
• Participate in product and technical grooming—be the voice that asks "what could go wrong here?" and identifies risks before development starts
• Collaborate with our Automation team to expand test coverage, improve regression suites, and identify which tests should be automated versus manual
• Own the testing and verification for assigned Scrum commitments—regression, exploratory, integration, and end-to-end testing as needed
• Leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate test scenario creation, analyse requirements for gaps, and reduce repetitive manual work—then share what you learn with the team
• Build strong working relationships with developers and cross-functional partners (Product, Business, Automation)—be the QA engineer they want in their grooming sessions
• Identify and implement at least one AI-driven QA initiative by month six, measure its impact, and present it to the wider Engineering organisation
What tells us you're the one
• You've “measurably improved a quality outcome across a real product or service”—tell us about a testing initiative you led, an automation effort you contributed to, or a bug-finding approach you designed that moved a specific metric (defects caught, time-to-resolution, test coverage, automation percentage, whatever matters in your context)
• You've worked in a startup or fast-paced tech environment and can show us how you adapted to changing priorities and ambiguity without losing ownership
• You have 2+ years of hands-on QA experience with demonstrated strength in test design, bug lifecycle management, and root-cause analysis—we care more about what you've shipped than years on a CV
• You've used AI tools practically in your QA or development work (not just read about them)—show us a concrete example of how you applied AI to improve testing, analysis, or productivity
• You understand automation concepts and test frameworks (Playwright, Selenium, Appium, or similar)—direct automation coding is nice to have, but you must speak the language and can collaborate effectively with automation engineers
• You work in a startup or complex product environment where you've seen mobile, web, and backend systems interact, and you understand the testing implications
Why Justlife
• Scale and impact: Your testing covers thousands of daily app sessions, multiple platforms (iOS, Android, web), and backend services that power home services across two countries—the quality bar you set affects real people's days
• Real growth: You'll move from IC2 to IC3 and beyond by owning QA initiatives, building AI-driven practices, and becoming the go-to quality partner for engineering teams
• A collaborative culture: You'll work closely with developers, product managers, and automation engineers who actually listen to QA and see quality as shared responsibility
• Startup spirit plus stability: birthday day off (JustHoliday), free Justlife credits, referral bonuses, team experiences, and a fair, transparent performance system with recognition through our JustHeroes program
