As AI, machine intelligence and agentic technologies reshape how research is discovered and consumed, we have a responsibility to ensure knowledge remains both discoverable and protected. 

About the role 
The way academic research is communicated is changing rapidly. Increasingly, Springer Nature content is being accessed through search engines, discovery platforms, AI-powered services, machine agents and content aggregation ecosystems. This creates significant opportunities to extend the reach and impact of research, but also introduces new challenges around content extraction, automated access, platform stability and commercial value protection. 

The Platform Engineer - Content Protection role sits within the Off-platform Discovery and Content Protection team and is responsible for turning analytical insight and content protection strategy into operational controls. Working closely with the Data Analyst, Product Manager, Managed Security Services, SEO teams, Product teams and Platform Engineering teams, this role owns the design, implementation and operation of traffic management and content protection controls. 

The role is responsible for ensuring Springer Nature can maximise discoverability while protecting content, platform performance and future business models. You will continuously evolve controls and responses to address emerging forms of automated access, including AI-driven and agentic technologies, while ensuring legitimate users retain access to our platforms and content. 

Responsibilities

Content Protection Execution & Operational Ownership 
• Build, operate and continuously improve WAF signals, policies and rules that detect and mitigate automated scraping, content extraction and abusive traffic. 
• Own the lifecycle of traffic protection controls including design, testing, deployment, tuning, validation and retirement. 
• Implement rate-limiting, bot-management and traffic-shaping strategies aligned to business objectives and platform requirements. 
• Ensure protection controls are effective without negatively impacting legitimate discoverability, accessibility or customer experience. 
• Turn analytical signals and intelligence into practical enforcement controls and measurable operational outcomes. 

Incident Management & Response 
• Lead response activities relating to scraping, automated abuse, enumeration and traffic-related incidents. 
• Maintain operational playbooks and runbooks for detection, escalation, mitigation and recovery. 
• Implement controls using staged rollout approaches, balancing risk reduction with customer impact. 
• Monitor effectiveness of controls and continually improve protection capabilities. 

Fastly Partnership & Vendor Management 
• Own the day-to-day technical relationship with Fastly MSS and associated content protection tooling. 
• Review, validate and operationalise Fastly recommendations and outputs. 
• Work with Fastly to maximise value from platform capabilities and identify future improvement opportunities. 
• Coordinate changes with stakeholders and communicate impacts, dependencies and implementation plans. 

Cross-functional Collaboration & Future Capability Development 
• Partner closely with the Data Analyst to operationalise detection signals and validate outcomes. 
• Work with SEO teams to ensure legitimate crawlers and discovery services remain appropriately supported. 
• Support Product and Platform teams with traffic-aware architectural decisions. 
• Help define organisational policies relating to acceptable, non-desirable and malicious automated access. 
• Contribute to future approaches for managing AI agents, machine access and emerging content consumption models. 

What's Expected 
In 1–3 Months: 
• Build strong relationships with Managed Services vendor, Product, Platform Engineering, SEO and Analytics stakeholders. 
• Develop an understanding of existing WAF configurations, controls and operating processes. 
• Review recent incidents and identify immediate improvement opportunities. 
• Begin establishing operational playbooks and governance processes. 

By 3–6 Months you will: 
• Establish repeatable workflows for traffic anomaly detection and response. 
• Create clear ownership and decision-making processes for content protection activities. 
• Reduce engineering involvement in reactive mitigation activities. 
• Deliver measurable improvements in response capability and operational readiness. 

By 6–12 Months you will: 
• Operate a mature content protection capability integrated into platform operations. 
• Develop trusted partnerships with Fastly and internal stakeholders. 
• Improve protection against both high-volume and slow accumulation content extraction techniques. 
• Lay the foundations for managing AI-driven and agentic access patterns at scale. 
• Help Springer Nature balance discoverability, content protection and future commercial opportunities. 

Essential Skills & Experience 
• Hands-on WAF engineering experience, ideally with Fastly Next-Gen WAF (Signal Sciences) or equivalent platforms. 
• Experience implementing bot management, rate limiting and traffic management controls.

We devise creative solutions to problems, find new ways of doing things, and trust colleagues who are doing so too. We are brave and feel empowered to take the initiative. We ask ourselves: is what I’m doing authentically Macs?

• Tread thoughtfully: We are considerate, empathetic and try to put ourselves in our customers’, suppliers’ and each other’s shoes. We support local, and find ways of having less negative impact on the planet. We find ways of having positive impact on people and communities. We are fair, and we do the right thing.

• Go the extra mile: We know that creating a perfect #MacsMoment involves going that bit further. We imagine the best feedback we can get and set out to earn it. We take ownership and accountability – it’s yours, not someone else’s, problem. We step up and help our team mates when they need us.

What you’ll do;

Our digital products play a vital role in how customers discover, book and experience their Macs adventures, as well as how our teams work behind the scenes. From our website and app to our data products and internal systems, we want to make sure we're investing in the right things, solving the right problems and continuously improving how our platforms perform.

As Head of Software Product, you'll bring together customer needs, business priorities and technical possibilities to shape what we deliver and why. You'll lead our product team, work closely with colleagues across Macs and our external development partners, and make sure we turn great ideas into improvements that deliver measurable results.

Here's where you'll make an impact:

• Own our product strategy and roadmap – setting a clear product vision and prioritised roadmap across our website, app, data products and back-office systems. You'll turn our wider business strategy into product priorities, making sure investment decisions balance customer value, commercial impact and technical feasibility.

• Lead product delivery from start to finish – overseeing the full product lifecycle, from understanding problems and exploring solutions through to launch, ongoing improvements and retirement. You'll balance competing priorities, manage dependencies and resources, and ensure we deliver against agreed plans and budgets.

• Improve the performance of our digital platforms – driving continuous improvements across our website, app, data and internal systems to make them more reliable, scalable and effective. You'll use customer insight, data and experimentation to identify opportunities, working closely with Engineering to manage technical constraints, architecture and technical debt.

• Deliver measurable customer and commercial results – using product improvements to increase online conversion, improve customer experience and retention, and support revenue growth. You'll build clear business cases for product investment and use data and customer feedback to measure the impact of what we deliver.

• Lead and develop our product team – building a high-performing team of product specialists, developing their skills and raising standards across product discovery, prioritisation and delivery. You'll create a culture of ownership, accountability and continuous improvement.

• Work across the business and with our development partners – collaborating with Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, Operations, Customer Service and Commercial teams to deliver shared priorities. You'll manage relationships with external development partners and suppliers, ensuring delivery meets business needs, whilst keeping senior stakeholders informed of progress, priorities and risks.

• Bring clarity to priorities, resources and delivery – establishing clear ways of prioritising work and managing product investment across the portfolio. You'll oversee product backlogs, sprint planning and reviews, whilst proactively managing budgets, resources, risks and dependencies to keep delivery on track.

What you’ll bring;

• Experienced product leader – 8–10+ years in product management, including experience leading and scaling product teams.

• Proven product strategy experience – a track record of owning end-to-end product strategy and roadmaps across customer-facing, data and back-office products.

• Strong product lifecycle management – experience across product vision, roadmapping, prioritisation, delivery and managing dependencies and resources.

• Experience working with external partners – comfortable managing a mix of in-house teams and external development partners or agencies.

• Strong technical collaboration – experience partnering with engineering teams in agile development environments.

• Experienced people leader – a track record of leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, including Product Managers, Product Owners and Business Analysts.

• Strong commercial awareness – able to connect product investment decisions to measurable business outcomes.

• Data-driven approach – confident using data, analytics and experimentation to inform product decisions.

• Excellent stakeholder management – able to influence senior leaders, build strong relationships and align priorities across the business.

Not essential, it would be a bonus if you have;

• Experience in ecommerce, travel or consumer digital platforms

The knowledge and skills we’ve listed represent “the perfect candidate”. No one’s perfect and we know the ‘confidence gap’ can stop brilliant people applying. If you love the sound of this opportunity please apply, we’d love to hear from you.

You could belong here;

To deliver adventures for more than 40,000 customers we need to build a company that’s reflective of their diversity. We’re building an inclusive workplace that promotes and values difference, where everyone, from any background, can do their best work and be proud to belong.

What we’ll offer

As well as your salary;

• GETTING TOGETHER: Regular team, management and leadership meetings and retreats.

• CULTURE: An innovative, fast growth, international and solution focused culture, where we work hard to embed our values across the business.

job_description:
Company Description

Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money. 
Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money. 
For everyone, everywhere.

More about our mission and what we offer.

Job Description

We are the Global KYC and Onboarding squad in the Servicing department and we have a mission: to enable teams at Wise to expand and fine-tune the business in a "config change" manner all across the globe, while remaining compliant and safe for the customers. There are three teams in the squad: Business Onboarding Verification, Personal Onboarding Verification and Wise Platform Verification (our B2B platform).

The scale we operate at: In FY2025, 15.6 million people and businesses used Wise, we onboarded over 5.9 million new customers (~500k/month), and moved £145.2bn across borders (~£400m/day) across 160+ countries and 40+ currencies. Our verification systems aren't supporting tools — they're core production infrastructure that protects customers, enables growth, and must stay reliable under constant change in regulations, policies, and evolving threat patterns.

All of the teams are diverse, cross-functional groups passionate about solving complex problems with elegant solutions. We bring together backend and frontend engineers, mobile developers, designers, data analysts, and product managers who collaborate closely to deliver exceptional customer experiences. Our teams are responsible for the critical verification journeys that business and personal customers complete before using Wise's products. We own the entire verification lifecycle – from document collection flows and automated review systems to agent tooling and compliance monitoring. We operate with high ownership in a bottom-up, transparent culture, make data-driven decisions, and celebrate both technical excellence and customer impact. Right now we're focused on building KYC/FinCrime as a configuration-driven product, refactoring and building new scalable microservice systems, and increasing automation using ML/AI where it genuinely improves decisioning, review quality, and operational efficiency — with safe fallbacks and clear observability. As a team that touches both regulatory requirements and customer experience, we have unique opportunities to innovate in a space traditionally resistant to change.

By joining one of our teams, you'll directly impact these customers by transforming a traditionally frustrating experience into one that's fast, intuitive, and fair. Your code will help individuals and small businesses access global banking faster, enable entrepreneurs to pay international employees on time, and allow people like you and your teammates support their families across borders without friction. We're not just building verification systems – we're removing barriers that stand between our customers and their financial freedom.

We need like-minded engineers in all the teams in the squad, so we'll use the interview process to discover where your unique skills shine brightest. Ultimately, we want to match you with the team that perfectly aligns with your experience and sets you up for success!

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will own large-sized, impactful projects within the domain. Your responsibilities span end-to-end:

- You will own the technical roadmap for your areas of ownership, ensuring they address important technical debt, reliability, scalability, and security concerns.
- You will be instrumental in designing and implementing robust backend systems that provide clean APIs and interfaces to hide the internal complexity.
- You will drive the integration with various risk and mitigation systems to ensure that Wise is compliant.
- You will take initiative to identify and solve impactful problems both within your team and beyond, contributing to high-impact cross-team initiatives.

What we expect from you:

- You have 4+ years of experience working with any language, asynchronous message queues (e.g., Kafka, RabbitMQ), and have architected and built highly scalable microservices.
- A strong product mindset and a deep passion for both customer experience and regulatory compliance.
- You will prioritize work with a holistic view of the customer and business impact, making data-driven decisions to solve complex, ambiguous problems.
- Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical and architectural concepts clearly to diverse audiences, including product managers, designers, and other engineering teams.
- You demonstrate a commitment to writing clean, testable, maintainable, and highly performant code, and you are a strong advocate for best coding practices and rigorous code reviews.
- Proven ability to identify and lead the technical delivery of large-scale, organisationally-complex projects, adept at anticipating and escalating organizational blockers.
- Extensive experience working with relational and non-relational databases, including advanced query optimization, schema design, and data lifecycle management for sensitive information.

What does success look like?

- You’ll have deeply embedded yourself within our mission, owning and delivering quarterly goals for the team, significantly impacting our ability to scale and improve verification processes.
- You’ll own the technical roadmap for your areas, ensuring it supports both immediate delivery needs and long-term strategic objectives, including addressing technical debt and improving system health.
- You’ll leverage your expertise to identify the right solutions to solve ambiguous, open-ended problems, driving tough prioritization decisions that deliver clear business and customer value.
- You’ll consistently define and implement technical solutions or efficient operational processes that level up your team and contribute beyond it, mentoring other engineers and sharing best practices.
- You’ll inspire a high-performing team environment where ideas are shared, technical excellence is pursued, and continuous learning is embraced.

Additional Information

For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.

We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.

If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.

Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

Full Stack Senior Developer

Help make accounting autonomous by owning features end-to-end across the platform that delivers real accounting for 1000+ businesses.
Team: Product engineering
Reports to: Founders & CEO
Location: Remote worldwide, or in person in the UK
Level: Senior (4+ years)
Type: Full-time

Our mission
Software should do the work. People should do the judgement.
Accounting software is a $23bn market. Accounting services, the actual work of bookkeeping, tax, compliance and advisory, is $720bn. Thirty times bigger, and still done by hand.
Every generation has moved that work somewhere new: paper, then spreadsheets, then the cloud. Each step made it quicker to record; none made it stop being work. We're building the platform that does it instead, with people in the loop only where judgement genuinely matters. We serve small and mid-sized businesses today.
Software has only ever given accountants a better place to do the work by hand. We're taking out the by hand.
What you'd be building
We didn't build software for accounting firms to buy. We own one, and we're automating it from the inside.
Clients don't buy a tool from us and then do their own books. They hire us to do their accounting, and more of that work is done by the platform every month, with qualified people reviewing what matters. The firm is how we reach clients and how we prove the software works. The direction of travel is the software doing nearly all of it.
The product runs all of it: client and lead management, document intake and OCR, invoice and bill processing, an internal double-entry ledger, VAT / MTD / ITSA / CIS compliance, billing, and a client portal. It's deeply integrated with the UK accounting and tax ecosystem, and increasingly driven by AI agents: document extraction, invoice automation, and an in-app assistant.
That structure is why the engineering is different here. We're not shipping a tool and hoping a firm adopts it. We run our own operation on it, so every manual step left in the product is a cost we pay ourselves, and every automation you ship shows up in the business the same week. There's no gap between shipping something and finding out whether it worked.
You'd work on both sides of it: the internal tooling our accountants and bookkeepers work in, and the client-facing product clients log into. This is not a prototype. The firm runs on it today, serving 1000+ businesses, with over £100M in transactions handled and 99.9% uptime. The numbers it produces get filed to HMRC, so correctness is not optional.
The team you'd join
You'd be joining a lean team of accountants, bookkeepers, and full-stack software developers, and working closely with the Founders and CEO directly.
That mix is the point. The people who know how UK accounting actually works sit on the team, and our own practice runs on what we ship, so a domain question gets answered in minutes instead of waiting on a spec, and you can watch someone use the feature you deployed this morning. You don't need to arrive knowing any of it. You do need to want to learn it.
What we need is a senior generalist who can own a feature end-to-end, from the UI through the service layer to the external integration and the background job behind it, and ship it to production without hand-holding. You add throughput and a senior voice in architecture reviews.
What you'll own
• Own features end-to-end. Take a product outcome (e.g. "clients can categorise bank transactions from the portal", "auto-create a payment when an invoice is published") and deliver the whole vertical slice: schema, service logic, API, UI, background jobs, and the integration touchpoints.
• Work across the whole stack. Roughly balanced frontend and backend: typed React on one side, Python services on the other, with background jobs and third-party integrations in between. You should be comfortable living in any of these on a given day.
• Own the external integrations. Build and maintain sync flows, webhook handling, and the data-mapping that keeps our ledger and the accounting and tax platforms we connect to in agreement. Get the edge cases right. This is where correctness bugs hide.
• Contribute to the AI-agent surface. Extend document-extraction and automation workflows built on our agent framework, and the shared service layer they call into.
• Raise the bar on quality. Write tests for the correctness-critical paths, review teammates' PRs, and help us catch phasing and edge-case errors before they reach production.
• Take architecture load off the founders. Be a senior person who can be handed an ambiguous problem and come back with a sound design, not just an implementation.
Our stack
LayerWhat we use
BackendModern typed Python: async web framework, ORM, background workers
FrontendReact / TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS, a component library
MobileiOS and Android apps
DataA relational database with versioned migrations, plus a cache
AuthA managed auth provider, with atomic RBAC
IntegrationsAccounting platforms (Xero), HMRC (MTD / ITSA / VAT / CIS), Outlook, Gmail, banking data, WhatsApp
AIAgent orchestration, tool servers, and tracing
InfraManaged cloud hosting, Docker, a monorepo with a service-layer architecture

You do not need every item on this list on day one. You do need to be genuinely strong on one of the Python backend or the typed React frontend, and competent and eager on the other.
What we're looking for
The people who do well here don't wait to be handed tickets. You get an outcome and the room to work out the design, the edge cases and everything it takes to get it live, then come back with something better than the brief. What follows is the technical floor, not the job.
Required
• 4+ years building and shipping web applications, with real ownership of features in production (not just tickets handed to you).
• Strong in both a modern typed frontend (React/TypeScript) and a Python web backend. Even if you lean one way, you can hold your own on the other.
• Solid relational-database fundamentals: schema design, migrations, writing and reasoning about non-trivial SQL, and thinking about data integrity.
• Experience integrating third-party APIs (webhooks, OAuth, sync reconciliation, handling partial failure).
• A demonstrable care for correctness: you write tests for the paths that matter, you think about edge cases and idempotency, and you don't ship money-affecting code on a hunch.
• Comfortable working remotely and asynchronously in a small team with high autonomy.
Strong bonus
• Experience with accounting, fintech, tax, or other financial-data systems, anywhere a wrong number has real consequences. Familiarity with double-entry bookkeeping, VAT, or the UK accounting-software ecosystem is a significant edge.
• Experience building on or integrating LLM / AI-agent frameworks (agent orchestration, tool use, RAG) beyond calling an API.
• Background-job systems, event-driven architecture.
• You've been an early engineer at a startup and know how to move fast without leaving a mess.
Not required
• A CS degree. We care about what you can build and how you reason, not your credential.
• Experience with our exact stack. We care that you're genuinely strong somewhere and quick everywhere else.
How we work
This suits people who want a lot of rope. There are few meetings, no ticket queue and nobody tracking your progress. That's freedom if you're self-directed, and uncomfortable if you'd rather be handed a plan.
• Latest practices, no ceremony. We work with current tooling and change it the moment something better comes along. If you've found a faster way to work, you don't need permission to adopt it. What matters is what ships and whether it's right, not whether it followed convention.
• Small, senior, high-trust. Direct access to the founders and to real users. No product manager relaying requirements, no layer between you and the people whose books this affects.
• Correctness culture. We review each other's plans and PRs. We'd rather catch the edge-case bug in review than after it has shipped.
How to apply
Send a CV plus a short note on one non-trivial full-stack feature you owned end-to-end: what the product problem was, the design decisions and trade-offs you made across the stack, and how you made sure it was correct. Links to shipped work or code we can look at are worth more than a long CV.

The current data estate is heavily SQL Server based. A lot of important operational and reporting logic lives in large stored procedures, views, functions, scheduled jobs and established ETL processes. Some of that SQL is complex, old and tightly coupled to business processes, so being able to read, diagnose and safely change it is a core part of the job.
Alongside that we have Power BI, on-premises gateways, Azure services and integration flows that need to keep working while we modernise. The destination is a much clearer Microsoft Fabric platform with governed data products, bronze/silver/gold layers and less dependence on opaque stored-procedure logic, but we need to get there without losing the business knowledge embedded in the current estate.
What you will be responsible for
SQL and the esisting data estate
• Build, support and improve complex SQL Server solutions used by operational systems, reporting and integrations.
• Work confidently with large stored procedures, views, functions, dynamic SQL, temp tables, table variables and established T-SQL patterns.
• Read and understand stored procedures that may contain a significant amount of business logic before changing or replacing them.
• Troubleshoot slow or unreliable SQL using execution plans, indexing, statistics, blocking/waits and query-level diagnostics.
• Refactor high-risk or difficult SQL pragmatically, preserving business behaviour while improving maintainability, performance and testability.
• Support data migrations, reconciliations, extracts and operational data fixes where correctness and traceability matter.
• Understand dependencies between operational databases, replicas, reporting workloads, integrations and downstream consumers before making changes.

Data engineering and integration
• Design and maintain reliable ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest, transform and publish data from operational and third-party systems.
• Combine data from multiple systems into trusted reusable datasets for reporting, analytics and operational processes.
• Build and support integrations using SQL, APIs, files and appropriate Azure data or messaging services.
• Design transformations that are testable, repeatable and observable rather than hidden in manual processes.
• Work closely with Software Engineering where data movement is part of an application or integration flow.
• Handle schema changes, late-arriving data, retries, reconciliation and error handling as normal engineering concerns.

Data quality, modelling and reporting
• Build validation and reconciliation into pipelines so problems are identified early and traced back to source.
• Investigate data-quality issues and work with system owners to fix root causes, not just patch reports.
• Work with BI colleagues to provide well-structured data for Power BI and semantic models.
• Understand the effect that model, query and refresh design has on report performance, SQL workload and gateway load.
• Design dimensional or analytical models where appropriate, with clear grain, keys and business definitions.
• Document important data definitions, lineage, ownership and transformation logic.

Engineering Practice
• Use Git, peer review and CI/CD for database and data-platform changes wherever practical.
• Automate deployment, validation and monitoring rather than relying on manual scripts and undocumented steps.
• Apply appropriate security, access, retention and privacy controls to healthcare and business data.
• Support incidents and production issues with clear root-cause analysis and follow-through.
• Treat data pipelines and SQL code as production software, with testing, observability and controlled change.

Technology you will work with now
• Microsoft SQL Server and very strong T-SQL, including large and complex stored procedures, dynamic SQL, views, functions, scheduled/database-driven processing and performance tuning.
• On-premises SQL Server workloads, replicas and legacy database patterns that support live operational processes and reporting.
• SSIS, SQL-driven ETL and other established Microsoft data-integration approaches that remain part of the current estate.
• Power BI, semantic models and on-premises data gateways.
• Azure SQL and Azure data/integration services.
• Azure Data Factory or comparable orchestration tooling.
• Logic Apps, APIs, file-based integrations and messaging patterns such as Azure Service Bus where appropriate.
• Git and Azure DevOps for source control, work management and delivery pipelines.

Where we are heading
• Microsoft Fabric as the strategic analytics platform.
• OneLake with governed Lakehouse and Warehouse patterns using a bronze/silver/gold approach.
• Power BI built on curated semantic models rather than direct dependence on operational databases or replicas.
• Fabric Data Factory and pipelines with stronger orchestration, monitoring and automated deployment.
• Python, notebooks and Spark/PySpark where they are the right tool for modern analytical workloads.
• Direct Lake and other Fabric-native patterns where they provide a genuine benefit.
• Better automated data-quality checks, lineage, metadata, ownership and platform governance.
• Reduced dependency on large opaque stored procedures over time, without destabilising the operational systems that rely on them.
• Progressive migration away from on-premises gateways and legacy analytical components as the platform matures.

What we are looking for
• Very strong SQL Server and T-SQL skills. This is essential, not a nice-to-have.
• Real experience supporting complex production SQL, including large stored procedures, dynamic SQL, query tuning and difficult data problems.
• Experience building and supporting ETL/ELT pipelines and production data integrations.
• A good understanding of relational and analytical data modelling, data quality and how reporting consumers use engineered data.
• Experience with Azure data services and Power BI or closely related Microsoft technologies.
• Comfortable working in a mixed legacy/modern environment and improving it incrementally.
• Able to reason about data end to end, from the source system through transformation to the report or consuming application.

Useful experience but not essential
• Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, Lakehouse, Warehouse, Data Factory or Direct Lake.
• Python, notebooks, Spark or PySpark.
• SSIS, Analysis Services or migration from older Microsoft BI tooling.
• Azure Service Bus, Logic Apps, APIs or integration-heavy data flows.
• Data governance, lineage, metadata management or data-quality frameworks.

How success looks
Data pipelines are reliable, SQL problems are diagnosed properly, reporting has trusted inputs, difficult legacy logic becomes easier to understand and maintain, and the organisation can move toward Fabric without losing the operational knowledge embedded in the current estate.

• Clear quality gates, faster feedback and fewer late-cycle surprises.

• Strong exploratory, functional, integration and regression testing skills.

Job Summary
The Team Leader will provide supervision and technical guidance as well as overall leadership to a team of colleagues working in a fixed costs environment. Caseloads are predominantly RTA and range in value from £5k up to £100k.
You will provide end to end technical support and coaching on cases, be responsible for the adherence to our robust supervision framework as well as be accountable for delivery of your teams’ objectives and KPIs.

· Protect client caseloads of your team through effective governance of milestones being achieved accurately and on time.
· Identify and implement litigation tactics to improve customer outcomes and maximise income generation.
· Where appropriate, ensure that complex cases are identified and highlighted in line with internal procedures for progression to the Multi Track Team.
· Optimise supervision across the team ensuring consistent application of standards, process, and working practice.
· Conduct file reviews and other technical supervision required under internal management controls.
· To support the Leadership Team in ensuring effective governance controls and measurements are in place to track and report progress.
· Provide effective coaching and feedback to team members, highlighting any issues identified to improve the quality of client outcomes.
· Support performance improvement of team members through creating and maintaining smart support plans.
· Be comfortable leading and developing a diverse team of newly tenured colleagues as well as experienced senior file handlers.
· Work with the Leadership Team to create a culture of continuous improvement and high levels of staff engagement and contribute to the overall operational plan.
· To understand the Minster Law cost process and provide technical support to fee-earners.
· Identify process issues and work with relevant stakeholders to resolve these.
· Identify training needs and skills gaps across the team.
· Work with the Leadership Team and support functions such as Learning and Development to organise training for colleagues.
· Working closely with the Leadership Team to ensure that both team and fee earner development is appropriately progressed, and business change is fully embedded.
· To undertake any other tasks as deemed relevant and reasonable by the business.
· Where appropriate have case ownership alongside the above accountabilities and handle matters in accordance with Team KPIs.

An experienced people leader that thrives on creating a high performing, motivated and engaged team

· Demonstrate consideration of our company values in day to day decision making.
· Ability to follow Company process / guidelines & make appropriate decisions.
· Be a cultural ambassador by displaying our values and behaviours in every aspect of the work they do.
· Ambassador for change, prepare and equip colleagues for change through engagement, communication and seamless implementation.

Essential
· A qualified Solicitor or Fellow of CILEx with Higher Practice Rights
· Proven track record of settling claims valued between £5k - £50k.
· Sound knowledge RTA.
· Experience of managing HR and People processes against policy.
· Managing performance & productivity, ideally in a professional services environment.
· IT skills – including Microsoft Word; Microsoft Teams; PowerPoint & Excel.
· Experience of conducting 1-2-1’s / personal development plans / performance reviews.
· Experienced in the use and interpretation of MI and data.

Overview: 

The Adelphi Group of companies is part of Omnicom Health, a division of Omnicom Group Inc.

The Adelphi Group of Companies includes primary market research consultancies, market access, real-world evidence and communications businesses. For over 30 years, the Group has provided strategic consulting services to global pharmaceutical clients and supported the development, launch and marketing of pharmaceutical brands. This role will serve as a key link between Compliance, IT and business stakeholders, translating governance requirements into practical day-to-day processes and supporting consistent information lifecycle management across the Group.

Data governance is an increasingly important part of Adelphi’s regulatory, contractual and operational framework. The Group operates across multiple entities, business systems and data environments, with growing client and regulatory expectations around information ownership, classification, retention, deletion and auditability. The Compliance function provides central oversight, while effective governance also depends on collaboration with Data Owners, IT and business stakeholders across the organisation.

Job purpose: 

The Data Governance Coordinator will provide dedicated support for data management activities across the Adelphi Group. Sitting within the Compliance function and reporting to the Director of Compliance, the role will act as the central coordinator for information governance activities, support Data Owners and help ensure that governance processes are implemented, maintained and evidenced consistently across the organisation. 

Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities

As Data Governance Coordinator, you will:
• Coordinate data governance activities across corporate systems and other relevant business systems.
• Support Data Owners in fulfilling their governance responsibilities and coordinate completion of required actions.
• Maintain and centralise Information Asset Registers across all entities, ensuring consistency, completeness and accuracy.
• Maintain governance records relating to information assets, including ownership, processing activities, retention requirements and classifications.
• Coordinate data mapping activities and maintain oversight of information flows across business units.
• Support the implementation and monitoring of information classification, retention and governance standards.
• Coordinate retention reviews, archiving programmes and deletion activities, including client notification and confirmation processes where required.
• Act as the central point of contact for retention, deletion and wider information governance queries.
• Monitor governance records within systems and coordinate remediation where gaps or inconsistencies are identified.
• Maintain supporting documentation, audit evidence and governance records for regulatory, client and internal audit requirements.
• Support the onboarding of new information assets and provide governance guidance to business users.
• Coordinate oversight of third-party data handling activities in conjunction with existing compliance and supplier management processes.
• Produce regular governance reporting and management information, including retention activities, outstanding actions, remediation progress and governance metrics.
• Support data governance training, awareness and Continuum onboarding activities across the organisation.
• Proactively identify governance gaps and work with relevant stakeholders to coordinate proportionate remediation

Key Skills & Competencies required:
• Experience in data governance, information governance, compliance, records management or a related coordination role.
• Good working knowledge of information lifecycle management, including data ownership, classification, retention, archiving and deletion.
• An understanding of the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR), the Data Protection Act 2018 and related data governance requirements.
• Strong organisational skills and the ability to maintain accurate, auditable records across multiple entities and systems.
• Ability to manage competing priorities, follow up actions and coordinate stakeholders in a complex matrix organisation.
• Good analytical skills, with the ability to identify gaps, inconsistencies and practical remediation actions.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to provide clear guidance to business users and work collaboratively with Data Owners, Compliance and IT.
• Strong attention to detail and a proactive, methodical approach.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook; experience of governance, data catalogue or records-management platforms would be advantageous.
• Ability to use appropriate influence and persuasion to help ensure governance processes are followed.

Hybrid – Wolverhampton, GBRMoog Commercial Aircraft Group is seeking a Senior Design Engineer.

Moog Commercial Aircraft Group is seeking a Senior Design Engineer (Mechanical) to develop and improve commercial flight control products. In this role, you will work with engineering teams to support new product introduction (NPI) and product improvement initiatives, taking designs from concept through prototype testing, manufacture, and product handover. You will report to the Commercial Engineering Manager (Design) and be based at either the Wolverhampton or Tewkesbury Moog site.

As a Senior Design Engineer, you will collaborate cross-functionally with project, systems, stress, manufacturing, supply chain, and product engineering teams to deliver innovative and robust engineering solutions. You will provide technical leadership, mentor junior engineers, and ensure designs meet customer requirements, regulatory expectations, quality standards, cost targets, and project schedules.

As a Senior Design Engineer, you will make critical contributions by holding responsibility for:

• Design and develop mechanical components and assemblies for rotating equipment and hydraulic systems from concept through production release.
• Provide technical ownership of design deliverables, ensuring quality, schedule, and performance objectives are achieved.
• Mentor and coach junior engineers while supporting the development of engineering best practices.
• Collaborate with project, systems, and stress engineering teams to ensure designs meet customer performance, airworthiness, and regulatory requirements.
• Create and review detailed technical drawings and 3D CAD models suitable for manufacturing and assembly.
• Apply GD&T principles and perform tolerance analysis to validate fit, function, and manufacturability.
• Support DFMEA activities, identify technical risks, and develop mitigation strategies throughout the product lifecycle.
• Present design concepts, development progress, and technical solutions to customers and key stakeholders.
• Partner with manufacturing, supply chain, and product engineering teams to deliver robust and producible product designs.
• Support prototype builds, testing, troubleshooting activities, and design refinements based on test results.
• Generate and maintain engineering documentation including bills of materials (BOMs), revision records, and engineering change notices (ECNs).
• Participate in design reviews, risk assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance engineering processes and product performance.
• Collaborate with suppliers and manufacturing partners to define components, tolerances, and manufacturing processes.
• Support occasional international travel as required by project and customer needs.

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
• Significant experience in mechanical product design and development.
• Experience designing complex mechanical systems, preferably within aerospace or another highly regulated industry.
• Working knowledge of GD&T, tolerance analysis, materials, and manufacturing processes.
• Experience using 3D CAD software, ideally Siemens NX, and PLM/PDM tools.
• Strong problem-solving, analytical, and technical decision-making skills.
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to present technical information to customers and stakeholders.
• Experience leading projects or providing technical leadership to engineering teams is preferred.

We are hiring an Applied AI Engineer to build AI agents and intelligent product capabilities that transform how finance teams work.

This is a product engineering role - not an isolated prototyping or research role. You will own agent-based features end to end: from architecture and evaluation through backend integration, deployment, and operation in production.




YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES



Build and Ship AI Agents

 - Design and build agents that automate complex finance workflows.

 - Own features from initial concept and prototype through production deployment.

 - Integrate agents deeply with our backend services, APIs, data model, permissions, and product workflows.

 - Design how agents securely access and use data from across the Moss platform.

 - Turn emerging AI capabilities into reliable, customer-facing product features.

Evaluate and Improve Agent Performance

 - Build systematic evaluations for agent quality, reliability, and business impact.

 - Create representative test datasets, evaluation criteria, regression tests, and human-review processes.

 - Measure and improve accuracy, latency, cost, and user experience.

 - Establish observability and feedback loops that make agent behavior understandable and continuously improvable.

Develop the AI Application Architecture

 - Apply context-engineering techniques such as RAG, MCP and knowledge graphs.

 - Design prompts, tools, memory, workflows and orchestration strategies for production agents.

 - Select and use appropriate orchestration frameworks, such as Google ADK, LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or comparable technologies.

 - Build appropriate guardrails, approval steps, and human-in-the-loop controls for sensitive financial workflows.

Integrate Machine-Learning Capabilities

 - Collaborate with data scientists to integrate machine-learning models into our production systems.

 - Build the services, data flows, APIs, and operational tooling required to make models usable within the product.

 - Take responsibility for the production integration rather than handing prototypes to another engineering team.




ABOUT YOU

 - You are a seasoned software engineer with experience building and operating production applications.

 - You are highly proficient in Python and/or Java and comfortable working across backend services, APIs, data, and application architecture.

 - You have built and shipped at least one agent or LLM-powered product capability end to end.

 - You have personally integrated agents into a broader product and backend architecture - not only developed standalone prototypes.

 - You have practical experience evaluating agents or other non-deterministic AI systems.

 - You understand how to provide agents with the right data and context while respecting security, permissions, and privacy.

 - You have hands-on experience with prompt engineering, context engineering, and agent orchestration.

 - You balance rapid experimentation with reliable, maintainable production engineering.

 - You communicate clearly and collaborate effectively across engineering, product, and data science.

Relevant Technologies

You do not need experience with every technology below. We care most about strong engineering judgment and demonstrated end-to-end ownership.

 - Agent orchestration: Google ADK, LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or comparable frameworks

 - Context engineering: RAG, MCP, knowledge graphs, tool use, memory, and retrieval systems

 - AI evaluation: offline and online evaluations, test datasets, regression testing, observability, and human review

 - Language models: Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Llama, Mistral, or similar

 - Backend engineering: Python or Java, REST APIs, Kafka, microservices, and distributed systems

 - Data systems: SQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, vector search, and data pipelines

 - Cloud AI platforms: GCP and Vertex AI, or comparable platforms

job_title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
job_description:
Mozilla Foundation is a non-profit building a better technology future — powered by people, open by design, fueled by imagination.

We deliver people-first alternatives to today’s extractive systems. We build side by side with developers, innovators and advocates, united in the belief that a better technology future is not only possible — it’s ours to create!

Team

Our CEO is increasingly focused outward on the Board, funders, partners, and public conversations that will shape the Foundation’s next chapter. This newly created Chief of Staff role exists to extend the CEO’s reach inside the organization and make that outward focus possible.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll serve as the CEO’s strategic partner, internal proxy and trusted extension of their leadership. You’ll hold the CEO’s strategic agenda, translate the CEO’s priorities into organizational alignment, represent the CEO internally where needed, and make decisions on the CEO’s behalf within clearly delegated authority. You’ll determine what reaches the CEO, prepare the CEO for consequential moments, and escalate only what requires the CEO’s judgment.

As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you’ll partner strategically with other members of the ELT and work closely with the CEO’s Executive Program Manager to make sure the CEO’s time, priorities, and commitments stay aligned and moving.

You’ll also partner with the Foundation’s Investment Committee and its technical and strategic advisors, keeping their focus on the right questions, their recommendations aligned with the Foundation’s strategic priorities, and decisions moving efficiently from evaluation to funding.

Job responsibilities

Here’s what you’ll likely be focused on for the first 6 months:

• Building a strong working partnership with the CEO, aligning on priorities, ways of working and clearly defining the scope of your delegated authority.

• Establishing a trusted partnership with each member of the Executive Leadership Team, learning their priorities, pressures and ways of working.

• Developing a deep, cross-functional understanding of the Foundation’s work and how each function connects to the CEO’s priorities.

• Translating the CEO’s priorities into a concise, clear set of strategic outcomes that leaders understand and can use to guide the decisions they own, with a current view of what’s changing and which decisions are approaching.

• Defining with the CEO what truly requires their attention, and ensuring issues reach them decision-ready, with context, options and a recommendation.

As the Chief of Staff to Mozilla Foundation’s CEO, you will…

• Serve as the CEO’s thought partner in developing, pressure-testing and refining strategic priorities, synthesizing executive insight and external developments to anticipate what will need to be known or decided in the next 30, 60 and 90 days.

• Direct the CEO’s time toward strategy, external relationships, development, Board leadership and the Foundation’s highest-consequence decisions.

• Filter rather than forward, so significant shifts in strategy, material risks, major budget decisions and Board-level matters reach the CEO early, with context, options and a recommendation.

• Maintain a current view of the CEO’s top priorities, identify where work is drifting from strategic intent, and surface conflicts in priorities, resources or attention before they become emergencies.

• Enable the Executive Leadership Team to operate as one team around the CEO’s priorities, so the right issues reach the ELT at the right level and decisions and commitments are followed through.

• Partner with ELT members on cross-functional issues that need CEO-level alignment but not the CEO’s direct involvement.

• Represent the CEO’s position in internal discussions and make decisions on the CEO’s behalf within delegated authority, bringing anything beyond it back to the CEO promptly.

• Ensure the CEO enters every Board meeting, funder and partner conversation, speech and public engagement fully prepared, with concise briefings, organizational context and answers to likely questions.

• Identify external opportunities that warrant the CEO’s attention, and ensure commitments the CEO makes externally translate into clear internal follow-through.

What this role is not

This is a role of influence. It exists to ensure the CEO can lead effectively through the Executive Leadership Team.

• The Chief of Staff does not manage the Executive Leadership Team or run the Foundation’s operations. Each executive leader owns execution and decisions within their area.

• This role does not make decisions beyond the authority the CEO has delegated. Anything outside that authority returns to the CEO.

• This role does not have any direct reports and also doesn’t manage the CEO’s calendar, scheduling or administrative support.

Your Professional Profile

• Significant, verifiable experience as a strategic partner at CEO or executive-team level, with a track record of leading high-stakes work and turning ambiguity into structure and action.

• Experience working across multiple legal entities is a plus, including navigating differences, building influence, and coordinating work across entities where relevant. 

• A proven record of driving complex, cross-functional priorities from idea to execution by defining outcomes, ownership, milestones and decision points.

• Exceptional judgment and discretion, including handling confidential information and navigating complex executive dynamics with integrity.

• Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority, build trust across functions and at the most senior levels, and give direct feedback with care.

• Outstanding written and verbal communication, with experience distilling complex information into decision-ready briefs, recommendations, presentations and executive communications.

• Strong analytical and strategic problem-solving skills: you frame the right question, gather the right information, test assumptions and recommend a practical path forward.

• Disciplined prioritization, with the agility to move between long-term priorities and time-sensitive issues without losing the thread.

• Direct experience supporting Board governance, fundraising or other high-stakes external relationships at an executive level.

• A track record of doing high-impact work out of the spotlight, measuring your success by the CEO’s and the team’s, and acting in the best interests of the CEO and the organization.

• A demonstrated commitment to Mozilla Foundation’s mission and to building an open, accessible and trustworthy internet.

• The ability to work across time zones and occasionally outside standard working hours for Board meetings, major events or urgent organizational needs.

• Comfortable traveling for Board meetings, leadership gatherings and major events.

We Are Excited To See Any Additional Experience With:

• Senior roles in nonprofit, philanthropic, technology or public-interest organizations.

• Supporting or advising investment, grantmaking or funding committees.

How We Work

A few things that are true about how we work at Mozilla Foundation. Here's a summary along with our expectation of how these should show up in this role:

• Move toward the hard thing: you surface conflicts in priorities, resources or attention early, and give the CEO and executives direct, actionable input, including what they may not want to hear. You disagree constructively in the room, not afterward, and you don’t wait for someone else to raise it.

• Stay curious and current: you stay close to what executives are seeing and what’s happening in our fields and communities, and turn it into the context the CEO needs. You pressure-test assumptions, including your own.

• Work in the open: you document decisions and the reasoning behind them, so executives and teams can follow how and why priorities are set. You favor shared channels over side conversations wherever appropriate.

• Focus and finish: you keep the CEO’s agenda focused on what matters most, make deliberate choices about what does and doesn’t need the CEO, and make sure decisions and commitments are seen through.

• Flex with purpose: you move between long-term priorities and time-sensitive issues as context shifts, and adapt how you work with each executive. Flexibility isn’t about being agreeable; it’s staying responsive while holding to the mission and the CEO’s priorities.

• Lead with care: you hold a high bar for the work while treating people as whole humans. You extend good faith to fellow executives, respect that each owns their area, and talk directly to the person who can solve the problem.

Salary and Benefits Information

Mozilla Foundation is dedicated to fair and equitable compensation for our staff. We aim to pay a competitive and market-based salary based on the responsibilities and requirements of the role. We do not ask for, or take into account, salary histories in our offer process.

The starting salary ranges for this role are listed below.

We also offer the following benefits:

Benefits are subject to change at any time at the discretion of Mozilla Foundation.

We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities and expressions.

At Rolls-Royce we are proud to be a business that has truly helped to shape the modern world and are committed to always being a force for progress; powering, protecting and connecting people everywhere.

• Extensive experience in the engineering industry, preferably in a technical support role

job_title: New Business Development Manager – Managed Services
job_description:
Colibri Digital are looking for a New Business Development Manager to win new customers for our managed data, cloud and AI services.

The key to this role is experience selling managed data platforms, cloud operations, FinOps or MLOps services and having a track record of co-selling with AWS or Databricks, including using partner funding programmes.

Our managed services aren't traditional break-fix support. One UK-based team runs the whole platform, including cloud, data, AI, FinOps, security, databases and applications, and we use AI-assisted operations to catch problems before they reach the business. Managed Services are how we turn successful projects into long-term partnerships, and growing them is a priority for us.

This is a pure new-logo role. There are no inherited accounts, no existing book of business and no handed-over pipeline. You will build your own territory from scratch, and you'll be doing it with a service that is easy to be proud of.

Why this role is worth a conversation:
You get to build, not just inherit. You'll define your target market, choose your accounts and build a self-generated pipeline from a blank sheet, with the autonomy to do it your way.
You'll sell something proven. Clients rate our managed services highly and stay with us for years, so you'll walk into conversations with real references in every sector we serve.
You'll have a strong team behind every deal. You will work closely with our managed service, delivery, solution architecture, finance and partner alliance teams to shape services that are commercially sound and deliverable from day one.
You'll help shape how a growing team wins. Managed Services is a priority for Colibri and we're building a new-business team around it. Your ideas on how we target and win will carry weight, and uncapped commission means your results are rewarded.

What you'll be selling
Managed services are bought differently to projects. Buyers are signing up for a multi-year relationship, so they weigh trust, service quality, risk and total cost of ownership. These are the proof points you will be able to put in front of them:
• Customers love us. We consistently achieve a customer NPS of 90+, so you will have referenceable clients in every sector we serve.
• Trusted with critical platforms. We've run mission-critical platforms for over 12 years, including a national rail ticketing platform and an automotive platform handling 250M+ transactions a day.
• Accredited, not asserted. We're an AWS Premier Tier Partner and certified AWS MSP, with AWS Data & Analytics and GenAI competencies, and a Databricks partner. We're also ISO 20000, 27001, 9001 and 22301 certified.
• Always on. UK-based 24/7 support and 99.9%+ availability across managed platforms.
• Measured on outcomes. We report on Experience Level Agreements as well as SLAs, covering user experience, data freshness, cost and business impact, not just uptime.
• Pays for itself. Clients typically see 20–35% recurring cloud savings through FinOps built into the service.
• Built for the AI era. AI-assisted monitoring and self-healing automation keep platforms improving, not just running.
• Easy to start. Structured onboarding takes clients from assessment to proactive operations in 4–8 weeks.
What you'll own
• Your territory. Defining your target market, prioritising accounts and building a self-generated pipeline from a blank sheet.
• New managed services customers. Identifying and engaging organisations we don't yet work with, and winning multi-year managed services contracts for their data, cloud and AI platforms.
• Consultative discovery. Uncovering how the client operates today, from platform reliability and cost to skills gaps, security and compliance, and building the business case around outcomes such as lower total cost of ownership, reduced risk and a better customer experience.
• The commercial case. Shaping pricing, service scope, SLAs and contract structure with our managed service and finance teams, so every deal is profitable and deliverable.
• Onboarding and transition. Working with delivery to build credible transition plans, so clients can see exactly how we will take over and run their service.
• Your own pipeline. Generating opportunities through outbound outreach, events, networking, referrals and co-sell with AWS and Databricks.
• Land and expand. Turning new relationships into long-term partnerships, and spotting where a Colibri project can lead into a managed service, and vice versa.
• The full sales cycle. Taking opportunities from first contact through discovery, solution shaping, proposal or RFP, negotiation and close.
• Forecasting. Achieving monthly, quarterly and annual new-logo targets for monthly recurring revenue (MRR), with an accurate, well-qualified pipeline in our CRM.

There isn't one particular route into this role. What matters most is a track record of winning managed services customers from scratch, and the commercial understanding to sell a multi-year relationship.

We're particularly interested in evidence that you have:
• A proven managed services new-logo record. You have consistently exceeded targets by winning net-new managed services customers rather than renewing or growing existing accounts. Be ready to walk us through specific contracts you won, their terms and value, and how you won them.
• Built from nothing. You've taken an empty territory and built a pipeline through your own prospecting, and you enjoy the autonomy that comes with it.
• Recurring-revenue know-how. You understand how managed services are scoped, priced and delivered, including SLAs, service scope, transition and the economics of a multi-year contract.
• Experience selling managed data platforms, cloud operations, FinOps or MLOps services
• A track record of co-selling with AWS or Databricks, including using partner funding programmes
• Familiarity with public sector buying routes such as G-Cloud and Crown Commercial Service frameworks
• Relationships and experience selling into financial services, energy or transport

What you'll get
• A competitive salary, depending on experience, with an uncapped commission structure
• Salary Sacrifice Pension plan of 5+3
• 25 days' annual leave + 1 birthday day
• Private Medical and wider benefits
• Remote-first within the UK, with flexibility around client needs

This is a client-facing role, so there will be travel to client sites, partner events and Colibri/Nasstar offices, including central London, when required.

 - Designed systems at real scale, and lived with them. You were the lead designer of production systems handling significant load, data, or complexity, and you stayed long enough to own the consequences: migrations, re-architectures, incidents, and the decisions you’d now reverse.

 - Led through serious incidents. You’ve owned production incidents with real business impact, from response through root cause to systemic fixes.

 - Made other engineers better at scale. You can point to engineers you grew into senior or Staff roles, and to standards or practices you introduced that outlasted your direct involvement.

 - Exceptional written communication. Your design docs and strategy documents change minds. We will read your writing before we meet you.

 - Deep AWS and infrastructure experience. Production cloud architecture, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, and observability at scale.

 - Built and operated AI/LLM-powered products in production, including evaluation, latency, cost, and reliability trade-offs.

 - Enterprise B2B SaaS at scale: multi-tenancy, SSO, data isolation, and compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR).

 - Public technical work, such as talks, writing, or meaningful open-source contributions.

 - You haven’t written production code regularly in the last two years.

Our process typically takes three weeks:

 1. Technical leadership conversation with Head of Engineering (45 mins): your scope, your impact, and how you operate.

 3. Take home assignment (1.5 hours): Prove that you can turn in high caliber work.

 4. Deep dive (1.5 hours): a deep-dive walkthrough of a system you led. Expect us to probe every decision, failure mode, and trade-off or an open-ended design problem.

 5. Cross-functional panel (1 hour) with product leadership: strategy, influence, and disagreement.

NeosAlpha is seeking a highly organised, commercially minded Chief of Staff / Business Operations Lead to work directly with the CEO and leadership team. The successful candidate will act as an extension of the CEO, helping drive execution across sales, delivery, recruitment, partnerships, operations, and strategic initiatives. The role is designed to reduce operational overhead on the CEO by ensuring that key actions, decisions, and priorities are effectively tracked, coordinated, and delivered. This is a highly visible role requiring strong business acumen, exceptional organisational skills, and the ability to operate across multiple business functions.

## Job Roles & Responsibilities

**CEO Support & Business Operations**

- Act as a trusted partner to the CEO in managing strategic and operational priorities.
- Capture, track, and follow up on actions arising from customer meetings, internal reviews, leadership meetings, and strategic discussions.
- Ensure accountability for agreed actions across the business.
- Proactively identify blockers and escalate risks where required.
- Maintain visibility of key initiatives and provide regular progress updates to the CEO.

- Support management of sales opportunities, renewals, and strategic accounts.
- Coordinate proposal submissions, commercial reviews, and contract processes.
- Track pipeline progression and ensure timely follow-up on opportunities.
- Assist with partner relationships and strategic alliance activities.
- Work with sales leadership to improve operational efficiency and reporting.

**Strategic Projects**

- Lead or coordinate cross-functional initiatives on the CEO’s behalf.
- Support acquisitions, partnerships, new service launches, and operational improvement projects.
- Conduct market, competitor, and industry research.
- Prepare briefing papers and recommendations for leadership decisions.

**Recruitment & Resource Management**

- Coordinate strategic hiring initiatives.
- Support workforce planning and resource forecasting.
- Track recruitment activity and key staffing requirements.
- Ensure critical hiring actions are completed in a timely manner.

**Governance & Reporting**

- Prepare executive dashboards and KPI reporting.

Who We Are
Oliver Wyman, a Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) business, is a management consulting firm driven by deep industry insight, bold innovation, and a collaborative approach that cuts through complexity to help organizations navigate their most defining transformative moments.

Role Overview
Oliver Wyman DNA team builds software products and solutions that aim to be re-used and adapted across different contexts or projects. Typical products span solutions that improve how financial institutions model and manage risk, how wealth managers run their advisory and client processes, how lenders perform credit analysis, and how retailers personalize digital marketing, among others. AI is a key component of all our solutions, and most of our products are either AI-native or largely AI-enhanced.

As Director of Product Management, you help grow one or more of these products. You work closely with the product’s ecosystem of partners and are accountable for the product itself: what it does, who buys it, why they keep using it, what it costs to run, what it earns, and where it goes next. You will work with products from initial idea (early-stage propositions still proving their first commercial case) to scale (established products carrying live client deployments and renewal commitments). Stakeholders are based in UK, Europe, India and US time zones.

Why Join Us?
• Own real, impactful products, used inside the firm and by our clients, and be accountable for where they go next
• Build products that materially improve how major institutions manage risk, advise clients, extend credit or reach their customers
• Combine the rigor of a product business with the domain depth and client access of a leading consulting firm
• Work directly with clients, partners and engineering leaders on decisions that matter
• Thrive in a culture that values innovation, diversity and continuous growth

Key Responsibilities
• Define the product vision, roadmap and backlog: what the product does, who it serves, and what gets built next.
• Work closely with the consulting Partners, their teams and their clients to understand their needs and propose the right support and collaboration.
• Support the sale directly, joining pitches, client conversations and pricing decisions where the product is in play.
• Build deep understanding of the domain, the users and the competition, and use it to position the product and decide what to build, buy or partner for.
• Contribute to the economics of the product alongside the Partners, covering pricing, packaging and licensing, as well as infrastructure and engineering spend.
• Work with the team to keep quality and runtime at the right level: testing, release readiness, security, support and escalation.

• Turn feedback from clients, users and delivery teams into a prioritized enhancement path, and be clear on what is out and why.
• Work with the wider product department on portfolio alignment, reuse of shared components and investment trade-offs, surfacing the hard choices early with options and a recommendation.
• Run the product operating rhythm and track how the product performs, from revenue and pipeline to adoption, reliability and client satisfaction. Rebuild the product P&L, quantify the impact it creates for the DNA business, and present it with the Partners to the DNA leads.

Technical Skills and Expertise

Commercial Product Ownership:
• Proven ownership of a software product used at scale, internally or sold to external clients, with accountability for its performance.
• Track record of defining and defending a revenue model, pricing and packaging, and of managing the trade-off between investment, margin and product ambition.
• Fluency with the numbers behind a product: able to rebuild a product-level P&L, defend the method behind it, and use it to demonstrate business impact.

Domain and Market Credibility:
• Depth in at least one relevant business domain such as risk modelling, wealth and asset management, credit, banking, insurance, retail or digital marketing.
• Enough command of the business processes the product improves to make product calls with conviction.
• Experience running credible market and competitive analysis, and translating it into positioning, pricing and roadmap implications.

AI Product Judgement:
• Understanding of how AI changes product decisions, covering evaluation of non-deterministic outputs, accuracy thresholds, human oversight and readiness for client use.
• Awareness of AI product economics, including inference and token cost per user, and how these shape pricing and unit economics.

• Product Definition, Delivery and Quality:
• Strong command of prioritization, feature definition, acceptance expectations and release planning.
• Experience working with engineers and architects on product definition, testing, release readiness, security and support needs.
• Knowledge of the support, SLA and maintenance model that a commercially sold product requires.
• Fluency with product and delivery tooling such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Confluence or equivalent.

Go-to-Market, Sales Support and Communication:
• Experience building the product narrative, demo and go-to-market package that let a product be sold credibly.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, and credibility in front of clients and partners.

Stakeholder Alignment and Trade-Off Management:
• Presence to convene Partners, sponsors, engineering leads and commercial teams, and to turn competing views into clear recommendations and decisions.
• Experience working across a product portfolio on alignment, reuse of shared components and investment trade-offs.

Additional Technologies (nice-to-have):
• Experience with enterprise SaaS or data and analytics products, particularly where the product embeds quantitative models or decisioning.
• Understanding how to use agentic flows and the latest AI tooling to raise the productivity and quality of product and delivery work.

What Makes a Great Candidate
• 10+ years of product leadership experience or equivalent, having owned a commercially sold software product end to end, covering vision, roadmap, quality, pricing, cost base and growth.
• Director-level credibility, with the presence to work directly with clients, partners and senior product and technology stakeholders.
• Real domain depth in a relevant field, and the appetite to build more.
• Experience taking AI into live, customer-facing products, and a clear view of what that requires. Having done so in a regulated environment, with the model risk, data privacy and explainability expectations that come with it, is a strong plus.
• Proven ability to operate across product, engineering, delivery, marketing and commercial teams without formal authority over all contributors.
• Strong judgement on when to push for product standardization and when to allow client-specific adaptation, with a clear view of what each exception costs.
• Comfort with imperfect information, evolving scope and competing senior opinions, at any stage of product maturity.
• Ability to make complex product and commercial trade-offs simple enough for busy stakeholders to act on, and the courage to name the hard choice.
• Personal qualities including ownership mindset, curiosity, resilience, strong collaboration skills and a passion for excellence.
