Within Oliver Wyman, the Data and Analytics (DNA) division was established in 2017. We are a dynamic and rapidly growing team of around 250 quants, data engineers, data scientists, software engineers, AI specialists and project managers, working closely with over 5,000 colleagues across the firm to cover a global footprint, supporting clients across multiple industries including, but not limited to, Financial Services, Climate & Sustainability, Energy, Retail, and Transportation. 

We are growing our project management team, and this role is central to that growth.

We believe in the power of diverse perspectives and collaborative teams to drive innovation. Our team comes from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences, and we embrace the unique skills and insights they bring to our work.

At Oliver Wyman and within DNA, we are proud of the values we uphold that guide us every day in how we work and collaborate. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their full potential.

Why Join us?
Expect a steep learning curve, as no two projects are ever the same. You’ll have the opportunity to travel internationally, gaining invaluable experiences and insights across different cultures and, with access to the latest technologies, you’ll constantly expand your toolkit with each new endeavour.
You won’t be alone on this journey; colleagues across the firm will guide and coach you throughout your career. You’ll have a dedicated buddy, a career adviser, and a talent manager to help you navigate your professional path. Progression here is not about time served or project size; it is earned through consistently demonstrating greater judgement, leadership, influence and impact.

This role will empower you to embrace your curiosity and step out of your comfort zone. You will have the opportunity to work alongside talented and supportive colleagues who measure success by the lasting impact we create together. If you’re excited by challenges and eager to make a meaningful impact, we look forward to welcoming you aboard!

Role Overview
These positions offer excellent career and growth opportunities for talented, highly motivated professionals with a passion for delivering complex technology, data, quantitative and AI-enabled work. We look for people who are flexible and who know the content and industry well enough to earn real credibility, leading delivery with fluency in the technical substance of the work rather than managing it from a distance. We call this content-fluent project management: the role is an orchestrator of delivery, not an administrator of it.

Above all, we look for people who create and maintain the conditions for excellent teams to deliver exceptional outcomes with our clients. 

We offer a competitive salary and benefits, with a clear career path through to Managing Director or Partner and potentially a steeper trajectory than in similar firms. These roles sit at Levels 3 to 5 of the Oliver Wyman competency model: Associate Team Leader (Level 3), Team Leader (Level 4) and Director (Level 5). Directors can pursue promotion to Managing Director or Partner

Key Responsibilities

• Associate Team Leaders and Team Leaders would typically work on one project at a time, while a Director would typically work on two smaller assignments or one large, more complex one

• Leading complex technology, data, quantitative and AI-enabled transformation programmes, running a workstream within one, or providing PMO support, depending on seniority: planning, governance, risk, dependencies and financials, working hand in hand with client teams throughout, who are core partners in delivery rather than an external stakeholder group

• Making things simple: turning complexity into something the team, Partners and clients can act on with confidence, not just a longer status update

• Creating the conditions for exceptional teams, spanning consulting, engineering, data and client colleagues, to do their best work: coaching alongside doing, with fast, frequent feedback, not managing through a tracking tool

• Building trust across the whole delivery ecosystem: client sponsors, Partners and engagement leaders, and using that network to bring technical, commercial and senior-level steer to projects

• Coaching Oliver Wyman and client team members to develop their skills, and contributing to DNA's growing project management community and discipline

Skills and Expertise

• Fluency in the content of the work, engaging directly and credibly with engineers, data scientists and technical leads rather than working through a translator

• An ability to tell emotive compelling stories: making people feel the weight of a decision or a risk, not just describe it to them

• An enthusiasm for project management as the craft it is, in its own right

• A flexible, adaptable approach: comfortable moving between projects, teams and client contexts as priorities shift

• A genuine commitment to team success: real satisfaction from helping other people do their best work, not just delivering your own

• Strong planning, governance, risk and communication skills, with real rigour applied to the discipline of delivery

• Independence and an ability to work under limited supervision while respecting defined timelines

• The ability to present results, issues and implications clearly and effectively

• Excellent command of the English language (verbal and written)

• Ability to manage a demanding workload and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment

• Ability to maintain and respect confidentiality

Associate Team Leader - At least 3 years of experience leading a workstream or providing PMO support within technology, data, quantitative or AI-enabled projects, managing scope, risk and stakeholders within a project or significant workstream, for example owning delivery of a single data or AI workstream within a larger client programme, including its own plan, risk log and client relationships

Team Leader - At least 5 years of experience, leading complex, multi-workstream technology, data or quantitative-enabled programmes, managing budgets, delivery risk and multiple stakeholders across a full programme, for example leading delivery across several consulting and engineering workstreams on one client programme, with senior client sponsors and Oliver Wyman Partners as regular counterparts

Director - At least 8 years of experience acting as the senior delivery authority on large-scale, technically complex transformation programmes, shaping delivery strategy alongside Partners and client executives, for example holding delivery accountability across a portfolio of major technology, data, quantitative or AI-enabled transformation engagements for a single client

Alignment with Microsoft is essential. 

Our ideal CAE is highly skilled with a partnership selling approach. We need relationship builders with a strong understanding of VDI and EUC technologies to continue to grow our most prized partnership with Microsoft and its sales teams. You must be highly motivated and take an entrepreneurial approach to growing the relationship and revenue in addition to being a team player. 

Integrity means everything to us – so you will need to do what you say you are going to do. This may involve coordinating with other departments in the wider team, putting your excellent listening, written and verbal communication skills to good use! 


What you'll do
Manage and close Nerdio opportunities in alignment with Microsoft's sales teams, channel partners, and direct customers. 
Achieve monthly, quarterly, and annual sales target goals.
Build, manage, and close pipeline and maintain 3x coverage to your assigned quota. 
Build and maintain strong relationships with Microsoft and its sales teams to grow the partnership and revenue.

Effectively communicate Nerdio's value proposition, capabilities, and benefits to potential customers. 
Work closely with the sales team to develop and execute strategies to meet sales targets.
Participate in field events with partners and Microsoft counterparts to nurture and drive business in your given territory. 
Coordinate with other departments within the organization to ensure customer needs are met and projects are delivered successfully. 
Demonstrate integrity and follow through on commitments to ensure customer satisfaction.
Continuously learn and stay up-to-date with industry trends, product knowledge, and sales techniques. 
Participate in quarterly business review, large deal reviews, and other business focused events. 

Qualifications
A minimum of 3-5+ years of experience in similar sales role, preferably in the technology industry: selling cloud computing, IT services, or software-as-service (SaaS) solutions. 
Proven track record of achieving sales targets and quotas. 
Familiarity with sales techniques and processes, including lead generation, prospecting, qualifying leads, and closing deals. 
Strong communication and negotiation skills to engage with potential customers and effectively convey the value proposition of the company's products or services. 
Experienced selling to the C-Suite. 
Experienced in MEDDPICC sales methodology. 
Ability to understand customer needs and identify opportunities for upselling or cross-selling. 
Experience with CRM software and other sales tools for managing and tracking customer interactions. 
Familiarity with Microsoft Azure and other cloud technologies.
Experience in conducting product demonstrations or presentations to potential customers. 
Bachelor's degree in related field.

At Nerdio, our mission is to simplify the lives of IT professionals and maximize their Microsoft cloud and end user computing investments. 

We support organizations of all sizes looking to deploy, manage, and cost-optimize native Microsoft technologies. We partner with Enterprises and Managed Service Providers all over the world to add value on top of their existing native Microsoft investments like Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), Windows 365, and Microsoft Intune. 

Created in 2016, Nerdio has always taken a market-leading and collaborative approach to cloud deployment and management. In fact, our product roadmap is greatly influenced by the regular feedback we receive from having seen companies deploy AVD into production environments several thousand times using Nerdio technology. 

Today, Nerdio is used in over 50 countries by more than 15,000 organizations of every size and vertical. We’re committed to delivering exceptional service and support, which starts with identifying and supporting the best staff possible. 

We are a fast-moving, nimble company looking for individuals who are collaborative, empathetic, driven and who love to move at the speed of light. If you want to be part of the AVD transformation that Microsoft and Nerdio are leading, then we want to speak with you.

About The Role

We are looking for a client-facing Support Engineer with strong technical depth and excellent communication skills. In this role, you will serve as a trusted resource for IT professionals and administrators using the Nerdio platform—helping them get the most out of Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, Microsoft Intune, and related Microsoft cloud technologies. This is a software and platform support role: you will be engaging with technically proficient customers, not end users, and your success will be measured by the quality, accuracy, and speed of your resolutions.

The schedule for this role is 8AM to 5Pm GMT Tuesday to Saturday, and we are only hiring in the UK, Serbia, Germany, and the Netherlands
What You’ll Do
Platform Onboarding & Deployment Support
• Guide customers through AVD environment deployments and Azure infrastructure setup using Nerdio Manager, drawing on practical experience with AVD deployments and Azure environment management.
• Collaborate with enterprise customers and MSP partners to assess requirements, validate infrastructure readiness, and ensure deployments are completed in line with best practices.
• Customer Support & Issue Resolution
• Provide hands-on technical support for IT professionals and administrators across the full Nerdio platform, including Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, and Microsoft Intune.
• Ensure successful incident and problem resolution by responding to cases promptly, diagnosing root causes thoroughly, and delivering clear, effective solutions.
• Technical Expertise
• Apply in-depth knowledge of Microsoft Intune, FSLogix, networking, and Active Directory (Entra ID, Entra Domain Services, AD DS) to resolve complex issues across customer environments.
• Work cross-functionally with internal engineering and product teams to escalate, reproduce, and drive resolution of advanced platform issues.
• Maintain current knowledge of Nerdio platform capabilities and Microsoft cloud technologies to advise customers accurately and confidently.
Communication & Customer Success
• Build strong working relationships with IT administrators and technical stakeholders, communicating clearly and professionally throughout every engagement.
• Deliver product guidance and technical walkthroughs that help customers maximize the value of their Nerdio deployment.
Required Qualifications
• 2+ years in a technical support, systems administration, or cloud infrastructure role.
• Demonstrated experience with Azure Virtual Desktop deployments or Azure environment management; equivalent experience with comparable virtualization platforms will be considered.
• Working knowledge of Microsoft Intune and Microsoft 365 administration, including endpoint policy management and identity configuration.
• Solid understanding of networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and firewall configuration.
• Experience administering Windows Server environments; Linux familiarity is a plus.
• roficiency in PowerShell for automation, scripting, and system configuration tasks.
• Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with a proven ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues in cloud and hybrid environments.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with IT professionals and convey technical information with clarity and precision.
• Strong documentation discipline—able to record cases, resolutions, and best practices to a high standard.
Preferred Qualifications
• Prior experience with the Nerdio platform (NME or NMM) is a significant advantage.
• Broader Microsoft cloud experience across Azure infrastructure, Intune device management, and Microsoft 365 services.
• Knowledge of Active Directory, Group Policy, and identity management concepts.
• Experience with Zendesk or comparable ITSM ticketing platforms.
• Familiarity with the ITIL framework and service management best practices.
• Microsoft Azure certifications (e.g., AZ-104 Azure Administrator, AZ-140 Azure Virtual Desktop Specialty, AZ-800/801 Windows Server Hybrid, or MD-102 Endpoint Administrator).
What We Offer
• Microsoft Azure certification sponsorship: Nerdio covers exam fees for relevant Azure certifications (including AZ-104, AZ-140, MD-102, and others) as you grow in the role. The AZ-104 is expected to be completed within your first 90 days, fully funded.

Benefits and Incentives
• Competitive Base and Incentive Plan
• Stock Options
• Health and Welfare Plans*
• Life and Disability Plans*
• Retirement Plan*
• Unlimited Flexible Paid Time Off, including your birthday off!
• Collaborative Team Culture
* Benefits for international employees, outside the US, vary by country.

Job Summary

The market has shifted. AI is accelerating. The key to AI success is intelligent data and the infrastructure to manage it. Customers are urgently rethinking how they modernize, secure, and unlock value from their data. NetApp is built for this exact moment — with a differentiated platform, deep enterprise credibility, and a clear strategy to win.  

Joining NetApp now means operating in a high achievement environment where you are empowered to own every moment. Our culture is grounded in three principles: innovate to elevate, drive results, excel as a team. These are more than words. They define how we show up, how we sell, and how we grow. 

As a Client Executive, you play a pivotal role as the trusted advisor supporting customers with their transformations - driving outcomes, expanding relationships, and growing NetApp's business through its integrated cloud, data, storage, security, and AI- ready platform.  

This is a role for sellers who want real ownership, complex challenges, and the opportunity to make a visible impact

Job Requirements

• Develop a deep understanding of customer’s strategies, goals, challenges, risks, and transformation priorities, and connect them to NetApp’s differentiated unified platform and solutions.   
• Act as a trusted advisor to the customer by combining technical curiosity, business acumen, and solution expertise to guide customer transformation.   
• Demonstrate strong hunting mentality - identifying whitespace opportunities, new workloads, emerging buyer personas, and expansion paths across your territory.   
• Execute with disciplined sales excellence, including pipeline management and forecast accuracy, using MEDDICC aligned with discovery and qualification.  
• Ensure delivery of in-quarter deal execution while driving multi-quarter account planning that creates demand and solves customers’ greatest pain points. 
• Lead the orchestration of an integrated pursuit team ensuring the customer experiences one, integrated team. Drive post sales handoff to Customer Success with a clear value realization plan tied to the original business case.  

Who You Are

• You understand hybrid cloud architectures, data and AI platforms, consumption economics, and how to translate technology decisions into KPI impact for executives.  
• You are results-driven, resilient, and committed to winning — not just personally, but as part of a team that elevates one another.  
• You thrive in whitespace, finding new workloads and buyers and turning customer challenges into high-value opportunities.    
• You are a credible executive seller with the ability to drive solution selling by tailoring discovery, storytelling, and creating value cases customized for buying personas across IT, Finance, Procurement, Security, Data/AI, and business leaders. 
• You are confident building ROI/TCO models, structuring deal economics, and guiding executives through financial decisions with clarity and credibility.  
• Your communication is crisp, timely, and tailored to the buying persona. Customers trust your ability to translate complexity into clear next steps and to guide them confidently toward the right outcome.  
• You believe in orchestration, clarity, and empowerment. You leverage partners, specialists, and internal resources as multipliers. You are committed to a culture of belonging where diverse perspectives fuel stronger outcomes.  
• You work to drive customer satisfaction and solution consumption to maintain long-term healthy relationships. 
• You are results-driven, resilient, and committed to winning — not just personally, but as part of a team that elevates one another.  

If you are a builder, a hunter, a strategic closer, and someone who thrives in a culture where expectations are high and impact is nonnegotiable — this is your arena.

job_title: Regional Sales Manager – Managed Security Services
job_description:
About the job

Join NETbuilder at a pivotal stage of growth and help scale a differentiated managed security services business.

About NETbuilder

NETbuilder is a rapidly growing, disruptive security services provider with a global footprint and a clear ambition: to redefine how organizations consume managed security services in an AI-driven threat landscape.

We are a leader in AI Managed Security Services and Security Engineering, combining innovative, differentiated offerings with deep engineering expertise and measurable customer outcomes. As a strategic partner of CrowdStrike and Splunk, we help customers maximize the value of their security platforms, strengthen resilience against modern threats, and prepare for emerging malicious AI activity.

Our mission is to secure our customers against modern threats, future adversaries, and emerging malicious AI activity through high-quality services tailored to their platforms and environments.

Every investment a customer makes with NETbuilder should improve security posture and increase operational efficiency. We achieve this by applying the right expertise, services, and tools at every critical stage.

About the Team

NETbuilder’s Managed Security Services practice specializes in running and improving security operations for mid-market and enterprise customers using the platforms in which they have already invested.

This is an early-stage opportunity with proven traction. NETbuilder has already onboarded its first fourteen managed security services customers and is now building the sales engine, partner motion, and delivery capacity required to expand that base to hundreds of customers.

We have distinct offerings for our two core markets. Enterprise customers receive tailored, engineering-led services for complex security environments, including co-managed and fully managed operations. Mid-market customers receive standardized, outcome-focused services designed for rapid onboarding, predictable value, and scalable protection.

Our expertise spans CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM, Splunk, and Cisco Security. We deliver holistic security services across detection engineering, telemetry and data-source health, threat intelligence, and 24/7/365 SOC monitoring and incident response.

We offer two primary engagement models:

- Augmenting existing security operations teams. We work alongside customers’ internal security teams, restoring valuable time and capacity so they can focus on critical security priorities, actions, and initiatives.
- Running day-to-day security operations. We take ownership and accountability for security operations on our customers’ behalf, operating 24/7/365. We improve security posture and data maturity while providing a clear path for service transition when the customer is ready.

We position ourselves as a managed service partner, not simply a managed service vendor: communication-first, engineering-led, and accountable for outcomes.

The practice is growing rapidly, and this role will be central to how we turn early customer success into a repeatable global growth business.

About the Role

Are you highly motivated and relentlessly focused on achieving the best outcomes for your customers?

Do you have an inquisitive mindset and a genuine desire to learn in an ever-evolving security landscape?

Are you successful yet humble, with a partner-first, customer-centric approach to creating shared success?

If this sounds like you, read on…

This is a critical, high-impact hire for NETbuilder as we accelerate growth across the United Kingdom. You will build your business by landing new logos, co-selling with our strategic platform and channel partners, and growing existing accounts across our enterprise and mid-market propositions.

You will own opportunities from the first conversation through the initial contract and beyond. You will lead discovery with security leaders, shape engagements alongside our solutions and service delivery teams, and close multi-year recurring-revenue agreements.

This is an individual-contributor sales leadership role reporting directly to the VP of Sales, EMEA. You will work closely with internal stakeholders, including our CISO and Global Head of Managed Services.

The territory and sales playbook are still being built. You will have the opportunity to shape both, influence how we take our differentiated offerings to market, and work directly with the managed services leadership and delivery organization behind what you sell.

What You’ll Do

- Hunt for new business. Build and manage pipeline through outbound prospecting into security and IT leadership teams at mid-market and enterprise organizations.
- Help turn early traction into scale. Build on our base of existing managed security services customers by developing repeatable sales motions that can support growth to hundreds.
- Activate the partner ecosystem. Develop strong relationships with CrowdStrike and Splunk field sellers, as well as reseller and distribution partners. Source referred and co-sold opportunities and keep NETbuilder top of mind within their accounts.
- Run the full sales cycle. Lead discovery, qualify opportunities against our engagement models, coordinate scoping with our solutions and delivery teams, develop proposals and statements of work with sales leadership, and negotiate through close.
- Sell to two distinct markets. Position NETbuilder’s enterprise and mid-market offerings clearly, adapting the value proposition, commercial approach, and sales motion to each customer’s needs.
- Grow existing accounts. Own managed security services sales across an agreed portfolio of existing services customers, identifying opportunities to protect, renew, and expand each relationship.
- Sell consultatively. Translate SOC operations, detection engineering, SIEM, and AI security concepts into meaningful business outcomes for CISOs, Security Directors, and SOC Managers. You will be comfortable contributing to technical conversations alongside our engineers.
- Keep the system honest. Maintain accurate pipeline, forecast, and activity data in our CRM, contributing to a forecast the business can confidently plan around.
- Show up in the market. Represent NETbuilder at industry events, partner events, and customer meetings, with travel as required.

What You’ll Bring

- 3-5+ years of quota-carrying B2B sales experience, including at least two years selling Managed Security Services such as MDR, MSSP, managed SIEM, SOC-as-a-Service, or co-managed security operations.
- A strong working knowledge of the cybersecurity market. You understand what a SOC does, how SIEM and EDR/XDR fit together, and why organizations invest in managed detection and response. You can speak credibly with the people responsible for running security programs.
- A track record of closing recurring-revenue service engagements involving MRR or ARR, rather than solely professional services, product, or license transactions. You have experience navigating multi-stakeholder deals involving security, IT, procurement, and legal teams.
- Experience working within partner ecosystems, including channel partners, distributors, or technology alliance programs. You have the instincts and experience to build pipeline through partners rather than around them.
- Strong discovery and consultative selling skills. You diagnose before you prescribe and scope engagements that customers can grow with rather than quickly churn out of.
- Disciplined pipeline management and CRM hygiene. You maintain accurate records and forecast what you genuinely expect to close.
- Highly preferred based in London, with the ability to travel for customer, partner, and industry engagements.
- A naturally curious and inquisitive mindset, with a commitment to continually expanding your knowledge in an ever-evolving security landscape.

Nice to Have

- Direct experience within the CrowdStrike or Splunk ecosystems, whether selling the platforms themselves, selling services built around them, or co-selling alongside their field teams. Experience with Cisco Security is also valuable.
- An existing network of security buyers, including CISOs, Security Directors, and SOC leaders, or channel relationships you can activate.
- Familiarity with how managed security engagements are scoped and contracted, including statements of work, service tiers, onboarding timelines, and renewal cycles.
- Experience working in a high-growth services business where sellers help shape the playbook, proposition, and routes to market rather than simply execute an established model.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

- Built a self-sustaining pipeline across direct, vendor and channel-partner routes to market.
- Closed new managed security services customers and created meaningful multi-year recurring revenue.
- Advanced our scale-up journey from an initial base of 14 customers toward a business capable of supporting hundreds.
- Protected and expanded your renewal portfolio.
- Become a seller that partners actively bring into their customer accounts, particularly across the CrowdStrike and Splunk ecosystems.
- Developed a strong understanding of our service catalog and the ability to position our enterprise and mid-market offerings confidently.
- Made a meaningful contribution to improving the sales playbook, propositions, and go-to-market approach.

You will leave the sales playbook better than you found it.

Technical System Design 

Serve as a subject matter expert and technical authority in image, sound, and integrated system design across Netflix’s global portfolio of specialty creative spaces.

Acoustic standards (e.g., NC ratings, isolation)
Room geometry, sightlines, and viewing conditions
Functional Room Orientation & layouts aligned to production and post-production workflows

Partner with internal network engineering teams to troubleshoot high-performance media and corporate networks, ensuring reliable A/V transport, data flow, and remote access.
Support post-production pipelines and video encoding workflows, enabling creative teams to deliver world-class content without friction.

Create and maintain clear documentation including SOPs, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides, keeping them current as systems evolve.

job_title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer, Geospatial Visual Localization
job_description:
ABOUT NIANTIC SPATIAL

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Research Engineer to help develop our Geospatial Visual Localization technologies, which allows people and robots to accurately localize themselves anywhere on the planet.

This is an end-to-end applied research role. You will develop new approaches to open problems alongside our researchers in 3D vision and machine learning, and publish your work at leading conferences. You will help build and train large models on large-scale multi-modal datasets, including our proprietary collection of 30 billion posed images and ship them into production, to be used by people and robots from all over the world.

Our team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and other handheld devices, 360 cameras, vehicles, and drones, as well as aerial and satellite imagery, LiDAR, and external geographic data. Your focus will be to improve accuracy and robustness across urban and rural locations, cameras, seasons, weather, and capture quality. The system must remain reliable with noisy GPS, in GPS-denied environments, and with outdated reference maps. Each pose estimate comes with an uncertainty that our customers rely on, and keeping it well calibrated across these conditions is part of the work.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, implement, and evaluate novel visual localization algorithms, combining 3D vision and deep learning.

 - Train large models on multi-modal data at scale, and build the benchmarks that measure their accuracy and robustness.

 - Develop robust solutions for difficult real-world conditions: noisy or denied GPS, changing appearance, varying capture quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps.

 - Work side-by-side with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping, as well as engineering and product teams, to identify the highest-impact problems and turn research into end-to-end solutions that operate at production scale.

 - Communicate results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, internal presentations, and publications.

 - Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, deep learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related field.

 - Demonstrated experience with multi-view geometry and related problems, such as camera pose estimation, monocular depth estimation, SfM, SLAM, georeferencing, point-cloud registration, or sensor fusion.

 - Knowledge of transformer models for 3D vision, such as vision foundation models, feed-forward 3D reconstruction, or multi-view and multi-modal attention.

 - Knowledge of geospatial data and coordinate reference systems.

 - Ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose appropriate mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously.

 - Strong Python skills and experience training deep learning models at scale, with libraries such as PyTorch, NumPy, and SciPy.

 - Strong software engineering skills, with the ability to turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems.

 - Experience taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data.

You will be the first product leader for the model and the data it learns from, reporting to the Chief Product Officer. You decide which capabilities it gains and in what order, the bar each release has to clear, and what data Niantic Spatial collects, licenses or partners for to get there. You set those priorities directly with the Chief Scientist and the London research team who train the model.

If you have shipped a frontier language model, most of the job will be familiar: evals, data mix and release decisions. The job differs in two ways. Every output of this model can be scored against a measured real place, so its evals rest on ground truth. And its data is collected in the physical world, so choosing what to capture next is a product decision with a real cost. Experience in 3D or mapping is welcome but not required.

By the end of your first year, research, engineering and the product leads for industrial, defense, robotics and platform customers work from one model roadmap that you own, each release ships against evals you wrote, and the model's newest capabilities are in customers' hands.

Set the curation, labeling, consent, privacy and training-rights requirements every dataset has to meet, and keep a record of which data went into each model version.

The Role
01 — AI Engineer

Agentic Finance · UK, Luxembourg, Portugal, Spain, Remote-EU · Several roles
AI Engineer, Agent Systems
Noumenai builds AI that does real finance work. Not summarisation. Not a copilot that drafts something a person then rewrites. Agents that go into a financial system, take a position on what a transaction is and — when the evidence and the confidence justify it — post it. Ledger, reconciliations, close, tax. The work that was always done by people because the cost of being wrong was too high to automate.
That cost hasn't gone away. The models are what finally got good enough to make it worth engineering around it. That engineering — not the model — is the company.
We're hiring several engineers into this team, and we're open at more than one level. If you're strong but unsure whether you're "senior enough", tell us where you think you sit and let us judge. We'd rather have that conversation than lose you to a job title.

We're hiring several. Open at more than one level.

The Role
02 — What you'd do

You own a surface, end to end.
Writing code is no longer the scarce resource. Judgment is.You'll own a real surface of the system — an agent tool family, a connector boundary, an evaluation harness — and you'll own it end to end: design, build, prove it against a live system, and keep it working when reality disagrees with the plan.
You'll work inside an architecture that already exists: the gates, the confidence policy, the agency budget, the tenancy model. You're not asked to invent those from nothing — you're asked to understand why they're there, build well within them, and say so clearly when something doesn't hold.
You'll drive an agent to build most of it. That's how this company works, and it's not optional.

In Production
03 — We are not an idea

There is product in production.
Today, in a client's real accounting, with a live write path into an ERP — reviewer, confidence gates, audit trail. Built in a matter of months.
There are enterprise clients in the pipeline, and the incubation of a joint venture with a multinational group.

The Domain
04 — What this domain actually demands

Agentic finance is not a normal software problem.
These four things apply at every level here, including yours. They are not seniority markers — they are how we work.

• 01
The failure mode is being confidently wrong.
A model produces a plausible number for anything. Accounting is full of numbers that look right. Our discipline is that the model never originates a value — it chooses the method and explains itself, and deterministic code produces the number. You need to feel why that boundary exists, not treat it as a rule someone handed you.

• 02
Some actions can't be undone.
A read is free. A posting to a client's ledger is not — some systems don't even offer reversal. Our agency budget tracks reversibility: reversible work runs autonomously, irreversible work is gated at the exit, always, with a reviewer and a human. You'll move fast and you'll be stopped hard, and both are the job.

• 03
The state of the code is not the real state.
Migration files are not the database. Mocks are not the API. Green CI has meant nothing, repeatedly. Bugs concentrate exactly at the boundaries where someone trusted the shape of a system instead of going to look. The engineer we want is the one who goes and looks — by reflex, unprompted, before claiming anything at all.

• 04
The domain has opinions.
Accountants and controllers have been doing this for a long time and are right more often than software assumes. When the system disagrees with an expert, the presumption is that the system is wrong. Engineering that can't hold that posture doesn't survive contact with a client.

The Work
05 — What you'll work on

Representative, not exhaustive.
Agent tools and tool families
Designing and building the tools an agent calls: their contracts, their failure modes, their observability. Tool design is product design — a badly shaped tool produces a badly behaved agent.

Connector boundaries
ERPs and financial platforms are hostile, badly documented and idiosyncratic. You'll probe them in a real environment before declaring a boundary functional, and build fixtures from captured real responses, never from imagination.

Evaluation harnesses
Making regressions visible instead of mysterious. If we can't measure whether a change made the system better or worse, we're guessing — and guessing is not available to us.

Features on the write path
Building within the gates: the audit trail, the identity of who acts, the failure semantics. You won't design the trust boundary, but you will build things that depend on it holding.

Data and retrieval surfaces
Institutional memory, grounding, and the retrieval that makes a proposal defensible rather than plausible.

The Fit
06 — What we're looking for

The same four qualities, at every level.
Scepticism, applied to your own work
The rarest quality and the one that counts most. You should feel uncomfortable saying something works before you've watched it work.

Judgment at the boundaries
Knowing which decisions are cheap to reverse and which ones you only get one attempt at — and spending your caution accordingly.

Fluency driving agents
If you're still typing everything by hand, you'll be slow. If you ship whatever comes out of the model, you'll be dangerous.

Honesty under commercial pressure
There will be moments when claiming a capability we haven't built would help close a deal. We don't — not even between ourselves.

Background
07 — You probably already have

What tends to be true of the right person.
• Production experience where being wrong had consequences — payments, fintech, healthcare, infrastructure, trading. Not demos.
• TypeScript and/or Python, and real comfort in a codebase you didn't write.
• Solid Postgres. You should not be frightened by row-level security, even if you haven't implemented it.
More→• Cloud fluency. We're on AWS: ECS/Fargate, SQS, Secrets Manager, Bedrock.
• Claude Code as a daily working instrument — not experimenting, but shipping with it: discovery before implementation, explicit stop gates, one logical unit per PR, diff review before merge.
• Familiarity with the Claude Agent SDK / API — agent loops, tool use, context management across hops.
• MCP (Model Context Protocol) — ideally building servers and tools, not just consuming them.
• LLM systems in production — not prompt engineering, not a RAG demo.
• The habit of reading the source, the docs, or the actual response before claiming something works.
• A quantitative foundation you can reason from, and the ability to read a paper critically when the problem calls for it.

Not Required
08 — What you don't need to have

Four things we don't ask for.
Knowing finance
We'll teach you the parts that matter and shield you from the rest.

A PhD
Not even a Computer Science degree — as long as the foundation is there.

Being a '10x engineer'
A 1x engineer with excellent judgment and a very good model is worth more, and that's what we prefer.

Having architected a trust boundary before
That's what the senior people here are for. You need to understand why it exists and build honestly within it.

The Process
09 — How this moves forward

Two conversations. No whiteboard.
No whiteboard, no algorithm puzzles, no unpaid weekend project.
In the first, we put a real problem on the table — not a sanitised version — and we think about it together, out loud. It doesn't matter whether you reach the right answer. It matters how you think when you don't know.
In the second, you take us to the bottom of a system you built, down to the layer where even you aren't certain any more.
If at any point you tell us I don't know, I'd have to go and look — that counts in your favour.

The conversation you'll want to have
You'll want to know what this actually is — compensation, level, how the day-to-day works, who we are to you and who you'd be to us. We're not going to answer that on a recruitment page. We'll answer it in the first conversation, plainly and without vagueness. What we can tell you now: we're not asking you to trade salary for a promise.

Proposer/reviewer loops, confidence policy, tool-calling over enterprise systems, evaluation harnesses that make regressions visible instead of mysterious.

Multi-tenancy done properly
Isolation enforced by the database, not by the discipline of whoever is writing. Entitlements with a single source of truth. This is a commercial and liability boundary, not tech debt.

The write path
The gates, the audit trail, the identity of who acts, the failure semantics. Getting this right is most of the trust.

Boundaries with enterprise systems
ERPs and financial platforms are hostile, badly documented and idiosyncratic. Probe in a real environment before declaring a boundary functional. Fixtures are born from captured real responses, never from imagination.

Joint venture incubation
Being part of the incubation of a joint venture with a multinational group.

Theory
06 — Why theory matters

This is a domain new enough that nobody has a playbook yet.
When you decide how much autonomy to give an agent, where to place the reviewer, what "confidence" means in a number, or why a model hallucinates precisely there and not somewhere else — you won't find the answer on Stack Overflow. You'll have to derive it.
That's why we want someone with a serious theoretical foundation. Not because we like credentials, but for three practical reasons:

Why we ask for it→Telling what's possible from what's hype
Half of what's claimed about agents today is false, and the other half is possible but nobody has built it yet. Knowing where to draw that line — with credibility, not by instinct — saves us quarters.

Knowing what has already been solved
A large share of the problems that look new in agentic finance are versions of old ones: verification, consensus under uncertainty, decision theory with asymmetric costs, distributed systems, control. Someone who knows the literature doesn't badly reinvent what already exists well.

Arguing from first principles
When the system's behaviour is surprising — and it will be — the question is why, not which workaround. We need someone who can reason from the mechanics, not the anecdote.

We're not asking for a PhD. We're asking for someone who reads papers and knows how to critique them, who understands the mathematics underneath what they use, and who can explain to a CFO — without overclaiming and without hiding behind jargon — what these systems can and cannot do.

The Fit
07 — What we're looking for

Four qualities, in order of rarity.
Scepticism, applied to your own work
The rarest quality and the one that counts most. You should feel uncomfortable saying something works before you've watched it work.

Judgment at the boundaries
Knowing which decisions are cheap to reverse and which ones you only get one attempt at — and spending your caution accordingly.

Fluency driving agents
If you're still typing everything by hand, you'll be slow. If you ship whatever comes out of the model, you'll be dangerous.

Honesty under commercial pressure
There will be moments when claiming a capability we haven't built would help close a deal. We don't — not even between ourselves.

Background
08 — You probably already have

What tends to be true of the right person.
• A credible, living theoretical foundation. Solid training in a quantitative discipline — computer science, mathematics, physics, engineering, economics, operations research — or a self-taught path that stands up to the same scrutiny. It matters less where you studied; it matters that you keep reading the state of the art, that you can read a paper with a critical eye rather than a reverent one, and that theory informs what you build instead of sitting on your CV. Published research is welcome, not required.
• Production systems where being wrong had real consequences — payments, fintech, healthcare, infrastructure, trading. Not demos.
• Serious Postgres. Row-level security, not just an ORM.
Seven more→• Cloud fluency. We're on AWS: ECS/Fargate, SQS, Secrets Manager, Bedrock.
• TypeScript and/or Python.
• Claude Code as a daily working instrument — not experimenting, but shipping with it: discovery before implementation, explicit stop gates, one logical unit per PR, diff review before merge.
• Experience with the Claude Agent SDK / API — agent loops, tool use, context management across hops; an agent with write access is an architecture decision, not a feature.
• MCP (Model Context Protocol) — building servers and tools, not just consuming them. Understanding that tool design is product design.
• LLM systems in production — not prompt engineering, not a RAG demo.
• A scar from a non-deterministic system, and you can describe it precisely.

Not Required
09 — What you don't need to have

Three things we don't ask for.
Knowing finance
We'll teach you the parts that matter and shield you from the rest.

A PhD
Not even a Computer Science degree — as long as the foundation is there.

Being a '10x engineer'
A 1x engineer with excellent judgment and a very good model is worth more, and that's what we prefer.

The Process
10 — How this moves forward

Two conversations. No whiteboard.
No whiteboard, no algorithm puzzles, no unpaid weekend project.
In the first, we put a real unsolved problem on the table — not a sanitised version — and we think about it together, out loud. It doesn't matter whether you reach the right answer. It matters how you think when you don't know.
In the second, you take us to the bottom of a system you built, down to the layer where even you aren't certain any more.
If at any point you tell us I don't know, I'd have to go and look — that counts in your favour.

The conversation you'll want to have
You'll want to know what this actually is — compensation, equity, how the day-to-day works, who we are to you and who you'd be to us. We're not going to answer that on a recruitment page. We'll answer it in the first conversation, plainly and without vagueness, because that's how we like to work and because it's the least we owe someone who is doing fine where they are. What we can tell you now: we're not asking you to trade salary for a promise.
